modules.title: Classical systems: unique decomposition into pure states
modules.doc:
Pure decompositions, simplex and Bauer simplex state spaces, and measures as functionals.

## i. Overview

A system is classical when every state is a mixture of pure states in exactly one way. A die is the
basic example. Its pure states are the six outcomes. Every state is a probability vector, and the
state fixes the probabilities.

Geometrically, the states of a die form a simplex: the convex hull of six affinely independent
points. The weights of a state are its barycentric coordinates. In infinite dimensions there can be
infinitely many pure states, and the weights become a probability measure on the pure states. We
call this measure a pure decomposition. The state space is a simplex when every state has exactly
one pure decomposition. It is a Bauer simplex when moreover the pure states form a closed set.

A qubit is not classical. The maximally mixed state is an equal mixture of spin up and spin down,
but also of spin left and spin right.

On a simplex, measures on the pure states are the same as positive functionals on the observables,
and this identification respects the order.

## ii. Key results

- `UnitalPositiveLinearMap.HasPureDecomposition` states that a state is a mixture of pure states.
- `UnitalPositiveLinearMap.HasUniquePureDecomposition` states that it is so in exactly one way.
- `IsSimplexStateSpace E` states that every state has exactly one pure decomposition.
- `IsBauerSimplexStateSpace E` states in addition that the pure states form a closed set.
- `PureState.toPositive` turns a measure on the pure states into a positive functional.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Pure decompositions and simplices
- B. Measures on the pure states as positive functionals
- C. Simplices identify functionals with measures

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.HasPureDecomposition

The state `ω` decomposes into pure states: some regular probability measure on the pure states
represents it.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.IsSimplexStateSpace
declarations.doc:
The state space of `E` is a simplex: every state is a unique mixture of pure states, given by
a regular probability measure on the pure states. In finite dimension this is the convex hull of
affinely independent pure states, every state having unique barycentric coordinates.
declarations.statement: def IsSimplexStateSpace : Prop

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.IsBauerSimplexStateSpace
declarations.doc:
The state space of `E` is a Bauer simplex: a simplex whose pure states form a closed, hence
compact, set.
declarations.statement: def IsBauerSimplexStateSpace : Prop

modules.title: Uniqueness of pure decompositions
modules.doc:
Choquet–Meyer uniqueness: when ensembles refine, pure decompositions are unique.

## i. Overview

When ensembles refine, every state has at most one pure decomposition. This is the uniqueness half
of the Choquet–Meyer theorem.

A measure on the pure states is fixed by the averages it gives to continuous functions. We test it
on special functions: the largest of finitely many expectation values, `ω ↦ max (ω A₁) … (ω Aₙ)`.
Every pure decomposition of a state `ω` averages this function to the same number, the upper
envelope of `A₁, …, Aₙ` at `ω`. To see this, cut the pure states into small pieces on each of which
one `Aᵢ` is nearly the largest, and glue the pieces with refinement. These test functions and their
differences are dense among all continuous functions, so two pure decompositions of the same state
agree.

## ii. Key results

- `StateSpace.maxApply` is the largest expectation value of a state on finitely many observables.
- `PureState.integral_maxApply_eq` proves that, when ensembles refine, a pure decomposition averages
  the largest value to the upper envelope.
- `EnsemblesRefine.eq_of_toPositive_eq` proves that two measures on the pure states giving the same
  positive functional are equal. This is **Choquet–Meyer uniqueness**.
- `EnsemblesRefine.hasUniquePureDecomposition` proves that, when ensembles refine, a pure
  decomposition is unique.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The largest value on a finite family
- B. Integrating the largest value
- C. Integrating the largest value when ensembles refine
- D. Density of largest values
- E. Uniqueness
- F. Unique pure decompositions

## iv. References

- G. Choquet and P.-A. Meyer, *Existence et unicité des représentations intégrales dans les
  convexes compacts quelconques*, Ann. Inst. Fourier 13 (1963), 139–154.
- E. M. Alfsen, *Compact Convex Sets and Boundary Integrals*, Springer, 1971, ch. II.3.

    ∃ W : Set (PureState E), IsOpen W ∧ e ∈ W ∧ ∀ A ⊆ W, MeasurableSet A →

    {r₁ r₂ : ℝ}

    (h₂ : upperEnvelope s (toPositive (μ.restrict (A \ W))) ≤

modules.title: Complete positivity of classical channels
modules.doc:
Channels into or out of a classical (nuclear) system are completely positive.

## i. Overview

A channel acting on one part of a composite system should keep every nonnegative composite
observable nonnegative, whatever the other part is. This is complete positivity, and it depends
on which composite is used. For a channel into or out of a classical system it holds for every
choice of composites: a classical system composes uniquely, so there is only one composite to
check, and positive maps preserve the minimal and the maximal cone.

Precisely, let `A` be any Archimedean ancilla. Then `φ ⊗ id` maps every composite observable in
the maximal cone into every Archimedean cone that contains the minimal cone, whenever the input or
the output of `φ` is classical. In particular it maps any composite of the input with `A` into any
Archimedean composite of the output with `A`. For a classical input `φ` must be a channel;
for a classical output any positive map works.

## ii. Key results

- `CompositeCone.map_mem_of_isNuclear_left` : a channel out of a nuclear system is completely
  positive.
- `CompositeCone.map_mem_of_isNuclear_right` : a positive map into a nuclear system is completely
  positive.
- `CompositeCone.map_mem_of_isNuclear_left'`, `CompositeCone.map_mem_of_isNuclear_right'` : the
  same, stated for composites.
- `CompositeCone.map_mem_of_isClassical_left`, `CompositeCone.map_mem_of_isClassical_right` : the
  same for classical systems.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Tensoring with the identity
- B. Nuclear inputs and outputs
- C. Classical inputs and outputs

## iv. References

* None.

      (1 : F) ⊗ₜ[ℝ] (1 : A)

**A channel out of a nuclear system is completely positive.** Applied to the first part of a

modules.title: Composite systems
modules.doc:
Composite systems: the minimal and maximal tensor cones, composites, and nuclear systems.

## i. Overview

Two systems with observables `E` and `F` are combined into a composite system whose observables
are the tensor products `E ⊗ F`. Which composite observables are nonnegative is not fixed by the
parts; there are two extreme choices.

The minimal cone contains only the sums of products `x ⊗ y` of nonnegative observables: nonnegative
local observations. The maximal cone contains every composite observable that no pair of local
preparations `φ ⊗ ψ` can assign a negative value. A composite of `E` and `F` is any choice of
nonnegative composite observables in between. Tensor products of positive maps preserve both
extreme cones.

A system is nuclear when, for every other system, the maximal cone lies in the closure of the
minimal cone: its composites are unique.

## ii. Key results

- `Composite E F` : the observables of the composite system.
- `PositiveLinearMap.tensor` : the product functional `φ ⊗ ψ`.
- `minTensorCone E F`, `maxTensorCone E F` : the minimal and the maximal cone.
- `mem_maxTensorCone` : the maximal cone consists of the composite observables that every product
  functional keeps nonnegative.
- `minTensorCone_map_le`, `maxTensorCone_map_le` : tensor products of positive maps preserve the
  minimal and the maximal cone.
- `CompositeCone E F` : a composite of `E` and `F`.
- `isDominatedCone_minTensorCone` : every composite observable plus a large multiple of `1 ⊗ 1` lies
  in the minimal cone.
- `minTensorClosure E F` : the Archimedean closure of the minimal cone.
- `IsNuclear E` : composition with every Archimedean system is unique, up to closure.
- `mem_maxTensorCone_iff_rslice` : for Archimedean `E`, the maximal cone consists of the composite
  observables that stay nonnegative when a positive functional is applied to the second factor.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Slices and product functionals
- B. The minimal and the maximal cone
- C. Tensor products of positive maps
- D. Composites
- E. The closure of the minimal cone and nuclear systems

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: PositiveLinearMap.rslice
declarations.doc: Apply a positive functional to the second factor.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def rslice (ψ : F →ₚ[ℝ] ℝ) : E ⊗[ℝ] F →ₗ[ℝ] E

declarations.name: PositiveLinearMap.lslice
declarations.doc: Apply a positive functional to the first factor.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def lslice (φ : E →ₚ[ℝ] ℝ) : E ⊗[ℝ] F →ₗ[ℝ] F

declarations.name: PositiveLinearMap.rslice_tmul
declarations.statement: lemma rslice_tmul (ψ : F →ₚ[ℝ] ℝ) (x : E) (y : F) : rslice ψ (x ⊗ₜ[ℝ] y) = ψ y • x

declarations.name: PositiveLinearMap.lslice_tmul
declarations.statement: lemma lslice_tmul (φ : E →ₚ[ℝ] ℝ) (x : E) (y : F) : lslice φ (x ⊗ₜ[ℝ] y) = φ x • y

declarations.name: PositiveLinearMap.tensor
declarations.doc: The product functional `φ ⊗ ψ`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def tensor (φ : E →ₚ[ℝ] ℝ) (ψ : F →ₚ[ℝ] ℝ) : E ⊗[ℝ] F →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ

declarations.name: PositiveLinearMap.tensor_tmul
declarations.statement:
lemma tensor_tmul (φ : E →ₚ[ℝ] ℝ) (ψ : F →ₚ[ℝ] ℝ) (x : E) (y : F) :
    tensor φ ψ (x ⊗ₜ[ℝ] y) = φ x * ψ y

declarations.name: PositiveLinearMap.tensor_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma tensor_apply (φ : E →ₚ[ℝ] ℝ) (ψ : F →ₚ[ℝ] ℝ) (z : E ⊗[ℝ] F) :
    tensor φ ψ z = φ (rslice ψ z)

declarations.name: PositiveLinearMap.tensor_apply_eq_lslice
declarations.statement:
lemma tensor_apply_eq_lslice (φ : E →ₚ[ℝ] ℝ) (ψ : F →ₚ[ℝ] ℝ) (z : E ⊗[ℝ] F) :
    tensor φ ψ z = ψ (lslice φ z)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.minTensorCone
declarations.doc: The minimal tensor cone: sums of products of nonnegative observables.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def minTensorCone : PointedCone ℝ (E ⊗[ℝ] F)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.maxTensorCone
declarations.doc:
The maximal tensor cone: composite observables to which no product of positive functionals
assigns a negative value.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def maxTensorCone : PointedCone ℝ (E ⊗[ℝ] F)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.tmul_mem_minTensorCone
declarations.statement:
lemma tmul_mem_minTensorCone {x : E} {y : F} (hx : 0 ≤ x) (hy : 0 ≤ y) :
    x ⊗ₜ[ℝ] y ∈ minTensorCone E F

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.smul_mem_minTensorCone
declarations.statement:
lemma smul_mem_minTensorCone {c : ℝ} (hc : 0 ≤ c) {w : E ⊗[ℝ] F} (hw : w ∈ minTensorCone E F) :
    c • w ∈ minTensorCone E F

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.minTensorCone_induction
declarations.doc:
An induction principle for the minimal cone: a property of composite observables that holds
for products of nonnegative observables and is stable under sums and nonnegative multiples holds
on the whole minimal cone.
declarations.statement:
lemma minTensorCone_induction {p : E ⊗[ℝ] F → Prop} {z : E ⊗[ℝ] F} (hz : z ∈ minTensorCone E F)
    (tmul : ∀ x y, 0 ≤ x → 0 ≤ y → p (x ⊗ₜ[ℝ] y)) (zero : p 0)
    (add : ∀ z w, p z → p w → p (z + w)) (smul : ∀ c : ℝ, 0 ≤ c → ∀ z, p z → p (c • z)) :
    p z

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.tensor_eq_dualDistrib
declarations.doc: The product functional of positive functionals is the pairing with their dual tensor.
declarations.statement:
lemma tensor_eq_dualDistrib (φ : E →ₚ[ℝ] ℝ) (ψ : F →ₚ[ℝ] ℝ) (z : E ⊗[ℝ] F) :
    tensor φ ψ z = dualDistrib ℝ E F (φ.toLinearMap ⊗ₜ[ℝ] ψ.toLinearMap) z

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.mem_maxTensorCone
declarations.doc:
A composite observable is in the maximal cone exactly when every product of positive
functionals assigns it a nonnegative value.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_maxTensorCone {z : E ⊗[ℝ] F} :
    z ∈ maxTensorCone E F ↔ ∀ (φ : E →ₚ[ℝ] ℝ) (ψ : F →ₚ[ℝ] ℝ), 0 ≤ tensor φ ψ z

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.minTensorCone_le_maxTensorCone
declarations.doc: Every observable in the minimal cone is in the maximal cone.
declarations.statement: lemma minTensorCone_le_maxTensorCone : minTensorCone E F ≤ maxTensorCone E F

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.posCone_map_le
declarations.statement: lemma posCone_map_le (φ : E →ₚ[ℝ] E') : (PosCone E).map φ.toLinearMap ≤ PosCone E'

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.minTensorCone_map_le
declarations.doc: Tensor products of positive maps preserve the minimal cone.
declarations.statement:
lemma minTensorCone_map_le (φ : E →ₚ[ℝ] E') (ψ : F →ₚ[ℝ] F') :
    (minTensorCone E F).map (TensorProduct.map φ.toLinearMap ψ.toLinearMap) ≤
      minTensorCone E' F'

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.maxTensorCone_map_le
declarations.doc: Tensor products of positive maps preserve the maximal cone.
declarations.statement:
lemma maxTensorCone_map_le (φ : E →ₚ[ℝ] E') (ψ : F →ₚ[ℝ] F') :
    (maxTensorCone E F).map (TensorProduct.map φ.toLinearMap ψ.toLinearMap) ≤
      maxTensorCone E' F'

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.map_mem_minTensorCone
ProbabilisticTheory.map_mem_maxTensorCone
ProbabilisticTheory.IsArchimedeanTensorCone
declarations.doc:
A cone of composite observables is Archimedean when a composite observable that becomes
nonnegative after adding any positive multiple of the unit `1 ⊗ 1` is already nonnegative.
declarations.statement: def IsArchimedeanTensorCone (C : PointedCone ℝ (E ⊗[ℝ] F)) : Prop

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.CompositeCone
declarations.doc:
A composite of two systems: a choice of nonnegative composite observables that contains every
product of nonnegative observables and that no product of positive functionals makes negative.
declarations.statement:
structure CompositeCone where
  /-- The nonnegative composite observables. -/
  toPointedCone : PointedCone ℝ (E ⊗[ℝ] F)
  /-- Products of nonnegative observables are nonnegative. -/
  min_le : minTensorCone E F ≤ toPointedCone
  /-- Products of positive functionals stay nonnegative. -/
  le_max : toPointedCone ≤ maxTensorCone E F
instance : SetLike (CompositeCone E F) (E ⊗[ℝ] F)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.CompositeCone.mem_toPointedCone
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_toPointedCone {C : CompositeCone E F} {z : E ⊗[ℝ] F} :
    z ∈ C.toPointedCone ↔ z ∈ C

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.CompositeCone.ext
declarations.statement: lemma ext {C D : CompositeCone E F} (h : ∀ z, z ∈ C ↔ z ∈ D) : C = D

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.CompositeCone.tmul_mem
declarations.statement:
lemma tmul_mem (C : CompositeCone E F) {x : E} {y : F} (hx : 0 ≤ x) (hy : 0 ≤ y) :
    x ⊗ₜ[ℝ] y ∈ C

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.CompositeCone.tensor_nonneg
declarations.doc: Every product of positive functionals is nonnegative on a composite.
declarations.statement:
lemma tensor_nonneg (C : CompositeCone E F) (φ : E →ₚ[ℝ] ℝ) (ψ : F →ₚ[ℝ] ℝ) {z : E ⊗[ℝ] F}
    (hz : z ∈ C) : 0 ≤ tensor φ ψ z

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.CompositeCone.instModuleNNReal
declarations.doc: The elements of a composite form an `ℝ≥0`-module.
declarations.statement: instance instModuleNNReal (C : CompositeCone E F) : Module ℝ≥0 C.toPointedCone

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.CompositeCone.minimal
declarations.doc: The minimal composite.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def minimal : CompositeCone E F

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.CompositeCone.maximal
declarations.doc: The maximal composite.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def maximal : CompositeCone E F

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.CompositeCone.IsArchimedean
declarations.doc:
A composite is Archimedean when a composite observable that becomes nonnegative after adding
any positive multiple of the unit `1 ⊗ 1` is already nonnegative.
declarations.statement: def IsArchimedean (C : CompositeCone E F) : Prop

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.CompositeCone.tmulRight
declarations.doc:
For fixed `0 ≤ y₀`, tensoring on the right with `y₀` maps nonnegative observables of `E`
`ℝ≥0`-linearly into any composite.
declarations.statement:
def tmulRight (C : CompositeCone E F) {y₀ : F} (hy₀ : 0 ≤ y₀) :
    PosCone E →ₗ[ℝ≥0] C.toPointedCone

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.CompositeCone.tmulRight_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma tmulRight_apply (C : CompositeCone E F) {y₀ : F} (hy₀ : 0 ≤ y₀) (x : PosCone E) :
    (C.tmulRight hy₀ x : E ⊗[ℝ] F) = (x : E) ⊗ₜ[ℝ] y₀

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.CompositeCone.tmulLeft
declarations.doc:
For fixed `0 ≤ x₀`, tensoring on the left with `x₀` maps nonnegative observables of `F`
`ℝ≥0`-linearly into any composite.
declarations.statement:
def tmulLeft (C : CompositeCone E F) {x₀ : E} (hx₀ : 0 ≤ x₀) :
    PosCone F →ₗ[ℝ≥0] C.toPointedCone

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.CompositeCone.tmulLeft_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma tmulLeft_apply (C : CompositeCone E F) {x₀ : E} (hx₀ : 0 ≤ x₀) (y : PosCone F) :
    (C.tmulLeft hx₀ y : E ⊗[ℝ] F) = x₀ ⊗ₜ[ℝ] (y : F)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.exists_eq_sub_minTensorCone
declarations.doc:
Every composite observable is a difference of two sums of products of nonnegative
observables.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_eq_sub_minTensorCone (t : E ⊗[ℝ] F) :
    ∃ tp ∈ minTensorCone E F, ∃ tn ∈ minTensorCone E F, t = tp - tn

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.exists_tmul_add_smul_mem
declarations.doc:
A product plus a large enough multiple of `1 ⊗ 1` lies in the minimal cone:
`x ⊗ y + (a * b) • (1 ⊗ 1)` is half the sum of `(a • 1 ± x) ⊗ (b • 1 ± y)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_tmul_add_smul_mem (x : E) (y : F) :
    ∃ t : ℝ, x ⊗ₜ[ℝ] y + t • ((1 : E) ⊗ₜ[ℝ] (1 : F)) ∈ minTensorCone E F

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.exists_add_smul_mem
declarations.doc: Every composite observable plus a large enough multiple of `1 ⊗ 1` lies in the minimal cone.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_add_smul_mem (z : E ⊗[ℝ] F) :
    ∃ t : ℝ, z + t • ((1 : E) ⊗ₜ[ℝ] (1 : F)) ∈ minTensorCone E F

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.isDominatedCone_minTensorCone
declarations.doc: The minimal cone is a convex cone dominated by `1 ⊗ 1`.
declarations.statement:
lemma isDominatedCone_minTensorCone :
    IsDominatedCone (minTensorCone E F : Set (E ⊗[ℝ] F)) ((1 : E) ⊗ₜ[ℝ] (1 : F))

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.minTensorClosure
declarations.doc:
The Archimedean closure of the minimal cone: composite observables that become sums of products
of nonnegative observables after adding any positive multiple of the unit `1 ⊗ 1`.
declarations.statement: def minTensorClosure : Set (E ⊗[ℝ] F)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.minTensorCone_subset_closure
declarations.statement:
lemma minTensorCone_subset_closure :
    (minTensorCone E F : Set (E ⊗[ℝ] F)) ⊆ minTensorClosure E F

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.minTensorClosure_subset_maxTensorCone
declarations.doc: The closure of the minimal cone lies in the maximal cone.
declarations.statement:
lemma minTensorClosure_subset_maxTensorCone :
    minTensorClosure E F ⊆ (maxTensorCone E F : Set (E ⊗[ℝ] F))

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.IsArchimedeanTensorCone.closure_subset
declarations.doc: An Archimedean cone containing the minimal cone contains its closure.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.CompositeCone.IsArchimedean.closure_subset
declarations.doc: An Archimedean composite contains the closure of the minimal cone.
declarations.statement:
lemma CompositeCone.IsArchimedean.closure_subset {C : CompositeCone E F} (hC : C.IsArchimedean) :
    minTensorClosure E F ⊆ C

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.IsNuclear
declarations.doc:
A system is nuclear when it composes uniquely with every Archimedean system: every composite
observable in the maximal cone lies in the closure of the minimal cone.
declarations.statement: def IsNuclear : Prop

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.mem_maxTensorCone_iff_rslice
declarations.doc:
For Archimedean `E`, a composite observable is in the maximal cone exactly when applying any
positive functional to the second factor leaves a nonnegative observable.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_maxTensorCone_iff_rslice {z : E ⊗[ℝ] F} :
    z ∈ maxTensorCone E F ↔ ∀ ψ : F →ₚ[ℝ] ℝ, 0 ≤ rslice ψ z

modules.title: ⋆-automorphisms and reversible dynamics
modules.doc:
⋆-automorphisms as channels on observables, and one-parameter groups of them as reversible dynamics.

## i. Overview

Reversible transformations of a quantum system act on its algebra by `⋆`-automorphisms. A
`⋆`-automorphism maps observables to observables, compatibly with composition, inverses and the Lie
bracket, and it is a quantum channel. A one-parameter group of `⋆`-automorphisms is reversible
dynamics; it can be transported along a `⋆`-isomorphism and induces dynamics of the observables.

## ii. Key results

- `StarAlgEquiv.observable` : a `⋆`-automorphism acting on observables.
- `StarAlgEquiv.observable_bracket` : `⋆`-automorphisms preserve the Lie bracket.
- `StarAlgEquiv.toQuantumChannel`, `StarAlgEquiv.toObservableChannel` : a `⋆`-isomorphism as a
  quantum channel and as a channel of observables.
- `AutomorphismGroup` : a one-parameter group of `⋆`-automorphisms.
- `AutomorphismGroup.conj` : conjugating dynamics by a `⋆`-automorphism.
- `AutomorphismGroup.toObservableDynamics` : the induced dynamics of observables.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Action on observables
- B. ⋆-isomorphisms as channels
- C. Reversible one-parameter dynamics
- D. Order-unit dynamics induced by C⋆-automorphisms
- E. Transporting and conjugating automorphism groups
- F. Conjugating an automorphism group by a star automorphism

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## D. Order-unit dynamics induced by C⋆-automorphisms

## E. Transporting and conjugating automorphism groups

A ⋆-isomorphism `β : A ≃⋆ₐ[ℂ] B` transports a dynamics on `A` to one on `B`. The defining
commuting square says that applying `β` after evolving in `A` agrees with evolving after applying
`β`. This is the dynamics-level counterpart of the channel covariance API: it is the form used by
a quadratic normal-form equivalence, and it also applies to any later change of algebraic
description.

Conjugation is the special case `A = B`.

## F. Conjugating an automorphism group by a star automorphism

Changing which ⋆-automorphism `β` identifies the algebra with itself conjugates a flow `α`:
`(conj β α) t = β ∘ α t ∘ β⁻¹`.

declarations.name: StarAlgEquiv.observable
declarations.doc: A ⋆-automorphism `β` acts on observables by `a ↦ β a`.
declarations.statement: def _root_.StarAlgEquiv.observable (β : A ≃⋆ₐ[ℂ] A) (a : Observable A) : Observable A

declarations.name: StarAlgEquiv.observable_coe
declarations.doc: Unfolds `StarAlgEquiv.observable` to its underlying algebra element.
declarations.statement:
lemma _root_.StarAlgEquiv.observable_coe (β : A ≃⋆ₐ[ℂ] A) (a : Observable A) :
    (β.observable a : A) = β (a : A)

declarations.name: StarAlgEquiv.refl_observable
declarations.doc: The identity automorphism acts trivially on observables.
declarations.statement:
lemma _root_.StarAlgEquiv.refl_observable :
    (StarAlgEquiv.refl (R := ℂ) (A := A)).observable = id

declarations.name: StarAlgEquiv.trans_observable
declarations.doc: Composing `β` then `γ` acts on observables as `γ ∘ β`.
declarations.statement:
lemma _root_.StarAlgEquiv.trans_observable (β γ : A ≃⋆ₐ[ℂ] A) (a : Observable A) :
    (β.trans γ).observable a = γ.observable (β.observable a)

declarations.name: StarAlgEquiv.symm_observable_observable
declarations.doc: Undoing `β.observable` by `β.symm.observable` recovers the original observable.
declarations.statement:
lemma _root_.StarAlgEquiv.symm_observable_observable (β : A ≃⋆ₐ[ℂ] A) (a : Observable A) :
    β.symm.observable (β.observable a) = a

declarations.name: StarAlgEquiv.observable_symm_observable
declarations.doc: Applying `β.observable` after `β.symm.observable` recovers the original observable.
declarations.statement:
lemma _root_.StarAlgEquiv.observable_symm_observable (β : A ≃⋆ₐ[ℂ] A) (a : Observable A) :
    β.observable (β.symm.observable a) = a

declarations.name: StarAlgEquiv.observable_bracket
declarations.doc: Star automorphisms preserve the observable Lie bracket.
declarations.statement:
lemma _root_.StarAlgEquiv.observable_bracket (β : A ≃⋆ₐ[ℂ] A) (a b : Observable A) :
    β.observable ⁅a, b⁆ = ⁅β.observable a, β.observable b⁆

declarations.name: StarAlgEquiv.toQuantumChannel
declarations.doc: The quantum channel of a ⋆-isomorphism.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def _root_.StarAlgEquiv.toQuantumChannel (β : A ≃⋆ₐ[ℂ] B) : QuantumChannel A B

declarations.name: StarAlgEquiv.toObservableChannel
declarations.doc: The channel a ⋆-isomorphism induces between the self-adjoint observables.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def _root_.StarAlgEquiv.toObservableChannel (β : A ≃⋆ₐ[ℂ] B) :
    Channel (selfAdjoint A) (selfAdjoint B)

declarations.name: StarAlgEquiv.coe_toObservableChannel_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma _root_.StarAlgEquiv.coe_toObservableChannel_apply (β : A ≃⋆ₐ[ℂ] B) (a : selfAdjoint A) :
    (β.toObservableChannel a : B) = β (a : A)

declarations.name: StarAlgEquiv.toObservableChannel_apply
declarations.doc: On observables of a single algebra, the induced channel is the action on observables.
declarations.statement:
lemma _root_.StarAlgEquiv.toObservableChannel_apply (β : A ≃⋆ₐ[ℂ] A) (a : selfAdjoint A) :
    β.toObservableChannel a = β.observable a

declarations.name: StarAlgEquiv.observableSymmetry
declarations.doc: Every C⋆-⋆-automorphism induces a symmetry of the self-adjoint observables.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def _root_.StarAlgEquiv.observableSymmetry (β : A ≃⋆ₐ[ℂ] A) :
    Symmetry (selfAdjoint A)

declarations.name: StarAlgEquiv.val_observableSymmetry
declarations.statement:
lemma _root_.StarAlgEquiv.val_observableSymmetry (β : A ≃⋆ₐ[ℂ] A) :
    (β.observableSymmetry : Channel (selfAdjoint A) (selfAdjoint A)) = β.toObservableChannel

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AutomorphismGroup
declarations.doc: A one-parameter group of star-algebra automorphisms.
declarations.statement:
structure AutomorphismGroup (A : Type*) [Ring A] [StarRing A] [Module ℂ A] where
  /-- The automorphism at time `t`. -/
  toFun : ℝ → (A ≃⋆ₐ[ℂ] A)
  /-- Evolution at time zero is the identity. -/
  map_zero_apply : ∀ a : A, toFun 0 a = a
  /-- The group law, with evolution by `t` followed by evolution by `s`. -/
  map_add_apply : ∀ (s t : ℝ) (a : A), toFun (s + t) a = toFun s (toFun t a)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AutomorphismGroup.ext
declarations.doc: An automorphism group is determined by its action at every time.
declarations.statement:
lemma AutomorphismGroup.ext {A : Type*} [Ring A] [StarRing A] [Module ℂ A]
    {α β : AutomorphismGroup A} (h : ∀ t a, α.toFun t a = β.toFun t a) : α = β

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AutomorphismGroup.toObservableDynamics
declarations.doc: The dynamics of observables induced by a one-parameter group of `⋆`-automorphisms.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def AutomorphismGroup.toObservableDynamics (α : AutomorphismGroup A) :
    OneParameterAutomorphismGroup (selfAdjoint A)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AutomorphismGroup.toObservableDynamics_apply
declarations.doc: The observable dynamics is the restriction of the algebraic dynamics at each time.
declarations.statement:
lemma AutomorphismGroup.toObservableDynamics_apply (α : AutomorphismGroup A) (t : ℝ)
    (a : selfAdjoint A) : α.toObservableDynamics t a = (α.toFun t).observable a

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AutomorphismGroup.transport
declarations.doc: Transport a one-parameter ⋆-automorphism group across a ⋆-isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
def AutomorphismGroup.transport (β : A ≃⋆ₐ[ℂ] B) (α : AutomorphismGroup A) :
    AutomorphismGroup B

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AutomorphismGroup.transport_apply
declarations.doc: Unfolds transported dynamics: evolve after pulling back through the ⋆-isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
lemma AutomorphismGroup.transport_apply (β : A ≃⋆ₐ[ℂ] B) (α : AutomorphismGroup A)
    (t : ℝ) (b : B) :
    (α.transport β).toFun t b = β (α.toFun t (β.symm b))

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AutomorphismGroup.IsIntertwining
declarations.doc: A ⋆-isomorphism intertwines two dynamics when its square commutes at every time.
declarations.statement:
def AutomorphismGroup.IsIntertwining (α : AutomorphismGroup A) (γ : AutomorphismGroup B)
    (β : A ≃⋆ₐ[ℂ] B) : Prop

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AutomorphismGroup.isIntertwining_transport
declarations.doc:
Transported dynamics is intertwined with the original dynamics by the transporting
⋆-isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
lemma AutomorphismGroup.isIntertwining_transport (β : A ≃⋆ₐ[ℂ] B)
    (α : AutomorphismGroup A) :
    α.IsIntertwining (α.transport β) β

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AutomorphismGroup.isIntertwining_iff_eq_transport
declarations.doc: A ⋆-isomorphism intertwines a flow with precisely the dynamics transported along it.
declarations.statement:
lemma AutomorphismGroup.isIntertwining_iff_eq_transport (α : AutomorphismGroup A)
    (γ : AutomorphismGroup B) (β : A ≃⋆ₐ[ℂ] B) :
    α.IsIntertwining γ β ↔ γ = α.transport β

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AutomorphismGroup.IsIntertwining.trans
declarations.doc: Intertwining squares compose along composable ⋆-isomorphisms.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AutomorphismGroup.transport_refl
declarations.doc: Transport through the identity ⋆-isomorphism leaves a flow unchanged.
declarations.statement:
lemma AutomorphismGroup.transport_refl (α : AutomorphismGroup A) :
    α.transport (StarAlgEquiv.refl (R := ℂ) (A := A)) = α

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AutomorphismGroup.transport_trans
declarations.doc: Successive changes of algebraic coordinates transport a flow by their composite.
declarations.statement:
lemma AutomorphismGroup.transport_trans (α : AutomorphismGroup A) (β : A ≃⋆ₐ[ℂ] B)
    (γ : B ≃⋆ₐ[ℂ] C) :
    (α.transport β).transport γ = α.transport (β.trans γ)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AutomorphismGroup.transport_symm_transport
declarations.doc: Transporting back through the inverse ⋆-isomorphism recovers the original flow.
declarations.statement:
lemma AutomorphismGroup.transport_symm_transport (α : AutomorphismGroup A) (β : A ≃⋆ₐ[ℂ] B) :
    (α.transport β).transport β.symm = α

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AutomorphismGroup.conj
declarations.doc:
The automorphism group `α`, viewed through the change of coordinates `β`:
`(conj β α) t = β ∘ (α t) ∘ β⁻¹`.
declarations.statement: def AutomorphismGroup.conj (β : A ≃⋆ₐ[ℂ] A) (α : AutomorphismGroup A) : AutomorphismGroup A

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AutomorphismGroup.conj_apply
declarations.doc: Unfolds `AutomorphismGroup.conj` to `(conj β α) t a = β (α t (β⁻¹ a))`.
declarations.statement:
lemma AutomorphismGroup.conj_apply (β : A ≃⋆ₐ[ℂ] A) (α : AutomorphismGroup A) (t : ℝ) (a : A) :
    (α.conj β).toFun t a = β (α.toFun t (β.symm a))

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AutomorphismGroup.conj_refl
declarations.doc: Conjugating by the identity automorphism changes nothing.
declarations.statement:
lemma AutomorphismGroup.conj_refl (α : AutomorphismGroup A) :
    α.conj (StarAlgEquiv.refl (R := ℂ) (A := A)) = α

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AutomorphismGroup.conj_conj
declarations.doc: Conjugating successively by `β` then `γ` is the same as conjugating once by `β.trans γ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma AutomorphismGroup.conj_conj (α : AutomorphismGroup A) (β γ : A ≃⋆ₐ[ℂ] A) :
    (α.conj β).conj γ = α.conj (β.trans γ)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AutomorphismGroup.conj_symm_conj
declarations.doc: Conjugating by `β` and then undoing it with `β.symm` recovers the original flow.
declarations.statement:
lemma AutomorphismGroup.conj_symm_conj (α : AutomorphismGroup A) (β : A ≃⋆ₐ[ℂ] A) :
    (α.conj β).conj β.symm = α

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AutomorphismGroup.conj_conj_symm
declarations.doc: Conjugating by `β.symm` and then undoing it with `β` recovers the original flow.
declarations.statement:
lemma AutomorphismGroup.conj_conj_symm (α : AutomorphismGroup A) (β : A ≃⋆ₐ[ℂ] A) :
    (α.conj β.symm).conj β = α

modules.title: Commutative C⋆-algebras are classical
modules.doc:
The observables of a commutative C⋆-algebra form a classical system, via its characters.

## i. Overview

A commutative C⋆-algebra is the algebra of continuous functions on its characters, the pure
states. An observable is nonnegative exactly when every character assigns it a nonnegative value,
and one observable lies below another exactly when every character says so. Minima can then be
taken character by character, which gives the Riesz decomposition of the observables. So the
self-adjoint part of a commutative C⋆-algebra is a classical system.

## ii. Key results

- `CommCStarAlgebra.character` : a character as a star-algebra homomorphism.
- `CommCStarAlgebra.nonneg_iff_forall_character` : characters detect positivity.
- `CommCStarAlgebra.hasRieszDecomposition` : the observables have the Riesz decomposition.
- `CommCStarAlgebra.isClassical` : the observables form a classical system.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Characters
- B. Order through characters
- C. Classicality

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: CommCStarAlgebra.character
declarations.doc: A character of a commutative C⋆-algebra, as a star-algebra homomorphism to `ℂ`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def character (χ : WeakDual.characterSpace ℂ A) : A →⋆ₐ[ℂ] ℂ

declarations.name: CommCStarAlgebra.character_apply
declarations.statement: lemma character_apply (χ : WeakDual.characterSpace ℂ A) (a : A) : character χ a = χ a

declarations.name: CommCStarAlgebra.ext_character
declarations.doc: Characters separate the elements of a commutative C⋆-algebra.
declarations.statement: lemma ext_character {a b : A} (h : ∀ χ : WeakDual.characterSpace ℂ A, χ a = χ b) : a = b

declarations.name: CommCStarAlgebra.character_eq_re
declarations.doc: A character takes real values on self-adjoint elements.
declarations.statement:
lemma character_eq_re {a : A} (ha : IsSelfAdjoint a) (χ : WeakDual.characterSpace ℂ A) :
    χ a = ((χ a).re : ℂ)

declarations.name: CommCStarAlgebra.inf
declarations.doc: The pointwise minimum of two self-adjoint elements, taken character by character.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def inf (a b : A) : A

declarations.name: CommCStarAlgebra.character_inf
declarations.statement:
lemma character_inf (a b : A) (χ : WeakDual.characterSpace ℂ A) :
    χ (inf a b) = ((min (χ a).re (χ b).re : ℝ) : ℂ)

declarations.name: CommCStarAlgebra.isSelfAdjoint_inf
declarations.statement: lemma isSelfAdjoint_inf (a b : A) : IsSelfAdjoint (inf a b)

declarations.name: CommCStarAlgebra.nonneg_iff_forall_character
declarations.doc: **Characters detect positivity.**
declarations.statement:
lemma nonneg_iff_forall_character {a : A} :
    0 ≤ a ↔ ∀ χ : WeakDual.characterSpace ℂ A, 0 ≤ χ a

declarations.name: CommCStarAlgebra.le_iff_forall_character
declarations.doc: Characters detect the order between self-adjoint elements.
declarations.statement:
lemma le_iff_forall_character {a b : A} (ha : IsSelfAdjoint a) (hb : IsSelfAdjoint b) :
    a ≤ b ↔ ∀ χ : WeakDual.characterSpace ℂ A, (χ a).re ≤ (χ b).re

declarations.name: CommCStarAlgebra.hasRieszDecomposition
declarations.doc:
**Riesz decomposition.** A nonnegative observable below a sum of two nonnegative observables
splits, character by character, into two pieces below the summands.
declarations.statement: lemma hasRieszDecomposition : HasRieszDecomposition (selfAdjoint A)

declarations.name: CommCStarAlgebra.isClassical
declarations.doc: **The observables of a commutative C⋆-algebra form a classical system.**
declarations.statement: lemma isClassical : IsClassical (selfAdjoint A)

modules.title: Unitary conjugation as a symmetry
modules.doc:
Conjugation by a unitary as a channel and a symmetry, and symmetry actions of representations.

## i. Overview

A symmetry of a quantum system is usually implemented as `a ↦ u a u⋆` for a unitary `u`. Conjugation
by a unitary maps self-adjoint elements to self-adjoint elements, preserves positivity and the unit,
and is inverted by conjugation by `u⋆`. So it is a symmetry of the observables, and `u ↦ u (·) u⋆`
is a group homomorphism from the unitaries to the symmetry group. Composing with a unitary
representation of a group `G` gives a symmetry action of `G`.

## ii. Key results

- `unitary.conjugationChannel` : conjugation by a unitary, as a channel.
- `unitary.conjugationSymmetry` : conjugation by a unitary, as a symmetry.
- `unitary.conjugationSymmetryHom` : the homomorphism from unitaries to symmetries.
- `Unitary.Representation.toSymmetryHom` : the symmetry action of a unitary representation.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Conjugation as a linear map
- B. Conjugation as a unital positive linear map
- C. Conjugation as a symmetry
- D. Unitary representations induce symmetry actions

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. Conjugation as a linear map
## B. Conjugation as a unital positive linear map
## D. Unitary representations induce symmetry actions

declarations.name: unitary.conjugationLinearMap
declarations.doc:
The underlying `ℝ`-linear map of conjugation by a unitary `u`, `a ↦ u a u*`, restricted to
self-adjoint elements. Lands back in `selfAdjoint A` by `IsSelfAdjoint.conjugate`.
declarations.statement: def conjugationLinearMap (u : unitary A) : selfAdjoint A →ₗ[ℝ] selfAdjoint A

declarations.name: unitary.coe_conjugationLinearMap
declarations.statement:
lemma coe_conjugationLinearMap (u : unitary A) (a : selfAdjoint A) :
    (conjugationLinearMap u a : A) = (u : A) * (a : A) * star (u : A)

declarations.name: unitary.conjugationLinearMap_conjugationLinearMap
declarations.doc: Conjugating by `v` and then by `u` is conjugating by `u * v`.
declarations.statement:
lemma conjugationLinearMap_conjugationLinearMap (u v : unitary A) (a : selfAdjoint A) :
    conjugationLinearMap u (conjugationLinearMap v a) = conjugationLinearMap (u * v) a

declarations.name: unitary.conjugationLinearMap_one
declarations.doc: Conjugation by `1` does nothing.
declarations.statement:
lemma conjugationLinearMap_one (a : selfAdjoint A) :
    conjugationLinearMap (1 : unitary A) a = a

declarations.name: unitary.conjugationLinearMap_star_conjugationLinearMap
declarations.doc:
Conjugating by `u` then by `star u` is the identity: this is
`conjugationLinearMap_conjugationLinearMap` specialized along `star u * u = 1`.
declarations.statement:
lemma conjugationLinearMap_star_conjugationLinearMap (u : unitary A) (a : selfAdjoint A) :
    conjugationLinearMap (star u) (conjugationLinearMap u a) = a

declarations.name: unitary.conjugationLinearMap_conjugationLinearMap_star
declarations.doc:
Conjugating by `star u` then by `u` is the identity: this is
`conjugationLinearMap_conjugationLinearMap` specialized along `u * star u = 1`.
declarations.statement:
lemma conjugationLinearMap_conjugationLinearMap_star (u : unitary A) (a : selfAdjoint A) :
    conjugationLinearMap u (conjugationLinearMap (star u) a) = a

declarations.name: unitary.conjugationChannel
declarations.doc:
Conjugation by a unitary `u`, `a ↦ u a u*`, as a unital positive linear map (channel) on
`selfAdjoint A`: positive by `star_right_conjugate_nonneg`, unital because `u * star u = 1`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def conjugationChannel (u : unitary A) : Channel (selfAdjoint A) (selfAdjoint A)

declarations.name: unitary.coe_conjugationChannel
declarations.statement:
lemma coe_conjugationChannel (u : unitary A) (a : selfAdjoint A) :
    (conjugationChannel u a : A) = (u : A) * (a : A) * star (u : A)

declarations.name: unitary.conjugationChannel_comp_conjugationChannel
declarations.statement:
lemma conjugationChannel_comp_conjugationChannel (u v : unitary A) :
    (conjugationChannel u).comp (conjugationChannel v) = conjugationChannel (u * v)

declarations.name: unitary.conjugationChannel_one
declarations.statement: lemma conjugationChannel_one : conjugationChannel (1 : unitary A) = .id ℝ (selfAdjoint A)

declarations.name: unitary.conjugationSymmetry
declarations.doc:
Conjugation by a unitary `u`, as a symmetry of the observables, with inverse conjugation by
`u⋆`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def conjugationSymmetry (u : unitary A) : Symmetry (selfAdjoint A)

declarations.name: unitary.val_conjugationSymmetry
declarations.statement:
lemma val_conjugationSymmetry (u : unitary A) :
    (conjugationSymmetry u : Channel (selfAdjoint A) (selfAdjoint A)) = conjugationChannel u

declarations.name: unitary.conjugationSymmetryHom
declarations.doc: Conjugation as a group homomorphism from the unitaries to the symmetries of the observables.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def conjugationSymmetryHom : unitary A →* Symmetry (selfAdjoint A)

declarations.name: unitary.conjugationSymmetryHom_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma conjugationSymmetryHom_apply (u : unitary A) :
    conjugationSymmetryHom u = conjugationSymmetry u

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Unitary.Representation.toSymmetryHom
declarations.doc: The symmetry action `α_g(a) = U_g a U_g*` of a unitary representation `U : G →* unitary A`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def Representation.toSymmetryHom {G : Type*} [Group G] (U : G →* unitary A) :
    G →* Symmetry (selfAdjoint A)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Unitary.Representation.toSymmetryHom_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma Representation.toSymmetryHom_apply {G : Type*} [Group G] (U : G →* unitary A) (g : G) :
    Representation.toSymmetryHom U g = unitary.conjugationSymmetry (U g)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Unitary.Representation.toSymmetryHom_apply_coe
declarations.doc:
Unwinding `Representation.toSymmetryHom` on an element `a` recovers `α_g(a) = U_g a U_g*`
literally.
declarations.statement:
lemma Representation.toSymmetryHom_apply_coe {G : Type*} [Group G] (U : G →* unitary A) (g : G)
    (a : selfAdjoint A) :
    ((Representation.toSymmetryHom U g).1 a : A) = (U g : A) * (a : A) * star (U g : A)

modules.title: The GNS construction
modules.doc:
Every state on a C⋆-algebra is the vector state of a cyclic unit vector in its GNS representation.

## i. Overview

Every state `ω` on a C⋆-algebra is a vector state of a representation. Mathlib's GNS construction
gives the Hilbert space `H_ω` and the representation `π_ω`. The image `Ω_ω` of `1` in `H_ω` is a
cyclic unit vector with `ω(a) = ⟪Ω_ω, π_ω(a) Ω_ω⟫`, and a faithful state gives a faithful
representation.

## ii. Key results

- `UnitalPositiveLinearMap.gnsRep` : the GNS representation of a state.
- `UnitalPositiveLinearMap.gnsCyclicVector` : the cyclic vector `Ω_ω`.
- `UnitalPositiveLinearMap.inner_gnsCyclicVector_gnsRep_gnsCyclicVector` : `ω(a) = ⟪Ω_ω, π_ω(a)
  Ω_ω⟫`.
- `UnitalPositiveLinearMap.denseRange_gnsRep_gnsCyclicVector` : `Ω_ω` is cyclic.
- `UnitalPositiveLinearMap.injective_gnsRep_of_isFaithful` : faithful states give faithful
  representations.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The GNS representation
- B. The cyclic vector
- C. Faithful states

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.GNS
declarations.doc:
The GNS Hilbert space `H_ω` carried by a state `ω` on a unital C⋆-algebra: the Hilbert space
completion of `A` with respect to the (semi-)inner product `⟨x, y⟩ := ω(x⋆y)`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable abbrev GNS

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.gnsRep
declarations.doc:
The GNS representation `π_ω : A → B(H_ω)` carried by a state `ω`: the unital
`⋆`-homomorphism into the bounded operators on `ω.GNS` induced by left multiplication.
declarations.statement: noncomputable abbrev gnsRep : A →⋆ₐ[ℂ] (ω.GNS →L[ℂ] ω.GNS)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.gnsCyclicVector
declarations.doc: The GNS cyclic vector `Ω_ω ∈ H_ω`: the image of `1 : A` under `A → ω.GNS`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def gnsCyclicVector : ω.GNS

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.gnsRep_gnsCyclicVector
declarations.doc:
`π_ω(a) Ω_ω` is, concretely, the image of `a` itself under `A → ω.GNS` — since
`π_ω(a) Ω_ω = π_ω(a) · (\text{image of } 1) = \text{image of } (a \cdot 1) = \text{image of } a`.
declarations.statement:
lemma gnsRep_gnsCyclicVector (a : A) :
    ω.gnsRep a ω.gnsCyclicVector =
      ((ω.toPositiveLinearMap.toPreGNS a : ω.toPositiveLinearMap.PreGNS) : ω.GNS)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.norm_gnsCyclicVector
declarations.doc: `Ω_ω` has unit norm: `‖Ω_ω‖² = ω(1⋆1) = ω(1) = 1`.
declarations.statement: lemma norm_gnsCyclicVector : ‖ω.gnsCyclicVector‖ = 1

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.inner_gnsCyclicVector_gnsRep_gnsCyclicVector
declarations.doc:
The defining identity of the GNS construction: `ω` is recovered as the vector state of `π_ω`
at the cyclic vector `Ω_ω`.
declarations.statement:
lemma inner_gnsCyclicVector_gnsRep_gnsCyclicVector (a : A) :
    ⟪ω.gnsCyclicVector, ω.gnsRep a ω.gnsCyclicVector⟫_ℂ = ω a

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.denseRange_gnsRep_gnsCyclicVector
declarations.doc:
`Ω_ω` is cyclic: the orbit `π_ω(A) Ω_ω` is dense in `H_ω`, so every vector in `H_ω` is a limit
of vectors reachable from `Ω_ω` by applying elements of `A`.
declarations.statement:
lemma denseRange_gnsRep_gnsCyclicVector :
    DenseRange (fun a : A => ω.gnsRep a ω.gnsCyclicVector)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.IsFaithful
declarations.doc:
A state is **faithful** when only `0` gives `x⋆x` weight `0` — the standard notion of a
faithful state on a C⋆-algebra, and the hypothesis under which the GNS representation `π_ω`
becomes injective.
declarations.statement: def IsFaithful (ω : 𝓢[ℂ, A]) : Prop

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.injective_gnsRep_of_isFaithful
declarations.doc: The GNS representation of a faithful state is faithful.
declarations.statement: lemma injective_gnsRep_of_isFaithful (h : ω.IsFaithful) : Function.Injective ω.gnsRep

modules.title: Symmetries of an invariant state are unitarily implemented
modules.doc:
A ⋆-automorphism preserving a state is implemented by a unitary operator on the GNS space that fixes
the cyclic vector.

## i. Overview

Let `ω` be a state on a unital C⋆-algebra `A` and `σ` a ⋆-automorphism of `A` with `ω ∘ σ = ω`.
Then `[a] ↦ [σ a]` preserves the GNS inner product `⟨a, b⟩ = ω(a⋆ b)`, so it extends to an
isometry of the GNS space `H_ω`, with inverse the extension of `σ⁻¹`. This unitary operator `U_σ`
fixes the cyclic vector and intertwines the GNS representation: `U_σ π_ω(a) = π_ω(σ a) U_σ`.
For a group of such automorphisms, for instance the translations of a lattice and a
translation-invariant state, this gives a unitary representation of the group on `H_ω`.

## ii. Key results

- `UnitalPositiveLinearMap.gnsUnitary` : the unitary operator implementing a symmetry.
- `UnitalPositiveLinearMap.gnsUnitary_cyclicVector` : it fixes the cyclic vector.
- `UnitalPositiveLinearMap.gnsUnitary_comp_gnsRep` : it intertwines the GNS representation.
- `UnitalPositiveLinearMap.gnsUnitaryRep` : the unitary representation of a group of symmetries.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The isometry on the pre-Hilbert space
- B. The unitary operator
- C. Representations of groups of symmetries

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. The isometry on the pre-Hilbert space
## C. Representations of groups of symmetries

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.preGNSAut
declarations.doc: The map `[a] ↦ [σ a]` on the pre-Hilbert space of a state.
declarations.statement: def preGNSAut : ω.toPositiveLinearMap.PreGNS →ₗ[ℂ] ω.toPositiveLinearMap.PreGNS

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.ofPreGNS_preGNSAut
declarations.statement:
lemma ofPreGNS_preGNSAut (x : ω.toPositiveLinearMap.PreGNS) :
    ω.toPositiveLinearMap.ofPreGNS (preGNSAut ω σ x) = σ (ω.toPositiveLinearMap.ofPreGNS x)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.inner_preGNSAut
declarations.doc: A symmetry preserving the state preserves the GNS inner product.
declarations.statement:
lemma inner_preGNSAut (hσ : ∀ a, ω (σ a) = ω a) (x y : ω.toPositiveLinearMap.PreGNS) :
    ⟪preGNSAut ω σ x, preGNSAut ω σ y⟫_ℂ = ⟪x, y⟫_ℂ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.norm_preGNSAut
declarations.statement:
lemma norm_preGNSAut (hσ : ∀ a, ω (σ a) = ω a) (x : ω.toPositiveLinearMap.PreGNS) :
    ‖preGNSAut ω σ x‖ = ‖x‖

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.preGNSAutCLM
declarations.doc: The symmetry as a bounded operator on the pre-Hilbert space.
declarations.statement:
def preGNSAutCLM (hσ : ∀ a, ω (σ a) = ω a) :
    ω.toPositiveLinearMap.PreGNS →L[ℂ] ω.toPositiveLinearMap.PreGNS

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.gnsAut
declarations.doc: The unitary operator on the GNS space implementing a symmetry that preserves the state.
declarations.statement: def gnsAut (hσ : ∀ a, ω (σ a) = ω a) : ω.GNS →L[ℂ] ω.GNS

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.gnsAut_coe
declarations.statement:
lemma gnsAut_coe (hσ : ∀ a, ω (σ a) = ω a) (x : ω.toPositiveLinearMap.PreGNS) :
    gnsAut hσ (x : ω.GNS) = ((preGNSAut ω σ x : ω.toPositiveLinearMap.PreGNS) : ω.GNS)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.inner_gnsAut
declarations.doc: The implementing operator preserves the inner product of the GNS space.
declarations.statement:
lemma inner_gnsAut (hσ : ∀ a, ω (σ a) = ω a) (x y : ω.GNS) :
    ⟪gnsAut hσ x, gnsAut hσ y⟫_ℂ = ⟪x, y⟫_ℂ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.gnsAut_mul
declarations.statement:
lemma gnsAut_mul (g h : Multiplicative G) :
    gnsAut (hα (g * h)) = gnsAut (hα g) * gnsAut (hα h)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.gnsAut_one
declarations.statement: lemma gnsAut_one : gnsAut (hα 1) = 1

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.star_gnsAut_mul_gnsAut
declarations.statement:
lemma star_gnsAut_mul_gnsAut (g : Multiplicative G) :
    star (gnsAut (hα g)) * gnsAut (hα g) = 1

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.star_gnsAut
declarations.statement: lemma star_gnsAut (g : Multiplicative G) : star (gnsAut (hα g)) = gnsAut (hα g⁻¹)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.gnsUnitary
declarations.doc:
**Translations of an invariant state are unitarily implemented**: the unitary operator on the
GNS space implementing the symmetry `α g`.
declarations.statement: def gnsUnitary (g : Multiplicative G) : unitary (ω.GNS →L[ℂ] ω.GNS)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.gnsUnitaryRep
declarations.doc: **The unitary representation of a symmetry group on the GNS space of an invariant state.**
declarations.statement: def gnsUnitaryRep : Multiplicative G →* unitary (ω.GNS →L[ℂ] ω.GNS)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.gnsUnitary_cyclicVector
declarations.doc: The implementing unitary fixes the cyclic vector.
declarations.statement:
lemma gnsUnitary_cyclicVector (g : Multiplicative G) :
    ((gnsUnitary hα g : unitary (ω.GNS →L[ℂ] ω.GNS)) : ω.GNS →L[ℂ] ω.GNS) ω.gnsCyclicVector =
      ω.gnsCyclicVector

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.gnsUnitary_gnsRep_cyclicVector
declarations.doc: The implementing unitary carries `π(a) Ω` to `π(α_g a) Ω`.
declarations.statement:
lemma gnsUnitary_gnsRep_cyclicVector (g : Multiplicative G) (a : A) :
    ((gnsUnitary hα g : unitary (ω.GNS →L[ℂ] ω.GNS)) : ω.GNS →L[ℂ] ω.GNS)
        (ω.gnsRep a ω.gnsCyclicVector) = ω.gnsRep (α g a) ω.gnsCyclicVector

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.gnsUnitary_comp_gnsRep
declarations.doc:
The implementing unitaries intertwine the GNS representation with the symmetry:
`U_g π(a) = π(α_g a) U_g`.
declarations.statement:
lemma gnsUnitary_comp_gnsRep (g : Multiplicative G) (a : A) :
    ((gnsUnitary hα g : unitary (ω.GNS →L[ℂ] ω.GNS)) : ω.GNS →L[ℂ] ω.GNS) * ω.gnsRep a =
      ω.gnsRep (α g a) * ((gnsUnitary hα g : unitary (ω.GNS →L[ℂ] ω.GNS)) : ω.GNS →L[ℂ] ω.GNS)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.inner_gnsRep_cyclicVector_gnsUnitary
declarations.doc:
The matrix coefficients of the GNS vectors `π(a) Ω` are the correlation functions of the
state: `⟪π(a) Ω, U_g π(a) Ω⟫ = ω(a⋆ α_g(a))`.
declarations.statement:
lemma inner_gnsRep_cyclicVector_gnsUnitary (g : Multiplicative G) (a : A) :
    ⟪ω.gnsRep a ω.gnsCyclicVector,
      ((gnsUnitary hα g : unitary (ω.GNS →L[ℂ] ω.GNS)) : ω.GNS →L[ℂ] ω.GNS)
        (ω.gnsRep a ω.gnsCyclicVector)⟫_ℂ = ω (star a * α g a)

modules.title: The momentum decomposition of an invariant state
modules.doc:
The GNS space of a translation-invariant state decomposes over the momenta, and the momentum
distribution of a local excitation is its structure factor.

## i. Overview

For a state `ω` of a C⋆-algebra and an abelian group `G` of ⋆-automorphisms preserving `ω`, the
unitary representation of `G` on the GNS space is the integral of the characters of `G` against a
projection-valued measure `P` on the Pontryagin dual of `G`. The cyclic vector `Ω` is invariant, so
it has momentum zero: `P` gives it to the trivial character. The vector `π(a) Ω` created by an
observable `a` has momentum distribution `μ_a`, the finite measure with
`∫ χ(g) dμ_a(χ) = ω(a⋆ α_g(a))`, the structure factor of `a`, and total mass `ω(a⋆ a)`.

## ii. Key results

- `UnitalPositiveLinearMap.gnsStructureFactor` : the momentum distribution of `π(a) Ω`.
- `UnitalPositiveLinearMap.integral_gnsStructureFactor` : its Fourier transform is the
  correlation function of `a`.
- `UnitalPositiveLinearMap.projection_one_gnsCyclicVector` : the invariant vector has momentum
  zero.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The momentum distribution of a local excitation
- B. The invariant vector

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. The momentum distribution of a local excitation

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.gnsStructureFactor
declarations.doc:
The momentum distribution of the excitation `π(a) Ω` created by the observable `a` from the
invariant state: the distribution of the vector `π(a) Ω` over the characters of the symmetry
group.
declarations.statement: def gnsStructureFactor (a : A) : Measure (PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G))
instance (a : A) : IsFiniteMeasure (gnsStructureFactor hα a)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.integral_gnsStructureFactor
declarations.doc:
**The Fourier transform of the momentum distribution is the correlation function**:
`∫ χ(g) dμ_a(χ) = ω(a⋆ α_g(a))`.
declarations.statement:
lemma integral_gnsStructureFactor (a : A) (g : Multiplicative G) :
    ∫ χ, ((χ g : Circle) : ℂ) ∂gnsStructureFactor hα a = ω (star a * α g a)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.gnsStructureFactor_univ
declarations.doc: The total momentum weight of the excitation `π(a) Ω` is `ω(a⋆ a)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma gnsStructureFactor_univ (a : A) :
    (gnsStructureFactor hα a).real Set.univ = (ω (star a * a)).re

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.gnsCyclicVector_mem_sector
declarations.doc:
The cyclic vector of an invariant state has momentum zero: its spectral measure is carried
by the trivial character.
declarations.statement:
lemma gnsCyclicVector_mem_sector :
    ω.gnsCyclicVector ∈ ProbabilisticTheory.Representation.sector (toEnd (gnsUnitaryRep hα))
      (fun g => (((1 : PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G)) g : Circle) : ℂ))

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.projection_one_gnsCyclicVector
declarations.doc:
**The vacuum has momentum zero.** For a countable symmetry group the spectral projection of
the trivial character fixes the cyclic vector.
declarations.statement:
lemma projection_one_gnsCyclicVector [Countable G] :
    projection (gnsUnitaryRep hα) {(1 : PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G))} ω.gnsCyclicVector =
      ω.gnsCyclicVector

modules.title: Positive and negative parts of observables
modules.doc:
Every observable of a C⋆-algebra splits uniquely into orthogonal positive and negative parts.

## i. Overview

Every observable `a` of a C⋆-algebra splits uniquely as `a = a⁺ - a⁻` with `a⁺`, `a⁻` positive and
orthogonal, `a⁺ a⁻ = 0`. This is the Jordan decomposition, the analogue of splitting a function or a
signed measure into its positive and negative parts. Mathlib builds `a⁺` and `a⁻` by the continuous
functional calculus; here they are positive observables.

## ii. Key results

- `Observable.posPart`, `Observable.negPart` : the positive and negative parts.
- `Observable.posPart_sub_negPart` : `a⁺ - a⁻ = a`.
- `Observable.posPart_mul_negPart` : the parts are orthogonal.
- `Observable.posPart_negPart_unique` : the decomposition is unique.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Positive observables
- B. Positive and negative parts

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Observable.nonneg_iff_exists_observable_sq
declarations.doc: An observable is positive exactly when it is the square of an observable.
declarations.statement:
lemma nonneg_iff_exists_observable_sq (a : Observable A) :
    0 ≤ (a : A) ↔ ∃ b : Observable A, (a : A) = (b : A) * b

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Observable.posPart
declarations.doc: The positive part of an observable.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def posPart (a : Observable A) : PositiveObservable A

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Observable.negPart
declarations.doc: The negative part of an observable.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def negPart (a : Observable A) : PositiveObservable A

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Observable.posPart_sub_negPart
declarations.doc: Every observable is the difference of its positive and negative parts.
declarations.statement:
lemma posPart_sub_negPart (a : Observable A) :
    (posPart a).1 - (negPart a).1 = a

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Observable.posPart_mul_negPart
declarations.doc: The positive and negative parts of an observable are orthogonal.
declarations.statement:
lemma posPart_mul_negPart (a : Observable A) :
    ((posPart a).1 : A) * (negPart a).1 = 0

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Observable.negPart_mul_posPart
declarations.doc: The negative and positive parts are orthogonal in the opposite order as well.
declarations.statement:
lemma negPart_mul_posPart (a : Observable A) :
    ((negPart a).1 : A) * (posPart a).1 = 0

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Observable.posPart_negPart_unique
declarations.doc:
The positive/negative decomposition is the unique decomposition into orthogonal positive
observables: this is the Jordan decomposition theorem.
declarations.statement:
lemma posPart_negPart_unique (a : Observable A) (b c : PositiveObservable A)
    (hsub : (a : A) = (b.1 : A) - c.1)
    (horth : (b.1 : A) * c.1 = 0) :
    posPart a = b ∧ negPart a = c

modules.title: Matrices over a C⋆-algebra as a composite system
modules.doc:
Matrices over a C⋆-algebra as composite observables with an n-level ancilla, and positivity.

## i. Overview

Coupling a quantum system with observables `A` to an `n`-level ancilla gives the `n × n` matrices
over `A`. The self-adjoint ones are the composite observables of the self-adjoint part of `A` with
the `n × n` Hermitian matrices: the product `a ⊗ h` is the matrix `(hᵢⱼ a)`. The positive
matrices form a cone of composite observables that contains every product of positive observables
and is Archimedean. When `A` is commutative, every positive matrix is also in the maximal cone:
applying a character entrywise turns it into a positive scalar matrix.

Applying a map entrywise to matrices is tensoring it with the identity of the ancilla. So complete
positivity of a map, in the sense of positive matrices, is the complete positivity of composite
systems, and for maps out of commutative C⋆-algebras it follows from classicality.

## ii. Key results

- `CStarMatrix.kron` : the matrix `(hᵢⱼ a)`.
- `CStarMatrix.toMatrix` : the matrix of a composite observable.
- `CStarMatrix.kron_nonneg` : products of positive observables are positive matrices.
- `CStarMatrix.matrixCone` : the positive matrices, as a cone of composite observables.
- `CStarMatrix.isArchimedeanTensorCone_matrixCone` : this cone is Archimedean.
- `CStarMatrix.exists_toMatrix_eq` : every self-adjoint matrix is a composite observable.
- `CStarMatrix.mem_maxTensorCone_of_nonneg` : for commutative `A`, positive matrices are in the
  maximal cone.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The matrix of a composite observable
- B. Positive matrices
- C. Every self-adjoint matrix is a composite observable
- D. Commutative algebras
- E. Applying a map entrywise
- F. Channels out of commutative algebras

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. The matrix of a composite observable
## C. Every self-adjoint matrix is a composite observable
## F. Channels out of commutative algebras

declarations.name: CStarMatrix.kron
declarations.doc: The matrix `(hᵢⱼ a)`: the observable `a` tensored with the scalar matrix `h`.
declarations.statement: def kron (h : CStarMatrix n n ℂ) (a : A) : CStarMatrix n n A

declarations.name: CStarMatrix.kron_apply
declarations.statement: lemma kron_apply (h : CStarMatrix n n ℂ) (a : A) (i j : n) : kron h a i j = h i j • a

declarations.name: CStarMatrix.kron_add_left
declarations.statement: lemma kron_add_left (h h' : CStarMatrix n n ℂ) (a : A) : kron (h + h') a = kron h a + kron h' a

declarations.name: CStarMatrix.kron_add_right
declarations.statement: lemma kron_add_right (h : CStarMatrix n n ℂ) (a a' : A) : kron h (a + a') = kron h a + kron h a'

declarations.name: CStarMatrix.kron_smul_left
declarations.statement: lemma kron_smul_left (r : ℝ) (h : CStarMatrix n n ℂ) (a : A) : kron (r • h) a = r • kron h a

declarations.name: CStarMatrix.kron_smul_right
declarations.statement: lemma kron_smul_right (r : ℝ) (h : CStarMatrix n n ℂ) (a : A) : kron h (r • a) = r • kron h a

declarations.name: CStarMatrix.kron_zero_left
declarations.statement: lemma kron_zero_left (a : A) : kron (0 : CStarMatrix n n ℂ) a = 0

declarations.name: CStarMatrix.kron_zero_right
declarations.statement: lemma kron_zero_right (h : CStarMatrix n n ℂ) : kron h (0 : A) = 0

declarations.name: CStarMatrix.map_add'
declarations.statement:
lemma map_add' {B : Type*} [AddCommMonoid B] (M N : CStarMatrix n n A) (f : A →+ B) :
    (M + N).map f = M.map f + N.map f

declarations.name: CStarMatrix.star_kron_mul_kron
declarations.doc: `kron g b` has adjoint-square `kron (g⋆ g) (b⋆ b)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma star_kron_mul_kron (g : CStarMatrix n n ℂ) (b : A) :
    star (kron g b) * kron g b = kron (star g * g) (star b * b)

declarations.name: CStarMatrix.sum_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_apply {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι) (f : ι → CStarMatrix n n A) (i j : n) :
    (∑ k ∈ s, f k) i j = ∑ k ∈ s, f k i j

declarations.name: CStarMatrix.toMatrix
declarations.doc:
The matrix of a composite observable of the self-adjoint part of `A` with the `n × n`
Hermitian matrices.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def toMatrix :
    Composite (selfAdjoint A) (selfAdjoint (CStarMatrix n n ℂ)) →ₗ[ℝ] CStarMatrix n n A

declarations.name: CStarMatrix.toMatrix_tmul
declarations.statement:
lemma toMatrix_tmul (a : selfAdjoint A) (h : selfAdjoint (CStarMatrix n n ℂ)) :
    toMatrix n A (Composite.tmul a h) = kron (h : CStarMatrix n n ℂ) (a : A)

declarations.name: CStarMatrix.toMatrix_one_tmul_one
declarations.statement:
lemma toMatrix_one_tmul_one :
    toMatrix n A (Composite.tmul (1 : selfAdjoint A) (1 : selfAdjoint (CStarMatrix n n ℂ))) = 1

declarations.name: CStarMatrix.isSelfAdjoint_kron
declarations.statement:
lemma isSelfAdjoint_kron {h : CStarMatrix n n ℂ} {a : A} (hh : IsSelfAdjoint h)
    (ha : IsSelfAdjoint a) : IsSelfAdjoint (kron h a)

declarations.name: CStarMatrix.isSelfAdjoint_toMatrix
declarations.statement:
lemma isSelfAdjoint_toMatrix (z : Composite (selfAdjoint A) (selfAdjoint (CStarMatrix n n ℂ))) :
    IsSelfAdjoint (toMatrix n A z)

declarations.name: CStarMatrix.kron_nonneg
declarations.doc:
**Products of positive observables are positive matrices.** Both factors are sums of
adjoint-squares, and `kron` of adjoint-squares is an adjoint-square.
declarations.statement: lemma kron_nonneg {h : CStarMatrix n n ℂ} {a : A} (hh : 0 ≤ h) (ha : 0 ≤ a) : 0 ≤ kron h a

declarations.name: CStarMatrix.matrixCone
declarations.doc: The positive matrices, as a cone of composite observables.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def matrixCone :
    PointedCone ℝ (Composite (selfAdjoint A) (selfAdjoint (CStarMatrix n n ℂ)))

declarations.name: CStarMatrix.mem_matrixCone
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_matrixCone {z : Composite (selfAdjoint A) (selfAdjoint (CStarMatrix n n ℂ))} :
    z ∈ matrixCone n A ↔ 0 ≤ toMatrix n A z

declarations.name: CStarMatrix.minTensorCone_le_matrixCone
declarations.doc: The positive matrices contain every product of positive observables.
declarations.statement:
lemma minTensorCone_le_matrixCone :
    minTensorCone (selfAdjoint A) (selfAdjoint (CStarMatrix n n ℂ)) ≤ matrixCone n A

declarations.name: CStarMatrix.isArchimedeanTensorCone_matrixCone
declarations.doc: **The positive matrices form an Archimedean cone.**
declarations.statement:
lemma isArchimedeanTensorCone_matrixCone :
    IsArchimedeanTensorCone (E := selfAdjoint A) (F := selfAdjoint (CStarMatrix n n ℂ))
      (matrixCone n A)

declarations.name: CStarMatrix.unit
declarations.doc: The matrix unit `eᵢⱼ`.
declarations.statement: def unit (i j : n) : CStarMatrix n n ℂ

declarations.name: CStarMatrix.unit_apply
declarations.statement: lemma unit_apply (i j p q : n) : unit i j p q = if i = p ∧ j = q then 1 else 0

declarations.name: CStarMatrix.star_unit
declarations.statement: lemma star_unit (i j : n) : star (unit i j) = unit j i

declarations.name: CStarMatrix.symUnit
declarations.doc: The Hermitian matrix `(eᵢⱼ + eⱼᵢ) / 2`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def symUnit (i j : n) : selfAdjoint (CStarMatrix n n ℂ)

declarations.name: CStarMatrix.asymUnit
declarations.doc: The Hermitian matrix `i (eᵢⱼ - eⱼᵢ) / 2`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def asymUnit (i j : n) : selfAdjoint (CStarMatrix n n ℂ)

declarations.name: CStarMatrix.entry
declarations.doc: The entry of a matrix, as a function of the matrix.
declarations.statement: def entry (M : CStarMatrix n n A) (i j : n) : A

declarations.name: CStarMatrix.ofMatrixSA
declarations.doc: The composite observable whose matrix is `M`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def ofMatrixSA (M : CStarMatrix n n A) :
    Composite (selfAdjoint A) (selfAdjoint (CStarMatrix n n ℂ))

declarations.name: CStarMatrix.kron_symUnit_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma kron_symUnit_apply (i j p q : n) (a : A) :
    kron (symUnit i j : CStarMatrix n n ℂ) a p q =
      (2 : ℝ)⁻¹ • ((if i = p ∧ j = q then a else 0) + (if j = p ∧ i = q then a else 0))

declarations.name: CStarMatrix.kron_asymUnit_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma kron_asymUnit_apply (i j p q : n) (a : A) :
    kron (asymUnit i j : CStarMatrix n n ℂ) a p q =
      (Complex.I / 2) • ((if i = p ∧ j = q then a else 0) - (if j = p ∧ i = q then a else 0))

declarations.name: CStarMatrix.toMatrix_ofMatrixSA
declarations.statement:
lemma toMatrix_ofMatrixSA (M : CStarMatrix n n A) :
    toMatrix n A (ofMatrixSA M) = ∑ i, ∑ j,
      (kron (symUnit i j : CStarMatrix n n ℂ) (realPart (entry M i j) : A) +
        kron (asymUnit i j : CStarMatrix n n ℂ) (imaginaryPart (entry M i j) : A))

declarations.name: CStarMatrix.toMatrix_ofMatrixSA_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma toMatrix_ofMatrixSA_apply (M : CStarMatrix n n A) (p q : n) :
    toMatrix n A (ofMatrixSA M) p q =
      (2 : ℝ)⁻¹ • ((realPart (entry M p q) : A) + realPart (entry M q p)) +
        (Complex.I / 2) • ((imaginaryPart (entry M p q) : A) - imaginaryPart (entry M q p))

declarations.name: CStarMatrix.exists_toMatrix_eq
declarations.doc: **Every self-adjoint matrix over `A` is a composite observable.**
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_toMatrix_eq {M : CStarMatrix n n A} (hM : IsSelfAdjoint M) :
    ∃ z, toMatrix n A z = M

declarations.name: CStarMatrix.characterFunctional
declarations.doc: A character of `C`, as a positive functional on its observables.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def characterFunctional (χ : WeakDual.characterSpace ℂ C) : selfAdjoint C →ₚ[ℝ] ℝ

declarations.name: CStarMatrix.coe_characterFunctional
declarations.statement:
lemma coe_characterFunctional (χ : WeakDual.characterSpace ℂ C) (x : selfAdjoint C) :
    (characterFunctional χ x : ℂ) = χ (x : C)

declarations.name: CStarMatrix.coe_lslice_characterFunctional
declarations.doc: Measuring the first factor with a character is applying the character entrywise.
declarations.statement:
lemma coe_lslice_characterFunctional (χ : WeakDual.characterSpace ℂ C)
    (z : Composite (selfAdjoint C) (selfAdjoint (CStarMatrix n n ℂ))) :
    ((PositiveLinearMap.lslice (characterFunctional χ) z : selfAdjoint (CStarMatrix n n ℂ)) :
      CStarMatrix n n ℂ) = (toMatrix n C z).map χ

declarations.name: CStarMatrix.mem_maxTensorCone_of_nonneg
declarations.doc:
**For commutative `C`, positive matrices are in the maximal cone.** Measuring the ancilla with a
positive functional leaves an observable of `C` on which every character is nonnegative, because
applying a character entrywise keeps a matrix positive.

declarations.name: CStarMatrix.toMatrix_map
declarations.doc:
Applying a positive unital map to the first factor of a composite observable is applying it
entrywise to its matrix.
declarations.statement:
lemma toMatrix_map (f : A →ₚ₁[ℂ] B)
    (z : Composite (selfAdjoint A) (selfAdjoint (CStarMatrix n n ℂ))) :
    toMatrix n B (TensorProduct.map
      (f.restrictSA : Channel (selfAdjoint A) (selfAdjoint B)).toLinearMap LinearMap.id z) =
      (toMatrix n A z).map f

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumChannel.map_nonneg_of_commutative
declarations.doc:
Entrywise, a positive unital map out of a commutative C⋆-algebra keeps positive matrices
positive: the input is classical, so the map is completely positive.
declarations.statement:
lemma map_nonneg_of_commutative (f : C →ₚ₁[ℂ] B) {k : ℕ} {M : CStarMatrix (Fin k) (Fin k) C}
    (hM : 0 ≤ M) : 0 ≤ M.map f

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumChannel.ofCommutative
declarations.doc:
**Stinespring's theorem.** A positive unital map out of a commutative C⋆-algebra is a quantum
channel: it is automatically completely positive.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def ofCommutative (f : C →ₚ₁[ℂ] B) : QuantumChannel C B

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumChannel.ofCommutative_apply
declarations.statement: lemma ofCommutative_apply (f : C →ₚ₁[ℂ] B) (x : C) : ofCommutative f x = f x

modules.title: Projections
modules.doc:
Projections of a C⋆-algebra: sharp idempotent effects with complements and spectrum in {0, 1}.

## i. Overview

A projection is an effect `p` with `p * p = p`. Projections are sharp effects, closed under
complement, and their spectrum lies in `{0, 1}`.

## ii. Key results

- `Projection` : projections of a C⋆-algebra.
- `Projection.isSharp` : projections are sharp.
- `Projection.complement` : the complementary projection `1 - p`.
- `Projection.spectrum_subset_zero_one` : the spectrum of a projection lies in `{0, 1}`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Projections
- B. Sharpness, complements and spectrum

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Projection
declarations.doc: A projection: an idempotent effect in the self-adjoint part of a C⋆-algebra.
declarations.statement: def Projection (A : Type*) [CStarAlgebra A] [PartialOrder A]

declarations.doc: A projection, viewed as an effect, forgetting idempotence.
declarations.statement: instance : CoeOut (Projection A) (Effect (selfAdjoint A))

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Projection.ext
declarations.statement:
lemma ext {p q : Projection A} (h : (p : Effect (selfAdjoint A)) = (q : Effect (selfAdjoint A))) :
    p = q

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Projection.isSharp
declarations.doc: Every projection is a sharp effect.
declarations.statement: lemma isSharp (p : Projection A) : Effect.IsSharp (p : Effect (selfAdjoint A))

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Projection.complement
declarations.doc: The complementary projection `1 - p`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def complement (p : Projection A) : Projection A

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Projection.complement_complement
declarations.doc: Taking the complement twice returns the original projection.
declarations.statement: lemma complement_complement (p : Projection A) : complement (complement p) = p

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Projection.spectrum_subset_zero_one
declarations.doc: The real spectrum of a projection is contained in `{0, 1}`.
declarations.statement:
lemma spectrum_subset_zero_one (p : Projection A) :
    spectrum ℝ (((p : Effect (selfAdjoint A)) : selfAdjoint A) : A) ⊆ {0, 1}

modules.title: Quantum channels
modules.doc:
Quantum channels as unital completely positive maps, and the channels they induce on observables.

## i. Overview

A quantum channel between C⋆-algebras is a unital completely positive map: it stays positive when
applied to one half of any larger, possibly entangled, system. Complete positivity is Mathlib's
`CompletelyPositiveMap`. On self-adjoint parts every quantum channel is a channel between the
order-unit spaces of observables.

## ii. Key results

- `QuantumChannel A₁ A₂` : unital completely positive maps from `A₁` to `A₂`.
- `QuantumChannel.toChannel` : the channel it induces between the self-adjoint parts.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Quantum channels
- B. The induced channel on observables

## iv. References

* None.

structure QuantumChannel (A₁ A₂ : Type*) [NonUnitalCStarAlgebra A₁] [NonUnitalCStarAlgebra A₂]

    [One A₁] [One A₂] extends A₁ →CP A₂, OneHom A₁ A₂

modules.title: Projections are sharp
modules.doc:
An idempotent effect of a C⋆-algebra is not a proper mixture of two different effects.

## i. Overview

A projection `p` is a sharp effect: it is not a proper mixture of two different effects. If `p = t
y₁ + s y₂`, conjugating by `1 - p` kills both `y₁` and `y₂`, so by the C⋆-identity both commute with
`p` and lie below it, which forces `y₁ = y₂ = p`.

## ii. Key results

- `IsIdempotentElem.isSharp` : idempotent effects are sharp.
- `ProbabilisticTheory.eq_of_mem_openSegment_of_isIdempotentElem` : the algebraic heart of the
  proof, stated on bare elements.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Consequences of the C⋆-identity
- B. Projections are sharp

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.nonneg_add_eq_zero
declarations.doc: In a partially ordered additive group, two nonnegative terms summing to zero vanish.
declarations.statement:
lemma nonneg_add_eq_zero {x y : A} (hx : 0 ≤ x) (hy : 0 ≤ y) (hxy : x + y = 0) :
    x = 0

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.sandwich_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
If `b * x * b = 0` for `b` self-adjoint and `x ≥ 0`, then `√x * b = 0`: the C⋆-identity
`‖z⋆z‖ = ‖z‖²`, applied to `z := √x * b`, since `z⋆z = b * √x * √x * b = b * x * b`.
declarations.statement:
lemma sandwich_eq_zero {b x : A} (hb : IsSelfAdjoint b) (hx : 0 ≤ x)
    (h : b * x * b = 0) : CFC.sqrt x * b = 0

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.eq_of_mem_openSegment_of_isIdempotentElem
declarations.doc:
The algebraic heart of `IsIdempotentElem.isSharp`, stated on bare elements of `A`: an
idempotent `a` between `0` and `1` cannot be written as a nontrivial mixture of two different
effects.
declarations.statement:
lemma eq_of_mem_openSegment_of_isIdempotentElem {a y₁ y₂ : A} (ha0 : 0 ≤ a) (_ha1 : a ≤ 1)
    (hidem : a * a = a) (hy₁0 : 0 ≤ y₁) (hy₁1 : y₁ ≤ 1) (hy₂0 : 0 ≤ y₂) (hy₂1 : y₂ ≤ 1)
    {t s : ℝ} (ht : 0 < t) (hs : 0 < s) (hts : t + s = 1) (heq : t • y₁ + s • y₂ = a) :
    y₁ = a

declarations.name: IsIdempotentElem.isSharp
declarations.doc:
**Projections are sharp**: an idempotent effect is not a proper mixture of two different
effects.
declarations.statement:
lemma _root_.IsIdempotentElem.isSharp {e : Effect (selfAdjoint A)}
    (h : IsIdempotentElem ((e : selfAdjoint A) : A)) : Effect.IsSharp e

modules.title: The distribution of an observable
modules.doc:
The outcome distribution of an observable in a state, and the measurement of an isolated eigenvalue.

## i. Overview

A state `ω` and an observable `a` determine a probability measure `μ_{ω,a}` on `ℝ`, the distribution
of the outcomes of measuring `a` in `ω`. It is the unique probability measure on the spectrum of `a`
with `ω(f(a)) = ∫ f dμ_{ω,a}` for continuous `f`, given by the Riesz–Markov–Kakutani theorem. At an
isolated point `x` of the spectrum the spectral projection gives a two-outcome measurement "does `a`
take the value `x`?", whose probability of `true` is `μ_{ω,a}({x})`.

## ii. Key results

- `realSpectralMeasure` : the distribution `μ_{ω,a}`.
- `realSpectralMeasure_integral` : `ω(f(a)) = ∫ f dμ_{ω,a}`.
- `realSpectralMeasure_unique` : the distribution is unique.
- `eigenMeasurement` : the measurement of an isolated eigenvalue.
- `eigenMeasurement_true` : its outcome probability is `μ_{ω,a}({x})`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Measuring an isolated eigenvalue

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text:
## A. Measuring an isolated eigenvalue

At an isolated point `x` of the spectrum of `a`, an eigenvalue separated from the rest of the
spectrum, the indicator of `{x}` is continuous on the spectrum, so the continuous functional
calculus gives the spectral projection `eigenEffect`. Its two-outcome measurement asks whether `a`
takes the value `x`, and the probability of `true` in `ω` is `μ_{ω,a}({x})`. Spectral projections of
arbitrary Borel sets need the Borel functional calculus.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.spectralFunctional
declarations.doc: The positive functional `f ↦ ω(f(a))` on continuous functions on the spectrum of `a`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def spectralFunctional (ω : 𝓢[ℂ, A]) (a : Observable A) :
    C(spectrum ℝ (a : A), ℝ) →ₚ[ℝ] ℝ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.spectralFunctionalCc
declarations.doc: `spectralFunctional` on compactly supported functions.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def spectralFunctionalCc (ω : 𝓢[ℂ, A]) (a : Observable A) :
    C_c(spectrum ℝ (a : A), ℝ) →ₚ[ℝ] ℝ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.spectralMeasure
declarations.doc: `spectralMeasure` on the spectrum itself; `realSpectralMeasure` below places it inside `ℝ`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def spectralMeasure (ω : 𝓢[ℂ, A]) (a : Observable A) :
    Measure (spectrum ℝ (a : A))

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.spectralMeasure_isFiniteMeasure
declarations.statement:
instance spectralMeasure_isFiniteMeasure (ω : 𝓢[ℂ, A]) (a : Observable A) :
    IsFiniteMeasure (spectralMeasure ω a)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.spectralFunctional_one
declarations.statement:
