lemma spectralFunctional_one (ω : 𝓢[ℂ, A]) (a : Observable A) :
    spectralFunctional ω a 1 = 1

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.spectralMeasure_isProbabilityMeasure
declarations.doc: Total mass one, matching `ω(1) = 1`.
declarations.statement:
instance spectralMeasure_isProbabilityMeasure (ω : 𝓢[ℂ, A]) (a : Observable A) :
    IsProbabilityMeasure (spectralMeasure ω a)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.spectralMeasure_integral
declarations.doc: `∫ f dμ = ω(f(a))` on the spectrum.
declarations.statement:
lemma spectralMeasure_integral (ω : 𝓢[ℂ, A]) (a : Observable A)
    (f : C(spectrum ℝ (a : A), ℝ)) :
    ω.onObservables ⟨cfcHom a.property f, cfcHom_predicate a.property f⟩ =
      ∫ x, f x ∂(spectralMeasure ω a)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.realSpectralMeasure
declarations.doc:
**The distribution of `a` in `ω`**, the probability measure `μ_{ω,a}` on `ℝ` with `ω(f(a)) = ∫ f
dμ_{ω,a}`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def realSpectralMeasure (ω : 𝓢[ℂ, A]) (a : Observable A) : Measure ℝ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.realSpectralMeasure_isProbabilityMeasure
declarations.statement:
instance realSpectralMeasure_isProbabilityMeasure (ω : 𝓢[ℂ, A]) (a : Observable A) :
    IsProbabilityMeasure (realSpectralMeasure ω a)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.realSpectralMeasure_compl_spectrum
declarations.doc: `μ_{ω,a}` is concentrated on `a`'s spectrum.
declarations.statement:
lemma realSpectralMeasure_compl_spectrum (ω : 𝓢[ℂ, A]) (a : Observable A) :
    realSpectralMeasure ω a (spectrum ℝ (a : A))ᶜ = 0

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.realSpectralMeasure_integral
declarations.doc: `∫ f dμ_{ω,a} = ω(f(a))`, for any `f` continuous on the spectrum of `a`.
declarations.statement:
lemma realSpectralMeasure_integral (ω : 𝓢[ℂ, A]) (a : Observable A) (f : ℝ → ℝ)
    (hf : ContinuousOn f (spectrum ℝ (a : A))) :
    ω.onObservables ⟨cfc f (a : A), cfc_predicate f (a : A)⟩ =
      ∫ y, f y ∂(realSpectralMeasure ω a)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.exists_continuousOn_extend
declarations.doc: Every continuous function on the spectrum extends to one on `ℝ`, continuous on the spectrum.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_continuousOn_extend (a : Observable A) (g : C(spectrum ℝ (a : A), ℝ)) :
    ∃ f : ℝ → ℝ, ContinuousOn f (spectrum ℝ (a : A)) ∧
      ∀ x : spectrum ℝ (a : A), f (x : ℝ) = g x

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.comap_integral_eq
declarations.doc:
If a measure `μ` on `ℝ` reproduces `ω(f(a))` for every continuous `f`, then pulling `μ` back
to the spectrum integrates every continuous test
function there exactly as `spectralMeasure ω a` does.
declarations.statement:
lemma comap_integral_eq (ω : 𝓢[ℂ, A]) (a : Observable A) (μ : Measure ℝ)
    (hrep : ∀ f : ℝ → ℝ, ContinuousOn f (spectrum ℝ (a : A)) →
      ω.onObservables ⟨cfc f (a : A), cfc_predicate f (a : A)⟩ = ((∫ y, f y ∂μ : ℝ)))
    (hcomap_map :
      Measure.map Subtype.val (μ.comap (Subtype.val : spectrum ℝ (a : A) → ℝ)) = μ)
    (g : C(spectrum ℝ (a : A), ℝ)) :
    (∫ x, g x ∂(μ.comap (Subtype.val : spectrum ℝ (a : A) → ℝ))) =
      ∫ x, g x ∂(spectralMeasure ω a)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.realSpectralMeasure_unique
declarations.doc:
`μ_{ω,a}` is the only probability measure on `ℝ`, concentrated on `a`'s spectrum, with
`∫ f dμ = ω(f(a))`: any other measure with these two properties already is `μ_{ω,a}`.
declarations.statement:
lemma realSpectralMeasure_unique (ω : 𝓢[ℂ, A]) (a : Observable A) (μ : Measure ℝ)
    [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] (hsupp : μ (spectrum ℝ (a : A))ᶜ = 0)
    (hrep : ∀ f : ℝ → ℝ, ContinuousOn f (spectrum ℝ (a : A)) →
      ω.onObservables ⟨cfc f (a : A), cfc_predicate f (a : A)⟩ = ((∫ y, f y ∂μ : ℝ))) :
    μ = realSpectralMeasure ω a

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.eigenIndicator
declarations.doc:
The indicator function of an isolated point `x` of `a`'s spectrum, as a continuous function on
the spectrum: continuous because `{x}` is clopen (`IsClopen.continuous_indicator`).
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def eigenIndicator (a : Observable A) {x : spectrum ℝ (a : A)}
    (hx : IsClopen ({x} : Set (spectrum ℝ (a : A)))) : C(spectrum ℝ (a : A), ℝ)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.eigenIndicator_apply
ProbabilisticTheory.eigenEffect
declarations.doc: The spectral projection of `a` at an isolated point `x` of its spectrum.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def eigenEffect (a : Observable A) {x : spectrum ℝ (a : A)}
    (hx : IsClopen ({x} : Set (spectrum ℝ (a : A)))) : Effect (Observable A)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.eigenIndicator_mul_self
ProbabilisticTheory.isIdempotentElem_eigenEffect
declarations.doc:
`eigenEffect` is idempotent: `cfcHom` is an algebra homomorphism, and the indicator function
`eigenIndicator a hx` is already idempotent under pointwise multiplication.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.isSharp_eigenEffect
declarations.doc: The spectral projection at an isolated point is sharp.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.eigenMeasurement
declarations.doc: The two-outcome measurement "does `a` read out the isolated spectral point `x`, or not?"
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def eigenMeasurement (a : Observable A) {x : spectrum ℝ (a : A)}
    (hx : IsClopen ({x} : Set (spectrum ℝ (a : A)))) : Measurement Bool (Observable A)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.eigenMeasurement_true
declarations.doc:
The probability that `eigenMeasurement` reads out `x` in `ω` is `μ_{ω,a}({x})`: the Born rule
of the two-outcome measurement "does `a` read out `x`?" agrees with the probability measure built
from `a`'s continuous functional calculus.
declarations.statement:
lemma eigenMeasurement_true (ω : 𝓢[ℂ, A]) (a : Observable A)
    {x : spectrum ℝ (a : A)} (hx : IsClopen ({x} : Set (spectrum ℝ (a : A))))
    (h : MeasurableSet {true}) :
    ω.onObservables (eigenMeasurement a hx {true} h : Observable A) =
      (realSpectralMeasure ω a).real ({(x : ℝ)} : Set ℝ)

modules.title: Stinespring's dilation theorem
modules.doc:
Stinespring's theorem: every completely positive map has the form J a = V⋆ π(a) V.

## i. Overview

Every completely positive map `J` from a C⋆-algebra `A` into the bounded operators on `H` has the
form `J a = V⋆ π(a) V` for a representation `π` of `A` on a Hilbert space `K` and an operator `V : H
→ K`. The space `K` is the completion of `A ⊗ H` for the inner product `⟪a ⊗ h, b ⊗ k⟫ = ⟪h, J(a⋆ b)
k⟫`, which is positive because `J` is completely positive, and `π` is left multiplication. For
commutative `A` this contains Naimark's dilation of a POVM.

## ii. Key results

- `Stinespring.Canonical.K` : the dilation space.
- `Stinespring.Canonical.canonicalRepresentation`, `Stinespring.Canonical.embedding` : the
  representation `π` and the operator `V`.
- `Stinespring.Canonical.canonical_stinespring_identity` : `J a = V⋆ π(a) V`.
- `Stinespring.exists_stinespringWitness` : **Stinespring's theorem.**

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The seminorm and pre-Hilbert structures induced by the kernel
- B. The canonical CP-dependent Hilbert space

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. The seminorm and pre-Hilbert structures induced by the kernel

## B. The canonical CP-dependent Hilbert space

The CP kernel changes the norm, so its pre-Hilbert space is made a type synonym. This is the same
pattern used by Mathlib's own scalar GNS construction (`PositiveLinearMap.PreGNS`): the synonym
lets the tensor product retain its original module structure while carrying a CP-dependent
seminorm and inner product.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Stinespring.T
declarations.doc: The tensor-product carrier `A ⊗[ℂ] H` the whole construction below lives on.
declarations.statement:
abbrev T (A H : Type*) [CStarAlgebra A] [PartialOrder A] [StarOrderedRing A]
    [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [CompleteSpace H]

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Stinespring.baseFunctional
declarations.doc: The functional `b ⊗ k ↦ ⟪h, J(a⋆b) k⟫`, the building block of the kernel inner product.
declarations.statement:
def baseFunctional (J : A →CP (H →L[ℂ] H)) (a : A) (h : H) :
    T A H →ₗ[ℂ] ℂ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Stinespring.baseFunctional_tmul
declarations.statement:
lemma baseFunctional_tmul (J : A →CP (H →L[ℂ] H)) (a b : A) (h k : H) :
    baseFunctional J a h (b ⊗ₜ[ℂ] k) = inner ℂ h (J (star a * b) k)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Stinespring.sesquiBilinear
declarations.doc: `baseFunctional`, packaged as a sesquilinear map in `(a, h)`.
declarations.statement:
def sesquiBilinear (J : A →CP (H →L[ℂ] H)) :
    A →ₛₗ[starRingEnd ℂ] H →ₛₗ[starRingEnd ℂ] (T A H →ₗ[ℂ] ℂ)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Stinespring.tensorInner
declarations.doc:
The (possibly degenerate) sesquilinear form on `T A H` induced by lifting `sesquiBilinear`
through the tensor product.
declarations.statement:
def tensorInner (J : A →CP (H →L[ℂ] H)) :
    T A H →ₛₗ[starRingEnd ℂ] (T A H →ₗ[ℂ] ℂ)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Stinespring.tensorInner_tmul
declarations.statement:
lemma tensorInner_tmul (J : A →CP (H →L[ℂ] H)) (a b : A) (h k : H) :
    tensorInner J (a ⊗ₜ[ℂ] h) (b ⊗ₜ[ℂ] k) =
      inner ℂ h (J (star a * b) k)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Stinespring.tensorInner_conj_symm_tmul
declarations.statement:
lemma tensorInner_conj_symm_tmul (J : A →CP (H →L[ℂ] H)) (a b : A) (h k : H) :
    starRingEnd ℂ (tensorInner J (a ⊗ₜ[ℂ] h) (b ⊗ₜ[ℂ] k)) =
      tensorInner J (b ⊗ₜ[ℂ] k) (a ⊗ₜ[ℂ] h)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Stinespring.tensorInner_conj_symm
declarations.statement:
lemma tensorInner_conj_symm (J : A →CP (H →L[ℂ] H)) (x y : T A H) :
    starRingEnd ℂ (tensorInner J x y) = tensorInner J y x

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Stinespring.tensorInner_nonneg
declarations.statement:
lemma tensorInner_nonneg (J : A →CP (H →L[ℂ] H)) (x : T A H) :
    0 ≤ tensorInner J x x

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Stinespring.tensorCore
declarations.doc: `tensorInner`, packaged as a `PreInnerProductSpace.Core` on `T A H`.
declarations.statement:
def tensorCore (J : A →CP (H →L[ℂ] H)) :
    PreInnerProductSpace.Core ℂ (T A H)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Stinespring.leftMul
declarations.doc: Left multiplication by `a` on the algebra factor of `T A H`.
declarations.statement: def leftMul (a : A) : T A H →ₗ[ℂ] T A H

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Stinespring.leftMul_tmul
declarations.statement:
lemma leftMul_tmul (a b : A) (h : H) :
    leftMul a (b ⊗ₜ[ℂ] h) = (a * b) ⊗ₜ[ℂ] h

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Stinespring.tensorInner_leftMul
declarations.statement:
lemma tensorInner_leftMul (J : A →CP (H →L[ℂ] H)) (a : A) (x y : T A H) :
    tensorInner J (leftMul a x) y = tensorInner J x (leftMul (star a) y)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Stinespring.leftMul_mul
declarations.statement:
lemma leftMul_mul (a b : A) (x : T A H) :
    leftMul (a * b) x = leftMul a (leftMul b x)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Stinespring.leftMul_add
declarations.statement:
lemma leftMul_add (a b : A) (x : T A H) :
    leftMul (a + b) x = leftMul a x + leftMul b x

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Stinespring.leftMul_smul
declarations.statement:
lemma leftMul_smul (r : ℂ) (a : A) (x : T A H) :
    leftMul (r • a) x = r • leftMul a x

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Stinespring.leftMul_one
declarations.statement: lemma leftMul_one (x : T A H) : leftMul (1 : A) x = x

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Stinespring.leftMul_norm_sub
declarations.statement:
lemma leftMul_norm_sub (a : A) (x : T A H) :
    leftMul ((‖a‖ ^ 2 : ℝ) • (1 : A) - star a * a) x =
      (‖a‖ ^ 2 : ℂ) • x - leftMul (star a * a) x

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Stinespring.tensorInner_leftMul_selfadjoint
declarations.statement:
lemma tensorInner_leftMul_selfadjoint (J : A →CP (H →L[ℂ] H)) {q : A} (hq : star q = q)
    (x : T A H) :
    tensorInner J (leftMul q x) x = tensorInner J x (leftMul q x)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Stinespring.tensorInner_leftMul_nonneg
declarations.statement:
lemma tensorInner_leftMul_nonneg (J : A →CP (H →L[ℂ] H)) {q : A} (hq : 0 ≤ q)
    (x : T A H) : 0 ≤ tensorInner J (leftMul q x) x

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Stinespring.tensorSeminormed
declarations.doc:
The seminormed-group structure `T A H` inherits from `tensorCore`'s (possibly degenerate)
inner product.
declarations.statement:
def tensorSeminormed (J : A →CP (H →L[ℂ] H)) :
    SeminormedAddCommGroup (T A H)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Stinespring.tensorInnerProductSpace
declarations.doc:
The inner product space structure on `T A H`, with respect to `tensorSeminormed`, coming
from `tensorCore`.
declarations.statement:
def tensorInnerProductSpace (J : A →CP (H →L[ℂ] H)) :
    @InnerProductSpace ℂ (T A H) inferInstance (tensorSeminormed J)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Stinespring.leftMul_norm_le
declarations.statement:
lemma leftMul_norm_le (a : A) (J : A →CP (H →L[ℂ] H)) (x : T A H) :
    letI : SeminormedAddCommGroup (T A H) := tensorSeminormed J
    ‖leftMul a x‖ ≤ ‖a‖ * ‖x‖

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Stinespring.uniformContinuous_add
declarations.statement:
lemma uniformContinuous_add (J : A →CP (H →L[ℂ] H)) :
    letI : SeminormedAddCommGroup (T A H) := tensorSeminormed J
    letI : PseudoMetricSpace (T A H) := SeminormedAddCommGroup.toPseudoMetricSpace
    UniformContinuous fun p : T A H × T A H => p.1 + p.2

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Stinespring.uniformContinuous_neg
declarations.statement:
lemma uniformContinuous_neg (J : A →CP (H →L[ℂ] H)) :
    letI : SeminormedAddCommGroup (T A H) := tensorSeminormed J
    letI : PseudoMetricSpace (T A H) := SeminormedAddCommGroup.toPseudoMetricSpace
    UniformContinuous fun x : T A H => -x

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Stinespring.leftMulCLM
declarations.doc: `leftMul a`, bundled as a continuous linear map for the kernel seminorm.
declarations.statement:
def leftMulCLM (J : A →CP (H →L[ℂ] H)) (a : A) :
    letI : SeminormedAddCommGroup (T A H) := tensorSeminormed J
    letI : InnerProductSpace ℂ (T A H) := tensorInnerProductSpace J
    T A H →L[ℂ] T A H

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Stinespring.leftMulCLM_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma leftMulCLM_apply (J : A →CP (H →L[ℂ] H)) (a : A) (x : T A H) :
    letI : SeminormedAddCommGroup (T A H) := tensorSeminormed J
    letI : InnerProductSpace ℂ (T A H) := tensorInnerProductSpace J
    leftMulCLM J a x = leftMul a x

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Stinespring.leftMulCompletion
declarations.doc: The continuous extension of `leftMulCLM` to the completion of `T A H`.
declarations.statement:
def leftMulCompletion (J : A →CP (H →L[ℂ] H)) (a : A) :
    letI : SeminormedAddCommGroup (T A H) := tensorSeminormed J
    letI : PseudoMetricSpace (T A H) := SeminormedAddCommGroup.toPseudoMetricSpace
    letI : InnerProductSpace ℂ (T A H) := tensorInnerProductSpace J
    letI : NormedSpace ℂ (T A H) := (tensorInnerProductSpace J).toNormedSpace
    UniformSpace.Completion (T A H) →L[ℂ] UniformSpace.Completion (T A H)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Stinespring.leftMulCompletion_coe
declarations.statement:
lemma leftMulCompletion_coe (J : A →CP (H →L[ℂ] H)) (a : A) (x : T A H) :
    letI : SeminormedAddCommGroup (T A H) := tensorSeminormed J
    letI : PseudoMetricSpace (T A H) := SeminormedAddCommGroup.toPseudoMetricSpace
    letI : InnerProductSpace ℂ (T A H) := tensorInnerProductSpace J
    leftMulCompletion J a (x : UniformSpace.Completion (T A H)) = leftMulCLM J a x

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Stinespring.leftMulCompletion_mul
declarations.statement:
lemma leftMulCompletion_mul (J : A →CP (H →L[ℂ] H)) (a b : A) :
    letI : SeminormedAddCommGroup (T A H) := tensorSeminormed J
    letI : PseudoMetricSpace (T A H) := SeminormedAddCommGroup.toPseudoMetricSpace
    letI : InnerProductSpace ℂ (T A H) := tensorInnerProductSpace J
    letI : NormedSpace ℂ (T A H) := (tensorInnerProductSpace J).toNormedSpace
    leftMulCompletion J (a * b) =
      (leftMulCompletion J a).comp (leftMulCompletion J b)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Stinespring.Canonical.Pre
declarations.doc:
A type synonym for `T A H` carrying the CP-kernel-dependent seminorm and inner product,
kept separate so the tensor product retains its own module structure.
declarations.statement: def Pre (_J : A →CP (H →L[ℂ] H))
instance (J : A →CP (H →L[ℂ] H)) : AddCommGroup (Pre J)
instance (J : A →CP (H →L[ℂ] H)) : Module ℂ (Pre J)
instance (J : A →CP (H →L[ℂ] H)) : SeminormedAddCommGroup (Pre J)
instance (J : A →CP (H →L[ℂ] H)) : InnerProductSpace ℂ (Pre J)
instance (J : A →CP (H →L[ℂ] H)) : IsUniformAddGroup (Pre J)
instance (J : A →CP (H →L[ℂ] H)) : IsBoundedSMul ℂ (Pre J)
instance (J : A →CP (H →L[ℂ] H)) : UniformContinuousConstSMul ℂ (Pre J)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Stinespring.Canonical.K
declarations.doc: The completion of `Pre J`: the canonical Stinespring Hilbert space attached to `J`.
declarations.statement: abbrev K (J : A →CP (H →L[ℂ] H))

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Stinespring.Canonical.preLeftMul
declarations.doc: `leftMul a`, viewed as an operator on `Pre J`.
declarations.statement:
def preLeftMul (J : A →CP (H →L[ℂ] H)) (a : A) :
    Pre J →ₗ[ℂ] Pre J

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Stinespring.Canonical.preLeftMul_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma preLeftMul_apply (J : A →CP (H →L[ℂ] H)) (a : A) (x : Pre J) :
    preLeftMul J a x = leftMul a x

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Stinespring.Canonical.preLeftMulCLM
declarations.doc: `preLeftMul`, bundled as a continuous linear map.
declarations.statement:
def preLeftMulCLM (J : A →CP (H →L[ℂ] H)) (a : A) :
    Pre J →L[ℂ] Pre J

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Stinespring.Canonical.preLeftMulCLM_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma preLeftMulCLM_apply (J : A →CP (H →L[ℂ] H)) (a : A) (x : Pre J) :
    preLeftMulCLM J a x = preLeftMul J a x

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Stinespring.Canonical.completion_leftMul_norm_le
declarations.statement:
lemma completion_leftMul_norm_le (J : A →CP (H →L[ℂ] H)) (a : A) (x : K J) :
    ‖(preLeftMulCLM J a).completion x‖ ≤ ‖a‖ * ‖x‖

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Stinespring.Canonical.leftMulK
declarations.doc: The continuous extension of `preLeftMulCLM` to the completion `K J`.
declarations.statement: def leftMulK (J : A →CP (H →L[ℂ] H)) (a : A) : K J →L[ℂ] K J

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Stinespring.Canonical.leftMulK_coe
declarations.statement:
lemma leftMulK_coe (J : A →CP (H →L[ℂ] H)) (a : A) (x : Pre J) :
    leftMulK J a (x : K J) = preLeftMulCLM J a x

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Stinespring.Canonical.leftMulK_mul
declarations.statement:
lemma leftMulK_mul (J : A →CP (H →L[ℂ] H)) (a b : A) :
    leftMulK J (a * b) = (leftMulK J a).comp (leftMulK J b)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Stinespring.Canonical.leftMulK_one
declarations.statement:
lemma leftMulK_one (J : A →CP (H →L[ℂ] H)) :
    leftMulK J (1 : A) = ContinuousLinearMap.id ℂ (K J)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Stinespring.Canonical.leftMulK_add
declarations.statement:
lemma leftMulK_add (J : A →CP (H →L[ℂ] H)) (a b : A) :
    leftMulK J (a + b) = leftMulK J a + leftMulK J b

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Stinespring.Canonical.leftMulK_smul
declarations.statement:
lemma leftMulK_smul (J : A →CP (H →L[ℂ] H)) (r : ℂ) (a : A) :
    leftMulK J (r • a) = r • leftMulK J a

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Stinespring.Canonical.leftMulK_star
declarations.statement:
lemma leftMulK_star (J : A →CP (H →L[ℂ] H)) (a : A) :
    leftMulK J (star a) = (leftMulK J a).adjoint

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Stinespring.Canonical.preEmbedding
declarations.doc: The canonical embedding `H → Pre J`, `h ↦ 1 ⊗ h`.
declarations.statement: def preEmbedding (J : A →CP (H →L[ℂ] H)) : H →ₗ[ℂ] Pre J

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Stinespring.Canonical.preEmbedding_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma preEmbedding_apply (J : A →CP (H →L[ℂ] H)) (h : H) :
    preEmbedding J h = (1 : A) ⊗ₜ[ℂ] h

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Stinespring.Canonical.preEmbedding_norm_sq
declarations.statement:
lemma preEmbedding_norm_sq (J : A →CP (H →L[ℂ] H)) (h : H) :
    ‖preEmbedding J h‖ ^ 2 = RCLike.re (inner ℂ h (J (1 : A) h))

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Stinespring.Canonical.preEmbedding_norm_le
declarations.statement:
lemma preEmbedding_norm_le (J : A →CP (H →L[ℂ] H)) (h : H) :
    ‖preEmbedding J h‖ ≤ Real.sqrt ‖J (1 : A)‖ * ‖h‖

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Stinespring.Canonical.preEmbeddingCLM
declarations.doc: `preEmbedding`, bundled as a continuous linear map.
declarations.statement: def preEmbeddingCLM (J : A →CP (H →L[ℂ] H)) : H →L[ℂ] Pre J

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Stinespring.Canonical.embedding
declarations.doc: The canonical embedding `H → K J` into the completed Stinespring space.
declarations.statement: def embedding (J : A →CP (H →L[ℂ] H)) : H →L[ℂ] K J

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Stinespring.Canonical.embedding_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma embedding_apply (J : A →CP (H →L[ℂ] H)) (h : H) :
    embedding J h = (preEmbedding J h : K J)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Stinespring.Canonical.canonicalRepresentation
declarations.doc: The representation of `A` on `K J` by (extended) left multiplication.
declarations.statement:
def canonicalRepresentation (J : A →CP (H →L[ℂ] H)) :
    A →⋆ₐ[ℂ] (K J →L[ℂ] K J)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Stinespring.Canonical.canonical_stinespring_identity
declarations.doc:
**Stinespring's dilation identity**: `J a = V⋆ π(a) V`, where `π` is `canonicalRepresentation`
and `V` is `embedding`.
declarations.statement:
lemma canonical_stinespring_identity (J : A →CP (H →L[ℂ] H)) (a : A) :
    J a = ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint (embedding J) ∘L
      (canonicalRepresentation J a) ∘L embedding J

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Stinespring.Canonical.canonicalWitness
declarations.doc:
The canonical Stinespring witness assembled from `canonicalRepresentation` and
`embedding`.
declarations.statement:
def canonicalWitness (J : A →CP (H →L[ℂ] H)) :
    StinespringWitness A H (K J) J

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Stinespring.exists_stinespringWitness
declarations.doc:
**Stinespring's dilation theorem.** Every completely positive map `J` into the bounded operators
on `H` is `J a = V⋆ π(a) V` for a representation `π` on some Hilbert space `K` and an operator `V :
H → K`.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_stinespringWitness (J : A →CP (H →L[ℂ] H)) :
    Nonempty (StinespringWitness A H (Canonical.K J) J)

modules.title: Completely positive maps as positive kernels
modules.doc:
Completely positive maps give positive operator-valued kernels; Stinespring witnesses.

## i. Overview

A completely positive map `J` into the bounded operators on `H` is a positive operator-valued
kernel: applied to the Gram matrix of finitely many elements of `A`, it gives a positive block
operator on `Hⁿ`. A Stinespring witness of `J` is a representation `π` on a Hilbert space `K` and an
operator `V : H → K` with `J a = V⋆ π(a) V`.

## ii. Key results

- `blockMatrixMap` : a matrix of operators acting on `Hⁿ`.
- `cpKernel_inner_nonneg_natural'` : completely positive maps give positive kernels.
- `StinespringWitness` : a Stinespring dilation of `J`.
- `completelyPositiveMap_map_star_general` : completely positive maps preserve the adjoint.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. `blockMatrixMap`: the finite block-operator representation
- B. The CP-map positivity kernel
- C. Stinespring witnesses

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text:
## A. `blockMatrixMap`: the finite block-operator representation

This part uses only the codomain Hilbert space `H`, no algebra `A` at all.

## B. The CP-map positivity kernel

From here on, `A` is a unital C⋆-algebra with the compatible Mathlib order (`[CStarAlgebra A]
[PartialOrder A] [StarOrderedRing A]`) — the field content of `OperatorAlgebra A`.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.blockMatrixMap
declarations.doc: The bounded operator on `PiLp 2 (Fin n → H)` acting block-by-block by `M`.
declarations.statement:
def blockMatrixMap {n : ℕ} (M : CStarMatrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (H →L[ℂ] H)) :
    PiLp 2 (fun _ : Fin n => H) →L[ℂ] PiLp 2 (fun _ : Fin n => H)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.blockMatrixMap_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma blockMatrixMap_apply {n : ℕ} (M : CStarMatrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (H →L[ℂ] H))
    (x : PiLp 2 (fun _ : Fin n => H)) (i : Fin n) :
    (blockMatrixMap M x).ofLp i = ∑ j, M i j (x.ofLp j)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.blockMatrixMap_star
declarations.statement:
lemma blockMatrixMap_star {n : ℕ} (M : CStarMatrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (H →L[ℂ] H)) :
    blockMatrixMap (star M) = (blockMatrixMap M).adjoint

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.blockMatrixMap_mul
declarations.statement:
lemma blockMatrixMap_mul {n : ℕ} (M N : CStarMatrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (H →L[ℂ] H)) :
    blockMatrixMap (M * N) = blockMatrixMap M ∘L blockMatrixMap N

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.blockMatrixMap_one
declarations.statement:
lemma blockMatrixMap_one {n : ℕ} :
    blockMatrixMap (1 : CStarMatrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (H →L[ℂ] H)) = ContinuousLinearMap.id ℂ _

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.blockMatrixMap_add
declarations.statement:
lemma blockMatrixMap_add {n : ℕ} (M N : CStarMatrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (H →L[ℂ] H)) :
    blockMatrixMap (M + N) = blockMatrixMap M + blockMatrixMap N

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.blockMatrixMap_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma blockMatrixMap_zero {n : ℕ} :
    blockMatrixMap (0 : CStarMatrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (H →L[ℂ] H)) = 0

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.blockMatrixRepresentation
declarations.doc:
`blockMatrixMap`, packaged as a star algebra homomorphism from
`CStarMatrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (H →L[ℂ] H)`.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.blockMatrixMap_isPositive
declarations.statement:
lemma blockMatrixMap_isPositive {n : ℕ} {M : CStarMatrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (H →L[ℂ] H)}
    (hM : 0 ≤ M) : (blockMatrixMap M).IsPositive

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.blockMatrixMap_inner_nonneg
ProbabilisticTheory.completelyPositiveMap_map_star_general
declarations.doc: A CP map between C⋆-algebras is automatically star-preserving.
declarations.statement:
lemma completelyPositiveMap_map_star_general
    {A B : Type*} [CStarAlgebra A] [PartialOrder A] [StarOrderedRing A]
    [CStarAlgebra B] [PartialOrder B] [StarOrderedRing B]
    (J : A →CP B) (a : A) : star (J a) = J (star a)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.rowMatrix
declarations.doc: A square matrix whose only nonzero row is the zeroth row.
declarations.statement:
def rowMatrix {n : ℕ} [NeZero n] (a : Fin n → A) :
    CStarMatrix (Fin n) (Fin n) A

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.gramMatrix
declarations.doc: The Gram matrix of a finite family of elements of a C⋆-algebra.
declarations.statement:
def gramMatrix {n : ℕ} [NeZero n] (a : Fin n → A) :
    CStarMatrix (Fin n) (Fin n) A

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.gramMatrix_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma gramMatrix_apply {n : ℕ} [NeZero n] (a : Fin n → A) (i j : Fin n) :
    gramMatrix a i j = star (a i) * a j

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.gramMatrix_nonneg
declarations.statement: lemma gramMatrix_nonneg {n : ℕ} [NeZero n] (a : Fin n → A) : 0 ≤ gramMatrix a

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.cpGramMatrix_nonneg
declarations.statement:
lemma cpGramMatrix_nonneg {n : ℕ} [NeZero n] (J : A →CP (H →L[ℂ] H)) (a : Fin n → A) :
    0 ≤ (gramMatrix a).map J

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.cpKernel_inner_nonneg
declarations.statement:
lemma cpKernel_inner_nonneg {n : ℕ} [NeZero n] (J : A →CP (H →L[ℂ] H)) (a : Fin n → A)
    (x : PiLp 2 (fun _ : Fin n => H)) :
    0 ≤ ∑ i, ∑ j, inner ℂ (J (star (a i) * a j) (x.ofLp j)) (x.ofLp i)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.cpKernel_inner_nonneg'
declarations.statement:
lemma cpKernel_inner_nonneg' {n : ℕ} (J : A →CP (H →L[ℂ] H)) (a : Fin n → A)
    (x : PiLp 2 (fun _ : Fin n => H)) :
    0 ≤ ∑ i, ∑ j, inner ℂ (J (star (a i) * a j) (x.ofLp j)) (x.ofLp i)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.cpKernel_inner_nonneg_natural
declarations.statement:
lemma cpKernel_inner_nonneg_natural {n : ℕ} [NeZero n] (J : A →CP (H →L[ℂ] H)) (a : Fin n → A)
    (x : PiLp 2 (fun _ : Fin n => H)) :
    0 ≤ ∑ i, ∑ j, inner ℂ (x.ofLp i) (J (star (a i) * a j) (x.ofLp j))

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.cpKernel_inner_nonneg_natural'
declarations.statement:
lemma cpKernel_inner_nonneg_natural' {n : ℕ} (J : A →CP (H →L[ℂ] H)) (a : Fin n → A)
    (x : PiLp 2 (fun _ : Fin n => H)) :
    0 ≤ ∑ i, ∑ j, inner ℂ (x.ofLp i) (J (star (a i) * a j) (x.ofLp j))

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.StinespringWitness
declarations.doc:
A Stinespring dilation of `J`: a representation `π` of `A` on a Hilbert space `K` and an
operator `V : H → K` with `J a = V⋆ π(a) V`.
declarations.statement:
structure StinespringWitness (A H K : Type*) [CStarAlgebra A] [PartialOrder A]
    [StarOrderedRing A] [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [CompleteSpace H]
    [NormedAddCommGroup K] [InnerProductSpace ℂ K] [CompleteSpace K]
    (J : A →CP (H →L[ℂ] H)) where
  /-- The representation of the input operator algebra on the auxiliary space. -/
  representation : A →⋆ₐ[ℂ] (K →L[ℂ] K)
  /-- The implementing bounded operator from the physical space to the auxiliary space. -/
  implementing : H →L[ℂ] K
  /-- The Stinespring identity: `J a = V⋆ π(a) V`. -/
  map_eq : ∀ a : A,
    J a = ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint implementing ∘L
      (representation a) ∘L implementing

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.StinespringWitness.map_eq_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma map_eq_apply (a : A) :
    J a = ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint W.implementing ∘L
      (W.representation a) ∘L W.implementing

modules.title: Uncertainty relations
modules.doc:
Cauchy–Schwarz for states and the Robertson and Robertson–Schrödinger uncertainty relations.

## i. Overview

A state gives the sesquilinear form `(x, y) ↦ ω(x⋆ y)`, which is the inner product of the GNS
vectors of `x` and `y`. Cauchy–Schwarz for it, applied to centered observables, gives the
Robertson–Schrödinger relation, and from it the Robertson relation `|ω⟨⁅a, b⁆⟩| ≤ σ_a σ_b` and the
bound on the covariance.

For a family of observables `a : ι → Observable A`, the covariance matrix `Σ` and the matrix `Ω`
of expectations of brackets give the matrix `Σ + iΩ` of GNS inner products of the centered
observables. It is a Gram matrix, and with its transpose `Σ − iΩ` it gives Robertson's relation
for several observables, `|det Ω| ≤ det Σ`.

The equality case: if `A` is positive definite and `‖det B‖ = det A`, the normalized `B` has all
its eigenvalues equal to `±1`, so `(A + B) A⁻¹ (A − B) = 0`, and the kernels of `A + B` and
`A − B` together span everything. For `A ± B = Σ ± iΩ` the two kernels have the same dimension.
This extends to `n` observables the equality case of two, `robertson_schrodinger_eq_iff_gram_zero`.

## ii. Key results

- `UnitalPositiveLinearMap.gns_cauchy_schwarz` : Cauchy–Schwarz for a state.
- `UnitalPositiveLinearMap.robertson_schrodinger` : **the Robertson–Schrödinger uncertainty
  relation.**
- `UnitalPositiveLinearMap.robertson` : **the Robertson uncertainty relation.**
- `UnitalPositiveLinearMap.covariance_cauchy_schwarz` : `|cov(a, b)| ≤ σ_a σ_b`.
- `Matrix.PosDef.norm_det_le_re_det` : `‖det B‖ ≤ det A` when `A ± B` are positive semidefinite.
- `Matrix.PosDef.add_mul_inv_mul_sub_eq_zero` : at equality, `(A + B) A⁻¹ (A − B) = 0`.
- `Matrix.card_le_two_mul_finrank_ker` : at equality `|det W| = det S ≠ 0`, the kernel of
  `S + iW` has at least half the dimension.
- `UnitalPositiveLinearMap.robertson_det` : **Robertson's uncertainty relation for several
  observables**, `|det Ω| ≤ det Σ`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Cauchy–Schwarz
- B. Uncertainty relations
- C. Equality in the uncertainty relations
- D. Normalized variance bounds
- E. A determinant bound for positive matrices
  - E.1. The equality case
- F. Several observables

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## C. Equality in the uncertainty relations
## E. A determinant bound for positive matrices

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.smul_one_comm
declarations.doc:
A real multiple of `1` commutes with everything: the algebraic fact making `commutator`
insensitive to shifting by a constant.
declarations.statement: lemma smul_one_comm (r : ℝ) (x : A) : (r • (1 : A)) * x = x * (r • (1 : A))

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.bracket_centered
declarations.doc:
The commutator only sees fluctuations, not means: centering `a` and `b` changes nothing about
how badly they fail to commute, since scalar multiples of `1` commute with everything and so
contribute nothing to `ab - ba`.
declarations.statement:
lemma bracket_centered (ω : 𝓢[ℂ, A]) (a b : Observable A) :
    ⁅centered ω a, centered ω b⁆ = ⁅a, b⁆

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.apply_centered_mul_centered
declarations.doc:
The expectation of a raw product of two fluctuations splits into a real symmetric part
(covariance) and an imaginary antisymmetric part (the commutator's expectation). This is what
turns the Cauchy–Schwarz bound below into simultaneous control on covariance and commutator.
declarations.statement:
lemma apply_centered_mul_centered (ω : 𝓢[ℂ, A]) (a b : Observable A) :
    ω ((centered ω a : A) * centered ω b) =
      (covariance ω a b : ℂ) + Complex.I * (ω⟨⁅a, b⁆⟩ : ℂ)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.inner_gnsRep_gnsCyclicVector_gnsRep_gnsCyclicVector
declarations.doc: `⟪π_ω(x) Ω_ω, π_ω(y) Ω_ω⟫ = ω(x⋆ y)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma inner_gnsRep_gnsCyclicVector_gnsRep_gnsCyclicVector (ω : 𝓢[ℂ, A]) (x y : A) :
    ⟪ω.gnsRep x ω.gnsCyclicVector, ω.gnsRep y ω.gnsCyclicVector⟫_ℂ = ω (star x * y)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.gns_cauchy_schwarz
declarations.doc: **Cauchy–Schwarz for a state**: `|ω(x⋆ y)|² ≤ ω(x⋆ x) ω(y⋆ y)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma gns_cauchy_schwarz (ω : 𝓢[ℂ, A]) (x y : A) :
    ‖ω (star x * y)‖ * ‖ω (star y * x)‖ ≤
      (ω (star x * x)).re * (ω (star y * y)).re

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.centered_gns_cauchy_schwarz
declarations.doc:
No state can correlate two fluctuations more strongly than the product of their spreads
allows — the GNS-Cauchy–Schwarz seed of every uncertainty relation below, before splitting the
left side via `apply_centered_mul_centered`.
declarations.statement:
lemma centered_gns_cauchy_schwarz (ω : 𝓢[ℂ, A]) (a b : Observable A) :
    ‖ω ((centered ω a : A) * centered ω b)‖ *
        ‖ω ((centered ω b : A) * centered ω a)‖ ≤
      variance ω a * variance ω b

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.centered_cauchy_schwarz
declarations.doc:
The squared-magnitude form of `centered_gns_cauchy_schwarz`, ready to be split via
`apply_centered_mul_centered` into `robertson_schrodinger`.
declarations.statement:
lemma centered_cauchy_schwarz (ω : 𝓢[ℂ, A]) (a b : Observable A) :
    Complex.normSq (ω ((centered ω a : A) * centered ω b)) ≤
      variance ω a * variance ω b

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.robertson_schrodinger
declarations.doc:
**The Robertson–Schrödinger uncertainty relation**, bounding the squared covariance plus the
squared expectation of the commutator by the product of the variances.
declarations.statement:
lemma robertson_schrodinger (ω : 𝓢[ℂ, A]) (a b : Observable A) :
    covariance ω a b ^ 2 + ω⟨⁅a, b⁆⟩ ^ 2 ≤
      variance ω a * variance ω b

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.covariance_cauchy_schwarz
declarations.doc:
Two observables cannot be more correlated than the product of their uncertainties allows —
the familiar `|correlation| ≤ σ_a · σ_b`, from dropping the commutator term in
`robertson_schrodinger`.
declarations.statement:
lemma covariance_cauchy_schwarz (ω : 𝓢[ℂ, A]) (a b : Observable A) :
    covariance ω a b ^ 2 ≤ variance ω a * variance ω b

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.robertson
declarations.doc:
Heisenberg's uncertainty relation: observables that fail to commute cannot both be measured
with arbitrary precision. For position and momentum, `⁅x, p⁆ = iℏ` gives `ΔxΔp ≥ ℏ/2`. Obtained
from `robertson_schrodinger` by dropping the covariance term.
declarations.statement:
lemma robertson (ω : 𝓢[ℂ, A]) (a b : Observable A) :
    ω⟨⁅a, b⁆⟩ ^ 2 ≤ variance ω a * variance ω b

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.centeredGramDefect
declarations.doc:
The Cauchy–Schwarz defect of two centered observables, the slack in the Robertson–Schrödinger
relation.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def centeredGramDefect (ω : 𝓢[ℂ, A]) (a b : Observable A) : ℝ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.centeredGramDefect_nonneg
declarations.doc: Positivity of the state makes the centered Gram defect nonnegative.
declarations.statement:
lemma centeredGramDefect_nonneg (ω : 𝓢[ℂ, A]) (a b : Observable A) :
    0 ≤ centeredGramDefect ω a b

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.normSq_centered_pairing
declarations.doc:
The squared centered pairing consists of squared covariance and squared
expectation of the observable Lie bracket.
declarations.statement:
lemma normSq_centered_pairing (ω : 𝓢[ℂ, A]) (a b : Observable A) :
    Complex.normSq (ω ((centered ω a : A) * centered ω b)) =
      covariance ω a b ^ 2 + ω⟨⁅a, b⁆⟩ ^ 2

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.robertson_gap_decomposition
declarations.doc: The slack in the Robertson relation is the Cauchy–Schwarz defect plus the squared covariance.
declarations.statement:
lemma robertson_gap_decomposition (ω : 𝓢[ℂ, A]) (a b : Observable A) :
    variance ω a * variance ω b - ω⟨⁅a, b⁆⟩ ^ 2 =
      centeredGramDefect ω a b + covariance ω a b ^ 2

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.robertson_schrodinger_eq_iff_gram_zero
declarations.doc: Robertson–Schrödinger saturates exactly when the centered Gram defect vanishes.
declarations.statement:
lemma robertson_schrodinger_eq_iff_gram_zero (ω : 𝓢[ℂ, A]) (a b : Observable A) :
    covariance ω a b ^ 2 + ω⟨⁅a, b⁆⟩ ^ 2 = variance ω a * variance ω b ↔
      centeredGramDefect ω a b = 0

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.robertson_eq_iff_gram_zero_and_covariance_zero
declarations.doc:
Robertson saturates exactly when Cauchy–Schwarz saturates for the centered
pairing and the covariance is zero. Includes zero-variance cases without division.
declarations.statement:
lemma robertson_eq_iff_gram_zero_and_covariance_zero (ω : 𝓢[ℂ, A])
    (a b : Observable A) :
    ω⟨⁅a, b⁆⟩ ^ 2 = variance ω a * variance ω b ↔
      centeredGramDefect ω a b = 0 ∧ covariance ω a b = 0

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.normalized_variance_product
declarations.doc:
A raw commutator expectation of magnitude one yields the normalized variance
product bound for arbitrary states, with no extra positivity hypotheses.
declarations.statement:
lemma normalized_variance_product (ω : 𝓢[ℂ, A]) (a b : Observable A)
    (hnorm : ω⟨⁅a, b⁆⟩ ^ 2 = (1 : ℝ) / 4) :
    1 ≤ 4 * variance ω a * variance ω b

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.variances_pos_of_normalized_pairing
declarations.doc: Normalization itself forces both variances to be positive.
declarations.statement:
lemma variances_pos_of_normalized_pairing (ω : 𝓢[ℂ, A]) (a b : Observable A)
    (hnorm : ω⟨⁅a, b⁆⟩ ^ 2 = (1 : ℝ) / 4) :
    0 < variance ω a ∧ 0 < variance ω b

declarations.name: Matrix.PosDef.normalizer
declarations.doc:
A matrix `T` with `T A Tᴴ = 1` for a positive definite `A`: the inverse square roots of the
eigenvalues of `A` times the adjoint of its eigenvector unitary.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def PosDef.normalizer {A : Matrix n n ℂ} (hA : A.PosDef) : Matrix n n ℂ

declarations.name: Matrix.PosDef.normalizer_mul_mul_conjTranspose
declarations.statement:
lemma PosDef.normalizer_mul_mul_conjTranspose {A : Matrix n n ℂ} (hA : A.PosDef) :
    hA.normalizer * A * hA.normalizerᴴ = 1

declarations.name: Matrix.IsHermitian.abs_eigenvalues_le_one
declarations.doc:
The eigenvalues of a hermitian `K` with `1 − K` and `1 + K` positive semidefinite lie in
`[−1, 1]`.
declarations.statement:
lemma IsHermitian.abs_eigenvalues_le_one {K : Matrix n n ℂ} (hK : K.IsHermitian)
    (hm : (1 - K).PosSemidef) (hp : (1 + K).PosSemidef) (i : n) : |hK.eigenvalues i| ≤ 1

declarations.name: Matrix.PosDef.norm_det_le_re_det
declarations.doc:
If `A` is positive definite, `B` hermitian and `A − B`, `A + B` positive semidefinite, then
`‖det B‖ ≤ re (det A)`: conjugating by the normalizer of `A` puts `B` between `−1` and `1`.
declarations.statement:
lemma PosDef.norm_det_le_re_det {A B : Matrix n n ℂ} (hA : A.PosDef) (hB : B.IsHermitian)
    (h₁ : (A - B).PosSemidef) (h₂ : (A + B).PosSemidef) : ‖B.det‖ ≤ (A.det).re

declarations.name: Matrix.map_ofReal_add_smul_one
declarations.statement:
lemma map_ofReal_add_smul_one (S : Matrix n n ℝ) (ε : ℝ) :
    (S + ε • 1).map ((↑) : ℝ → ℂ) = S.map ((↑) : ℝ → ℂ) + (ε : ℂ) • 1

declarations.name: Matrix.abs_det_le_det_of_posSemidef
declarations.doc:
For real `S` and `W`, if `S − iW` and `S + iW` are positive semidefinite then
`|det W| ≤ det S`.
declarations.statement:
lemma abs_det_le_det_of_posSemidef {S W : Matrix n n ℝ}
    (h₁ : (S.map ((↑) : ℝ → ℂ) - Complex.I • W.map ((↑) : ℝ → ℂ)).PosSemidef)
    (h₂ : (S.map ((↑) : ℝ → ℂ) + Complex.I • W.map ((↑) : ℝ → ℂ)).PosSemidef) :
    |W.det| ≤ S.det

declarations.name: Matrix.IsHermitian.mul_self_eq_one
declarations.doc: A hermitian `K` with eigenvalues in `[−1, 1]` and `‖det K‖ = 1` squares to the identity.
declarations.statement:
lemma IsHermitian.mul_self_eq_one {K : Matrix n n ℂ} (hK : K.IsHermitian)
    (hle : ∀ i, |hK.eigenvalues i| ≤ 1) (h1 : ‖K.det‖ = 1) : K * K = 1

declarations.name: Matrix.PosDef.inv_eq_conjTranspose_normalizer_mul
declarations.doc: The normalizer of a positive definite `A` is invertible, and `A⁻¹ = Tᴴ T`.
declarations.statement:
lemma PosDef.inv_eq_conjTranspose_normalizer_mul {A : Matrix n n ℂ} (hA : A.PosDef) :
    A⁻¹ = hA.normalizerᴴ * hA.normalizer

declarations.name: Matrix.PosDef.add_mul_inv_mul_sub_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**The equality case.** If `A` is positive definite, `B` hermitian, `A ∓ B` positive
semidefinite and `‖det B‖ = re (det A)`, then `(A + B) A⁻¹ (A − B) = 0`: every eigenvalue of the
normalized `B` is `±1`.
declarations.statement:
lemma PosDef.add_mul_inv_mul_sub_eq_zero {A B : Matrix n n ℂ} (hA : A.PosDef)
    (hB : B.IsHermitian) (h₁ : (A - B).PosSemidef) (h₂ : (A + B).PosSemidef)
    (heq : ‖B.det‖ = (A.det).re) : (A + B) * A⁻¹ * (A - B) = 0

declarations.name: Matrix.PosDef.card_le_finrank_ker_add_finrank_ker
declarations.doc:
At equality the kernels of `A + B` and `A − B` together have dimension at least `n`: every
vector is `A⁻¹ (A − B) x / 2 + A⁻¹ (A + B) x / 2`.
declarations.statement:
lemma PosDef.card_le_finrank_ker_add_finrank_ker {A B : Matrix n n ℂ} (hA : A.PosDef)
    (hB : B.IsHermitian) (h₁ : (A - B).PosSemidef) (h₂ : (A + B).PosSemidef)
    (heq : ‖B.det‖ = (A.det).re) :
    Fintype.card n ≤ Module.finrank ℂ (LinearMap.ker (A + B).mulVecLin) +
      Module.finrank ℂ (LinearMap.ker (A - B).mulVecLin)

declarations.name: Matrix.finrank_ker_transpose
declarations.doc: `G` and `Gᵀ` have kernels of the same dimension.
declarations.statement:
lemma finrank_ker_transpose (G : Matrix n n ℂ) :
    Module.finrank ℂ (LinearMap.ker Gᵀ.mulVecLin) =
      Module.finrank ℂ (LinearMap.ker G.mulVecLin)

declarations.name: Matrix.card_le_two_mul_finrank_ker
declarations.doc:
**Equality in Robertson's determinant relation.** Let `G = S + iW` be positive semidefinite
with `Gᵀ = S − iW`, for real `S` and `W`. If `|det W| = det S ≠ 0`, the kernel of `G` has at
least half the dimension.
declarations.statement:
lemma card_le_two_mul_finrank_ker {G : Matrix n n ℂ} {S W : Matrix n n ℝ} (hG : G.PosSemidef)
    (hGS : G = S.map ((↑) : ℝ → ℂ) + Complex.I • W.map ((↑) : ℝ → ℂ))
    (hGT : Gᵀ = S.map ((↑) : ℝ → ℂ) - Complex.I • W.map ((↑) : ℝ → ℂ)) (hW : W.det ≠ 0)
    (heq : |W.det| = S.det) :
    Fintype.card n ≤ 2 * Module.finrank ℂ (LinearMap.ker G.mulVecLin)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.covarianceMatrix
declarations.doc: The covariance matrix `Σ_jk = cov(a_j, a_k)` of a family of observables.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def covarianceMatrix (ω : 𝓢[ℂ, A]) (a : ι → Observable A) : Matrix ι ι ℝ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.bracketMatrix
declarations.doc: The matrix `Ω_jk = ω⟨⁅a_j, a_k⁆⟩` of expectations of brackets of a family of observables.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def bracketMatrix (ω : 𝓢[ℂ, A]) (a : ι → Observable A) : Matrix ι ι ℝ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.centeredGNSVector
declarations.doc: The GNS vectors of the centered observables.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def centeredGNSVector (ω : 𝓢[ℂ, A]) (a : Observable A)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.gram_centeredGNSVector
declarations.doc: `Σ + iΩ` is the Gram matrix of the GNS vectors of the centered observables.
declarations.statement:
lemma gram_centeredGNSVector (ω : 𝓢[ℂ, A]) (a : ι → Observable A) :
    gram ℂ (fun j => centeredGNSVector ω (a j)) =
      (covarianceMatrix ω a).map ((↑) : ℝ → ℂ) +
        Complex.I • (bracketMatrix ω a).map ((↑) : ℝ → ℂ)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.transpose_gram_centeredGNSVector
declarations.doc: `Σ − iΩ` is the transpose of the Gram matrix.
declarations.statement:
lemma transpose_gram_centeredGNSVector (ω : 𝓢[ℂ, A]) (a : ι → Observable A) :
    (gram ℂ (fun j => centeredGNSVector ω (a j)))ᵀ =
      (covarianceMatrix ω a).map ((↑) : ℝ → ℂ) -
        Complex.I • (bracketMatrix ω a).map ((↑) : ℝ → ℂ)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.robertson_det
declarations.doc:
**Robertson's uncertainty relation for several observables**: for every state and every
finite family of observables, `|det Ω| ≤ det Σ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma robertson_det [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (ω : 𝓢[ℂ, A]) (a : ι → Observable A) :
    |(bracketMatrix ω a).det| ≤ (covarianceMatrix ω a).det

modules.title: Generators of one-parameter groups
modules.doc:
The generator of a one-parameter family on a normed space, and its uniqueness.

## i. Overview

The generator of a one-parameter family `α` on a normed space is `D a = lim_{t → 0} (α t a - a) /
t`, stated with `HasDerivAt`. It needs a topology but no algebraic structure, and it is unique when
it exists.

## ii. Key results

- `IsGenerator` : `D` generates `α`.
- `IsGenerator.unique` : the generator is unique.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The generator

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.IsGenerator
declarations.doc:
`D` is the infinitesimal generator, at `t = 0`, of the one-parameter family `α`: for every `a`,
`t ↦ α t a` is differentiable at `0` with derivative `D a`. No algebraic structure on `E` (product,
order, `⋆`) is assumed — this is purely about the curve `t ↦ α t a` in a normed space.
declarations.statement: def IsGenerator (α : ℝ → E → E) (D : E → E) : Prop

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.IsGenerator.unique
declarations.doc:
The generator of a one-parameter family, if it exists, is unique — immediate from uniqueness of
derivatives (`HasDerivAt.unique`).
declarations.statement:
lemma IsGenerator.unique {α : ℝ → E → E} {D₁ D₂ : E → E} (h₁ : IsGenerator α D₁)
    (h₂ : IsGenerator α D₂) : D₁ = D₂

modules.title: Generators of automorphism groups are derivations
modules.doc:
The generator of a one-parameter family of automorphisms is a derivation.

## i. Overview

If a one-parameter family `α` with `α 0 = id` preserves a bounded bilinear multiplication at every
time, its generator is a derivation of that multiplication. Differentiating `α t (a b) = α t a α t
b` at `0` with the product rule gives `D (a b) = D a b + a D b`. Only boundedness and bilinearity of
the product are used.

## ii. Key results

- `IsGenerator.isDerivation_of_isAutomorphismFamily` : the generator of a family of automorphisms is
  a derivation.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The generator is a derivation

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. The generator is a derivation

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.IsGenerator.isDerivation_of_isAutomorphismFamily
declarations.doc:
**The generator of a family of automorphisms is a derivation.** If `α 0 = id` and every `α t`
preserves a bounded bilinear multiplication, the generator of `α` is a derivation of it.
declarations.statement:
lemma IsGenerator.isDerivation_of_isAutomorphismFamily
    (bilin : IsBoundedBilinearMap ℝ (fun p : E × E => p.1 * p.2))
    {α : ℝ → E → E} (hα0 : ∀ a, α 0 a = a) (hmul : ∀ t a b, α t (a * b) = α t a * α t b)
    {D : E →ₗ[ℝ] E} (hD : IsGenerator α D) : IsDerivation D

modules.title: One-parameter groups
modules.doc:
Defines one-parameter groups `α : ℝ → E → E` satisfying `α 0 = id` and the group law.

## i. Overview

A one-parameter group is a family `α : ℝ → E → E` with `α 0 = id` and `α (s + t) = α s ∘ α t`. It is
stated for an arbitrary type `E`; preservation of structure and continuity are separate conditions.

## ii. Key results

- `IsOneParameterGroup` : one-parameter groups.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The group law

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.IsOneParameterGroup
declarations.doc:
`α : ℝ → E → E` is a one-parameter group of (not-yet-specified-as-anything) transformations of
`E`: `α 0 = id` and `α (s + t) = α s ∘ α t`. Nothing about linearity, order, a product, or
continuity is assumed — those are independent, composable hypotheses to add at the point of use.
declarations.statement:
structure IsOneParameterGroup {E : Type*} (α : ℝ → E → E) : Prop where
  /-- Evolving for zero time does nothing. -/
  map_zero : ∀ a : E, α 0 a = a
  /-- Evolving for `s` then `t` is the same as evolving for `s + t`. -/
  map_add : ∀ s t a, α (s + t) a = α s (α t a)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.IsOneParameterGroup.left_inv
declarations.doc:
Every time-`t` map has a two-sided inverse, `α (-t)`: an immediate consequence of the group
law, recorded once here rather than re-derived at each point of use.
declarations.statement: lemma left_inv (t : ℝ) (a : E) : α (-t) (α t a) = a

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.IsOneParameterGroup.right_inv
declarations.statement: lemma right_inv (t : ℝ) (a : E) : α t (α (-t) a) = a

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.IsOneParameterGroup.bijective
declarations.statement: lemma bijective (t : ℝ) : Function.Bijective (α t)

modules.title: Orthogonal effects
modules.doc:
Effects: the order interval `[0, 1]` of an ordered space, modelling yes/no measurement outcomes.

## i. Overview

Two effects are orthogonal when their sum is still an effect, that is, still bounded by the order
unit. Their partial sum is then again an effect.

## ii. Key results

- `Effect.Orthogonal` : two effects whose sum is bounded by the order unit.
- `Effect.addOfOrthogonal` : the partial sum of two orthogonal effects.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Orthogonal effects

## iv. References

- G. Ludwig, *Foundations of Quantum Mechanics I*, Springer, 1983.
  <https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-3-642-86751-4>

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Effect.Orthogonal
declarations.doc: Two effects are orthogonal when their sum is still bounded by the order unit.
declarations.statement: def Orthogonal (e f : Effect E) : Prop

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Effect.addOfOrthogonal
declarations.doc: The partial sum of two orthogonal effects.
declarations.statement: def addOfOrthogonal (e f : Effect E) (h : Orthogonal e f) : Effect E

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Effect.coe_addOfOrthogonal
declarations.doc: The underlying observable of an orthogonal effect sum is the ordinary sum.
declarations.statement:
lemma coe_addOfOrthogonal (e f : Effect E) (h : Orthogonal e f) :
    (addOfOrthogonal e f h : E) = (e : E) + (f : E)

modules.title: The generalized bit
modules.doc:
The generalized bit: the sup-norm cone over `ℝ³`, with an octahedral, non-simplex state space.

## i. Overview

The generalized bit is the norm cone over `ℝ³` with the sup norm in place of the Euclidean norm
of the qubit. Its states form an octahedron with `6` pure states, its vertices. That is finitely
many, but too many for a simplex in a `4`-dimensional space. So the gbit is not classical, and
not a qubit either: the shape of the cone matters, not just the dimension.

## ii. Key results

- `GBit` : the generalized bit.
- `GBit.stateEquiv` : the states are the octahedron.
- `GBit.isPure_purePoint` : the vertices of the octahedron are pure states.
- `GBit.not_isSimplex_stateSpace` : the state space is not a simplex.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The gbit as a norm cone
- B. Too many pure states

## iv. References

- J. Barrett, *Information processing in generalized probabilistic theories*, Phys. Rev. A 75,
  032304 (2007).
- P. Janotta and H. Lal, *Generalized probabilistic theories without the no-restriction
  hypothesis*, Phys. Rev. A 87, 052131 (2013).

sections.text: ## A. The gbit as a norm cone

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.GBit
declarations.doc: The generalized bit: `ℝ × ℝ³` ordered by the sup-norm cone.
declarations.statement: abbrev GBit : Type

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.GBit.stateEquiv
declarations.doc: The states of the gbit are the octahedron `∑ i, |a i| ≤ 1`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def stateEquiv : 𝓢[ℝ, GBit] ≃ {a : Fin 3 → ℝ // ∑ i, |a i| ≤ 1}

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.GBit.dualEquiv
declarations.doc: A functional on `Fin 3 → ℝ` is its vector of values on the standard basis.
declarations.statement: noncomputable abbrev dualEquiv : ((Fin 3 → ℝ) →L[ℝ] ℝ) ≃ₗ[ℝ] (Fin 3 → ℝ)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.GBit.dualEquiv_symm_image_ball
declarations.statement:
lemma dualEquiv_symm_image_ball :
    dualEquiv.symm '' {a : Fin 3 → ℝ | ∑ i, |a i| ≤ 1} = {f | ‖f‖ ≤ 1}

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.GBit.purePoint
declarations.doc: The pure state whose functional is `±1` times a coordinate.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def purePoint (j : Fin 3 × Bool) : 𝓢[ℝ, GBit]

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.GBit.isPure_purePoint
declarations.statement: lemma isPure_purePoint (j : Fin 3 × Bool) : (purePoint j).IsPure

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.GBit.purePoint_injective
declarations.statement: lemma purePoint_injective : Function.Injective purePoint

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.GBit.finrank_eq_four
declarations.statement: lemma finrank_eq_four : Module.finrank ℝ GBit = 4

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.GBit.not_isSimplex_stateSpace
declarations.doc:
**The gbit is not classical**: it has `6` pure states in a `4`-dimensional space, too many
for a simplex.
declarations.statement:
lemma not_isSimplex_stateSpace :
    ¬ IsSimplex (UnitalPositiveLinearMap.algebraicStateSpace (E := GBit))

modules.title: Order-unit spaces built from a normed vector space
modules.doc:
The order-unit space `ℝ × V` ordered by the norm cone of `V`, and its states as the dual ball.

## i. Overview

Any real normed vector space `V` carries a natural order-unit structure on `ℝ × V`: order unit
`(1, 0)`, and positive cone the "ice-cream" cone `{(r, x) | ‖x‖ ≤ r}` built from `V`'s norm. States
of this order-unit space correspond exactly to the closed unit ball of the continuous dual of `V`.

The qubit is the norm cone over Euclidean `ℝ³` and the generalized bit the norm cone over `ℝ³`
with the sup norm: same dimension, different norm, different state space.

## ii. Key results

- `NormCone V` : the order-unit space `ℝ × V`, ordered by the ice-cream cone built from `V`'s norm.
- `NormCone.instArchimedeanOrderUnitSpace` : `NormCone V` is an Archimedean order-unit space.
- `NormCone.mem_effect_iff` : an explicit description of `Effect (NormCone V)`.
- `NormCone.stateEquiv` : states of `NormCone V` correspond exactly to the closed unit ball of the
  continuous dual of `V`.
- `NormCone.lpStateEquiv`, `NormCone.supStateEquiv` : the states of an `ℓp` norm cone are the closed
  `ℓq` ball, those of the sup-normed cone the `ℓ1` ball.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The ice-cream cone order
- B. `NormCone V` is an Archimedean order-unit space
- C. Effects
- D. States correspond to the closed unit ball of the dual
- E. States, expanded against a basis
- F. Purity and extreme points of the dual ball
- G. States of `ℓp` and sup norm cones

## iv. References

- J. Barrett, *Information processing in generalized probabilistic theories*, Phys. Rev. A 75,
  032304 (2007).
- P. Janotta and H. Lal, *Generalized probabilistic theories without the no-restriction
  hypothesis*, Phys. Rev. A 87, 052131 (2013).

sections.text: ## B. `NormCone V` is an Archimedean order-unit space
## D. States correspond to the closed unit ball of the dual
## E. States, expanded against a basis
## F. Purity and extreme points of the dual ball
## G. States of `ℓp` and sup norm cones

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.NormCone
declarations.doc:
The order-unit space `ℝ × V` built from a real normed vector space `V`, ordered by the
ice-cream cone `{(r, x) | ‖x‖ ≤ r}`, as a type synonym so its order does not clash with the
product order on `ℝ × V`.
declarations.statement: def NormCone (V : Type*) [NormedAddCommGroup V] [NormedSpace ℝ V]

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.NormCone.toProd
declarations.doc: The linear equivalence to the underlying product, forgetting the order.
declarations.statement: def toProd : NormCone V ≃ ℝ × V
instance : AddCommGroup (NormCone V)
instance : Module ℝ (NormCone V)
instance : One (NormCone V)
instance : Nontrivial (NormCone V)

declarations.doc: `NormCone V` is finite-dimensional when `V` is.
declarations.statement: instance [FiniteDimensional ℝ V] : Module.Finite ℝ (NormCone V)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.NormCone.toProd_zero
declarations.statement: lemma toProd_zero : toProd (0 : NormCone V) = 0

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.NormCone.toProd_add
declarations.statement: lemma toProd_add (x y : NormCone V) : toProd (x + y) = toProd x + toProd y

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.NormCone.toProd_neg
declarations.statement: lemma toProd_neg (x : NormCone V) : toProd (-x) = -toProd x

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.NormCone.toProd_sub
declarations.statement: lemma toProd_sub (x y : NormCone V) : toProd (x - y) = toProd x - toProd y

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.NormCone.toProd_smul
declarations.statement: lemma toProd_smul (c : ℝ) (x : NormCone V) : toProd (c • x) = c • toProd x

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.NormCone.toProd_one
declarations.statement: lemma toProd_one : toProd (1 : NormCone V) = (1, 0)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.NormCone.toProd_smul_one
declarations.doc: The order unit `1 : NormCone V` scaled by a real number, in coordinates.
declarations.statement: lemma toProd_smul_one (r : ℝ) : toProd (r • (1 : NormCone V)) = (r, 0)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.NormCone.mk
declarations.doc: Build an element of `NormCone V` from its coordinates.
declarations.statement: def mk (r : ℝ) (v : V) : NormCone V

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.NormCone.toProd_mk
declarations.statement: lemma toProd_mk (r : ℝ) (v : V) : toProd (mk r v) = (r, v)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.NormCone.NonnegCone
declarations.doc: The ice-cream cone: `(r, x)` is nonnegative when `‖x‖ ≤ r`.
declarations.statement: def NonnegCone (z : NormCone V) : Prop
instance : LE (NormCone V)
instance : LT (NormCone V)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.NormCone.le_iff
declarations.statement:
lemma le_iff {x y : NormCone V} :
    x ≤ y ↔ ‖(toProd y).2 - (toProd x).2‖ ≤ (toProd y).1 - (toProd x).1

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.NormCone.mk_le_mk_iff
declarations.statement:
lemma mk_le_mk_iff {r₁ r₂ : ℝ} {v₁ v₂ : V} :
    mk r₁ v₁ ≤ mk r₂ v₂ ↔ ‖v₂ - v₁‖ ≤ r₂ - r₁
instance : PartialOrder (NormCone V)
instance : IsOrderedAddMonoid (NormCone V)
instance : PosSMulMono ℝ (NormCone V)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.NormCone.instOrderUnitSpace
declarations.statement: instance instOrderUnitSpace : OrderUnitSpace (NormCone V)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.NormCone.instArchimedeanOrderUnitSpace
declarations.statement: instance instArchimedeanOrderUnitSpace : ArchimedeanOrderUnitSpace (NormCone V)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.NormCone.mem_effect_iff
declarations.doc: The effects of `NormCone V` are the pairs `(r, v)` with `‖v‖ ≤ r` and `‖v‖ ≤ 1 - r`.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_effect_iff {z : NormCone V} :
    z ∈ (Effect (NormCone V) : Set (NormCone V)) ↔
      ‖(toProd z).2‖ ≤ (toProd z).1 ∧ ‖(toProd z).2‖ ≤ 1 - (toProd z).1

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.NormCone.mk_add
declarations.statement: lemma mk_add (r₁ r₂ : ℝ) (v₁ v₂ : V) : mk r₁ v₁ + mk r₂ v₂ = mk (r₁ + r₂) (v₁ + v₂)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.NormCone.mk_smul
declarations.statement: lemma mk_smul (c : ℝ) (r : ℝ) (v : V) : c • mk r v = mk (c * r) (c • v)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.NormCone.mk_neg
declarations.statement: lemma mk_neg (r : ℝ) (v : V) : -mk r v = mk (-r) (-v)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.NormCone.smul_one_eq_mk
declarations.statement: lemma smul_one_eq_mk (r : ℝ) : r • (1 : NormCone V) = mk r 0

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.NormCone.mk_toProd
declarations.statement: lemma mk_toProd (z : NormCone V) : mk (toProd z).1 (toProd z).2 = z

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.NormCone.neg_smul_one_le_mk_zero_iff
declarations.statement: lemma neg_smul_one_le_mk_zero_iff {r : ℝ} {v : V} : -(r • (1 : NormCone V)) ≤ mk 0 v ↔ ‖v‖ ≤ r

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.NormCone.mk_zero_le_smul_one_iff
declarations.statement: lemma mk_zero_le_smul_one_iff {r : ℝ} {v : V} : mk 0 v ≤ r • (1 : NormCone V) ↔ ‖v‖ ≤ r

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.NormCone.orderUnitNorm_mk_zero
declarations.doc:
The order-unit norm of a purely spatial coordinate `(0, v)` is exactly the norm of `v`: the
order-unit norm restricted to this slice is the norm it was built from.
declarations.statement: lemma orderUnitNorm_mk_zero (v : V) : orderUnitNorm (mk 0 v) = ‖v‖

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.NormCone.mkZeroLinear
declarations.doc: The linear map `v ↦ (0, v)` from `V` into `NormCone V`.
declarations.statement: def mkZeroLinear : V →ₗ[ℝ] NormCone V

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.NormCone.mkZeroLinear_apply
declarations.statement: lemma mkZeroLinear_apply (v : V) : mkZeroLinear v = mk 0 v

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.NormCone.apply_mk_eq
declarations.doc: Every state is a "radius plus a bounded linear functional of the spatial part".
declarations.statement:
lemma apply_mk_eq (ω : 𝓢[ℝ, NormCone V]) (r : ℝ) (v : V) :
    ω (mk r v) = r + ω (mkZeroLinear v)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.NormCone.abs_apply_mkZeroLinear_le
declarations.doc: The functional a state induces on `V`, `v ↦ ω (0, v)`, is `1`-Lipschitz.
declarations.statement:
lemma abs_apply_mkZeroLinear_le (ω : 𝓢[ℝ, NormCone V]) (v : V) :
    |ω (mkZeroLinear v)| ≤ ‖v‖

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.NormCone.dualOfLinear
declarations.doc: The linear functional `v ↦ ω (0, v)` induced by a state.
declarations.statement: def dualOfLinear (ω : 𝓢[ℝ, NormCone V]) : V →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.NormCone.dualOfLinear_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma dualOfLinear_apply (ω : 𝓢[ℝ, NormCone V]) (v : V) :
    dualOfLinear ω v = ω (mkZeroLinear v)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.NormCone.dualOf
declarations.doc: The bounded linear functional on `V` induced by a state of `NormCone V`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def dualOf (ω : 𝓢[ℝ, NormCone V]) : V →L[ℝ] ℝ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.NormCone.dualOf_apply
declarations.statement: lemma dualOf_apply (ω : 𝓢[ℝ, NormCone V]) (v : V) : dualOf ω v = ω (mkZeroLinear v)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.NormCone.norm_dualOf_le
declarations.statement: lemma norm_dualOf_le (ω : 𝓢[ℝ, NormCone V]) : ‖dualOf ω‖ ≤ 1

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.NormCone.stateOfDual
declarations.doc:
Build a state of `NormCone V` from a bounded linear functional `f` of norm at most `1`:
`ω (r, x) = r + f x`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def stateOfDual (f : V →L[ℝ] ℝ) (hf : ‖f‖ ≤ 1) : 𝓢[ℝ, NormCone V]

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.NormCone.stateOfDual_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma stateOfDual_apply (f : V →L[ℝ] ℝ) (hf : ‖f‖ ≤ 1) (z : NormCone V) :
    stateOfDual f hf z = (toProd z).1 + f (toProd z).2

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.NormCone.stateEquiv
declarations.doc:
States of `NormCone V` correspond exactly to the closed unit ball of the continuous dual
of `V`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def stateEquiv : 𝓢[ℝ, NormCone V] ≃ {f : V →L[ℝ] ℝ // ‖f‖ ≤ 1}

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.NormCone.apply_mk_basis
declarations.doc: A state is determined by its values on a basis.
declarations.statement:
lemma apply_mk_basis (b : Module.Basis ι ℝ V) (ω : 𝓢[ℝ, NormCone V]) (r : ℝ) (v : V) :
    ω (mk r v) = r + ∑ i, b.repr v i * ω (mk 0 (b i))

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.NormCone.dualOf_mix
declarations.doc: `dualOf` sends mixtures to convex combinations.
declarations.statement:
lemma dualOf_mix (φ ψ : 𝓢[ℝ, NormCone V]) (t : unitInterval) :
    dualOf (UnitalPositiveLinearMap.mix φ ψ t) =
      (t : ℝ) • dualOf φ + (1 - (t : ℝ)) • dualOf ψ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.NormCone.dualOf_injective
declarations.doc: `dualOf` is injective.
declarations.statement: lemma dualOf_injective : Function.Injective (dualOf (V := V))

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.NormCone.dualOf_stateOfDual
declarations.doc: `dualOf` undoes `stateOfDual`.
declarations.statement:
lemma dualOf_stateOfDual (f : V →L[ℝ] ℝ) (hf : ‖f‖ ≤ 1) :
    dualOf (stateOfDual f hf) = f

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.NormCone.range_dualOf
declarations.statement: lemma range_dualOf : Set.range (dualOf (V := V)) = {g | ‖g‖ ≤ 1}

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.NormCone.isPure_stateOfDual_iff
declarations.doc:
A state is pure exactly when its functional is an extreme point of the unit ball of the
dual.
declarations.statement:
lemma isPure_stateOfDual_iff {f : V →L[ℝ] ℝ} (hf : ‖f‖ ≤ 1) :
    (stateOfDual f hf).IsPure ↔ f ∈ Set.extremePoints ℝ {g : V →L[ℝ] ℝ | ‖g‖ ≤ 1}

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.NormCone.lpStateEquiv
declarations.doc: The states of an `ℓp` norm cone are the closed `ℓq` ball.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.NormCone.lpCone_mem_effect_iff
declarations.statement:
lemma lpCone_mem_effect_iff (hnorm : ∀ v : V, ‖v‖ = (∑ i, |b.repr v i| ^ p) ^ (1 / p))
    {z : NormCone V} : z ∈ (Effect (NormCone V) : Set (NormCone V)) ↔
      (∑ i, |b.repr (toProd z).2 i| ^ p) ^ (1 / p) ≤ (toProd z).1 ∧
        (∑ i, |b.repr (toProd z).2 i| ^ p) ^ (1 / p) ≤ 1 - (toProd z).1

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.NormCone.supStateEquiv
declarations.doc: The states of the sup-normed norm cone are the closed `ℓ1` ball.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def supStateEquiv {m : ℕ} :
    𝓢[ℝ, NormCone (Fin m → ℝ)] ≃ {a : Fin m → ℝ // ∑ i, |a i| ≤ 1}

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.NormCone.supCone_mem_effect_iff
declarations.statement:
lemma supCone_mem_effect_iff {m : ℕ} {z : NormCone (Fin m → ℝ)} :
    z ∈ (Effect (NormCone (Fin m → ℝ)) : Set (NormCone (Fin m → ℝ))) ↔
      ‖(toProd z).2‖ ≤ (toProd z).1 ∧ ‖(toProd z).2‖ ≤ 1 - (toProd z).1

modules.title: The qubit, in Bloch-vector coordinates
modules.doc:
The qubit as the Euclidean norm cone over `ℝ³`: its states form the Bloch ball, not a simplex.

## i. Overview

A qubit state is a density matrix `ρ = ½(r • I + x · σ)`, given by a number `r` and a Bloch
vector `x ∈ ℝ³`, and `ρ` is positive exactly when `‖x‖ ≤ r`. So in Bloch coordinates the qubit is
the norm cone over Euclidean `ℝ³`. Its states form the Bloch ball and every point of the Bloch
sphere is a pure state. With infinitely many pure states, the state space is not a simplex: the
qubit is not classical.

## ii. Key results

- `ProbabilisticTheory.Qubit` : the qubit in Bloch coordinates.
- `ProbabilisticTheory.Qubit.stateEquiv` : the states are the Bloch ball.
- `ProbabilisticTheory.Qubit.isPure_purePoint` : unit Bloch vectors give pure states.
- `ProbabilisticTheory.Qubit.not_isSimplex_stateSpace` : the state space is not a simplex.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The qubit as a norm cone
- B. Infinitely many pure states

## iv. References

- J. Barrett, *Information processing in generalized probabilistic theories*, Phys. Rev. A 75,
  032304 (2007).
- P. Janotta and H. Lal, *Generalized probabilistic theories without the no-restriction
  hypothesis*, Phys. Rev. A 87, 052131 (2013).

sections.text: ## A. The qubit as a norm cone

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Qubit
declarations.doc: The qubit in Bloch coordinates: `ℝ × ℝ³` ordered by the Lorentz cone.
declarations.statement: abbrev Qubit : Type

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Qubit.stateEquiv
declarations.doc: The states of the qubit are the Bloch ball.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def stateEquiv :
    𝓢[ℝ, Qubit] ≃ {a : Fin 3 → ℝ // ∑ i, |a i| ^ (2 : ℝ) ≤ 1}

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Qubit.toDualEquiv
declarations.doc: The Riesz isomorphism between `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)` and its dual.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def toDualEquiv :
    EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3) ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3) →L[ℝ] ℝ)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Qubit.blochVec
declarations.doc: The Bloch vector `(t, √(1 - t²), 0)`, a unit vector for `t ∈ [0, 1]`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def blochVec (t : ℝ) : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Qubit.norm_blochVec
declarations.statement: lemma norm_blochVec {t : ℝ} (ht0 : 0 ≤ t) (ht1 : t ≤ 1) : ‖blochVec t‖ = 1

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Qubit.blochVec_injective
declarations.statement: lemma blochVec_injective : Function.Injective fun t : Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1 => blochVec t

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Qubit.purePoint
declarations.doc: The pure state dual to the Bloch vector at parameter `t ∈ [0, 1]`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def purePoint (t : Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1) : 𝓢[ℝ, Qubit]

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Qubit.image_toDualEquiv_closedBall
declarations.statement:
lemma image_toDualEquiv_closedBall :
    toDualEquiv '' Metric.closedBall (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) 1 = {g | ‖g‖ ≤ 1}

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Qubit.isPure_purePoint
declarations.doc:
Every state `purePoint t` is pure: its Bloch vector lies on the sphere, and the sphere
consists of extreme points of the ball.
declarations.statement: lemma isPure_purePoint (t : Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1) : (purePoint t).IsPure

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Qubit.purePoint_injective
declarations.statement: lemma purePoint_injective : Function.Injective purePoint

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Qubit.not_isSimplex_stateSpace
declarations.doc:
**The qubit is not classical**: it has infinitely many pure states, while a simplex has
finitely many extreme points.
declarations.statement:
lemma not_isSimplex_stateSpace :
    ¬ IsSimplex (UnitalPositiveLinearMap.algebraicStateSpace (E := Qubit))

modules.title: The square
modules.doc:
The square state space: its observables, its four facets and vertex values of composites.

## i. Overview

The square is the simplest state space that is not a simplex: it has four pure states, the
vertices, and the two diagonals of the square have the same midpoint. Its observables are the affine
functions on the square, recorded by their values at the four vertices `0, 1, 2, 3`, with the
diagonal relation `v 0 + v 3 = v 1 + v 2`. An observable is nonnegative when all four values are.

The nonnegative observables are generated by the four facets: the affine functions that vanish on
one side of the square. An observable of the composite of `E` with the square is recorded by its
four vertex values in `E`, which again satisfy the diagonal relation.

## ii. Key results

- `Square` : the observables of the square, an order-unit space.
- `Square.facet` : the four facets.
- `Square.exists_eq_sum_facet` : every nonnegative observable is a nonnegative combination of
  facets.
- `Square.vals` : the vertex values of an observable of `E ⊗ Square`.
- `Square.vals_injective` : vertex values determine the observable.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The square
- B. Facets
- C. Vertex values of composite observables

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## C. Vertex values of composite observables

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.squareSubmodule
declarations.doc: Vertex values `v 0, v 1, v 2, v 3` satisfying the diagonal relation `v 0 + v 3 = v 1 + v 2`.
declarations.statement: def squareSubmodule : Submodule ℝ (Fin 4 → ℝ)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Square
declarations.doc: The observables of the square: affine functions, recorded by their values at the vertices.
declarations.statement: def Square : Type
instance : AddCommGroup Square
instance : Module ℝ Square

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Square.val
declarations.doc: The value at the `i`-th vertex.
declarations.statement: def val (q : Square) (i : Fin 4) : ℝ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Square.mk
declarations.doc: The observable with the given vertex values.
declarations.statement: def mk (v : Fin 4 → ℝ) (h : v 0 + v 3 = v 1 + v 2) : Square

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Square.val_mk
declarations.statement: lemma val_mk (v : Fin 4 → ℝ) (h) (i : Fin 4) : (mk v h).val i = v i

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Square.ext
declarations.statement: lemma ext {q r : Square} (h : ∀ i, q.val i = r.val i) : q = r

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Square.diagonal
declarations.statement: lemma diagonal (q : Square) : q.val 0 + q.val 3 = q.val 1 + q.val 2

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Square.val_add
declarations.statement: lemma val_add (q r : Square) (i : Fin 4) : (q + r).val i = q.val i + r.val i

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Square.val_smul
declarations.statement: lemma val_smul (c : ℝ) (q : Square) (i : Fin 4) : (c • q).val i = c * q.val i

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Square.val_zero
declarations.statement: lemma val_zero (i : Fin 4) : (0 : Square).val i = 0
instance : PartialOrder Square

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Square.le_def
declarations.statement: lemma le_def {q r : Square} : q ≤ r ↔ ∀ i, q.val i ≤ r.val i
instance : IsOrderedAddMonoid Square
instance : PosSMulMono ℝ Square

declarations.doc: The unit: the constant function `1`.
declarations.statement: instance : One Square

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Square.val_one
declarations.statement: lemma val_one (i : Fin 4) : (1 : Square).val i = 1
instance : OrderUnitSpace Square
instance : ArchimedeanOrderUnitSpace Square

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Square.ev
declarations.doc: Evaluation at the `i`-th vertex: a pure state of the square.
declarations.statement: def ev (i : Fin 4) : Square →ₚ[ℝ] ℝ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Square.ev_apply
declarations.statement: lemma ev_apply (i : Fin 4) (q : Square) : ev i q = q.val i

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Square.facet
declarations.doc:
The four facets: `facet 0` vanishes on vertices `0, 2`, `facet 1` on `0, 1`, `facet 2` on
`1, 3`, and `facet 3` on `2, 3`.
declarations.statement: def facet : Fin 4 → Square

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Square.facet_nonneg
declarations.statement: lemma facet_nonneg (j : Fin 4) : 0 ≤ facet j

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Square.val_sum
declarations.statement: lemma val_sum (q : Fin 4 → Square) (i : Fin 4) : (∑ j, q j).val i = ∑ j, (q j).val i

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Square.exists_eq_sum_facet
declarations.doc: Every nonnegative observable of the square is a nonnegative combination of the facets.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_eq_sum_facet {q : Square} (hq : 0 ≤ q) :
    ∃ c : Fin 4 → ℝ, (∀ j, 0 ≤ c j) ∧ q = ∑ j, c j • facet j

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Square.eq_add_facet
declarations.doc: An observable of the square is determined by its values at the vertices `0, 1, 2`.
declarations.statement:
lemma eq_add_facet (q : Square) :
    q = q.val 0 • 1 + (q.val 1 - q.val 0) • facet 0 + (q.val 2 - q.val 0) • facet 1

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Square.vals
declarations.doc: The vertex values of an observable of the composite with the square.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def vals : E ⊗[ℝ] Square →ₗ[ℝ] (Fin 4 → E)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Square.vals_tmul
declarations.statement: lemma vals_tmul (x : E) (q : Square) : vals (x ⊗ₜ[ℝ] q) = fun i => q.val i • x

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Square.vals_diagonal
declarations.doc: The vertex values of a composite observable satisfy the diagonal relation.
declarations.statement: lemma vals_diagonal (z : E ⊗[ℝ] Square) : vals z 0 + vals z 3 = vals z 1 + vals z 2

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Square.ofVals
declarations.doc: The composite observable with the given vertex values, where only `A 0, A 1, A 2` matter.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def ofVals (A : Fin 4 → E) : E ⊗[ℝ] Square

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Square.ofVals_add
declarations.statement: lemma ofVals_add (A B : Fin 4 → E) : ofVals (A + B) = ofVals A + ofVals B

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Square.ofVals_vals
declarations.statement: lemma ofVals_vals (z : E ⊗[ℝ] Square) : ofVals (vals z) = z

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Square.vals_ofVals
declarations.doc:
Vertex values satisfying the diagonal relation are the vertex values of a composite
observable.
declarations.statement: lemma vals_ofVals {A : Fin 4 → E} (hA : A 0 + A 3 = A 1 + A 2) : vals (ofVals A) = A

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Square.vals_injective
declarations.doc: Vertex values determine the composite observable.
declarations.statement: lemma vals_injective : Function.Injective (vals : E ⊗[ℝ] Square →ₗ[ℝ] (Fin 4 → E))

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Square.val_lslice
declarations.doc:
Applying a positive functional to the `E` factor gives the observable of the square whose
vertex values are the values of the functional on the vertex values.
declarations.statement:
lemma val_lslice (φ : E →ₚ[ℝ] ℝ) (z : E ⊗[ℝ] Square) (i : Fin 4) :
    (lslice φ z).val i = φ (vals z i)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Square.mem_maxTensorCone_of_vals_nonneg
declarations.doc: A composite observable whose vertex values are nonnegative is in the maximal cone.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_maxTensorCone_of_vals_nonneg {z : E ⊗[ℝ] Square} (h : ∀ i, 0 ≤ vals z i) :
    z ∈ maxTensorCone E Square

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Square.mem_maxTensorCone_iff
declarations.doc:
For Archimedean `E`, the maximal cone of the composite with the square consists of the
observables with nonnegative vertex values.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_maxTensorCone_iff {E : Type*} [ArchimedeanOrderUnitSpace E] {z : E ⊗[ℝ] Square} :
    z ∈ maxTensorCone E Square ↔ ∀ i, 0 ≤ vals z i

modules.title: Automorphisms of the bounded operators
modules.doc:
⋆-automorphisms of bounded operators are unitary conjugations; conjugation flows are unique.
