## i. Overview

Every `⋆`-automorphism of the bounded operators on a Hilbert space is conjugation `A ↦ U A U⋆` by a
unitary, and two unitaries give the same automorphism exactly when they differ by a phase. So the
automorphism group is the projective unitary group.

A norm-continuous unitary one-parameter group `U` acts by `αₜ(a) = U(t) a U(t)⋆`. This flow is the
unique solution of the Heisenberg equation `d/dt αₜ(a) = ⁅αₜ(a), i G⁆` with `α₀ = id`, where `G` is
the generator of `U` and the bracket is the ring commutator.

## ii. Key results

- `conjStarAlgAut_surjective` : every `⋆`-automorphism is unitary conjugation.
- `conjStarAlgAut_eq_iff` : two unitaries give the same automorphism iff they differ by a phase.
- `projectiveUnitaryEquivStarAlgAut` : the automorphism group is the projective unitary group.
- `UnitaryOneParameterGroup.toAutomorphism_unique` : the conjugation flow is the unique solution of
  the Heisenberg equation.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Every ⋆-automorphism is unitary conjugation
- B. The automorphism group generated by unitary conjugation
- C. Differential characterization

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## B. The automorphism group generated by unitary conjugation

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.conjStarAlgAut_surjective
declarations.doc: Every ⋆-automorphism of `H →L[ℂ] H` is implemented by unitary conjugation.
declarations.statement:
lemma conjStarAlgAut_surjective :
    Function.Surjective (Unitary.conjStarAlgAut ℂ (H →L[ℂ] H))

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.conjStarAlgAut_eq_iff
declarations.doc:
Two unitaries implement the same ⋆-automorphism of `H →L[ℂ] H` exactly when they differ by a
scalar phase.
declarations.statement:
lemma conjStarAlgAut_eq_iff (u v : unitary (H →L[ℂ] H)) :
    Unitary.conjStarAlgAut ℂ (H →L[ℂ] H) u =
        Unitary.conjStarAlgAut ℂ (H →L[ℂ] H) v ↔
      ∃ c : unitary ℂ, u = c • v

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.ProjectiveUnitary
declarations.doc: The projective unitary group of `H`, obtained by quotienting out scalar phases.
declarations.statement:
def ProjectiveUnitary (H : Type*) [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℂ H]
    [CompleteSpace H]
noncomputable instance : Group (ProjectiveUnitary H)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.projectiveUnitaryEquivStarAlgAut
declarations.doc: Reversible transformations of `H →L[ℂ] H` are precisely projective unitaries.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def projectiveUnitaryEquivStarAlgAut :
    ProjectiveUnitary H ≃* ((H →L[ℂ] H) ≃⋆ₐ[ℂ] (H →L[ℂ] H))

declarations.name: UnitaryOneParameterGroup.toAutomorphism
declarations.doc: The reversible dynamics `a ↦ U(t) a U(t)⋆` induced by a unitary one-parameter group.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def toAutomorphism (U : UnitaryOneParameterGroup H) :
    AutomorphismGroup (H →L[ℂ] H)

declarations.name: UnitaryOneParameterGroup.toAutomorphism_apply
declarations.doc: The induced automorphism is unitary conjugation.
declarations.statement:
lemma toAutomorphism_apply (U : UnitaryOneParameterGroup H) (t : ℝ) (a : H →L[ℂ] H) :
    (toAutomorphism U).toFun t a = U t * a * star (U t)

declarations.name: UnitaryOneParameterGroup.hasDerivAt_toAutomorphism
declarations.doc:
The conjugation flow satisfies the Heisenberg equation
`d/dt αₜ(a) = ⁅αₜ(a), i • generator⁆`.
declarations.statement:
lemma hasDerivAt_toAutomorphism (U : UnitaryOneParameterGroup H) (a : H →L[ℂ] H) (t : ℝ) :
    HasDerivAt (fun s : ℝ => (toAutomorphism U).toFun s a)
      ⁅(toAutomorphism U).toFun t a, Complex.I • U.generator⁆ t

declarations.name: UnitaryOneParameterGroup.const_of_hasDerivAt_zero
declarations.doc: A function on `ℝ` with everywhere-zero derivative is constant.
declarations.statement:
lemma const_of_hasDerivAt_zero {f : ℝ → H →L[ℂ] H} (hf : ∀ s, HasDerivAt f 0 s) (t : ℝ) :
    f t = f 0

declarations.name: UnitaryOneParameterGroup.hasDerivAt_conj_zero
declarations.doc:
Along a solution `α` of the Heisenberg equation, the conjugated path
`s ↦ U(s)⋆ αₛ(a) U(s)` has zero derivative.
declarations.statement:
lemma hasDerivAt_conj_zero (U : UnitaryOneParameterGroup H)
    (α : ℝ → (H →L[ℂ] H) → H →L[ℂ] H) (a : H →L[ℂ] H)
    (hα : ∀ t, HasDerivAt (fun s => α s a) ⁅α t a, Complex.I • U.generator⁆ t)
    (s : ℝ) :
    HasDerivAt (fun r => star (U r) * α r a * U r) 0 s

declarations.name: UnitaryOneParameterGroup.toAutomorphism_unique
declarations.doc: The conjugation flow is the unique solution of its Heisenberg initial-value problem.
declarations.statement:
lemma toAutomorphism_unique (U : UnitaryOneParameterGroup H)
    (α : ℝ → (H →L[ℂ] H) → H →L[ℂ] H) (hα0 : α 0 = id)
    (hα : ∀ a t, HasDerivAt (fun s : ℝ => α s a) ⁅α t a, Complex.I • U.generator⁆ t) :
    α = fun t a => (toAutomorphism U).toFun t a

modules.title: Hamiltonian dynamics
modules.doc:
The unitary evolution and Heisenberg flow of a bounded Hamiltonian, and their uniqueness.

## i. Overview

A bounded Hamiltonian `H` generates the unitary evolution `U(t) = exp(-i t H / ℏ)` and the flow
`αₜ(a) = U(t) a U(t)⋆`, the unique solution of `d/dt αₜ(a) = -(i / ℏ) [H, αₜ(a)]` with `α₀ = id`.
Shifting `H` by a real multiple of the identity changes `U(t)` only by a phase and leaves the flow
unchanged, and this is the only freedom.

## ii. Key results

- `UnitaryOneParameterGroup.unitaryEvolution` : the unitary evolution of a bounded Hamiltonian.
- `UnitaryOneParameterGroup.hamiltonianFlow` : the Heisenberg-picture flow.
- `UnitaryOneParameterGroup.hamiltonianFlow_unique` : the flow solves the Heisenberg equation
  uniquely.
- `UnitaryOneParameterGroup.hamiltonianFlow_add_smul_one` : shifting the Hamiltonian by a constant
  leaves the flow unchanged.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Unitary evolution
- B. Hamiltonian flow
- C. Equivariance under star automorphisms
- D. Differential characterization
- E. Hamiltonians modulo scalar shifts
- F. Classification up to star-automorphism conjugation

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text:
## C. Equivariance under star automorphisms

Changing the representation by `β` conjugates the flow generated by `β(H)` by `β`.

## D. Differential characterization

A one-line specialization of the generic `UnitaryOneParameterGroup` API to
`U = unitaryEvolution ℏ H`, with generator `(i/ℏ) H`.

## F. Classification up to star-automorphism conjugation

`hamiltonianFlow_map` and `hamiltonianFlow_add_smul_one` give the easy direction: `K` generates the
`β`-conjugate of `H`'s flow whenever `K = β(H) + c • 1`. The converse needs a differential argument,
`hamiltonianFlow_eq_iff` below.

declarations.doc: Needed for `NormedSpace.map_exp` at `H →L[ℂ] H`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable local instance : NormedAlgebra ℚ (H →L[ℂ] H)

declarations.name: UnitaryOneParameterGroup.real_smul_eq_complex_smul
declarations.doc: A real scalar multiple on `H →L[ℂ] H` agrees with the corresponding complex scalar multiple.
declarations.statement: lemma real_smul_eq_complex_smul (r : ℝ) (x : H →L[ℂ] H) : r • x = (r : ℂ) • x

declarations.name: UnitaryOneParameterGroup.unitaryEvolution
declarations.doc: The unitary evolution `U_H(t) = exp(-itH/ℏ)` generated by `H`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def unitaryEvolution
    (ℏ : ℝ) (Hm : Observable (H →L[ℂ] H)) :
    UnitaryOneParameterGroup H

declarations.name: UnitaryOneParameterGroup.unitaryEvolution_generator
declarations.doc: The generator of `unitaryEvolution` is `ℏ⁻¹ • H`.
declarations.statement:
lemma unitaryEvolution_generator
    (ℏ : ℝ) (Hm : Observable (H →L[ℂ] H)) :
    (unitaryEvolution ℏ Hm).generator =
      (ℏ⁻¹ : ℝ) • (Hm : H →L[ℂ] H)

declarations.name: UnitaryOneParameterGroup.unitaryEvolution_apply
declarations.doc: The closed form `U_H(t) = exp(-itH/ℏ)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma unitaryEvolution_apply
    (ℏ : ℝ) (Hm : Observable (H →L[ℂ] H)) (t : ℝ) :
    unitaryEvolution ℏ Hm t =
      NormedSpace.exp
        ((-(t : ℂ) * Complex.I) •
          ((ℏ⁻¹ : ℝ) • (Hm : H →L[ℂ] H)))

declarations.name: UnitaryOneParameterGroup.hamiltonianFlow
declarations.doc: The automorphism flow induced by the unitary evolution generated by `H`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def hamiltonianFlow
    (ℏ : ℝ) (Hm : Observable (H →L[ℂ] H)) :
    AutomorphismGroup (H →L[ℂ] H)

declarations.name: UnitaryOneParameterGroup.hamiltonianFlow_apply
declarations.doc: Unfolds `hamiltonianFlow` to `a ↦ U(t) a U(t)⋆`.
declarations.statement:
lemma hamiltonianFlow_apply
    (ℏ : ℝ) (Hm : Observable (H →L[ℂ] H)) (t : ℝ) (a : H →L[ℂ] H) :
    (hamiltonianFlow ℏ Hm).toFun t a =
      unitaryEvolution ℏ Hm t * a * star (unitaryEvolution ℏ Hm t)

declarations.name: UnitaryOneParameterGroup.unitaryEvolution_map
declarations.doc: Conjugating the generating unitary by `β` amounts to applying `β` pointwise.
declarations.statement:
lemma unitaryEvolution_map (ℏ : ℝ) (β : (H →L[ℂ] H) ≃⋆ₐ[ℂ] (H →L[ℂ] H))
    (Hm : Observable (H →L[ℂ] H)) (t : ℝ) :
    unitaryEvolution ℏ (β.observable Hm) t = β (unitaryEvolution ℏ Hm t)

declarations.name: UnitaryOneParameterGroup.hamiltonianFlow_map
declarations.doc:
The Hamiltonian flow is equivariant under ⋆-automorphism conjugation: `β(H)`'s flow is `H`'s
flow viewed through the change of coordinates `β`.
declarations.statement:
lemma hamiltonianFlow_map (ℏ : ℝ) (β : (H →L[ℂ] H) ≃⋆ₐ[ℂ] (H →L[ℂ] H))
    (Hm : Observable (H →L[ℂ] H)) :
    hamiltonianFlow ℏ (β.observable Hm) = (hamiltonianFlow ℏ Hm).conj β

declarations.name: UnitaryOneParameterGroup.hamiltonianFlow_conj_unitary
declarations.doc: The unitary specialization of `hamiltonianFlow_map`, at `β = Ad_V` for a unitary `V`.
declarations.statement:
lemma hamiltonianFlow_conj_unitary (ℏ : ℝ) (V : unitary (H →L[ℂ] H))
    (Hm : Observable (H →L[ℂ] H)) :
    hamiltonianFlow ℏ ((Unitary.conjStarAlgAut ℂ (H →L[ℂ] H) V).observable Hm) =
      (hamiltonianFlow ℏ Hm).conj (Unitary.conjStarAlgAut ℂ (H →L[ℂ] H) V)

declarations.name: UnitaryOneParameterGroup.G
declarations.doc: The scaled Hamiltonian `(i/ℏ) H`, the generator on the right of the Heisenberg equation.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def G (ℏ : ℝ) (Hm : Observable (H →L[ℂ] H)) : H →L[ℂ] H

declarations.name: UnitaryOneParameterGroup.smul_I_generator
declarations.doc: `G` is `i` times `unitaryEvolution`'s generator.
declarations.statement:
lemma smul_I_generator (ℏ : ℝ) (Hm : Observable (H →L[ℂ] H)) :
    Complex.I • (unitaryEvolution ℏ Hm).generator = G ℏ Hm

declarations.name: UnitaryOneParameterGroup.hasDerivAt_hamiltonianFlow
declarations.doc: The Hamiltonian flow satisfies the Heisenberg equation `d/dt αₜ(a) = ⁅αₜ(a), G⁆`.
declarations.statement:
lemma hasDerivAt_hamiltonianFlow (ℏ : ℝ) (Hm : Observable (H →L[ℂ] H)) (a : H →L[ℂ] H)
    (t : ℝ) :
    HasDerivAt (fun t : ℝ => (hamiltonianFlow ℏ Hm).toFun t a)
      ⁅(hamiltonianFlow ℏ Hm).toFun t a, G ℏ Hm⁆ t

declarations.name: UnitaryOneParameterGroup.hamiltonianFlow_unique
declarations.doc: The Hamiltonian flow is the unique solution of its Heisenberg initial-value problem.
declarations.statement:
lemma hamiltonianFlow_unique (ℏ : ℝ) (Hm : Observable (H →L[ℂ] H))
    (α : ℝ → (H →L[ℂ] H) → H →L[ℂ] H) (hα0 : α 0 = id)
    (hα : ∀ a t, HasDerivAt (fun s : ℝ => α s a) ⁅α t a, G ℏ Hm⁆ t) :
    α = fun t a => (hamiltonianFlow ℏ Hm).toFun t a

declarations.name: UnitaryOneParameterGroup.G_add_smul_one
declarations.doc: Shifting `H` by `c • 1` shifts `G` by a central term.
declarations.statement:
lemma G_add_smul_one (ℏ : ℝ) (Hm : Observable (H →L[ℂ] H)) (c : ℝ) :
    G ℏ (Hm + c • 1) = G ℏ Hm + ((Complex.I / (ℏ : ℂ)) * (c : ℂ)) • (1 : H →L[ℂ] H)

declarations.name: UnitaryOneParameterGroup.central_cancel
declarations.doc: A central element (a scalar multiple of `1`) brackets to zero with anything.
declarations.statement:
lemma central_cancel (z : ℂ) (x : H →L[ℂ] H) :
    ⁅x, z • (1 : H →L[ℂ] H)⁆ = 0

declarations.name: UnitaryOneParameterGroup.lie_add'
declarations.doc: The bracket is additive in its second argument.
declarations.statement: lemma lie_add' (x m n : H →L[ℂ] H) : ⁅x, m + n⁆ = ⁅x, m⁆ + ⁅x, n⁆

declarations.name: UnitaryOneParameterGroup.hamiltonianFlow_add_smul_one
declarations.doc: Scalar shifts of `H` don't change the Hamiltonian flow.
declarations.statement:
lemma hamiltonianFlow_add_smul_one
    (ℏ : ℝ) (Hm : Observable (H →L[ℂ] H)) (c : ℝ) :
    hamiltonianFlow ℏ (Hm + c • 1) =
      hamiltonianFlow ℏ Hm

declarations.name: UnitaryOneParameterGroup.hamiltonianFlow_eq_of_eq_add_smul_one
declarations.doc: Hamiltonians differing by a real scalar multiple of the identity generate the same flow.
declarations.statement:
lemma hamiltonianFlow_eq_of_eq_add_smul_one
    (ℏ : ℝ) (Hm K : Observable (H →L[ℂ] H)) (c : ℝ)
    (h : Hm = K + c • 1) :
    hamiltonianFlow ℏ Hm = hamiltonianFlow ℏ K

declarations.name: UnitaryOneParameterGroup.hamiltonianFlow_map_add_smul_one
declarations.doc: If `K = β(H) + c • 1`, `K`'s flow is `H`'s flow viewed through `β`.
declarations.statement:
lemma hamiltonianFlow_map_add_smul_one (ℏ : ℝ) (β : (H →L[ℂ] H) ≃⋆ₐ[ℂ] (H →L[ℂ] H))
    (Hm K : Observable (H →L[ℂ] H)) (c : ℝ) (h : K = β.observable Hm + c • 1) :
    hamiltonianFlow ℏ K = (hamiltonianFlow ℏ Hm).conj β

declarations.name: UnitaryOneParameterGroup.comm_G_of_hamiltonianFlow_eq
declarations.doc:
If `H` and `K` generate the same flow, `G ℏ H - G ℏ K` commutes with everything: equal flows
have equal derivatives at `0`, and the Heisenberg equation reads that off as a bracket.
declarations.statement:
lemma comm_G_of_hamiltonianFlow_eq (ℏ : ℝ) (Hm K : Observable (H →L[ℂ] H))
    (heq : hamiltonianFlow ℏ Hm = hamiltonianFlow ℏ K) (a : H →L[ℂ] H) :
    a * (G ℏ Hm - G ℏ K) = (G ℏ Hm - G ℏ K) * a

declarations.name: UnitaryOneParameterGroup.exists_real_of_isSelfAdjoint_sub_smul_one
declarations.doc:
A self-adjoint difference of self-adjoint elements that is a scalar multiple of `1` has a real
scalar: self-adjointness of `w • 1` forces `conj w = w`.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_real_of_isSelfAdjoint_sub_smul_one [Nontrivial (H →L[ℂ] H)]
    {x y : H →L[ℂ] H} (hx : IsSelfAdjoint x) (hy : IsSelfAdjoint y) {w : ℂ}
    (h : x - y = w • (1 : H →L[ℂ] H)) :
    ∃ c : ℝ, x = y + c • 1

declarations.name: UnitaryOneParameterGroup.hamiltonianFlow_eq_iff
declarations.doc:
Two Hamiltonians generate the same flow (at a fixed representation) exactly when they differ
by a real scalar multiple of the identity.
declarations.statement:
lemma hamiltonianFlow_eq_iff (ℏ : ℝ) (hℏ : ℏ ≠ 0) [Nontrivial (H →L[ℂ] H)]
    (Hm K : Observable (H →L[ℂ] H)) :
    hamiltonianFlow ℏ Hm = hamiltonianFlow ℏ K ↔ ∃ c : ℝ, Hm = K + c • 1

declarations.name: UnitaryOneParameterGroup.hamiltonianFlow_conj_iff
declarations.doc:
Two Hamiltonians generate conjugate flows exactly when they agree up to a change of
representation `β` and a real scalar shift.
declarations.statement:
lemma hamiltonianFlow_conj_iff (ℏ : ℝ) (hℏ : ℏ ≠ 0) [Nontrivial (H →L[ℂ] H)]
    (β : (H →L[ℂ] H) ≃⋆ₐ[ℂ] (H →L[ℂ] H)) (Hm K : Observable (H →L[ℂ] H)) :
    hamiltonianFlow ℏ K = (hamiltonianFlow ℏ Hm).conj β ↔ ∃ c : ℝ, K = β.observable Hm + c • 1

declarations.name: UnitaryOneParameterGroup.hamiltonianFlow_iff_exists_unitary
declarations.doc:
Two Hamiltonians generate flows related by some automorphism of `H →L[ℂ] H` exactly when one
is a unitary conjugate of the other, up to a real scalar shift.
declarations.statement:
lemma hamiltonianFlow_iff_exists_unitary (ℏ : ℝ) (hℏ : ℏ ≠ 0) [Nontrivial (H →L[ℂ] H)]
    (Hm K : Observable (H →L[ℂ] H)) :
    (∃ β : (H →L[ℂ] H) ≃⋆ₐ[ℂ] (H →L[ℂ] H), hamiltonianFlow ℏ K = (hamiltonianFlow ℏ Hm).conj β) ↔
      ∃ (V : unitary (H →L[ℂ] H)) (c : ℝ),
        (K : H →L[ℂ] H) = (V : H →L[ℂ] H) * (Hm : H →L[ℂ] H) * star (V : H →L[ℂ] H) +
          c • 1

modules.title: The joint spectral measure of a commuting family
modules.doc:
A commuting family of bounded operators closed under adjoints has a joint spectral measure on the
Gelfand spectrum of the C⋆-algebra it generates.

## i. Overview

The closed ⋆-subalgebra of `B(H)` generated by a family of operators that commute with each other
and with each other's adjoints is a commutative C⋆-algebra `A`. By Gelfand duality it is the
algebra of continuous functions on its character space, so the inclusion `A → B(H)` is a unital
⋆-homomorphism from `C(X, ℂ)`, where `X` is the character space. Its spectral measure is the joint
spectral measure of the family: every operator of the family is the integral of its Gelfand
transform, and every operator commuting with the family commutes with the spectral measure.

## ii. Key results

- `CommutingStarFamily` : a commuting family of operators closed under adjoints.
- `CommutingStarFamily.algebra` : the commutative C⋆-algebra generated by the family.
- `CommutingStarFamily.spectralMeasure` : the joint spectral measure, on the character space.
- `CommutingStarFamily.boundedIntegral_gelfandTransform` : each operator of the algebra is the
  integral of its Gelfand transform.
- `CommutingStarFamily.spectralMeasure_commute` : the spectral measure commutes with every operator
  commuting with the family.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The commutative C⋆-algebra of a family
- B. The joint spectral measure

## iv. References

* None.

modules.title: Measurements in an orthonormal family
modules.doc:
The measurement of a quantum system on a complex Hilbert space in a finite orthonormal family.

## i. Overview

Let `b x`, for `x` in a finite type `X`, be orthonormal vectors of a complex Hilbert space `H`.
The rank-one projections `|b x⟩⟨b x|` are effects, and by Bessel's inequality their sum is at most
`1`. Adding the remainder `1 - ∑ x, |b x⟩⟨b x|` to the effect of a chosen outcome `x₀` gives a
measurement with outcomes `X`. On a unit vector `φ`, the outcome `x` has probability
`‖⟪b x, φ⟫‖ ^ 2`, plus `1 - ∑ y, ‖⟪b y, φ⟫‖ ^ 2` when `x = x₀`. In particular, if `φ` lies in the
span of the `b x`, the outcome `x` has probability `‖⟪b x, φ⟫‖ ^ 2`.

## ii. Key results

- `rankOneObservable` : the rank-one observable `|v⟩⟨v|`.
- `orthonormalObservable` : the observable of an outcome, `|b x⟩⟨b x|` plus the remainder on `x₀`.
- `sum_orthonormalObservable`, `orthonormalObservable_nonneg` : the outcome observables are
  positive and add up to `1`.
- `Measurement.ofOrthonormal` : the measurement in an orthonormal family.
- `Measurement.expectation_ofOrthonormal_singleton` : the Born rule for this measurement.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Rank-one observables
- B. The outcome observables
- C. The measurement and its Born rule

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.inner_rankOne_self_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma inner_rankOne_self_apply (v φ : H) :
    ⟪φ, rankOne ℂ v v φ⟫_ℂ = (‖⟪v, φ⟫_ℂ‖ ^ 2 : ℝ)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.inner_sum_rankOne_self_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma inner_sum_rankOne_self_apply (b : X → H) (φ : H) :
    ⟪φ, (∑ y, rankOne ℂ (b y) (b y)) φ⟫_ℂ = (∑ y, ‖⟪b y, φ⟫_ℂ‖ ^ 2 : ℝ)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.isPositive_one_sub_sum_rankOne
declarations.doc: By Bessel's inequality, `1 - ∑ y, |b y⟩⟨b y|` is positive for an orthonormal family `b`.
declarations.statement:
lemma isPositive_one_sub_sum_rankOne {b : X → H} (hb : Orthonormal ℂ b) :
    (1 - ∑ y, rankOne ℂ (b y) (b y)).IsPositive

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.rankOneObservable
declarations.doc: The rank-one observable `|v⟩⟨v|`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def rankOneObservable (v : H) : Observable (H →L[ℂ] H)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.coe_rankOneObservable
declarations.statement:
lemma coe_rankOneObservable (v : H) :
    (rankOneObservable v : H →L[ℂ] H) = rankOne ℂ v v

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.rankOneObservable_nonneg
declarations.doc: The rank-one observable `|v⟩⟨v|` is positive.
declarations.statement: lemma rankOneObservable_nonneg (v : H) : 0 ≤ rankOneObservable v

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.orthonormalObservable
declarations.doc:
The observable of the outcome `x` in the measurement in the family `b`: `|b x⟩⟨b x|`, plus
the remainder `1 - ∑ y, |b y⟩⟨b y|` when `x = x₀`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def orthonormalObservable (b : X → H) (x₀ x : X) : Observable (H →L[ℂ] H)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.coe_orthonormalObservable
declarations.doc: The operator underlying the observable of the outcome `x`.
declarations.statement:
lemma coe_orthonormalObservable (b : X → H) (x₀ x : X) :
    (orthonormalObservable b x₀ x : H →L[ℂ] H) =
      rankOne ℂ (b x) (b x) + if x = x₀ then 1 - ∑ y, rankOne ℂ (b y) (b y) else 0

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.sum_orthonormalObservable
declarations.doc: The outcome observables add up to `1`.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_orthonormalObservable (b : X → H) (x₀ : X) :
    ∑ x, orthonormalObservable b x₀ x = 1

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.orthonormalObservable_nonneg
declarations.doc: The outcome observables of an orthonormal family are positive.
declarations.statement:
lemma orthonormalObservable_nonneg {b : X → H} (hb : Orthonormal ℂ b) (x₀ x : X) :
    0 ≤ orthonormalObservable b x₀ x

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.orthonormalEffect
declarations.doc: The outcome effects of the measurement in an orthonormal family.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def orthonormalEffect {b : X → H} (hb : Orthonormal ℂ b) (x₀ x : X) :
    Effect (Observable (H →L[ℂ] H))

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.coe_orthonormalEffect
declarations.statement:
lemma coe_orthonormalEffect {b : X → H} (hb : Orthonormal ℂ b) (x₀ x : X) :
    (orthonormalEffect hb x₀ x : Observable (H →L[ℂ] H)) = orthonormalObservable b x₀ x

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Measurement.ofOrthonormal
declarations.doc:
The measurement in the orthonormal family `b`: the outcome `x` has effect `|b x⟩⟨b x|`, and
the outcome `x₀` also registers the orthogonal complement of the span of the family.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def ofOrthonormal {b : X → H} (hb : Orthonormal ℂ b) (x₀ : X) :
    Measurement X (Observable (H →L[ℂ] H))

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Measurement.coe_ofOrthonormal_singleton
declarations.doc:
The outcome `x` of the measurement in an orthonormal family has the observable
`orthonormalObservable b x₀ x`.
declarations.statement:
lemma coe_ofOrthonormal_singleton {b : X → H} (hb : Orthonormal ℂ b) (x₀ x : X)
    (hx : MeasurableSet {x}) :
    (ofOrthonormal hb x₀ {x} hx : Observable (H →L[ℂ] H)) = orthonormalObservable b x₀ x

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Measurement.expectation_ofOrthonormal_singleton
declarations.doc:
The Born rule for the measurement in an orthonormal family: on a unit vector `φ`, the
outcome `x` has probability `‖⟪b x, φ⟫‖ ^ 2`, plus `1 - ∑ y, ‖⟪b y, φ⟫‖ ^ 2` when `x = x₀`.
declarations.statement:
lemma expectation_ofOrthonormal_singleton [MeasurableSingletonClass X] {b : X → H}
    (hb : Orthonormal ℂ b) (x₀ : X) {φ : H} (hφ : ‖φ‖ = 1) (x : X) :
    (ofVec hφ)⟨ofOrthonormal hb x₀ {x} (measurableSet_singleton x)⟩ =
      ‖⟪b x, φ⟫_ℂ‖ ^ 2 + if x = x₀ then 1 - ∑ y, ‖⟪b y, φ⟫_ℂ‖ ^ 2 else 0

modules.title: Density operators
modules.doc:
A positive trace-one operator on a Hilbert space defines the state `x ↦ Tr (x ρ)`.

## i. Overview

A positive operator `ρ` with trace `1` defines the state `x ↦ Tr (x ρ)`. The trace here is the
linear-algebra trace, so this applies to finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces.

## ii. Key results

- `UnitalPositiveLinearMap.ofDensity` : the state of a density operator.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The state of a density operator

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. The state of a density operator

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.ofDensity
declarations.doc: A trace-one positive continuous linear map defines a state.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def ofDensity : 𝓢[ℂ, H →L[ℂ] H]

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.ofDensity_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma ofDensity_apply {ρ : H →L[ℂ] H} (hpos : 0 ≤ ρ)
    (hnorm : (ρ : H →ₗ[ℂ] H).trace ℂ H = 1) (x : H →L[ℂ] H) :
    ofDensity hpos hnorm x = (↑x * ↑ρ : H →ₗ[ℂ] H).trace ℂ H

modules.title: Uncertainty in density-operator states
modules.doc:
Expectation, covariance, variance and Robertson–Schrödinger for density-operator states.

## i. Overview

The state of a density operator `ρ` is a state on the C⋆-algebra of bounded operators, so the
uncertainty relations of C⋆-algebras apply to it. Its expectation, covariance and variance are
traces against `ρ`, and the state of a rank-one projection `|ψ⟩⟨ψ|` is the vector state of `ψ`.

## ii. Key results

- `UnitalPositiveLinearMap.expectation_ofDensity` : the expectation of `a` is `Re Tr(a ρ)`.
- `UnitalPositiveLinearMap.covariance_ofDensity`, `UnitalPositiveLinearMap.variance_ofDensity` :
  covariance and variance as traces.
- `UnitalPositiveLinearMap.robertson_schrodinger_ofDensity` : the Robertson–Schrödinger relation for
  density operators.
- `UnitalPositiveLinearMap.ofDensity_rankOne` : rank-one density operators give vector states.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Statistics of density states as traces
- B. Robertson–Schrödinger for density operators
- C. Vector states as rank-one density states

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. Statistics of density states as traces
## C. Vector states as rank-one density states

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.expectation_ofDensity
declarations.doc: The expectation of an observable in a density state is the real part of `Tr(a ρ)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma expectation_ofDensity (a : Observable (H →L[ℂ] H)) :
    (ofDensity hpos hnorm)⟨a⟩ = ((↑(a : H →L[ℂ] H) * ↑ρ : H →ₗ[ℂ] H).trace ℂ H).re

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.covariance_ofDensity
declarations.doc: The covariance in a density state is `Re Tr(δa δb ρ)` for the centered observables.
declarations.statement:
lemma covariance_ofDensity (a b : Observable (H →L[ℂ] H)) :
    covariance (ofDensity hpos hnorm) a b =
      ((↑((centered (ofDensity hpos hnorm) a : H →L[ℂ] H) *
        centered (ofDensity hpos hnorm) b) * ↑ρ : H →ₗ[ℂ] H).trace ℂ H).re

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.variance_ofDensity
declarations.doc: The variance in a density state is `Re Tr(δa² ρ)` for the centered observable.
declarations.statement:
lemma variance_ofDensity (a : Observable (H →L[ℂ] H)) :
    variance (ofDensity hpos hnorm) a =
      ((↑((centered (ofDensity hpos hnorm) a : H →L[ℂ] H) *
        centered (ofDensity hpos hnorm) a) * ↑ρ : H →ₗ[ℂ] H).trace ℂ H).re

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.robertson_schrodinger_ofDensity
declarations.doc:
**Robertson–Schrödinger relation for mixed states.** For a density operator `ρ` and
observables `a`, `b` with centered parts `δa`, `δb`,
`(Re Tr(δa δb ρ))² + (Re Tr(⁅a, b⁆ ρ))² ≤ Re Tr(δa² ρ) · Re Tr(δb² ρ)`,
where `⁅a, b⁆ = -(i/2)(ab - ba)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma robertson_schrodinger_ofDensity (a b : Observable (H →L[ℂ] H)) :
    ((↑((centered (ofDensity hpos hnorm) a : H →L[ℂ] H) *
        centered (ofDensity hpos hnorm) b) * ↑ρ : H →ₗ[ℂ] H).trace ℂ H).re ^ 2 +
      ((↑((⁅a, b⁆ : Observable (H →L[ℂ] H)) : H →L[ℂ] H) * ↑ρ : H →ₗ[ℂ] H).trace ℂ H).re ^ 2 ≤
      ((↑((centered (ofDensity hpos hnorm) a : H →L[ℂ] H) *
        centered (ofDensity hpos hnorm) a) * ↑ρ : H →ₗ[ℂ] H).trace ℂ H).re *
      ((↑((centered (ofDensity hpos hnorm) b : H →L[ℂ] H) *
        centered (ofDensity hpos hnorm) b) * ↑ρ : H →ₗ[ℂ] H).trace ℂ H).re

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.trace_rankOne_self
declarations.doc: For a unit vector `ψ`, the projection `|ψ⟩⟨ψ|` has trace one.
declarations.statement:
lemma trace_rankOne_self {ψ : H} (h : ‖ψ‖ = 1) :
    ((InnerProductSpace.rankOne ℂ ψ ψ : H →L[ℂ] H) : H →ₗ[ℂ] H).trace ℂ H = 1

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.ofDensity_rankOne
declarations.doc:
The density state of the projection `|ψ⟩⟨ψ|` is the vector state of `ψ`: pure states are
the rank-one mixed states.
declarations.statement:
lemma ofDensity_rankOne {ψ : H} (h : ‖ψ‖ = 1) :
    ofDensity (nonneg_iff_isPositive.mpr (InnerProductSpace.isPositive_rankOne_self ψ))
      (trace_rankOne_self h) = ofVec h

modules.title: Vector states
modules.doc:
A unit vector `ψ` defines the vector state `x ↦ ⟪ψ, x ψ⟫` on the bounded operators.

## i. Overview

A unit vector `ψ` defines the vector state `x ↦ ⟪ψ, x ψ⟫` on the bounded operators.
Multiplying `ψ` by a phase does not change its vector state, so two unit vectors with different
vector states are not parallel: their overlap has norm `‖⟪ψ, φ⟫‖ < 1`.

## ii. Key results

- `PositiveLinearMap.ofVec` : the positive functional of a vector.
- `UnitalPositiveLinearMap.ofVec` : the vector state of a unit vector.
- `UnitalPositiveLinearMap.ofVec_smul` : vector states do not see a global phase.
- `UnitalPositiveLinearMap.norm_inner_lt_one_of_ofVec_ne` : unit vectors with different vector
  states have overlap of norm less than one.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Vector states
- B. Phase invariance
- C. Example

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: PositiveLinearMap.ofVec
declarations.doc: The vector functional associated with `ψ`.
declarations.statement: def _root_.PositiveLinearMap.ofVec (ψ : H) : 𝓟[𝕜, H →L[𝕜] H]

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.ofVec
declarations.doc: The vector state associated with a unit vector.
declarations.statement: def UnitalPositiveLinearMap.ofVec {ψ : H} (h : ‖ψ‖ = 1) : 𝓢[𝕜, H →L[𝕜] H]

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.ofVec_apply
declarations.doc: Evaluation of a vector state is the corresponding quadratic form.
declarations.statement:
lemma UnitalPositiveLinearMap.ofVec_apply {ψ : H} (h : ‖ψ‖ = 1) (x : H →L[𝕜] H) :
    UnitalPositiveLinearMap.ofVec h x = ⟪ψ, x • ψ⟫_𝕜

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.ofVec_smul
declarations.doc: Vector states do not see a global phase: `ofVec (c • ψ) = ofVec ψ` for `‖c‖ = 1`.
declarations.statement:
lemma UnitalPositiveLinearMap.ofVec_smul {ψ : H} (h : ‖ψ‖ = 1) {c : 𝕜} (hc : ‖c‖ = 1)
    (h' : ‖c • ψ‖ = 1) :
    UnitalPositiveLinearMap.ofVec (𝕜 := 𝕜) h' = UnitalPositiveLinearMap.ofVec (𝕜 := 𝕜) h

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.norm_inner_lt_one_of_ofVec_ne
declarations.doc: Unit vectors with different vector states are not parallel: `‖⟪ψ, φ⟫‖ < 1`.
declarations.statement:
lemma UnitalPositiveLinearMap.norm_inner_lt_one_of_ofVec_ne {ψ φ : H} (hψ : ‖ψ‖ = 1)
    (hφ : ‖φ‖ = 1) (h : ofVec (𝕜 := 𝕜) hψ ≠ ofVec (𝕜 := 𝕜) hφ) : ‖⟪ψ, φ⟫_𝕜‖ < 1

modules.title: Uncertainty in vector states
modules.doc:
Variance and uncertainty defect in a vector state via fluctuation vectors `a ψ - ⟨a⟩ ψ`.

## i. Overview

In a vector state `ψ` the centered observable `a - ⟨a⟩` sends `ψ` to the fluctuation vector `a ψ -
⟨a⟩ ψ`. The variance is its squared norm, and the uncertainty defect of two observables is the
Cauchy–Schwarz defect of their fluctuation vectors.

For a family of observables, `Σ + iΩ` is the Gram matrix of the fluctuation vectors. Equality in
Robertson's relation `|det Ω| ≤ det Σ`, with `det Ω ≠ 0`, forces the kernel of this Gram matrix to
have at least half the dimension: the fluctuation vectors satisfy many linear relations.

## ii. Key results

- `UnitalPositiveLinearMap.apply_centered_mul_centered_ofVec` : the covariance matrix entry is the
  inner product of fluctuation vectors.
- `UnitalPositiveLinearMap.variance_ofVec` : the variance is the squared norm of the fluctuation
  vector.
- `UnitalPositiveLinearMap.centeredGramDefect_ofVec` : the uncertainty defect is `‖x‖² ‖y‖² - ‖⟪x,
  y⟫‖²`.
- `UnitalPositiveLinearMap.gram_fluctuation` : `Σ + iΩ` is the Gram matrix of the fluctuation
  vectors.
- `UnitalPositiveLinearMap.card_le_two_mul_finrank_ker_gram_fluctuation` : at equality in
  Robertson's relation for several observables, the fluctuation vectors satisfy at least half as
  many independent linear relations as there are observables.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Fluctuation vectors in vector states
- B. Equality in Robertson's relation for several observables

## iv. References

* H. P. Robertson, *An indeterminacy relation for several observables and its classical
  interpretation*, Phys. Rev. 46 (1934) 794.

sections.text: ## A. Fluctuation vectors in vector states
## B. Equality in Robertson's relation for several observables

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.centered_ofVec_apply
declarations.doc: The fluctuation vector `a ψ - ⟨a⟩ ψ` is the centered observable applied to `ψ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma centered_ofVec_apply (h : ‖ψ‖ = 1) (a : Observable (H →L[ℂ] H)) :
    (centered (ofVec h) a : H →L[ℂ] H) ψ = (a : H →L[ℂ] H) ψ - (ofVec h)⟨a⟩ • ψ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.apply_centered_mul_centered_ofVec
declarations.doc:
The state of a product of centered observables is the inner product of the two fluctuation
vectors.
declarations.statement:
lemma apply_centered_mul_centered_ofVec (h : ‖ψ‖ = 1) (a b : Observable (H →L[ℂ] H)) :
    ofVec h ((centered (ofVec h) a : H →L[ℂ] H) * (centered (ofVec h) b : H →L[ℂ] H)) =
      ⟪(a : H →L[ℂ] H) ψ - (ofVec h)⟨a⟩ • ψ, (b : H →L[ℂ] H) ψ - (ofVec h)⟨b⟩ • ψ⟫_ℂ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.variance_ofVec
declarations.doc: The variance in a vector state is the squared norm of the fluctuation vector.
declarations.statement:
lemma variance_ofVec (h : ‖ψ‖ = 1) (a : Observable (H →L[ℂ] H)) :
    variance (ofVec h) a = ‖(a : H →L[ℂ] H) ψ - (ofVec h)⟨a⟩ • ψ‖ ^ 2

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.centeredGramDefect_ofVec
declarations.doc:
The centered Gram defect of a vector state is the Cauchy–Schwarz defect of the two
fluctuation vectors.
declarations.statement:
lemma centeredGramDefect_ofVec (h : ‖ψ‖ = 1) (a b : Observable (H →L[ℂ] H)) :
    centeredGramDefect (ofVec h) a b =
      ‖(a : H →L[ℂ] H) ψ - (ofVec h)⟨a⟩ • ψ‖ ^ 2 * ‖(b : H →L[ℂ] H) ψ - (ofVec h)⟨b⟩ • ψ‖ ^ 2 -
        ‖⟪(a : H →L[ℂ] H) ψ - (ofVec h)⟨a⟩ • ψ, (b : H →L[ℂ] H) ψ - (ofVec h)⟨b⟩ • ψ⟫_ℂ‖ ^ 2

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.fluctuation
declarations.doc: The fluctuation vector `a ψ - ⟨a⟩ ψ` of an observable in a vector state.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def fluctuation (h : ‖ψ‖ = 1) (a : Observable (H →L[ℂ] H)) : H

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.gram_fluctuation
declarations.doc: In a vector state, `Σ + iΩ` is the Gram matrix of the fluctuation vectors.
declarations.statement:
lemma gram_fluctuation (h : ‖ψ‖ = 1) (a : ι → Observable (H →L[ℂ] H)) :
    gram ℂ (fun j => fluctuation h (a j)) =
      (covarianceMatrix (ofVec h) a).map ((↑) : ℝ → ℂ) +
        Complex.I • (bracketMatrix (ofVec h) a).map ((↑) : ℝ → ℂ)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.transpose_gram_fluctuation
declarations.doc: In a vector state, `Σ − iΩ` is the transpose of the Gram matrix of the fluctuation vectors.
declarations.statement:
lemma transpose_gram_fluctuation (h : ‖ψ‖ = 1) (a : ι → Observable (H →L[ℂ] H)) :
    (gram ℂ (fun j => fluctuation h (a j)))ᵀ =
      (covarianceMatrix (ofVec h) a).map ((↑) : ℝ → ℂ) -
        Complex.I • (bracketMatrix (ofVec h) a).map ((↑) : ℝ → ℂ)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.gram_mulVec_eq_zero_iff
declarations.doc: The kernel of a Gram matrix is the space of linear relations among the vectors.
declarations.statement:
lemma gram_mulVec_eq_zero_iff [Fintype ι] (v : ι → H) (c : ι → ℂ) :
    gram ℂ v *ᵥ c = 0 ↔ ∑ j, c j • v j = 0

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.card_le_two_mul_finrank_ker_gram_fluctuation
declarations.doc:
**Equality in Robertson's relation for several observables.** In a vector state with
`|det Ω| = det Σ ≠ 0`, the fluctuation vectors of the family satisfy linear relations
`∑ j, c j • (a_j ψ - ⟨a_j⟩ ψ) = 0` forming a space of at least half the size of the family.
declarations.statement:
lemma card_le_two_mul_finrank_ker_gram_fluctuation [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (h : ‖ψ‖ = 1)
    (a : ι → Observable (H →L[ℂ] H)) (hΩ : (bracketMatrix (ofVec h) a).det ≠ 0)
    (heq : |(bracketMatrix (ofVec h) a).det| = (covarianceMatrix (ofVec h) a).det) :
    Fintype.card ι ≤
      2 * Module.finrank ℂ (LinearMap.ker (gram ℂ fun j => fluctuation h (a j)).mulVecLin)

modules.title: The trace as a positive map
modules.doc:
The trace on bounded operators as a positive tracial functional, and the functional `Tr (x ρ)`.

## i. Overview

The linear-algebra trace is a positive tracial functional on the bounded operators; on a
finite-dimensional Hilbert space it is the usual trace. For positive `ρ`, `x ↦ Tr (x ρ)` is
positive.

## ii. Key results

- `PositiveLinearMap.conjugateₚ` : conjugation as a positive map.
- `ContinuousLinearMap.traceₚ` : the trace as a positive map.
- `ContinuousLinearMap.traceMulOpₚ` : `x ↦ Tr (x ρ)`.
- `ContinuousLinearMap.traceₚ_isTracial` : the trace is tracial.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Conjugation as a positive map
- B. The trace as a positive functional

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. Conjugation as a positive map
## B. The trace as a positive functional

declarations.doc: Conjugation `x ↦ c * x * star x`, as a positive linear map.
declarations.statement: def _root_.PositiveLinearMap.conjugateₚ (c : A) : A →ₚ[R] A

declarations.name: ContinuousLinearMap.traceₚ
declarations.doc: The trace on continuous linear maps, bundled as a positive linear map.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def traceₚ : (E →L[ℂ] E) →ₚ[ℂ] ℂ

declarations.doc: The trace is tracial.
declarations.statement: lemma traceₚ_isTracial : (traceₚ (E := E)).toLinearMap.IsTracial

declarations.name: ContinuousLinearMap.traceMulOpₚ
declarations.doc: The positive linear functional `x ↦ tr (√ρ * x * √ρ†)`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def traceMulOpₚ (ρ : E →L[ℂ] E) : (E →L[ℂ] E) →ₚ[ℂ] ℂ

declarations.name: ContinuousLinearMap.traceMulOpₚ_apply_of_nonneg
declarations.statement:
lemma traceMulOpₚ_apply_of_nonneg {ρ : E →L[ℂ] E} (h : 0 ≤ ρ) (x : E →L[ℂ] E) :
    ρ.traceMulOpₚ x = (↑x * ↑ρ : E →ₗ[ℂ] E).trace ℂ E

modules.title: The trace-class Banach space
modules.doc:
Trace-class operators form a Banach space under the trace norm.

## i. Overview

The trace-class operators form a Banach space `𝒮₁(H)` under the trace norm. The trace norm dominates
the operator norm, so an absolutely convergent series of trace-class operators converges in operator
norm. Its limit is trace class because the trace norm is lower semicontinuous along such limits,
which gives completeness.

## ii. Key results

- `TraceClass` : the trace-class operators with the trace norm.
- `opNorm_le_traceNorm` : the operator norm is at most the trace norm.
- `isTraceClass_of_tendsto_of_traceNorm_bounded` : an operator-norm limit of trace-class operators
  with bounded trace norms is trace class.
- `TraceClass.instCompleteSpace` : `𝒮₁(H)` is complete.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Arithmetic closure of `IsTraceClass`
- B. The trace-class submodule and Banach space

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## B. The trace-class submodule and Banach space

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.isTraceClass_zero
declarations.statement: lemma isTraceClass_zero : IsTraceClass (0 : H →L[ℂ] H)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.isTraceClass_smul
declarations.doc: Trace-class operators are closed under scalar multiplication.
declarations.statement:
lemma isTraceClass_smul (c : ℂ) {T : H →L[ℂ] H} (hT : IsTraceClass T) :
    IsTraceClass (c • T)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.isTraceClass_neg
declarations.statement: lemma isTraceClass_neg {T : H →L[ℂ] H} (hT : IsTraceClass T) : IsTraceClass (-T)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.traceNorm_zero
declarations.statement: lemma traceNorm_zero : traceNorm (0 : H →L[ℂ] H) isTraceClass_zero = 0

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.traceNorm_smul
declarations.doc: The trace norm is absolutely homogeneous: `‖c • T‖₁ = ‖c‖ ‖T‖₁`.
declarations.statement:
lemma traceNorm_smul (c : ℂ) {T : H →L[ℂ] H} (hT : IsTraceClass T) :
    traceNorm (c • T) (isTraceClass_smul c hT) = ‖c‖ * traceNorm T hT

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.traceNorm_neg
declarations.statement:
lemma traceNorm_neg {T : H →L[ℂ] H} (hT : IsTraceClass T) (hnegT : IsTraceClass (-T)) :
    traceNorm (-T) hnegT = traceNorm T hT

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.opNorm_le_traceNorm
declarations.doc:
**The operator norm is at most the trace norm.** With `S = √|T|`, Parseval and Cauchy–Schwarz
give `‖S x‖² ≤ ‖T‖₁ ‖x‖²`, and `‖T‖ = ‖S‖²`.
declarations.statement: lemma opNorm_le_traceNorm {T : H →L[ℂ] H} (hT : IsTraceClass T) : ‖T‖ ≤ traceNorm T hT

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.traceClassSubmodule
declarations.doc: The trace-class operators, as a submodule of the bounded operators.
declarations.statement:
def traceClassSubmodule (H : Type*) [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℂ H]
    [CompleteSpace H] : Submodule ℂ (H →L[ℂ] H)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.TraceClass
declarations.doc:
**The trace-class Banach space `𝒮₁(H)`**, normed by the trace norm. It is a `def` so that the
operator norm inherited from the ambient submodule is not found as an instance.
declarations.statement:
def TraceClass (H : Type*) [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [CompleteSpace H] :
    Type _

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.TraceClass.instAddCommGroup
declarations.statement: noncomputable instance instAddCommGroup : AddCommGroup (TraceClass H)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.TraceClass.instModule
declarations.statement: noncomputable instance instModule : Module ℂ (TraceClass H)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.TraceClass.mem_iff
declarations.statement: lemma mem_iff {T : H →L[ℂ] H} : T ∈ traceClassSubmodule H ↔ IsTraceClass T

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.TraceClass.isTraceClass_coe
declarations.doc: The trace-class witness carried by an element of `TraceClass H`.
declarations.statement: lemma isTraceClass_coe (T : TraceClass H) : IsTraceClass T.1

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.TraceClass.ofOperator
declarations.doc: The element of `TraceClass H` given by a trace-class operator.
declarations.statement: def ofOperator (T : H →L[ℂ] H) (hT : IsTraceClass T) : TraceClass H

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.TraceClass.ofOperator_coe
declarations.statement:
lemma ofOperator_coe (T : H →L[ℂ] H) (hT : IsTraceClass T) :
    (ofOperator T hT).1 = T

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.TraceClass.traceClassAddGroupNorm
declarations.doc:
**The trace norm as an `AddGroupNorm`** on the trace-class submodule: nonnegativity, the
triangle inequality (`traceNorm_add_le`), invariance under negation, and the zero-detection
property (via `opNorm_le_traceNorm`).
declarations.statement: noncomputable def traceClassAddGroupNorm : AddGroupNorm (TraceClass H)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.TraceClass.instNormedAddCommGroup
declarations.doc: **The trace-class Banach space's `NormedAddCommGroup` instance**, with norm `traceNorm`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable instance instNormedAddCommGroup : NormedAddCommGroup (TraceClass H)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.TraceClass.norm_eq_traceNorm
declarations.statement:
lemma norm_eq_traceNorm (T : TraceClass H) :
    ‖T‖ = traceNorm T.1 (isTraceClass_coe T)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.TraceClass.instNormedSpace
declarations.doc:
**The trace-class Banach space's `NormedSpace ℂ` instance**: scalar multiplication scales the
trace norm exactly, by `traceNorm_smul`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable instance instNormedSpace : NormedSpace ℂ (TraceClass H)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.TraceClass.isTraceClass_of_tendsto_of_traceNorm_bounded
declarations.doc:
**Lower semicontinuity of the trace norm.** An operator-norm limit of trace-class operators with
trace norms bounded by `C` is trace class, with trace norm at most `C`.
declarations.statement:
lemma isTraceClass_of_tendsto_of_traceNorm_bounded {Tn : ℕ → H →L[ℂ] H} {T : H →L[ℂ] H} {C : ℝ}
    (hTn : ∀ n, IsTraceClass (Tn n)) (hbound : ∀ n, traceNorm (Tn n) (hTn n) ≤ C)
    (htendsto : Tendsto Tn atTop (𝓝 T)) :
    ∃ hT : IsTraceClass T, traceNorm T hT ≤ C

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.TraceClass.instCompleteSpace
declarations.doc:
**The trace-class operators form a Banach space.** The partial sums of an absolutely convergent
series converge in operator norm, and lower semicontinuity bounds the trace norm of the tails.
declarations.statement: noncomputable instance instCompleteSpace : CompleteSpace (TraceClass H)

modules.title: Trace-class operators
modules.doc:
Defines trace-class operators, their trace norm and trace, and shows basis independence.

## i. Overview

For a bounded operator `T` on a complex Hilbert space, `|T| = √(T⋆T)` is its absolute value. `T` is
trace class when the diagonal sum `∑ᵢ ⟪eᵢ, |T| eᵢ⟫` converges for a Hilbert basis `{eᵢ}`. The sum is
the trace norm `‖T‖₁`, and `Tr T = ∑ᵢ ⟪eᵢ, T eᵢ⟫` is the trace.

For positive and self-adjoint operators the diagonal sums do not depend on the basis. The proof
writes `⟪eᵢ, S eᵢ⟫ = ‖√S eᵢ‖²`, expands in a second basis by Parseval and exchanges the two
nonnegative sums. In finite dimension the trace agrees with the linear-algebra trace.

A projection has finite multiplicity when it is trace class, that is, when its range is finite
dimensional.

## ii. Key results

- `IsTraceClass` : a bounded operator is trace class.
- `traceNorm`, `trace` : the trace norm and the trace.
- `summable_inner_abs_of_hilbertBasis` : trace class does not depend on the basis.
- `traceNorm_eq_of_hilbertBasis` : the trace norm does not depend on the basis.
- `trace_eq_of_hilbertBasis_of_isSelfAdjoint` : the trace of a self-adjoint trace-class operator
  does not depend on the basis.
- `trace_eq_sum_inner_hilbertBasis_of_finiteDimensional` : in finite dimension the linear-algebra
  trace is the diagonal sum.
- `HasFiniteMultiplicity` : a projection of finite rank.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Trace class
  - A.1. Basis independence
- B. Finite multiplicity

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text:
### A.1. Basis independence

The proofs use the square root of the functional calculus and Parseval's identity for Hilbert
bases.

Basis-independent trace for positive trace-class operators.

For a positive operator the absolute value is the operator itself.  Taking its continuous-
functional-calculus square root turns every diagonal coefficient into a squared norm, so the
Parseval double-sum theorem already proved above gives the same sum in every Hilbert basis.  This
is the positive case needed by density operators and does not use polar decomposition.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.IsTraceClass
declarations.doc:
**`T` is trace class**: `∑ᵢ ⟪eᵢ, |T| eᵢ⟫` converges for some Hilbert basis `{eᵢ}` of `H`
(`|T| := CFC.abs T`, Mathlib's continuous functional calculus absolute value `√(T⋆T)`). By the
basis-independence theorem below, "some" is equivalent to "every".
declarations.statement: def IsTraceClass (T : H →L[ℂ] H) : Prop

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.hasSum_norm_sq_inner_basis
declarations.doc: **Parseval's identity**: `∑ᵢ |⟪eᵢ, y⟫|² = ‖y‖²` for a Hilbert basis `{eᵢ}`.
declarations.statement:
lemma hasSum_norm_sq_inner_basis {w : Set H} (b : HilbertBasis w ℂ H) (y : H) :
    HasSum (fun i : w => ‖⟪b i, y⟫_ℂ‖ ^ 2) (‖y‖ ^ 2)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.hasSum_norm_sq_apply_of_selfAdjoint
declarations.doc: For self-adjoint `S`, the sum `∑ᵢ ‖S eᵢ‖²` does not depend on the Hilbert basis.
declarations.statement:
lemma hasSum_norm_sq_apply_of_selfAdjoint {S : H →L[ℂ] H} (hS : IsSelfAdjoint S)
    {w w' : Set H} (b : HilbertBasis w ℂ H) (c : HilbertBasis w' ℂ H)
    (hb : Summable (fun i : w => ‖S (b i)‖ ^ 2)) :
    HasSum (fun j : w' => ‖S (c j)‖ ^ 2) (∑' i : w, ‖S (b i)‖ ^ 2)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.summable_inner_abs_of_hilbertBasis
declarations.doc:
**Trace class does not depend on the basis**: the diagonal of `|T|` is summable in every Hilbert
basis.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.isTraceClass_iff
declarations.doc: An operator is trace class iff the diagonal of `|T|` is summable in every Hilbert basis.
declarations.statement:
lemma isTraceClass_iff {T : H →L[ℂ] H} :
    IsTraceClass T ↔
      ∀ (w : Set H) (b : HilbertBasis w ℂ H),
        Summable (fun i => (⟪b i, CFC.abs T (b i)⟫_ℂ).re)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.isTraceClass_of_finiteDimensional
declarations.doc: Every operator on a finite-dimensional Hilbert space is trace class.
declarations.statement:
lemma isTraceClass_of_finiteDimensional [FiniteDimensional ℂ H] (T : H →L[ℂ] H) :
    IsTraceClass T

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.trace_eq_sum_inner_hilbertBasis_of_finiteDimensional
declarations.doc: The ordinary finite-dimensional trace is the diagonal sum in any Hilbert basis.
declarations.statement:
lemma trace_eq_sum_inner_hilbertBasis_of_finiteDimensional
    [FiniteDimensional ℂ H] (T : H →L[ℂ] H) {w : Set H} (b : HilbertBasis w ℂ H) :
    LinearMap.trace ℂ H T.toLinearMap = ∑' i : w, ⟪b i, T (b i)⟫_ℂ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.traceNorm
declarations.doc:
The trace norm `‖T‖₁ := ∑ᵢ ⟪eᵢ, |T| eᵢ⟫`, computed via a chosen witness Hilbert basis (any
basis gives the same value, by `summable_inner_abs_of_hilbertBasis` — this definition just needs
*a* witness to compute with).
declarations.statement: def traceNorm (T : H →L[ℂ] H) (h : IsTraceClass T) : ℝ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.traceNorm_congr
declarations.doc:
The witness proof argument of `traceNorm` is immaterial.  This small lemma is useful when
transporting a trace-class operator through a construction that produces a new proof of the same
proposition.
declarations.statement:
lemma traceNorm_congr {T : H →L[ℂ] H} {h₁ h₂ : IsTraceClass T} :
    traceNorm T h₁ = traceNorm T h₂

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.trace
declarations.doc:
**The trace** `Tr T = ∑ᵢ ⟪eᵢ, T eᵢ⟫` of a trace-class operator, in the basis witnessing that it
is trace class.
declarations.statement: def trace (T : H →L[ℂ] H) (h : IsTraceClass T) : ℂ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.trace_congr
declarations.doc: The trace does not depend on the proof that the operator is trace class.
declarations.statement:
lemma trace_congr {T : H →L[ℂ] H} {h₁ h₂ : IsTraceClass T} :
    trace T h₁ = trace T h₂

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.traceNorm_eq_of_hilbertBasis
declarations.doc:
The trace norm is independent of the witness basis used in `IsTraceClass`.  This is the
strong form of `summable_inner_abs_of_hilbertBasis`: the square-root/Parseval argument identifies
the actual sums, not merely their convergence.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.real_inner_nonneg_of_nonneg
declarations.statement:
lemma real_inner_nonneg_of_nonneg {T : H →L[ℂ] H} (hT : 0 ≤ T) (x : H) :
    0 ≤ (⟪x, T x⟫_ℂ).re

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.traceNorm_nonneg
declarations.doc:
The trace norm is nonnegative.  This is exposed separately from its basis-independence result
so norm estimates can use it without unpacking the chosen Hilbert-basis witness.
declarations.statement: lemma traceNorm_nonneg (T : H →L[ℂ] H) (h : IsTraceClass T) : 0 ≤ traceNorm T h

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.real_inner_mono_of_le
declarations.statement:
lemma real_inner_mono_of_le {P Q : H →L[ℂ] H} (hPQ : P ≤ Q) (x : H) :
    (⟪x, P x⟫_ℂ).re ≤ (⟪x, Q x⟫_ℂ).re

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.isTraceClass_posPart_of_isSelfAdjoint
declarations.statement:
lemma isTraceClass_posPart_of_isSelfAdjoint {T : H →L[ℂ] H} (hT : IsSelfAdjoint T)
    (h : IsTraceClass T) : IsTraceClass T⁺

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.isTraceClass_negPart_of_isSelfAdjoint
declarations.statement:
lemma isTraceClass_negPart_of_isSelfAdjoint {T : H →L[ℂ] H} (hT : IsSelfAdjoint T)
    (h : IsTraceClass T) : IsTraceClass T⁻

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.summable_inner_of_nonneg
declarations.statement:
lemma summable_inner_of_nonneg {T : H →L[ℂ] H} (hT : 0 ≤ T) (h : IsTraceClass T)
    {w : Set H} (b : HilbertBasis w ℂ H) :
    Summable (fun i => ⟪b i, T (b i)⟫_ℂ)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.trace_eq_of_hilbertBasis_of_nonneg
declarations.statement:
lemma trace_eq_of_hilbertBasis_of_nonneg {T : H →L[ℂ] H} (hT : 0 ≤ T)
    (h : IsTraceClass T) {w : Set H} (b : HilbertBasis w ℂ H) :
    trace T h = ∑' i, ⟪b i, T (b i)⟫_ℂ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.trace_eq_of_hilbertBasis_of_isSelfAdjoint
declarations.doc:
Basis-independent trace for self-adjoint trace-class operators.  The proof reduces to the
positive theorem through the continuous-functional-calculus decomposition `T = T⁺ - T⁻`; no
polar decomposition is needed for this self-adjoint case.
declarations.statement:
lemma trace_eq_of_hilbertBasis_of_isSelfAdjoint {T : H →L[ℂ] H} (hT : IsSelfAdjoint T)
    (h : IsTraceClass T) {w : Set H} (b : HilbertBasis w ℂ H) :
    trace T h = ∑' i, ⟪b i, T (b i)⟫_ℂ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.HasFiniteMultiplicity
declarations.doc: A projection has finite multiplicity when it is trace class.
declarations.statement: def HasFiniteMultiplicity (p : H →L[ℂ] H) : Prop

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.HasFiniteMultiplicity.finiteDimensional_range
declarations.doc: A projection of finite multiplicity has finite-dimensional range.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.HasFiniteMultiplicity.trace_eq_finrank_range
declarations.doc:
A finite-multiplicity projection has the expected trace.  The basis calculation is finite-rank:
extend an orthonormal basis of the range to one of `H`; the projection vanishes on the complementary
basis vectors and is the identity on the range basis.
declarations.statement:
lemma HasFiniteMultiplicity.trace_eq_finrank_range
    {p : H →L[ℂ] H} (hp : HasFiniteMultiplicity p) :
    trace p hp.2 = (Module.finrank ℂ (LinearMap.range p.toLinearMap) : ℂ)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.HasFiniteMultiplicity.trace_eq_finrank_range_of_finiteDimensional
declarations.doc: In finite dimension, the trace of a projection is the dimension of its range.
declarations.statement:
lemma HasFiniteMultiplicity.trace_eq_finrank_range_of_finiteDimensional
    [FiniteDimensional ℂ H] {p : H →L[ℂ] H} (hp : HasFiniteMultiplicity p) :
    trace p hp.2 = (Module.finrank ℂ (LinearMap.range p.toLinearMap) : ℂ)

modules.title: Basis independence of the trace
modules.doc:
The trace of every trace-class operator is an absolutely summable, basis-independent sum.

## i. Overview

For a trace-class operator `T`, `√|T|` is Hilbert–Schmidt, so the diagonal of `T = (U √|T|) √|T|` is
a diagonal of a product of Hilbert–Schmidt operators. This shows that the trace of every trace-class
operator is an absolutely convergent sum whose value does not depend on the basis.

## ii. Key results

- `isHilbertSchmidt_sqrt_abs_of_isTraceClass` : `√|T|` is Hilbert–Schmidt.
- `summable_trace_diagonal_of_isTraceClass` : the diagonal of a trace-class operator is absolutely
  summable.
- `trace_eq_of_hilbertBasis` : the trace does not depend on the basis.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The Hilbert–Schmidt square root of `|T|`
- B. Basis independence of the trace

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. The Hilbert–Schmidt square root of `|T|`
## B. Basis independence of the trace

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.sqrt_abs_diagonal_eq_norm_sq
declarations.statement:
lemma sqrt_abs_diagonal_eq_norm_sq {T : H →L[ℂ] H} {w : Set H} (b : HilbertBasis w ℂ H)
    (i : w) :
    (⟪b i, CFC.abs T (b i)⟫_ℂ).re = ‖(CFC.sqrt (CFC.abs T)) (b i)‖ ^ 2

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.isHilbertSchmidt_sqrt_abs_of_isTraceClass
declarations.statement:
lemma isHilbertSchmidt_sqrt_abs_of_isTraceClass {T : H →L[ℂ] H} (hT : IsTraceClass T) :
    IsHilbertSchmidt (CFC.sqrt (CFC.abs T))

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.summable_trace_diagonal_of_isTraceClass
declarations.statement:
lemma summable_trace_diagonal_of_isTraceClass {T : H →L[ℂ] H} (hT : IsTraceClass T)
    {w : Set H} (b : HilbertBasis w ℂ H) :
    Summable (fun i : w => ⟪b i, T (b i)⟫_ℂ)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.tsum_diagonal_eq_of_isTraceClass
declarations.statement:
lemma tsum_diagonal_eq_of_isTraceClass {T : H →L[ℂ] H} (hT : IsTraceClass T)
    {w w' : Set H} (b : HilbertBasis w ℂ H) (c : HilbertBasis w' ℂ H) :
    (∑' i : w, ⟪b i, T (b i)⟫_ℂ) = ∑' j : w', ⟪c j, T (c j)⟫_ℂ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.trace_eq_of_hilbertBasis_unconditional
ProbabilisticTheory.trace_eq_of_hilbertBasis
declarations.doc:
**Basis-independent trace evaluation for an arbitrary trace-class operator.** Unlike the
witness-basis definition, this requires no self-adjointness/positivity hypothesis.

modules.title: Products of Hilbert–Schmidt operators
modules.doc:
Products of Hilbert–Schmidt operators are trace class; trace class is a ⋆-closed ideal.

## i. Overview

A product of two Hilbert–Schmidt operators is trace class. Every trace-class operator `T` factors as
`(U √|T|) √|T|` with both factors Hilbert–Schmidt, so trace-class operators form a two-sided ideal
closed under sums and adjoints.

## ii. Key results

- `isTraceClass_mul_of_isHilbertSchmidt` : a product of two Hilbert–Schmidt operators is trace
  class.
- `isTraceClass_add` : trace-class operators are closed under addition.
- `isTraceClass_mul_mul` : trace-class operators form a two-sided ideal.
- `isTraceClass_star` : trace-class operators are closed under the adjoint.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Products of Hilbert–Schmidt operators
- B. Closure properties of trace class

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## B. Closure properties of trace class

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.diagonal_star_mul_eq_inner
declarations.doc:
The diagonal of `star W * (R * S)` (for any contraction `W`) unwinds to a Hilbert–Schmidt
Cauchy–Schwarz pairing. This is the pointwise identity feeding both the master product theorem and
the general additive/ideal closure results below.
declarations.statement:
lemma diagonal_star_mul_eq_inner {R S W : H →L[ℂ] H} {w : Set H} (b : HilbertBasis w ℂ H)
    (i : w) :
    ⟪b i, (star W * (R * S)) (b i)⟫_ℂ = ⟪(ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint R * W) (b i), S (b i)⟫_ℂ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.isTraceClass_mul_of_isHilbertSchmidt
declarations.doc: **A product of two Hilbert–Schmidt operators is trace class.**
declarations.statement:
lemma isTraceClass_mul_of_isHilbertSchmidt {R S : H →L[ℂ] H}
    (hR : IsHilbertSchmidt R) (hS : IsHilbertSchmidt S) : IsTraceClass (R * S)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.isHilbertSchmidt_polarFactor_mul_sqrt_abs_and_sqrt_abs
declarations.doc:
Every trace-class operator factors as a product of two Hilbert–Schmidt operators: the polar
factor composed with the Hilbert–Schmidt square root of `|T|`, and that same square root again.
declarations.statement:
lemma isHilbertSchmidt_polarFactor_mul_sqrt_abs_and_sqrt_abs {T : H →L[ℂ] H}
    (hT : IsTraceClass T) :
    IsHilbertSchmidt (Polar.polarFactor T * CFC.sqrt (CFC.abs T)) ∧
      IsHilbertSchmidt (CFC.sqrt (CFC.abs T)) ∧
      Polar.polarFactor T * CFC.sqrt (CFC.abs T) * CFC.sqrt (CFC.abs T) = T

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.isTraceClass_add
declarations.doc: Trace-class operators are closed under addition.
declarations.statement:
lemma isTraceClass_add {T T' : H →L[ℂ] H} (hT : IsTraceClass T) (hT' : IsTraceClass T') :
    IsTraceClass (T + T')

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.isTraceClass_mul_mul
declarations.doc:
**Trace-class operators form a two-sided ideal**: `A T B` is trace class for trace-class `T` and
bounded `A`, `B`.
declarations.statement:
lemma isTraceClass_mul_mul {A B T : H →L[ℂ] H} (hT : IsTraceClass T) :
    IsTraceClass (A * T * B)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.isTraceClass_star
declarations.doc: Taking the adjoint preserves trace class.
declarations.statement: lemma isTraceClass_star {T : H →L[ℂ] H} (hT : IsTraceClass T) : IsTraceClass (star T)

modules.title: Hilbert–Schmidt operators
modules.doc:
Hilbert–Schmidt operators: a ⋆-closed two-sided ideal whose products have summable diagonals.

## i. Overview

A bounded operator `S` is Hilbert–Schmidt when `∑ᵢ ‖S eᵢ‖²` converges for a Hilbert basis `{eᵢ}`.
Hilbert–Schmidt operators form a two-sided ideal closed under the adjoint, `S⋆S` is trace class for
Hilbert–Schmidt `S`, and a product of two Hilbert–Schmidt operators has an absolutely summable
diagonal in every basis, with the diagonal sum symmetric in the two factors.

## ii. Key results

- `IsHilbertSchmidt` : a bounded operator is Hilbert–Schmidt.
- `isHilbertSchmidt_add`, `isHilbertSchmidt_star` : closure under sums and adjoints.
- `isHilbertSchmidt_mul_left`, `isHilbertSchmidt_mul_right` : the ideal property.
- `isTraceClass_star_mul_self_of_isHilbertSchmidt` : `S⋆S` is trace class.
- `summable_diagonal_of_hilbertSchmidt` : the diagonal of a product of two Hilbert–Schmidt operators
  is absolutely summable.
- `tsum_diagonal_mul_eq_tsum_diagonal_swap` : the diagonal sums of `R S` and `S R` agree.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Elementary algebraic closure
- B. Cauchy–Schwarz estimates on Hilbert–Schmidt diagonals
- C. Quantitative right-multiplication estimate

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## B. Cauchy–Schwarz estimates on Hilbert–Schmidt diagonals

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.HilbertSchmidt.IsHilbertSchmidt
declarations.doc:
A bounded operator is Hilbert–Schmidt when its squared norm sum is summable in one Hilbert
basis. The basis-independence theorem below shows this existential definition is equivalent to
using any basis.
declarations.statement: def IsHilbertSchmidt (S : H →L[ℂ] H) : Prop

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.HilbertSchmidt.hasSum_norm_sq_apply_eq_adjoint
declarations.doc:
The Hilbert–Schmidt square sum of `S` in one basis equals the square sum of `S⋆` in a second
basis. This is the nonnegative double-sum identity; the usual basis-independence statement follows
by applying it twice.
declarations.statement:
lemma hasSum_norm_sq_apply_eq_adjoint {S : H →L[ℂ] H}
    {w w' : Set H} (b : HilbertBasis w ℂ H) (c : HilbertBasis w' ℂ H)
    (hb : Summable (fun i : w => ‖S (b i)‖ ^ 2)) :
    HasSum (fun j : w' => ‖(ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint S) (c j)‖ ^ 2)
      (∑' i : w, ‖S (b i)‖ ^ 2)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.HilbertSchmidt.summable_norm_sq_adjoint_of_summable_norm_sq
declarations.statement:
lemma summable_norm_sq_adjoint_of_summable_norm_sq {S : H →L[ℂ] H}
    {w : Set H} (b : HilbertBasis w ℂ H)
    (hb : Summable (fun i : w => ‖S (b i)‖ ^ 2)) :
    Summable (fun i : w => ‖(ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint S) (b i)‖ ^ 2)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.HilbertSchmidt.hasSum_norm_sq_apply_of_basis
declarations.statement:
lemma hasSum_norm_sq_apply_of_basis {S : H →L[ℂ] H} {w w' : Set H}
    (b : HilbertBasis w ℂ H) (c : HilbertBasis w' ℂ H)
    (hb : Summable (fun i : w => ‖S (b i)‖ ^ 2)) :
    HasSum (fun j : w' => ‖S (c j)‖ ^ 2) (∑' i : w, ‖S (b i)‖ ^ 2)
