    (hS : IsHilbertSchmidt S) : IsTraceClass (S * star S)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.HilbertSchmidt.holder_two_two
declarations.statement: lemma holder_two_two : (2 : ℝ).HolderConjugate 2

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.HilbertSchmidt.tsum_mul_le_sqrt_mul_sqrt
declarations.doc: The real `ℓ²` Cauchy–Schwarz estimate, in the tsum form needed for operator diagonal bounds.
declarations.statement:
lemma tsum_mul_le_sqrt_mul_sqrt {w : Set H} {f g : w → ℝ}
    (hf : Summable (fun i => f i ^ 2)) (hg : Summable (fun i => g i ^ 2))
    (hf_nonneg : ∀ i, 0 ≤ f i) (hg_nonneg : ∀ i, 0 ≤ g i) :
    ∑' i : w, f i * g i ≤ Real.sqrt (∑' i : w, f i ^ 2) * Real.sqrt (∑' i : w, g i ^ 2)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.HilbertSchmidt.summable_norm_mul_of_square_sums
declarations.statement:
lemma summable_norm_mul_of_square_sums {w : Set H}
    (f g : w → ℝ) (hf : Summable (fun i => f i ^ 2)) (hg : Summable (fun i => g i ^ 2))
    (hf_nonneg : ∀ i, 0 ≤ f i) (hg_nonneg : ∀ i, 0 ≤ g i) :
    Summable (fun i => f i * g i)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.HilbertSchmidt.tsum_norm_inner_mul_inner_le
declarations.statement:
lemma tsum_norm_inner_mul_inner_le {w : Set H} (b : HilbertBasis w ℂ H) (x y : H) :
    ∑' i : w, ‖⟪x, b i⟫_ℂ‖ * ‖⟪b i, y⟫_ℂ‖ ≤ ‖x‖ * ‖y‖

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.HilbertSchmidt.summable_norm_inner_mul_inner
declarations.statement:
lemma summable_norm_inner_mul_inner {w : Set H} (b : HilbertBasis w ℂ H) (x y : H) :
    Summable (fun i : w => ‖⟪x, b i⟫_ℂ‖ * ‖⟪b i, y⟫_ℂ‖)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.HilbertSchmidt.summable_diagonal_of_hilbertSchmidt
declarations.doc:
The diagonal coefficients of a product of two Hilbert–Schmidt operators are absolutely
summable.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.HilbertSchmidt.summable_matrix_of_hilbertSchmidt
declarations.statement:
lemma summable_matrix_of_hilbertSchmidt {R S : H →L[ℂ] H}
    {w w' : Set H} (b : HilbertBasis w ℂ H) (c : HilbertBasis w' ℂ H)
    (hR : IsHilbertSchmidt R) (hS : IsHilbertSchmidt S) :
    Summable (Function.uncurry (fun (i : w) (j : w') =>
      ⟪(ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint R) (b i), c j⟫_ℂ * ⟪c j, S (b i)⟫_ℂ))

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.HilbertSchmidt.hasSum_matrix_row_of_hilbertSchmidt
declarations.statement:
lemma hasSum_matrix_row_of_hilbertSchmidt {R S : H →L[ℂ] H}
    {w w' : Set H} (b : HilbertBasis w ℂ H) (c : HilbertBasis w' ℂ H) (i : w) :
    HasSum (fun j : w' => ⟪(ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint R) (b i), c j⟫_ℂ * ⟪c j, S (b i)⟫_ℂ)
      ⟪b i, (R * S) (b i)⟫_ℂ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.HilbertSchmidt.hasSum_matrix_col_of_hilbertSchmidt
declarations.statement:
lemma hasSum_matrix_col_of_hilbertSchmidt {R S : H →L[ℂ] H}
    {w w' : Set H} (b : HilbertBasis w ℂ H) (c : HilbertBasis w' ℂ H) (j : w') :
    HasSum (fun i : w => ⟪(ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint R) (b i), c j⟫_ℂ * ⟪c j, S (b i)⟫_ℂ)
      ⟪c j, (S * R) (c j)⟫_ℂ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.HilbertSchmidt.tsum_diagonal_mul_eq_tsum_diagonal_swap
declarations.doc:
For Hilbert–Schmidt `R` and `S`, the diagonal sum of `R S` in one basis equals the diagonal sum
of `S R` in any other.
declarations.statement:
lemma tsum_diagonal_mul_eq_tsum_diagonal_swap {R S : H →L[ℂ] H}
    {w w' : Set H} (b : HilbertBasis w ℂ H) (c : HilbertBasis w' ℂ H)
    (hR : IsHilbertSchmidt R) (hS : IsHilbertSchmidt S) :
    (∑' i : w, ⟪b i, (R * S) (b i)⟫_ℂ) = ∑' j : w', ⟪c j, (S * R) (c j)⟫_ℂ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.HilbertSchmidt.tsum_norm_sq_mul_right_le_of_opNorm_le_one
declarations.doc:
**Quantitative right-multiplication-by-a-contraction bound**: for `X` and a contraction `W`,
the Hilbert–Schmidt square sum of `X * W` never exceeds that of `X` itself, in the same basis.
declarations.statement:
lemma tsum_norm_sq_mul_right_le_of_opNorm_le_one {X W : H →L[ℂ] H} (hW : ‖W‖ ≤ 1)
    (hX : IsHilbertSchmidt X) {w : Set H} (b : HilbertBasis w ℂ H) :
    (∑' i : w, ‖(X * W) (b i)‖ ^ 2) ≤ ∑' i : w, ‖X (b i)‖ ^ 2

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.HilbertSchmidt.tsum_norm_sq_mul_right_le_of_selfAdjoint
declarations.doc: Right multiplication by a self-adjoint contraction does not increase the Hilbert–Schmidt sum.
declarations.statement:
lemma tsum_norm_sq_mul_right_le_of_selfAdjoint {S A : H →L[ℂ] H}
    (hSself : IsSelfAdjoint S) (hS : IsHilbertSchmidt S)
    {w w' : Set H} (b : HilbertBasis w ℂ H) (c : HilbertBasis w' ℂ H) :
    (∑' i : w', ‖(S * A) (c i)‖ ^ 2) ≤ ‖A‖ ^ 2 * (∑' j : w, ‖S (b j)‖ ^ 2)

modules.title: Trace-norm estimates
modules.doc:
The duality bound for the trace norm, its subadditivity and the two-sided ideal estimate.

## i. Overview

For a trace-class operator `A`, a contraction `W` and a Hilbert basis `{eᵢ}`, `∑ᵢ ‖⟪W eᵢ, A eᵢ⟫‖ ≤
‖A‖₁`, with equality for the polar factor. From this the trace norm is subadditive and satisfies the
two-sided ideal estimate `‖B T C‖₁ ≤ ‖B‖ ‖T‖₁ ‖C‖`.

## ii. Key results

- `tsum_norm_inner_contraction_le_traceNorm` : the duality bound against contractions.
- `traceNorm_eq_tsum_norm_inner_polarFactor` : the bound is attained at the polar factor.
- `traceNorm_add_le` : the trace norm is subadditive.
- `traceNorm_mul_mul_le` : the two-sided ideal estimate.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The duality bound against contractions
- B. Attainment at the polar factor and subadditivity
- C. The two-sided ideal estimate

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. The duality bound against contractions
## B. Attainment at the polar factor and subadditivity

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.traceNorm_transport
declarations.doc: The trace norm of an operator only depends on the operator, not on the trace-class witness.
declarations.statement:
lemma traceNorm_transport {X Y : H →L[ℂ] H} (hEq : X = Y) (hX : IsTraceClass X) :
    traceNorm X hX = traceNorm Y (hEq ▸ hX)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.tsum_sqrt_abs_norm_sq_eq_traceNorm
declarations.doc: The Hilbert–Schmidt square sum of `√|A|` computes the trace norm, in every basis.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.summable_norm_inner_contraction_of_isTraceClass
declarations.doc:
The contraction pairing `i ↦ ⟪W eᵢ, A eᵢ⟫` is absolutely summable, for trace-class `A` and any
contraction `W`.
declarations.statement:
lemma summable_norm_inner_contraction_of_isTraceClass {A W : H →L[ℂ] H} (hA : IsTraceClass A)
    (hW : ‖W‖ ≤ 1) {w : Set H} (b : HilbertBasis w ℂ H) :
    Summable (fun i : w => ‖⟪W (b i), A (b i)⟫_ℂ‖)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.tsum_norm_inner_contraction_le_traceNorm
declarations.doc:
**The duality bound**: for trace-class `A`, any contraction `W`, and any basis, the pairing
`∑ᵢ ‖⟪W eᵢ, A eᵢ⟫‖` never exceeds `‖A‖₁`. This is the single quantitative estimate feeding
subadditivity of the trace norm, and the general two-sided ideal estimate below.
declarations.statement:
lemma tsum_norm_inner_contraction_le_traceNorm {A W : H →L[ℂ] H} (hA : IsTraceClass A)
    (hW : ‖W‖ ≤ 1) {w : Set H} (b : HilbertBasis w ℂ H) :
    (∑' i : w, ‖⟪W (b i), A (b i)⟫_ℂ‖) ≤ traceNorm A hA

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.traceNorm_eq_tsum_norm_inner_polarFactor
declarations.doc:
The trace-norm diagonal in the basis `b` equals the norm-diagonal pairing against `T`'s own
polar factor: `⟪eᵢ, |T| eᵢ⟫ = ⟪(polarFactor T) eᵢ, T eᵢ⟫` exactly, and the latter is already a
nonnegative real.
declarations.statement:
lemma traceNorm_eq_tsum_norm_inner_polarFactor {T : H →L[ℂ] H} (hT : IsTraceClass T)
    {w : Set H} (b : HilbertBasis w ℂ H) :
    traceNorm T hT = ∑' i : w, ‖⟪Polar.polarFactor T (b i), T (b i)⟫_ℂ‖

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.traceNorm_add_le
declarations.doc: **The trace norm is subadditive.**
declarations.statement:
lemma traceNorm_add_le {T T' : H →L[ℂ] H} (hT : IsTraceClass T) (hT' : IsTraceClass T')
    (hTT' : IsTraceClass (T + T')) :
    traceNorm (T + T') hTT' ≤ traceNorm T hT + traceNorm T' hT'

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.traceNorm_mul_le_of_isHilbertSchmidt
declarations.doc:
**Quantitative master lemma**: the trace norm of a product of two Hilbert–Schmidt operators is
bounded by the product of their Hilbert–Schmidt square-root sums, in any common basis.
declarations.statement:
lemma traceNorm_mul_le_of_isHilbertSchmidt {R S : H →L[ℂ] H} (hR : IsHilbertSchmidt R)
    (hS : IsHilbertSchmidt S) (hRS : IsTraceClass (R * S)) {w : Set H} (b : HilbertBasis w ℂ H) :
    traceNorm (R * S) hRS ≤
      Real.sqrt (∑' i : w, ‖R (b i)‖ ^ 2) * Real.sqrt (∑' i : w, ‖S (b i)‖ ^ 2)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.traceNorm_mul_mul_le
declarations.doc: **The two-sided ideal estimate**: `‖A T B‖₁ ≤ ‖A‖ ‖T‖₁ ‖B‖`.
declarations.statement:
lemma traceNorm_mul_mul_le {A B T : H →L[ℂ] H} (hT : IsTraceClass T)
    (hABT : IsTraceClass (A * T * B)) :
    traceNorm (A * T * B) hABT ≤ ‖A‖ * traceNorm T hT * ‖B‖

modules.title: The trace pairing
modules.doc:
The trace pairing `T ↦ Tr (A T)` as a bounded functional on trace-class operators.

## i. Overview

A bounded operator `A` defines a bounded functional `T ↦ Tr (A T)` on the trace-class operators, of
norm at most `‖A‖`. The assignment `A ↦ Tr (A ·)` is itself a bounded linear map from bounded
operators to the dual of `𝒮₁(H)`.

## ii. Key results

- `norm_trace_le` : `‖Tr T‖ ≤ ‖T‖₁`.
- `TraceClass.tracePairing` : the functional `T ↦ Tr (A T)`.
- `TraceClass.norm_tracePairing_le` : its norm is at most `‖A‖`.
- `TraceClass.tracePairingContinuousLinearMap` : the trace pairing as a bounded linear map into the
  dual.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Trace bounds and transport
- B. The trace pairing at a fixed operator
- C. The trace pairing as a bounded linear map

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## B. The trace pairing at a fixed operator
## C. The trace pairing as a bounded linear map

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.TraceClass.norm_trace_le
declarations.doc:
**The trace is dominated by the trace norm**, for an arbitrary (not necessarily positive or
self-adjoint) trace-class operator. Proved from the duality bound
`tsum_norm_inner_contraction_le_traceNorm` at the identity contraction.
declarations.statement: lemma norm_trace_le {T : H →L[ℂ] H} (hT : IsTraceClass T) : ‖trace T hT‖ ≤ traceNorm T hT

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.TraceClass.trace_transport
declarations.doc:
Transporting `trace` across an equality of the underlying operator. Needed because `rw` cannot
rewrite `trace`'s operator argument directly (the motive depends on the witness proof).
declarations.statement:
lemma trace_transport {X Y : H →L[ℂ] H} (hEq : X = Y) (hX : IsTraceClass X) :
    trace X hX = trace Y (hEq ▸ hX)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.TraceClass.isTraceClass_mul_coe
declarations.doc:
Every trace-class `T.1` sandwiched by a bounded `A` on the left (and `1` on the right) is
trace class: the general two-sided ideal estimate, specialized.
declarations.statement: lemma isTraceClass_mul_coe (A : H →L[ℂ] H) (T : TraceClass H) : IsTraceClass (A * T.1)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.TraceClass.tracePairingLinearMap
declarations.doc:
**The trace pairing at a fixed bounded operator `A`**, `T ↦ Tr(A T)`, as a `ℂ`-linear map on
the trace-class Banach space.
declarations.statement: def tracePairingLinearMap (A : H →L[ℂ] H) : TraceClass H →ₗ[ℂ] ℂ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.TraceClass.tracePairingLinearMap_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma tracePairingLinearMap_apply (A : H →L[ℂ] H) (T : TraceClass H) :
    tracePairingLinearMap A T = trace (A * T.1) (isTraceClass_mul_coe A T)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.TraceClass.norm_tracePairingLinearMap_apply_le
declarations.doc:
**The trace pairing is bounded**: `‖φ_A T‖ ≤ ‖A‖ ‖T‖₁`. Combines `norm_trace_le` with the
general two-sided ideal norm estimate `traceNorm_mul_mul_le`.
declarations.statement:
lemma norm_tracePairingLinearMap_apply_le (A : H →L[ℂ] H) (T : TraceClass H) :
    ‖tracePairingLinearMap A T‖ ≤ ‖A‖ * ‖T‖

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.TraceClass.tracePairing
declarations.doc:
**The trace pairing `T ↦ Tr(A T)`, as a continuous (bounded) linear functional** on the
trace-class Banach space.
declarations.statement: def tracePairing (A : H →L[ℂ] H) : TraceClass H →L[ℂ] ℂ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.TraceClass.tracePairing_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma tracePairing_apply (A : H →L[ℂ] H) (T : TraceClass H) :
    tracePairing A T = trace (A * T.1) (isTraceClass_mul_coe A T)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.TraceClass.norm_tracePairing_le
declarations.doc: The trace pairing's operator norm is bounded by `‖A‖`.
declarations.statement: lemma norm_tracePairing_le (A : H →L[ℂ] H) : ‖tracePairing A‖ ≤ ‖A‖

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.TraceClass.tracePairingLinear
declarations.doc:
**`A ↦ φ_A` is itself a `ℂ`-linear map** from `H →L[ℂ] H` into the strong dual of the
trace-class Banach space.
declarations.statement: def tracePairingLinear : (H →L[ℂ] H) →ₗ[ℂ] (TraceClass H →L[ℂ] ℂ)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.TraceClass.tracePairingContinuousLinearMap
declarations.doc:
The trace pairing `A ↦ (T ↦ Tr (A T))`, as a bounded linear map from bounded operators to the
dual of the trace-class operators.
declarations.statement: def tracePairingContinuousLinearMap : (H →L[ℂ] H) →L[ℂ] (TraceClass H →L[ℂ] ℂ)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.TraceClass.tracePairingContinuousLinearMap_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma tracePairingContinuousLinearMap_apply (A : H →L[ℂ] H) :
    tracePairingContinuousLinearMap A = tracePairing A

modules.title: Polar decomposition of bounded operators
modules.doc:
Polar decomposition `T = U |T|` of a bounded operator with a partial-isometry factor `U`.

## i. Overview

For a bounded operator `T` with absolute value `|T|`, `‖T x‖ = ‖|T| x‖`. The resulting isometry from
the range of `|T|` onto the range of `T` extends to the closure of that range and gives a partial
isometry `U` with `T = U |T|` and `U⋆ T = |T|`.

## ii. Key results

- `Polar.polarFactor` : the partial isometry of the polar decomposition.
- `Polar.polarFactor_mul_absOperator` : `T = U |T|`.
- `Polar.star_polarFactor_mul_self` : `U⋆ T = |T|`.
- `Polar.polarFactor_opNorm_le` : the polar factor is a contraction.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The polar factor
  - A.1. The partial-isometry adjoint identity

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Polar.absOperator
declarations.doc: The absolute value used in the polar construction.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def absOperator (T : H →L[ℂ] H) : H →L[ℂ] H

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Polar.rangeClosure
declarations.doc: The closed range subspace of the absolute value.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def rangeClosure (T : H →L[ℂ] H) : Submodule ℂ H

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Polar.absIntoRange
declarations.doc: The absolute value, with codomain restricted to its closed range.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def absIntoRange (T : H →L[ℂ] H) : H →ₗ[ℂ] rangeClosure T

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Polar.rangeInClosure
declarations.doc: The inclusion of `range |T|` into its closed range, bundled continuously.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def rangeInClosure (T : H →L[ℂ] H) :
    (LinearMap.range (absOperator T).toLinearMap) →L[ℂ] rangeClosure T

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Polar.rangeInClosure_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma rangeInClosure_apply (T : H →L[ℂ] H) (x : LinearMap.range (absOperator T).toLinearMap) :
    (rangeInClosure T x : H) = x

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Polar.denseRange_rangeInClosure
declarations.statement: lemma denseRange_rangeInClosure (T : H →L[ℂ] H) : DenseRange (rangeInClosure T)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Polar.absIntoRange_factor
declarations.statement:
lemma absIntoRange_factor (T : H →L[ℂ] H) (x : H) :
    absIntoRange T x = rangeInClosure T ⟨absOperator T x, LinearMap.mem_range_self _ x⟩

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Polar.denseRange_absIntoRange
declarations.statement: lemma denseRange_absIntoRange (T : H →L[ℂ] H) : DenseRange (absIntoRange T)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Polar.absIntoRange_apply
declarations.statement: lemma absIntoRange_apply (T : H →L[ℂ] H) (x : H) : (absIntoRange T x : H) = absOperator T x

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Polar.norm_apply_eq_norm_abs_apply
declarations.statement: lemma norm_apply_eq_norm_abs_apply (T : H →L[ℂ] H) (x : H) : ‖T x‖ = ‖absOperator T x‖

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Polar.norm_absIntoRange_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma norm_absIntoRange_apply (T : H →L[ℂ] H) (x : H) :
    ‖absIntoRange T x‖ = ‖absOperator T x‖

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Polar.instCompleteSpaceRangeClosure
declarations.doc:
The closed-range subspace is complete, so it admits the orthogonal projection used to define
the bounded polar factor.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable instance instCompleteSpaceRangeClosure (T : H →L[ℂ] H) :
    CompleteSpace (rangeClosure T)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Polar.polarOnRange
declarations.doc: The polar factor on the closed range of `|T|`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def polarOnRange (T : H →L[ℂ] H) : rangeClosure T →L[ℂ] H

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Polar.polarOnRange_eq_on_abs
declarations.statement:
lemma polarOnRange_eq_on_abs (T : H →L[ℂ] H) (x : H) :
    polarOnRange T (absIntoRange T x) = T x

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Polar.polarOnRange_norm_le
declarations.statement: lemma polarOnRange_norm_le (T : H →L[ℂ] H) (x : rangeClosure T) : ‖polarOnRange T x‖ ≤ ‖x‖

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Polar.polarFactor
declarations.doc:
The bounded polar factor, obtained by extending the range isometry by zero on the orthogonal
complement of `closure (range |T|)`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def polarFactor (T : H →L[ℂ] H) : H →L[ℂ] H

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Polar.polarFactor_eq_on_abs
declarations.statement: lemma polarFactor_eq_on_abs (T : H →L[ℂ] H) (x : H) : polarFactor T (absOperator T x) = T x

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Polar.polarFactor_norm_le
declarations.statement: lemma polarFactor_norm_le (T : H →L[ℂ] H) (x : H) : ‖polarFactor T x‖ ≤ ‖x‖

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Polar.polarFactor_opNorm_le
declarations.statement: lemma polarFactor_opNorm_le (T : H →L[ℂ] H) : ‖polarFactor T‖ ≤ 1

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Polar.polarFactor_mul_absOperator
declarations.statement: lemma polarFactor_mul_absOperator (T : H →L[ℂ] H) : polarFactor T * absOperator T = T

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Polar.polarOnRange_norm_eq
declarations.statement:
lemma polarOnRange_norm_eq (T : H →L[ℂ] H) (y : rangeClosure T) :
    ‖polarOnRange T y‖ = ‖y‖

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Polar.adjoint_polarOnRange_comp_self
declarations.doc: `polarOnRange T` is an isometry: its adjoint is a left inverse.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjoint_polarOnRange_comp_self (T : H →L[ℂ] H) :
    ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint (polarOnRange T) ∘L polarOnRange T = 1

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Polar.star_polarFactor_mul_polarFactor
declarations.doc:
`star (polarFactor T) * polarFactor T` is exactly the orthogonal projection onto
`rangeClosure T`.
declarations.statement:
lemma star_polarFactor_mul_polarFactor (T : H →L[ℂ] H) :
    star (polarFactor T) * polarFactor T = (rangeClosure T).starProjection

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Polar.star_polarFactor_mul_self
declarations.doc: **`U⋆ T = |T|`** for the polar factor `U` of any bounded operator `T`.
declarations.statement: lemma star_polarFactor_mul_self (T : H →L[ℂ] H) : star (polarFactor T) * T = absOperator T

modules.title: Rank-one positive operators
modules.doc:
The rank-one operator `|x⟩⟨x|` is trace class with trace and trace norm `‖x‖²`.

## i. Overview

The positive rank-one operator `|x⟩⟨x|` is trace class, with trace and trace norm `‖x‖²`. This is
the normalization of vector states.

## ii. Key results

- `isTraceClass_rankOne_self` : `|x⟩⟨x|` is trace class.
- `trace_rankOne_self`, `traceNorm_rankOne_self` : its trace and trace norm are `‖x‖²`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Rank-one positive operators

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.rankOne_self_diagonal
declarations.statement:
lemma rankOne_self_diagonal {x : H} {w : Set H}
    (b : HilbertBasis w ℂ H) (i : w) :
    (⟪b i, (InnerProductSpace.rankOne ℂ x x) (b i)⟫_ℂ).re =
      ‖⟪x, b i⟫_ℂ‖ ^ 2

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.isTraceClass_rankOne_self
declarations.statement:
lemma isTraceClass_rankOne_self (x : H) :
    IsTraceClass (InnerProductSpace.rankOne ℂ x x)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.trace_rankOne_self
declarations.statement:
lemma trace_rankOne_self (x : H) :
    trace (InnerProductSpace.rankOne ℂ x x) (isTraceClass_rankOne_self x) =
      (‖x‖ ^ 2 : ℝ)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.traceNorm_rankOne_self
declarations.statement:
lemma traceNorm_rankOne_self (x : H) :
    traceNorm (InnerProductSpace.rankOne ℂ x x) (isTraceClass_rankOne_self x) =
      ‖x‖ ^ 2

modules.title: Linearity and cyclicity of the trace
modules.doc:
The trace is linear on trace-class operators and cyclic against bounded operators.

## i. Overview

The trace is linear on trace-class operators and cyclic against bounded operators: `Tr (A T) = Tr (T
A)` for trace-class `T` and bounded `A`.

## ii. Key results

- `trace_add`, `trace_smul` : the trace is linear.
- `trace_mul_cycle` : the trace is cyclic.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Linearity and cyclicity of the trace
  - A.1. Additivity and cyclicity

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. Linearity and cyclicity of the trace

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.trace_smul
declarations.doc:
Scalar homogeneity of the trace, with the canonical trace-class proof for the scaled
operator.
declarations.statement:
lemma trace_smul {T : H →L[ℂ] H} (c : ℂ) (hT : IsTraceClass T) :
    trace (c • T) (isTraceClass_smul c hT) = c * trace T hT

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.trace_add
declarations.doc: Additivity of the unconditional trace.
declarations.statement:
lemma trace_add {T T' : H →L[ℂ] H} (hT : IsTraceClass T) (hT' : IsTraceClass T') :
    trace (T + T') (isTraceClass_add hT hT') = trace T hT + trace T' hT'

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.trace_mul_cycle
declarations.doc: Cyclicity of the trace across a bounded factor and a trace-class factor.
declarations.statement:
lemma trace_mul_cycle {A T : H →L[ℂ] H} (hT : IsTraceClass T) :
    trace (A * T) (isTraceClass_mul_mul (A := A) (B := 1) hT) =
      trace (T * A) (isTraceClass_mul_mul (A := 1) (B := A) hT)

modules.title: Analytic vectors
modules.doc:
Analytic and entire vectors, their exponential series and an essential self-adjointness test.

## i. Overview

A vector `ψ` in the domain of all powers of an operator `T` is analytic when `∑ₙ ‖Tⁿ ψ‖ tⁿ / n!`
converges for some `t > 0`, and entire when it converges for every `t`. Along an analytic vector of
a symmetric operator the exponential series `∑ₙ (-i s)ⁿ Tⁿ ψ / n!` defines a local orbit that
preserves the norm and is orthogonal to both deficiency spaces. If the entire vectors are dense, a
symmetric operator is therefore essentially self-adjoint.

## ii. Key results

- `IsAnalyticVector`, `IsEntireVector` : analytic and entire vectors.
- `analyticExp` : the exponential series along an analytic vector.
- `analyticExp_norm_eq_norm` : the exponential series of a symmetric operator preserves the norm.
- `isEntireVector_of_eigenvector` : eigenvectors are entire.
- `IsSymmetric.isEssentiallySelfAdjoint_of_denseEntireVectors` : a symmetric operator with a dense
  set of entire vectors is essentially self-adjoint.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The definition
- B. The local exponential series
- C. Structural closure properties
- D. Eigenvectors are analytic
- E. The global-orbit essential-self-adjointness criterion
- F. Common domain infrastructure for the finite-radius argument
- G. The global-orbit certificate targeted by Nelson continuation

## iv. References

- M. Reed and B. Simon, *Methods of Modern Mathematical Physics II*, Academic Press, 1975, Thm.
  X.39.

sections.text: ## F. Common domain infrastructure for the finite-radius argument
## G. The global-orbit certificate targeted by Nelson continuation

declarations.name: LinearPMap.IteratesSeq
declarations.doc:
`v` is the sequence of iterates of `x` under `T`: `v 0 = x` and `v (n + 1) = T (v n)`. In
particular `x` lies in the domain of every power of `T`.
declarations.statement: def IteratesSeq (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (x : H) (v : ℕ → T.domain) : Prop

declarations.name: LinearPMap.IteratesSeq.ext
LinearPMap.IsAnalyticVector
declarations.doc:
**Analytic vector** (Reed–Simon Vol. II, §X.6). `x` is an analytic vector for `T` if it lies
in the domain of every iterated power `Tⁿ` (witnessed by an iterate sequence `v`, so `v n`
represents `Tⁿ x`) and the exponential-type series `∑ ‖Tⁿx‖ tⁿ / n!` converges for some `t > 0`.
declarations.statement: def IsAnalyticVector (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (x : H) : Prop

declarations.name: LinearPMap.AnalyticVectorWitness
declarations.doc:
The data hidden by `IsAnalyticVector`, retained as a structure for recursive continuation.
The proposition is ideal for stating density assumptions; this structure is the corresponding
proof-relevant package needed to name the next exponential chart.
declarations.statement:
structure AnalyticVectorWitness (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) where
  /-- The vector the witness is analytic for. -/
  state : H
  /-- The iterate sequence witnessing `Tⁿ state`. -/
  iterates : ℕ → T.domain
  iterates_spec : IteratesSeq T state iterates
  /-- The radius at which the majorant series is known to converge. -/
  radius : ℝ
  radius_pos : 0 < radius
  summable : Summable (fun n => ‖(iterates n : H)‖ * radius ^ n / n.factorial)

declarations.name: LinearPMap.AnalyticVectorWitness.isAnalytic
declarations.statement:
lemma AnalyticVectorWitness.isAnalytic {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} (W : AnalyticVectorWitness T) :
    T.IsAnalyticVector W.state

declarations.name: LinearPMap.AnalyticVectorWitness.ofIsAnalytic
declarations.doc: Extracts an explicit `AnalyticVectorWitness` from a proof that `x` is an analytic vector.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def AnalyticVectorWitness.ofIsAnalytic
    {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} {x : H} (h : T.IsAnalyticVector x) : AnalyticVectorWitness T

declarations.name: LinearPMap.IsEntireVector
declarations.doc:
An entire vector has an iterate witness whose factorial majorant converges at every positive
radius.  This is stronger than `IsAnalyticVector`; it is the class on which the local exponential
series can be evaluated at arbitrary real times without the global patching argument.
declarations.statement: def IsEntireVector (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (x : H) : Prop

declarations.name: LinearPMap.analyticExpTerm
declarations.doc: The `n`-th term `(I s)ⁿ / n! • Tⁿ x` of the exponential series along the iterates `v`.
declarations.statement: def analyticExpTerm (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (v : ℕ → T.domain) (s : ℝ) (n : ℕ) : H

declarations.name: LinearPMap.analyticExp
declarations.doc: The exponential series `∑ₙ (I s)ⁿ / n! • Tⁿ x` along the iterates `v`.
declarations.statement: def analyticExp (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (v : ℕ → T.domain) (s : ℝ) : H

declarations.name: LinearPMap.analyticExp_congr_iterates
LinearPMap.norm_analyticExpTerm
declarations.statement:
lemma norm_analyticExpTerm (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (v : ℕ → T.domain) (s : ℝ) (n : ℕ) :
    ‖analyticExpTerm T v s n‖ = ‖(v n : H)‖ * |s| ^ n / n.factorial

declarations.name: LinearPMap.analyticExpDerivTerm
declarations.doc:
The formal derivative of an exponential-series term with respect to its real time parameter.
The `n - 1` convention makes the definition uniform at `n = 0`, where the leading factor `n`
annihilates the term.
declarations.statement: def analyticExpDerivTerm (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (v : ℕ → T.domain) (s : ℝ) (n : ℕ) : H

declarations.name: LinearPMap.analyticExpTerm_hasDerivAt
declarations.statement:
lemma analyticExpTerm_hasDerivAt (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (v : ℕ → T.domain) (s : ℝ) (n : ℕ) :
    HasDerivAt (fun r : ℝ => analyticExpTerm T v r n)
      (analyticExpDerivTerm T v s n) s

declarations.name: LinearPMap.norm_analyticExpDerivTerm
declarations.statement:
lemma norm_analyticExpDerivTerm (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (v : ℕ → T.domain) (s : ℝ) (n : ℕ) :
    ‖analyticExpDerivTerm T v s n‖ =
      ‖(v n : H)‖ * n * |s| ^ (n - 1) / n.factorial

declarations.name: LinearPMap.analyticExp_hasDerivAt_of_mem_half_radius
declarations.statement:
lemma analyticExp_hasDerivAt_of_mem_half_radius
    {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} {v : ℕ → T.domain} {t s : ℝ} (ht : 0 < t)
    (hs : s ∈ Set.Ioo (-t / 2) (t / 2))
    (hsum : Summable (fun n => ‖(v n : H)‖ * t ^ n / n.factorial)) :
    HasDerivAt (fun r : ℝ => analyticExp T v r)
      (∑' n, analyticExpDerivTerm T v s n) s

declarations.name: LinearPMap.analyticExp_hasDerivAt_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma analyticExp_hasDerivAt_zero {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} {x : H} {v : ℕ → T.domain}
    (hv : IteratesSeq T x v) {t : ℝ} (ht : 0 < t)
    (hsum : Summable (fun n => ‖(v n : H)‖ * t ^ n / n.factorial)) :
    HasDerivAt (fun s : ℝ => analyticExp T v s) (Complex.I • T (v 0)) 0

declarations.name: LinearPMap.summable_analyticExpDerivTerm_of_mem_half_radius
declarations.statement:
lemma summable_analyticExpDerivTerm_of_mem_half_radius
    {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} {v : ℕ → T.domain} {t s : ℝ} (ht : 0 < t)
    (hs : s ∈ Set.Ioo (-t / 2) (t / 2))
    (hsum : Summable (fun n => ‖(v n : H)‖ * t ^ n / n.factorial)) :
    Summable (fun n => analyticExpDerivTerm T v s n)

declarations.name: LinearPMap.analyticExp_mem_closure_graph
declarations.statement:
lemma analyticExp_mem_closure_graph
    {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} {x : H} {v : ℕ → T.domain} (hv : IteratesSeq T x v)
    {t s : ℝ} (hT : T.IsClosable)
    (hs : s ∈ Set.Ioo (-t / 2) (t / 2))
    (hsum : Summable (fun n => ‖(v n : H)‖ * t ^ n / n.factorial)) :
    (analyticExp T v s, (-Complex.I) • (∑' n, analyticExpDerivTerm T v s n)) ∈
      T.closure.graph

declarations.name: LinearPMap.analyticExp_mem_closure_domain
declarations.statement:
lemma analyticExp_mem_closure_domain
    {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} {x : H} {v : ℕ → T.domain} (hv : IteratesSeq T x v)
    {t s : ℝ} (hT : T.IsClosable)
    (hs : s ∈ Set.Ioo (-t / 2) (t / 2))
    (hsum : Summable (fun n => ‖(v n : H)‖ * t ^ n / n.factorial)) :
    analyticExp T v s ∈ T.closure.domain

declarations.name: LinearPMap.closure_analyticExp_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma closure_analyticExp_apply
    {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} {x : H} {v : ℕ → T.domain} (hv : IteratesSeq T x v)
    {t s : ℝ} (hT : T.IsClosable)
    (hs : s ∈ Set.Ioo (-t / 2) (t / 2))
    (hsum : Summable (fun n => ‖(v n : H)‖ * t ^ n / n.factorial)) :
    T.closure ⟨analyticExp T v s, analyticExp_mem_closure_domain hv hT hs hsum⟩ =
      (-Complex.I) • (∑' n, analyticExpDerivTerm T v s n)

declarations.name: LinearPMap.analyticExp_hasDerivAt_eq_smul_closure
declarations.statement:
lemma analyticExp_hasDerivAt_eq_smul_closure
    {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} {x : H} {v : ℕ → T.domain} (hv : IteratesSeq T x v)
    {t s : ℝ} (hT : T.IsClosable)
    (hs : s ∈ Set.Ioo (-t / 2) (t / 2))
    (hsum : Summable (fun n => ‖(v n : H)‖ * t ^ n / n.factorial)) :
    HasDerivAt (fun r : ℝ => analyticExp T v r)
      (Complex.I • T.closure ⟨analyticExp T v s,
        analyticExp_mem_closure_domain hv hT hs hsum⟩) s

declarations.name: LinearPMap.IsSymmetric.re_inner_smul_I_apply_self
declarations.statement:
lemma IsSymmetric.re_inner_smul_I_apply_self
    {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} (hT : T.IsSymmetric) (x : T.domain) :
    (⟪(x : H), Complex.I • T x⟫_ℂ).re = 0

declarations.name: LinearPMap.analyticExp_normSq_hasDerivAt_eq_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma analyticExp_normSq_hasDerivAt_eq_zero
    {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} (hsym : T.IsSymmetric)
    (hdense : (Submodule.span ℂ {x : H | T.IsAnalyticVector x}).topologicalClosure = ⊤)
    {x : H} {v : ℕ → T.domain} (hv : IteratesSeq T x v)
    {t s : ℝ} (hs : s ∈ Set.Ioo (-t / 2) (t / 2))
    (hsum : Summable (fun n => ‖(v n : H)‖ * t ^ n / n.factorial)) :
    HasDerivAt (fun r : ℝ => ‖analyticExp T v r‖ ^ 2) 0 s

declarations.name: LinearPMap.analyticExp_normSq_eq_normSq_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma analyticExp_normSq_eq_normSq_zero
    {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} (hsym : T.IsSymmetric)
    (hdense : (Submodule.span ℂ {x : H | T.IsAnalyticVector x}).topologicalClosure = ⊤)
    {x : H} {v : ℕ → T.domain} (hv : IteratesSeq T x v)
    {t s : ℝ} (hs : s ∈ Set.Ioo (-t / 2) (t / 2))
    (hsum : Summable (fun n => ‖(v n : H)‖ * t ^ n / n.factorial)) :
    ‖analyticExp T v s‖ ^ 2 = ‖x‖ ^ 2

declarations.name: LinearPMap.analyticExp_norm_eq_norm
declarations.statement:
lemma analyticExp_norm_eq_norm
    {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} (hsym : T.IsSymmetric)
    (hdense : (Submodule.span ℂ {x : H | T.IsAnalyticVector x}).topologicalClosure = ⊤)
    {x : H} {v : ℕ → T.domain} (hv : IteratesSeq T x v)
    {t s : ℝ} (hs : s ∈ Set.Ioo (-t / 2) (t / 2))
    (hsum : Summable (fun n => ‖(v n : H)‖ * t ^ n / n.factorial)) :
    ‖analyticExp T v s‖ = ‖x‖

declarations.name: LinearPMap.analyticExp_eq_zero_iff
declarations.statement:
lemma analyticExp_eq_zero_iff
    {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} (hsym : T.IsSymmetric)
    (hdense : (Submodule.span ℂ {x : H | T.IsAnalyticVector x}).topologicalClosure = ⊤)
    {x : H} {v : ℕ → T.domain} (hv : IteratesSeq T x v)
    {t s : ℝ} (hs : s ∈ Set.Ioo (-t / 2) (t / 2))
    (hsum : Summable (fun n => ‖(v n : H)‖ * t ^ n / n.factorial)) :
    analyticExp T v s = 0 ↔ x = 0

declarations.name: LinearPMap.IsEntireVector.isAnalyticVector
declarations.statement:
lemma IsEntireVector.isAnalyticVector
    {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} {x : H} (h : T.IsEntireVector x) : T.IsAnalyticVector x

declarations.name: LinearPMap.analyticExp_mem_closure_domain_of_entire
declarations.statement:
lemma analyticExp_mem_closure_domain_of_entire
    {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} {x : H} {v : ℕ → T.domain} (hv : IteratesSeq T x v)
    (hall : ∀ t : ℝ, 0 < t → Summable (fun n => ‖(v n : H)‖ * t ^ n / n.factorial))
    (hT : T.IsClosable) (s : ℝ) :
    analyticExp T v s ∈ T.closure.domain

declarations.name: LinearPMap.IsEntireVector.analyticExp_mem_closure_domain
declarations.statement:
lemma IsEntireVector.analyticExp_mem_closure_domain
    {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} {x : H} (h : T.IsEntireVector x)
    (hT : T.IsClosable) (s : ℝ) :
    ∃ v : ℕ → T.domain, IteratesSeq T x v ∧
      analyticExp T v s ∈ T.closure.domain

declarations.name: LinearPMap.IsEntireVector.analyticExp_norm_eq_norm
declarations.statement:
lemma IsEntireVector.analyticExp_norm_eq_norm
    {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} {x : H} (h : T.IsEntireVector x)
    (hsym : T.IsSymmetric)
    (hdense : (Submodule.span ℂ {x : H | T.IsAnalyticVector x}).topologicalClosure = ⊤)
    (s : ℝ) :
    ∃ v : ℕ → T.domain, IteratesSeq T x v ∧ ‖analyticExp T v s‖ = ‖x‖

declarations.name: LinearPMap.analyticExp_hasDerivAt_of_entire
declarations.statement:
lemma analyticExp_hasDerivAt_of_entire
    {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} {x : H} {v : ℕ → T.domain} (hv : IteratesSeq T x v)
    (hall : ∀ t : ℝ, 0 < t → Summable (fun n => ‖(v n : H)‖ * t ^ n / n.factorial))
    (hT : T.IsClosable) (s : ℝ) :
    HasDerivAt (fun r : ℝ => analyticExp T v r)
      (Complex.I • T.closure ⟨analyticExp T v s,
        analyticExp_mem_closure_domain_of_entire hv hall hT s⟩) s

declarations.name: LinearPMap.analyticExp_inner_deficiency_hasDerivAt
declarations.statement:
lemma analyticExp_inner_deficiency_hasDerivAt
    {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} {x : H} {v : ℕ → T.domain} (hv : IteratesSeq T x v)
    (hall : ∀ t : ℝ, 0 < t → Summable (fun n => ‖(v n : H)‖ * t ^ n / n.factorial))
    (hT : T.IsClosable) {y : H}
    (hy : y ∈ (T.closure - Complex.I • 1).toFun.rangeᗮ) (s : ℝ) :
    HasDerivAt (fun r : ℝ => ⟪y, analyticExp T v r⟫_ℂ)
      (-⟪y, analyticExp T v s⟫_ℂ) s

declarations.name: LinearPMap.analyticExp_inner_deficiency_eq_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma analyticExp_inner_deficiency_eq_zero
    {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} (hsym : T.IsSymmetric)
    (hdense : (Submodule.span ℂ {x : H | T.IsAnalyticVector x}).topologicalClosure = ⊤)
    {x : H} {v : ℕ → T.domain} (hv : IteratesSeq T x v)
    (hall : ∀ t : ℝ, 0 < t → Summable (fun n => ‖(v n : H)‖ * t ^ n / n.factorial))
    (hT : T.IsClosable) {y : H}
    (hy : y ∈ (T.closure - Complex.I • 1).toFun.rangeᗮ) :
    ⟪y, x⟫_ℂ = 0

declarations.name: LinearPMap.analyticExp_inner_deficiency_hasDerivAt_neg
declarations.statement:
lemma analyticExp_inner_deficiency_hasDerivAt_neg
    {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} {x : H} {v : ℕ → T.domain} (hv : IteratesSeq T x v)
    (hall : ∀ t : ℝ, 0 < t → Summable (fun n => ‖(v n : H)‖ * t ^ n / n.factorial))
    (hT : T.IsClosable) {y : H}
    (hy : y ∈ (T.closure - (-Complex.I) • 1).toFun.rangeᗮ) (s : ℝ) :
    HasDerivAt (fun r : ℝ => ⟪y, analyticExp T v r⟫_ℂ)
      (⟪y, analyticExp T v s⟫_ℂ) s

declarations.name: LinearPMap.analyticExp_inner_deficiency_eq_zero_neg
declarations.statement:
lemma analyticExp_inner_deficiency_eq_zero_neg
    {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} (hsym : T.IsSymmetric)

declarations.doc:
A local norm-preserving orbit on a symmetric operator's analytic radius.  The finite-radius
Nelson construction starts with this object and must extend it by overlapping local pieces.
declarations.statement:
structure LocalAnalyticOrbit (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (x : H) where
  /-- The radius on which the orbit is defined. -/
  radius : ℝ
  radius_pos : 0 < radius
  /-- The orbit itself, as a function of real time. -/
  toFun : ℝ → H
  initial : toFun 0 = x
  mem_domain : ∀ s, |s| < radius → toFun s ∈ T.closure.domain
  hasDerivAt : ∀ (s : ℝ) (hs : |s| < radius),
    HasDerivAt toFun
      (Complex.I • T.closure ⟨toFun s, mem_domain s hs⟩) s
  norm_eq : ∀ (s : ℝ) (_hs : |s| < radius), ‖toFun s‖ = ‖x‖

modules.title: Local and global analytic orbits
modules.doc:
Local analytic orbits agree on overlaps and glue into a global orbit orthogonal to deficiencies.

## i. Overview

A local analytic orbit is the exponential series of an analytic vector on a finite time interval.
Two local orbits starting from the same vector agree where both are defined, so a countable cover of
the real line by overlapping local orbits glues to a global orbit. A global norm-preserving orbit is
orthogonal to both deficiency spaces.

## ii. Key results

- `LocalAnalyticOrbit.eq_of_same_initial` : local orbits with the same initial vector agree.
- `GlobalAnalyticOrbit` : a norm-preserving orbit defined for all times.
- `LocalOrbitCover.toGlobal` : gluing a cover of local orbits into a global orbit.
- `GlobalAnalyticOrbit.inner_deficiency_eq_zero` : a global orbit is orthogonal to the deficiency
  spaces.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Gluing local orbits

## iv. References

- M. Reed and B. Simon, *Methods of Modern Mathematical Physics II*, Academic Press, 1975, Thm.
  X.39.

sections.text:
A translated chart and a chart independently based at the translated state agree on every
smaller symmetric core.  This is the elementary overlap statement used by the integer-chart
continuation below; the explicit radius inequalities keep the asymmetric translated radius out of
the later gluing proof.

A cover may use smaller symmetric cores of its charts.  This avoids requiring compatibility on
the full overlap of two symmetric charts, which need not be contained in a recentered symmetric
domain.

The purely one-dimensional part of integer-chart gluing.  If consecutive charts agree after
translation by `δ`, agreement propagates along the whole integer chain.  The endpoint hypotheses
are enough: the distance to the affine integer grid is convex, so every intermediate coordinate
remains in the same core.

declarations.name: LinearPMap.GlobalAnalyticOrbit
declarations.doc:
A global norm-preserving orbit for a vector, with the differential equation interpreted in the
closed operator.  This is the exact analytic certificate needed by the deficiency argument; the
finite-radius Nelson proof constructs it by patching the local exponential series.
declarations.statement:
structure GlobalAnalyticOrbit (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (x : H) where
  /-- The orbit itself, as a function of real time. -/
  toFun : ℝ → H
  initial : toFun 0 = x
  mem_domain : ∀ s, toFun s ∈ T.closure.domain
  hasDerivAt : ∀ s, HasDerivAt toFun
    (Complex.I • T.closure ⟨toFun s, mem_domain s⟩) s
  norm_eq : ∀ s, ‖toFun s‖ = ‖x‖

instance {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} {x : H} : CoeFun (GlobalAnalyticOrbit T x)
    (fun _ => ℝ → H)

declarations.name: LinearPMap.GlobalAnalyticOrbit.LocalOrbitCover
declarations.doc:
A countable cover of `ℝ` by local analytic orbits, all based at states of the same norm as
`x`, agreeing pairwise on their overlaps.
declarations.statement:
structure LocalOrbitCover (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (x : H) where
  /-- The state each local chart is based at. -/
  state : ℕ → H
  /-- The real-time center of each local chart. -/
  center : ℕ → ℝ
  /-- The local analytic orbit chart based at `state n`. -/
  chart : ∀ n, LocalAnalyticOrbit T (state n)
  center_zero : center 0 = 0
  state_zero : state 0 = x
  state_norm : ∀ n, ‖state n‖ = ‖x‖
  cover : ∀ s : ℝ, ∃ n : ℕ, |s - center n| < (chart n).radius
  compatible : ∀ (m n : ℕ) (s : ℝ),
    |s - center m| < (chart m).radius → |s - center n| < (chart n).radius →
      chart m (s - center m) = chart n (s - center n)

declarations.name: LinearPMap.GlobalAnalyticOrbit.LocalOrbitCoreCover
declarations.doc:
A `LocalOrbitCover` where compatibility is only required on a (possibly smaller) symmetric
core of each chart's radius.
declarations.statement:
structure LocalOrbitCoreCover (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (x : H) where
  /-- The state each local chart is based at. -/
  state : ℕ → H
  /-- The real-time center of each local chart. -/
  center : ℕ → ℝ
  /-- The local analytic orbit chart based at `state n`. -/
  chart : ∀ n, LocalAnalyticOrbit T (state n)
  /-- The radius of the (possibly smaller) core used for compatibility. -/
  coreRadius : ℕ → ℝ
  core_pos : ∀ n, 0 < coreRadius n
  core_le : ∀ n, coreRadius n ≤ (chart n).radius
  center_zero : center 0 = 0
  state_zero : state 0 = x
  state_norm : ∀ n, ‖state n‖ = ‖x‖
  cover : ∀ s : ℝ, ∃ n : ℕ, |s - center n| < coreRadius n
  compatible : ∀ (m n : ℕ) (s : ℝ),
    |s - center m| < coreRadius m → |s - center n| < coreRadius n →
      chart m (s - center m) = chart n (s - center n)

    {F : ℤ → ℝ → H} {δ R s : ℝ} (hδ : 0 < δ) (hR : 0 < R)
    (hadj : ∀ k : ℤ, ∀ z : ℝ, |z| < R →
      F k (δ + z) = F (k + 1) z)
    {m n : ℤ}
    (hm : |s - (m : ℝ) * δ| < R) (hn : |s - (n : ℝ) * δ| < R) :
    F m (s - (m : ℝ) * δ) = F n (s - (n : ℝ) * δ)

declarations.name: LinearPMap.GlobalAnalyticOrbit.LocalOrbitCoreCover.ofIntIndex
declarations.doc:
Reindex a bi-infinite integer-indexed core cover by `ℕ`.  The reindexing is purely set-theoretic
and uses `Equiv.intEquivNat`; it lets the existing choice-based gluing implementation remain
backwards-compatible while continuation is naturally developed on integer time centers.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def LocalOrbitCoreCover.ofIntIndex
    {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} {x : H}
    (state : ℤ → H) (center coreRadius : ℤ → ℝ)
    (chart : ∀ n : ℤ, LocalAnalyticOrbit T (state n))
    (core_pos : ∀ n, 0 < coreRadius n)
    (core_le : ∀ n, coreRadius n ≤ (chart n).radius)
    (center_zero : center 0 = 0) (state_zero : state 0 = x)
    (state_norm : ∀ n, ‖state n‖ = ‖x‖)
    (cover : ∀ s : ℝ, ∃ n : ℤ, |s - center n| < coreRadius n)
    (compatible : ∀ (m n : ℤ) (s : ℝ),
      |s - center m| < coreRadius m → |s - center n| < coreRadius n →
      chart m (s - center m) = chart n (s - center n)) :
    LocalOrbitCoreCover T x

declarations.name: LinearPMap.GlobalAnalyticOrbit.LocalOrbitCoreCover.ofAdjacentIntIndex
declarations.doc:
A family of local orbits centered at integer multiples of a step, agreeing on adjacent overlaps,
is a core cover of the real line.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def LocalOrbitCoreCover.ofAdjacentIntIndex
    {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} {x : H} {δ R : ℝ}
    (hδ : 0 < δ) (hδR : δ < R)
    (state : ℤ → H) (chart : ∀ n : ℤ, LocalAnalyticOrbit T (state n))
    (core_pos : 0 < R) (core_le : ∀ n : ℤ, R ≤ (chart n).radius)
    (state_zero : state 0 = x)
    (state_norm : ∀ n : ℤ, ‖state n‖ = ‖x‖)
    (hadj : ∀ n : ℤ, ∀ z : ℝ, |z| < R →
      chart n (δ + z) = chart (n + 1) z) :
    LocalOrbitCoreCover T x

declarations.name: LinearPMap.GlobalAnalyticOrbit.LocalOrbitCoreCover.toLocalOrbitCover
declarations.doc:
Restricts every chart of a core cover down to its core radius, forgetting the extra room
outside it.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def LocalOrbitCoreCover.toLocalOrbitCover

modules.title: Nelson's analytic-vector theorem
modules.doc:
Nelson's theorem: a symmetric operator with dense analytic vectors is essentially self-adjoint.

## i. Overview

The exponential series of an analytic vector can be restarted from any point of its orbit with a
uniform radius, which gives a cover of the real line by local orbits and hence a global orbit. So a
symmetric operator with a dense set of analytic vectors is essentially self-adjoint.

## ii. Key results

- `IsSymmetric.isEssentiallySelfAdjoint_of_denseAnalyticVectors` : **Nelson's theorem**: a symmetric
  operator with a dense set of analytic vectors is essentially self-adjoint.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Nelson's single-operator criterion

## iv. References

- M. Reed and B. Simon, *Methods of Modern Mathematical Physics II*, Academic Press, 1975, Thm.
  X.39.

sections.text: A two-sided sequence of local orbits with a uniform radius glues to a global orbit.

declarations.name: LinearPMap.IsEntireVector.globalAnalyticOrbit
declarations.doc:
Every entire vector supplies a `GlobalAnalyticOrbit` once the operator is known to be
symmetric on a dense domain.  This packages the global case through the same certificate used by
the finite-radius Nelson argument.
declarations.statement:

    {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} {x : H} (h : T.IsEntireVector x)

    Nonempty (GlobalAnalyticOrbit T x)

    (hsym : T.IsSymmetric)

    LocalAnalyticOrbit T x

declarations.name: LinearPMap.IsAnalyticVector.localAnalyticOrbit_at_exp_of_radius
declarations.doc:
At a point reached by the exponential series, a new local orbit exists with any radius below the

declarations.name: LinearPMap.AnalyticVectorWitness.advance
declarations.doc:
Move an analytic vector along its exponential series by a given time. The new radius is the
midpoint of a fixed lower bound and the old radius, so repeated steps keep a uniform radius.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def AnalyticVectorWitness.advance
    {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} (hclosed : T.closure = T)
    (hsym : T.IsSymmetric)
    (hdense : (Submodule.span ℂ {x : H | T.IsAnalyticVector x}).topologicalClosure = ⊤)
    (W : AnalyticVectorWitness T) {r a : ℝ}
    (hr : 0 < r) (hrW : r < W.radius) (ha : |a| < W.radius / 2) :
    AnalyticVectorWitness T

declarations.name: LinearPMap.AnalyticVectorWitness.advance_radius
declarations.statement:
lemma AnalyticVectorWitness.advance_radius
    {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} (hclosed : T.closure = T)
    (hsym : T.IsSymmetric)
    (hdense : (Submodule.span ℂ {x : H | T.IsAnalyticVector x}).topologicalClosure = ⊤)
    (W : AnalyticVectorWitness T) {r a : ℝ}
    (hr : 0 < r) (hrW : r < W.radius) (ha : |a| < W.radius / 2) :
    (W.advance hclosed hsym hdense hr hrW ha).radius = (r + W.radius) / 2

declarations.name: LinearPMap.AnalyticVectorWitness.advance_norm
declarations.statement:
lemma AnalyticVectorWitness.advance_norm
    {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} (hclosed : T.closure = T)
    (hsym : T.IsSymmetric)
    (hdense : (Submodule.span ℂ {x : H | T.IsAnalyticVector x}).topologicalClosure = ⊤)
    (W : AnalyticVectorWitness T) {r a : ℝ}
    (hr : 0 < r) (hrW : r < W.radius) (ha : |a| < W.radius / 2) :
    ‖(W.advance hclosed hsym hdense hr hrW ha).state‖ = ‖W.state‖

declarations.name: LinearPMap.AnalyticVectorWitness.uniformIntegerLineData
declarations.doc:
A two-sided line of witnesses with a fixed lower-radius invariant.  Positive indices advance
by `δ`, negative indices by `-δ`; the midpoint choice in `advance` makes the invariant stable in
both directions.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def AnalyticVectorWitness.uniformIntegerLineData
    {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} (hclosed : T.closure = T)
    (hsym : T.IsSymmetric)
    (hdense : (Submodule.span ℂ {x : H | T.IsAnalyticVector x}).topologicalClosure = ⊤)
    (W0 : AnalyticVectorWitness T) {r δ : ℝ}
    (hr : 0 < r) (hrW0 : r < W0.radius)
    (hδ : 0 < δ) (h2δ : 2 * δ < r) :
    ℤ → {W : AnalyticVectorWitness T // r < W.radius ∧ ‖W.state‖ = ‖W0.state‖}

declarations.name: LinearPMap.AnalyticVectorWitness.uniformIntegerLine
declarations.doc: The two-sided line of witnesses underlying `uniformIntegerLineData`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def AnalyticVectorWitness.uniformIntegerLine

    (hsym : T.IsSymmetric)
    (hdense : (Submodule.span ℂ {x : H | T.IsAnalyticVector x}).topologicalClosure = ⊤)
    (W0 : AnalyticVectorWitness T) {r δ : ℝ}
    (hr : 0 < r) (hrW0 : r < W0.radius)
    (hδ : 0 < δ) (h2δ : 2 * δ < r) :
    ℤ → AnalyticVectorWitness T

declarations.name: LinearPMap.AnalyticVectorWitness.uniformIntegerLine_succ_of_nonneg
declarations.statement:
lemma AnalyticVectorWitness.uniformIntegerLine_succ_of_nonneg
    {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} (hclosed : T.closure = T)
    (hsym : T.IsSymmetric)
    (hdense : (Submodule.span ℂ {x : H | T.IsAnalyticVector x}).topologicalClosure = ⊤)
    (W0 : AnalyticVectorWitness T) {r δ : ℝ}
    (hr : 0 < r) (hrW0 : r < W0.radius)
    (hδ : 0 < δ) (h2δ : 2 * δ < r) {n : ℤ} (hn : 0 ≤ n) :
    (AnalyticVectorWitness.uniformIntegerLine hclosed hsym hdense W0
      hr hrW0 hδ h2δ (n + 1)).state =
      analyticExp T (AnalyticVectorWitness.uniformIntegerLine hclosed hsym hdense W0
      hr hrW0 hδ h2δ n).iterates δ

declarations.name: LinearPMap.AnalyticVectorWitness.uniformIntegerLine_pred_of_nonpos
declarations.statement:

    {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} (hclosed : T.closure = T)
    (hsym : T.IsSymmetric)
    (hdense : (Submodule.span ℂ {x : H | T.IsAnalyticVector x}).topologicalClosure = ⊤)
    (W0 : AnalyticVectorWitness T) {r δ : ℝ}

    (AnalyticVectorWitness.uniformIntegerLine hclosed hsym hdense W0
      hr hrW0 hδ h2δ (n - 1)).state =

declarations.name: LinearPMap.AnalyticVectorWitness.uniformIntegerLine_step
declarations.statement:

    {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} (hclosed : T.closure = T)
    (hsym : T.IsSymmetric)
    (hdense : (Submodule.span ℂ {x : H | T.IsAnalyticVector x}).topologicalClosure = ⊤)

    (hr : 0 < r) (hrW0 : r < W0.radius)
    (hδ : 0 < δ) (h4δ : 4 * δ < r) {n : ℤ} :
    (AnalyticVectorWitness.uniformIntegerLine hclosed hsym hdense W0
      hr hrW0 hδ (by linarith) (n + 1)).state =
      analyticExp T (AnalyticVectorWitness.uniformIntegerLine hclosed hsym hdense W0
        hr hrW0 hδ (by linarith) n).iterates δ

lemma GlobalAnalyticOrbit.of_uniform_witness_line

modules.title: Weak-operator spectral measures
modules.doc:
Projection-valued measures that are countably additive in the weak operator topology.

## i. Overview

A spectral measure of an unbounded self-adjoint operator is a projection-valued measure that is
countably additive in the weak operator topology, that is, on each pair of vectors.
`WOTSpectralMeasure` is such a measure, valued in `H →WOT[ℂ] H`. Its values are commuting
projections, orthogonal on disjoint sets and multiplicative on intersections. A spectral measure
that is countably additive in norm is in particular a weak spectral measure, and weak spectral
measures push forward along measurable maps.

## ii. Key results

- `WOTSpectralMeasure` : a projection-valued measure, countably additive in the weak operator
  topology.
- `WOTSpectralMeasure.comp_eq_of_inter` : `μ A μ B = μ (A ∩ B)`.
- `WOTSpectralMeasure.map` : the pushforward along a measurable map.
- `SpectralMeasure.toWOT` : a norm-additive spectral measure as a weak spectral measure.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The structure and its basic algebra
- B. Pushforward along a measurable map
- C. Coming from a norm-continuous `SpectralMeasure`

## iv. References

* None.

modules.title: Integrating bounded functions against a spectral measure
modules.doc:
The integral of a bounded measurable function against a weak spectral measure.

## i. Overview

For a weak spectral measure `μ` and a bounded measurable `f`, the operator `∫ f dμ` is defined in
three steps. A simple function `f` has the finite sum `∑ z • μ (f⁻¹{z})`. Its norm is controlled by
the sup norm of `f`, so for a uniform limit of simple functions the finite sums converge in operator
norm. Every bounded measurable function is such a limit, which gives the integral.

## ii. Key results

- `simpleIntegral` : the integral of a simple function.
- `simpleIntegral_norm_le` : the integral of a simple function is bounded by its sup norm.
- `simpleIntegral_piecewise_indicator` : `∫ 𝟙_S dμ = μ S`.
- `boundedIntegral` : the integral of a bounded measurable function.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The simple-function integral
- B. Uniform approximation and the limiting integral
- C. The canonical integral

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text:
## A. The simple-function integral

The integral of a simple function is a finite sum. It is defined in the weak operator topology,
since a weak spectral measure need not have finite variation in operator norm.

## B. Uniform approximation and the limiting integral

The WOT type is a topological copy of the bounded-operator space; its underlying normed operator
is still available through `toCLM`. The finite estimate above therefore gives a norm completion
for any explicitly supplied uniformly convergent simple approximation. Keeping the approximation
sequence as an argument makes the analytic hypotheses visible at this low level.
The integral of an indicator is the value of the spectral measure.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.simpleIntegral
declarations.doc: The weak-operator integral of a complex-valued simple function.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def simpleIntegral (f : SimpleFunc α ℂ) : H →WOT[ℂ] H

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.simpleIntegral_inner
declarations.statement:
lemma simpleIntegral_inner (f : SimpleFunc α ℂ) (x y : H) :
    ⟪y, simpleIntegral μS f x⟫_ℂ =
      ∑ z ∈ f.range, z * μS.scalarMeasure x y (f ⁻¹' {z})

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.simpleIntegral_norm_sq
declarations.statement:
lemma simpleIntegral_norm_sq (f : SimpleFunc α ℂ) (x : H) :
    ENNReal.ofReal (‖simpleIntegral μS f x‖ ^ 2) =
      ∑ z ∈ f.range, ENNReal.ofReal (‖z‖ ^ 2) *
        (μS.diagonalMeasure x) (f ⁻¹' {z})

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.simpleIntegral_norm_sq_eq_lintegral
declarations.statement:
lemma simpleIntegral_norm_sq_eq_lintegral (f : SimpleFunc α ℂ) (x : H) :
    ENNReal.ofReal (‖simpleIntegral μS f x‖ ^ 2) =
      ∫⁻ z, ENNReal.ofReal (‖f z‖ ^ 2) ∂μS.diagonalMeasure x

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.simpleIntegral_norm_sq_le
declarations.statement:
lemma simpleIntegral_norm_sq_le (f : SimpleFunc α ℂ) (x : H) {C : ℝ}
    (hC : ∀ z ∈ f.range, ‖z‖ ^ 2 ≤ C ^ 2) :
    ENNReal.ofReal (‖simpleIntegral μS f x‖ ^ 2) ≤
      ENNReal.ofReal (C ^ 2 * ‖x‖ ^ 2)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.simpleIntegral_norm_le
ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.simpleIntegral_const
declarations.statement:
lemma simpleIntegral_const [Nonempty α] (c : ℂ) :
    simpleIntegral μS (SimpleFunc.const α c) = c • (1 : H →WOT[ℂ] H)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.spectralCLM
declarations.doc: The real-linear map `z ↦ z • μS(S)`, as a bounded operator, for each `z : ℂ`.
declarations.statement: def spectralCLM (S : Set α) : ℂ →L[ℝ] (H →L[ℂ] H)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.spectralCLM_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma spectralCLM_apply (S : Set α) (z : ℂ) :
    spectralCLM μS S z = z • ContinuousLinearMapWOT.toCLM (μS S)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.spectralCLM_finMeasAdditive
declarations.statement:
lemma spectralCLM_finMeasAdditive (μ : Measure α) :
    FinMeasAdditive μ (spectralCLM μS)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.simpleFunc_integrable_dirac
declarations.statement:
lemma simpleFunc_integrable_dirac (f : SimpleFunc α ℂ) [Nonempty α] :
    Integrable f (Measure.dirac (Classical.choice (inferInstance : Nonempty α)))

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.simpleIntegral_eq_setToSimpleFunc
declarations.statement:
lemma simpleIntegral_eq_setToSimpleFunc (f : SimpleFunc α ℂ) (_μ : Measure α) :
    ContinuousLinearMapWOT.toCLM (simpleIntegral μS f) = f.setToSimpleFunc (spectralCLM μS)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.simpleIntegral_piecewise_indicator
declarations.statement:
lemma simpleIntegral_piecewise_indicator {S : Set α} (hS : MeasurableSet S) :
    simpleIntegral μS
        (SimpleFunc.piecewise S hS (SimpleFunc.const α (1 : ℂ))
          (SimpleFunc.const α (0 : ℂ))) = μS S

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.simpleIntegral_add
declarations.statement:
lemma simpleIntegral_add [Nonempty α] (f g : SimpleFunc α ℂ) :
    simpleIntegral μS (f + g) = simpleIntegral μS f + simpleIntegral μS g

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.simpleIntegral_neg
declarations.statement:
lemma simpleIntegral_neg [Nonempty α] (f : SimpleFunc α ℂ) :
    simpleIntegral μS (-f) = -simpleIntegral μS f

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.simpleIntegral_sub
declarations.statement:
lemma simpleIntegral_sub [Nonempty α] (f g : SimpleFunc α ℂ) :
    simpleIntegral μS (f - g) = simpleIntegral μS f - simpleIntegral μS g

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.simpleIntegral_mul
declarations.statement:
lemma simpleIntegral_mul [Nonempty α] (f g : SimpleFunc α ℂ) :
    simpleIntegral μS (f * g) = simpleIntegral μS f * simpleIntegral μS g

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.simpleIntegral_star
declarations.statement:
lemma simpleIntegral_star [Nonempty α] (f : SimpleFunc α ℂ) :
    simpleIntegral μS (star f) = star (simpleIntegral μS f)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.simpleIntegral_toCLM_norm_le
ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.simpleIntegral_toCLM_diff_norm_le
declarations.statement:
lemma simpleIntegral_toCLM_diff_norm_le [Nonempty α] (f g : SimpleFunc α ℂ) {C : ℝ}
    (hC : 0 ≤ C) (hfg : ∀ x, ‖f x - g x‖ ≤ C) :
    ‖ContinuousLinearMapWOT.toCLM (simpleIntegral μS f) -
        ContinuousLinearMapWOT.toCLM (simpleIntegral μS g)‖ ≤ C

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.simpleIntegral_toCLM_cauchySeq
ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.boundedIntegralOfUniformApprox
declarations.doc:
The bounded operator integral obtained from an explicit uniformly convergent simple
approximation. The limit is taken in the normed space of bounded operators and then viewed in the
WOT copy.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def boundedIntegralOfUniformApprox [Nonempty α]
    (f : α → ℂ) (s : ℕ → SimpleFunc α ℂ)
    (_hs : ∀ ε > 0, ∃ N, ∀ n ≥ N, ∀ x, ‖s n x - f x‖ < ε) :
    H →WOT[ℂ] H

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.boundedIntegralOfUniformApprox_eq_limUnder
declarations.statement:
lemma boundedIntegralOfUniformApprox_eq_limUnder
    [Nonempty α]
    (f : α → ℂ) (s : ℕ → SimpleFunc α ℂ)
    (hs : ∀ ε > 0, ∃ N, ∀ n ≥ N, ∀ x, ‖s n x - f x‖ < ε) :
    ContinuousLinearMapWOT.toCLM (boundedIntegralOfUniformApprox μS f s hs) =
      Filter.atTop.limUnder
        (fun n => ContinuousLinearMapWOT.toCLM (simpleIntegral μS (s n)))

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.boundedIntegralOfUniformApprox_norm_le
declarations.statement:
lemma boundedIntegralOfUniformApprox_norm_le
    [Nonempty α]
    (f : α → ℂ) (s : ℕ → SimpleFunc α ℂ)
    (hs : ∀ ε > 0, ∃ N, ∀ n ≥ N, ∀ x, ‖s n x - f x‖ < ε)
    {C : ℝ} (hC : ∀ n x, ‖s n x‖ ≤ C) :
    ‖ContinuousLinearMapWOT.toCLM (boundedIntegralOfUniformApprox μS f s hs)‖ ≤ C

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.boundedIntegralOfUniformApprox_eq_of_uniform_approx
declarations.statement:
lemma boundedIntegralOfUniformApprox_eq_of_uniform_approx
    [Nonempty α]
    {f : α → ℂ} {s t : ℕ → SimpleFunc α ℂ}
    (hs : ∀ ε > 0, ∃ N, ∀ n ≥ N, ∀ x, ‖s n x - f x‖ < ε)
    (ht : ∀ ε > 0, ∃ N, ∀ n ≥ N, ∀ x, ‖t n x - f x‖ < ε)
    (hst : ∀ ε > 0, ∃ N, ∀ n ≥ N, ∀ x, ‖s n x - t n x‖ < ε) :
    boundedIntegralOfUniformApprox μS f s hs =
      boundedIntegralOfUniformApprox μS f t ht

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.boundedIntegralOfUniformApprox_eq_of_same_target
declarations.statement:
lemma boundedIntegralOfUniformApprox_eq_of_same_target
    [Nonempty α]
    {f : α → ℂ} {s t : ℕ → SimpleFunc α ℂ}
    (hs : ∀ ε > 0, ∃ N, ∀ n ≥ N, ∀ x, ‖s n x - f x‖ < ε)
    (ht : ∀ ε > 0, ∃ N, ∀ n ≥ N, ∀ x, ‖t n x - f x‖ < ε) :
    boundedIntegralOfUniformApprox μS f s hs =
      boundedIntegralOfUniformApprox μS f t ht

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.exists_uniform_simple_approx
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_uniform_simple_approx [Nonempty α] {f : α → ℂ} (hf : Measurable f)
    (hbdd : ∃ C, ∀ x, ‖f x‖ ≤ C) :
    ∃ s : ℕ → SimpleFunc α ℂ,
      (∀ ε > 0, ∃ N, ∀ n ≥ N, ∀ x, ‖s n x - f x‖ < ε) ∧
      ∃ C, ∀ n x, ‖s n x‖ ≤ C

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.boundedIntegral
declarations.doc:
The weak-operator-topology integral of a bounded measurable `f : α → ℂ` against `μS`,
defined as the limit of simple-function integrals under uniform approximation.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def boundedIntegral [Nonempty α] (f : α → ℂ) (hf : Measurable f)
    (hbdd : ∃ C, ∀ x, ‖f x‖ ≤ C) : H →WOT[ℂ] H

modules.title: The bounded functional calculus of a spectral measure
modules.doc:
The bounded integral against a spectral measure is a unital ⋆-homomorphism.

## i. Overview

The integral of a bounded measurable function against a weak spectral measure does not depend on the
approximating simple functions. It is a unital `⋆`-homomorphism from bounded measurable functions to
bounded operators, with `‖(∫ f dμ) x‖² = ∫ |f|² dμₓ`. A spectral measure is determined by its
bounded integrals.

## ii. Key results

- `boundedIntegral_add`, `boundedIntegral_mul`, `boundedIntegral_star` : the integral is a
  `⋆`-homomorphism.
- `boundedIntegral_norm_sq_eq_integral` : `‖(∫ f dμ) x‖² = ∫ |f|² dμₓ`.
- `ext_of_boundedIntegral_eq` : a spectral measure is determined by its bounded integrals.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Independence from the approximating sequence
- B. The algebra of the integral
- C. Extensionality by the integral

## iv. References

* None.

## B. The algebra of the integral

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.boundedIntegral_eq_of_uniform_approx
declarations.statement:
lemma boundedIntegral_eq_of_uniform_approx [Nonempty α]
    {f : α → ℂ} (hf : Measurable f) (hbdd : ∃ C, ∀ x, ‖f x‖ ≤ C)
    {s : ℕ → SimpleFunc α ℂ}
    (hs : ∀ ε > 0, ∃ N, ∀ n ≥ N, ∀ x, ‖s n x - f x‖ < ε) :
    boundedIntegral μS f hf hbdd = boundedIntegralOfUniformApprox μS f s hs

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.boundedIntegral_eq_of_same_target
declarations.statement:
lemma boundedIntegral_eq_of_same_target [Nonempty α]
    {f : α → ℂ} {s t : ℕ → SimpleFunc α ℂ}
    (hs : ∀ ε > 0, ∃ N, ∀ n ≥ N, ∀ x, ‖s n x - f x‖ < ε)
    (ht : ∀ ε > 0, ∃ N, ∀ n ≥ N, ∀ x, ‖t n x - f x‖ < ε)
    (hf : Measurable f) (hbdd : ∃ C, ∀ x, ‖f x‖ ≤ C) :
    boundedIntegralOfUniformApprox μS f s hs = boundedIntegral μS f hf hbdd

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.boundedIntegral_norm_le
declarations.statement:
lemma boundedIntegral_norm_le [Nonempty α]
    {f : α → ℂ} (hf : Measurable f) (hbdd : ∃ C, ∀ x, ‖f x‖ ≤ C) :
    ∃ C : ℝ, ‖ContinuousLinearMapWOT.toCLM (boundedIntegral μS f hf hbdd)‖ ≤ C

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.boundedIntegral_norm_sq
declarations.statement:
lemma boundedIntegral_norm_sq [Nonempty α]
    {f : α → ℂ} (hf : Measurable f) (hbdd : ∃ C, ∀ x, ‖f x‖ ≤ C) (x : H) :
    ENNReal.ofReal (‖boundedIntegral μS f hf hbdd x‖ ^ 2) =
      ∫⁻ z, ENNReal.ofReal (‖f z‖ ^ 2) ∂μS.diagonalMeasure x

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.boundedIntegral_norm_le_of_bound
declarations.statement:
lemma boundedIntegral_norm_le_of_bound [Nonempty α]
    {f : α → ℂ} (hf : Measurable f) {C : ℝ} (hC : 0 ≤ C)
    (hCf : ∀ x, ‖f x‖ ≤ C) :
    ‖ContinuousLinearMapWOT.toCLM
      (boundedIntegral μS f hf (⟨C, hCf⟩ : ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ x, ‖f x‖ ≤ C))‖ ≤ C

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.boundedIntegral_norm_sq_eq_integral
declarations.statement:
lemma boundedIntegral_norm_sq_eq_integral [Nonempty α]
    {f : α → ℂ} (hf : Measurable f) (hbdd : ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ x, ‖f x‖ ≤ C) (x : H) :
    ‖boundedIntegral μS f hf hbdd x‖ ^ 2 =
      ∫ z, ‖f z‖ ^ 2 ∂μS.diagonalMeasure x

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.boundedIntegralOfUniformApprox_add
declarations.statement:
lemma boundedIntegralOfUniformApprox_add [Nonempty α]
    {f g : α → ℂ} {s t : ℕ → SimpleFunc α ℂ}
    (hs : ∀ ε > 0, ∃ N, ∀ n ≥ N, ∀ x, ‖s n x - f x‖ < ε)
    (ht : ∀ ε > 0, ∃ N, ∀ n ≥ N, ∀ x, ‖t n x - g x‖ < ε)
    (hsg : ∀ ε > 0, ∃ N, ∀ n ≥ N, ∀ x,
      ‖(s n + t n) x - (f + g) x‖ < ε) :
    boundedIntegralOfUniformApprox μS (f + g) (fun n => s n + t n) hsg =
      boundedIntegralOfUniformApprox μS f s hs +
        boundedIntegralOfUniformApprox μS g t ht

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.boundedIntegralOfUniformApprox_neg
declarations.statement:
lemma boundedIntegralOfUniformApprox_neg [Nonempty α]
    {f : α → ℂ} {s : ℕ → SimpleFunc α ℂ}
    (hs : ∀ ε > 0, ∃ N, ∀ n ≥ N, ∀ x, ‖s n x - f x‖ < ε)
    (hneg : ∀ ε > 0, ∃ N, ∀ n ≥ N, ∀ x,
      ‖(-s n) x - (-f x)‖ < ε) :
    boundedIntegralOfUniformApprox μS (fun x => -f x) (fun n => -s n) hneg =
      -boundedIntegralOfUniformApprox μS f s hs

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.boundedIntegral_neg
declarations.statement:
lemma boundedIntegral_neg [Nonempty α]
    {f : α → ℂ} (hf : Measurable f) (hbf : ∃ C, ∀ x, ‖f x‖ ≤ C) :
    boundedIntegral μS (fun x => -f x) (continuous_neg.measurable.comp hf)
        (by
          rcases hbf with ⟨C, hC⟩
          exact ⟨C, fun x => by simpa using hC x⟩) =
      -boundedIntegral μS f hf hbf

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.boundedIntegral_add
declarations.statement:
lemma boundedIntegral_add [Nonempty α]
    {f g : α → ℂ} (hf : Measurable f) (hg : Measurable g)
    (hbf : ∃ C, ∀ x, ‖f x‖ ≤ C) (hbg : ∃ C, ∀ x, ‖g x‖ ≤ C) :
    boundedIntegral μS (f + g) (hf.add hg)
        (by
          rcases hbf with ⟨Cf, hCf⟩
          rcases hbg with ⟨Cg, hCg⟩
          refine ⟨Cf + Cg, fun x => ?_⟩
          exact (norm_add_le _ _).trans (add_le_add (hCf x) (hCg x))) =
      boundedIntegral μS f hf hbf + boundedIntegral μS g hg hbg

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.boundedIntegral_const
declarations.statement:
lemma boundedIntegral_const [Nonempty α] (c : ℂ) :
    boundedIntegral μS (fun _ : α => c) measurable_const
        (⟨‖c‖, fun _ => le_rfl⟩) = c • (1 : H →WOT[ℂ] H)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.boundedIntegral_congr
declarations.statement:
lemma boundedIntegral_congr [Nonempty α]
    {f g : α → ℂ} (hf : Measurable f) (hg : Measurable g)
    (hbf : ∃ C, ∀ x, ‖f x‖ ≤ C) (hbg : ∃ C, ∀ x, ‖g x‖ ≤ C)
    (hfg : ∀ x, f x = g x) :
    boundedIntegral μS f hf hbf = boundedIntegral μS g hg hbg

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.boundedIntegral_indicator
declarations.statement:
lemma boundedIntegral_indicator [Nonempty α] {S : Set α} (hS : MeasurableSet S) :
    boundedIntegral μS (S.indicator (fun _ : α => (1 : ℂ)))
        (measurable_const.indicator hS)
        (⟨1, fun x => by by_cases hx : x ∈ S <;> simp [hx]⟩) = μS S

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.ext_of_boundedIntegral_eq
declarations.doc:
A bounded spectral integral determines a weak spectral measure. In particular, this gives a
usable uniqueness principle for any construction which agrees with the canonical integral on
bounded Borel multipliers.
declarations.statement:
lemma ext_of_boundedIntegral_eq [Nonempty α]
    {μS νS : WOTSpectralMeasure α H}
    (h : ∀ (f : α → ℂ) (hf : Measurable f) (hfb : ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ a, ‖f a‖ ≤ C),
      μS.boundedIntegral f hf hfb = νS.boundedIntegral f hf hfb) :
    μS = νS

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.boundedIntegral_sub
declarations.statement:
lemma boundedIntegral_sub [Nonempty α]
    {f g : α → ℂ} (hf : Measurable f) (hg : Measurable g)
    (hbf : ∃ C, ∀ x, ‖f x‖ ≤ C) (hbg : ∃ C, ∀ x, ‖g x‖ ≤ C) :
    boundedIntegral μS (f - g) (hf.sub hg)
        (by
          rcases hbf with ⟨Cf, hCf⟩
          rcases hbg with ⟨Cg, hCg⟩
          refine ⟨Cf + Cg, fun x => ?_⟩
          exact (norm_sub_le _ _).trans (add_le_add (hCf x) (hCg x))) =
      boundedIntegral μS f hf hbf - boundedIntegral μS g hg hbg

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.boundedIntegralOfUniformApprox_mul
declarations.statement:
lemma boundedIntegralOfUniformApprox_mul [Nonempty α]
    {f g : α → ℂ} {s t : ℕ → SimpleFunc α ℂ}
    (hs : ∀ ε > 0, ∃ N, ∀ n ≥ N, ∀ x, ‖s n x - f x‖ < ε)
    (ht : ∀ ε > 0, ∃ N, ∀ n ≥ N, ∀ x, ‖t n x - g x‖ < ε)
    (hprod : ∀ ε > 0, ∃ N, ∀ n ≥ N, ∀ x,
      ‖(s n * t n) x - (f * g) x‖ < ε) :
    boundedIntegralOfUniformApprox μS (f * g) (fun n => s n * t n) hprod =
      boundedIntegralOfUniformApprox μS f s hs *
        boundedIntegralOfUniformApprox μS g t ht

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.boundedIntegral_mul
declarations.statement:
lemma boundedIntegral_mul [Nonempty α]
    {f g : α → ℂ} (hf : Measurable f) (hg : Measurable g)
    (hbf : ∃ C, ∀ x, ‖f x‖ ≤ C) (hbg : ∃ C, ∀ x, ‖g x‖ ≤ C) :
    boundedIntegral μS (f * g) (hf.mul hg)
        (by
          rcases hbf with ⟨Cf, hCf⟩
          rcases hbg with ⟨Cg, hCg⟩
          let a₀ : α := Classical.choice (inferInstance : Nonempty α)
          have hCf0 : 0 ≤ Cf := (norm_nonneg (f a₀)).trans (hCf a₀)
          refine ⟨Cf * Cg, fun x => ?_⟩
          rw [Pi.mul_apply, norm_mul]
          exact mul_le_mul (hCf x) (hCg x) (norm_nonneg _) hCf0) =
      boundedIntegral μS f hf hbf * boundedIntegral μS g hg hbg

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.boundedIntegral_smul
declarations.statement:
lemma boundedIntegral_smul [Nonempty α] (c : ℂ) {f : α → ℂ} (hf : Measurable f)
    (hbf : ∃ C, ∀ x, ‖f x‖ ≤ C) :
    boundedIntegral μS (fun x => c * f x)
        (measurable_const.mul hf)
        (by
          rcases hbf with ⟨C, hC⟩
          refine ⟨‖c‖ * C, fun x => ?_⟩
          rw [norm_mul]
          exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (hC x) (norm_nonneg c)) =
      c • boundedIntegral μS f hf hbf

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.boundedIntegralOfUniformApprox_star
declarations.statement:
lemma boundedIntegralOfUniformApprox_star [Nonempty α]
    {f : α → ℂ} {s : ℕ → SimpleFunc α ℂ}
    (hs : ∀ ε > 0, ∃ N, ∀ n ≥ N, ∀ x, ‖s n x - f x‖ < ε)
    (hstar : ∀ ε > 0, ∃ N, ∀ n ≥ N, ∀ x,
      ‖(star (s n)) x - star (f x)‖ < ε) :
    boundedIntegralOfUniformApprox μS (fun x => star (f x)) (fun n => star (s n)) hstar =
      star (boundedIntegralOfUniformApprox μS f s hs)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.boundedIntegral_star
declarations.statement:
lemma boundedIntegral_star [Nonempty α]
    {f : α → ℂ} (hf : Measurable f) (hbf : ∃ C, ∀ x, ‖f x‖ ≤ C) :
    boundedIntegral μS (fun x => star (f x)) (continuous_star.measurable.comp hf)
        (by
          rcases hbf with ⟨C, hC⟩
          exact ⟨C, fun x => by simpa using hC x⟩) =
      star (boundedIntegral μS f hf hbf)

modules.title: Operators commuting with a spectral measure
modules.doc:
An operator commuting with every spectral projection commutes with every bounded spectral integral.

## i. Overview

The matrix-coefficient measures of a spectral measure have finite variation on every spectral
variable space, not only on the real line. If `T` commutes with every spectral projection, the
matrix-coefficient measure of `(T x, y)` agrees with that of `(x, T⋆ y)`. Integrating a bounded
measurable function against these measures shows that `T` commutes with the integral.

## ii. Key results

- `WOTSpectralMeasure.scalarMeasure_isFiniteVariation'` : matrix-coefficient measures have finite
  variation.
- `WOTSpectralMeasure.boundedIntegral_commute` : an operator commuting with the spectral
  projections commutes with every bounded integral.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Finite variation of the matrix-coefficient measures
- B. Commutation with the bounded integrals

## iv. References

* None.

modules.title: Spectral measures of bounded self-adjoint operators
modules.doc:
The real spectral measure of a bounded self-adjoint operator.

## i. Overview

The spectral measure of a bounded normal operator lives on its complex spectrum. For a self-adjoint
operator the spectrum is real, and pushing the measure forward along `Complex.re` gives a spectral
measure on `ℝ` that reconstructs the operator.

## ii. Key results

- `boundedSelfAdjointSpectralMeasure` : the real spectral measure of a bounded self-adjoint
  operator.
- `boundedSelfAdjointSpectralMeasure_reconstruction` : the operator is the integral of the identity.
- `boundedSelfAdjointSpectralMeasure_commute_of_commute` : operators commuting with `T` commute with
  its spectral projections.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The real spectral measure
- B. Commutation and bounded support

## iv. References

* None.

modules.title: The Cayley transform
modules.doc:
The Cayley transform of a self-adjoint operator is a unitary.

## i. Overview

The Cayley transform `c(x) = (x - i) / (x + i)` maps the real line onto the unit circle without `1`.
Applied to a self-adjoint operator `T`, it gives the bounded operator `(T - i)(T + i)⁻¹`, which is
unitary. This reduces the spectral theory of unbounded self-adjoint operators to that of unitaries.

## ii. Key results

- `cayley`, `cayleyInverse` : the scalar Cayley transform and its inverse.
- `cayleyPMap` : the Cayley transform of a partially defined operator.
- `cayleyUnitary` : the Cayley transform of a self-adjoint operator, as a unitary.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The scalar Cayley transform
- B. The Cayley transform of a partial operator
- C. The bounded, unitary Cayley transform

## iv. References

* None.

modules.title: Spectral data of bounded normal and unitary operators
modules.doc:
Spectral measures reconstructing bounded normal and unitary operators.

## i. Overview

`BoundedNormalSpectralData` is a spectral measure on `ℂ` whose integral of the identity is a given
bounded normal operator. `BoundedUnitarySpectralData` is the same for a unitary whose spectral
measure is supported on the unit circle away from `1`. Pulling such a measure back along the Cayley
transform gives a spectral measure on `ℝ`, which is determined by its Cayley pushforward.

## ii. Key results

- `BoundedNormalSpectralData` : a spectral measure reconstructing a bounded normal operator.
- `BoundedUnitarySpectralData` : a spectral measure reconstructing a unitary, supported away from
  `1`.
- `BoundedUnitarySpectralData.realSpectralMeasure` : the pulled-back spectral measure on `ℝ`.
- `BoundedUnitarySpectralData.realSpectralMeasure_eq_of_cayleyMap_eq` : a real spectral measure is
  determined by its Cayley pushforward.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Bounded normal spectral data
- B. Bounded unitary spectral data

## iv. References

* None.

  /-- The spectral measure. -/

    spectralMeasure.complexWeakIntegral id x y = ⟪y, U x⟫_ℂ

modules.title: The inverse Cayley transform
modules.doc:
The inverse Cayley transform of a unitary without eigenvalue 1 is self-adjoint.

## i. Overview

For a unitary `u`, the inverse Cayley transform is the operator `i (1 + u)(1 - u)⁻¹`, defined on the
range of `1 - u`. If `1` is not an eigenvalue of `u`, the range of `1 - u` is dense and the inverse
Cayley transform is self-adjoint. It inverts the Cayley transform of a self-adjoint operator.

## ii. Key results

- `inverseCayleyPMap` : the inverse Cayley transform of a unitary.
- `CayleyUnitaryData` : a unitary without eigenvalue `1`.
- `inverseCayleyPMap_isSelfAdjoint` : the inverse Cayley transform is self-adjoint.
- `cayleyContinuousLinearMap_inverseCayleyPMap_eq` : the Cayley transform of the inverse Cayley
  transform is `u`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The partial inverse Cayley transform
- B. Density of the range of `1 - u`
- C. Self-adjointness of the inverse Cayley transform
- D. Round trip with the forward Cayley transform

## iv. References

* None.

modules.title: Spectral measures and the Cayley transform
modules.doc:
Spectral measures on ℝ correspond to Cayley-supported spectral measures on ℂ.

## i. Overview

Spectral measures on `ℝ` push forward along the Cayley transform to spectral measures on `ℂ`
supported on the unit circle away from `1`. Pulling back along the inverse Cayley transform undoes
this, which gives an equivalence between spectral measures on `ℝ` and such measures on `ℂ`.

## ii. Key results

- `cayleyMap`, `cayleyInverseMap` : pushing forward along the Cayley transform and its inverse.
- `cayleyMap_injective` : the pushforward is injective.
- `CayleySupported` : a spectral measure on `ℂ` supported on the unit circle away from `1`.
- `cayleyMeasureEquiv` : the equivalence between spectral measures on `ℝ` and Cayley-supported ones
  on `ℂ`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Pushforward and pullback along the Cayley transform
- B. The Cayley equivalence of spectral-measure data

## iv. References

* None.
