modules.title: The spectral measure of the Cayley transform
modules.doc:
The spectral measure of the Cayley transform, pulled back to a spectral measure on ℝ.

## i. Overview

The Cayley transform `U` of a self-adjoint operator `T` is a unitary. The continuous functional
calculus gives it a spectral measure on the unit circle. Since `1` is not an eigenvalue of `U`, this
measure gives no mass to `1`, so it pulls back along the inverse Cayley transform to a spectral
measure on `ℝ`, the candidate spectral measure of `T`.

## ii. Key results

- `cayleyBoundedOperator` : the Cayley transform of `T`, as a bounded operator.
- `cayleyBoundedSpectralMeasure` : its spectral measure on `ℂ`.
- `cayleyBoundedSpectralMeasure_singleton_one` : the spectral measure gives no mass to `1`.
- `cayleyRealSpectralMeasure` : the pulled-back spectral measure on `ℝ`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Spectral data from the functional calculus
  - A.1. A bounded extension of the Cayley difference multiplier

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text:
## A. Spectral data from the functional calculus

The Riesz--Markov construction is carried out on the compact spectrum.  The public spectral
certificate should expose a measure on the ambient scalar field, since that is what the later
functional-calculus and Cayley APIs consume.  This wrapper performs exactly that harmless subtype
pushforward and does not impose any unitary or Cayley support hypothesis.

A unitary with no spectral mass at `1` is now the exact input expected by the Cayley inverse.
The only extra work is the support calculation: the normal PVM is pushed forward from the compact
spectrum, and the spectrum of a unitary lies on the unit circle.

### A.1. A bounded extension of the Cayley difference multiplier

The function `1 - z` is bounded on the unit circle, where the spectral measure lives, but not on
`ℂ`. It is extended by zero outside the closed unit disk.

modules.title: The spectral theorem for unbounded self-adjoint operators
modules.doc:
The spectral theorem for unbounded self-adjoint operators via the Cayley transform.

## i. Overview

The spectral measure on `ℝ` obtained from the Cayley transform of a self-adjoint operator `T`
reconstructs `T`: its domain is the set of vectors `x` with `∫ λ² dμₓ < ∞`, and on it `⟪y, T x⟫ = ∫
λ d⟪y, μ x⟫`. This is the spectral theorem for unbounded self-adjoint operators, and it also applies
to the closure of an essentially self-adjoint operator.

## ii. Key results

- `unboundedSpectralTheorem` : **the spectral theorem** for a self-adjoint operator.
- `unboundedSpectralTheorem_of_essentiallySelfAdjoint` : the same for the closure of an essentially
  self-adjoint operator.
- `cayleyRealSpectralMeasure_eq_maximal` : the spectral measure has the maximal domain.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Restriction identities for PVM scalar measures
- B. Complex vector-measure density transport
- C. The inverse-moment transport lemma

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text:
## A. Restriction identities for PVM scalar measures

These identities are independent of the Cayley transform.  They express the elementary fact
that testing a projection-valued measure after applying one of its projections restricts the
corresponding scalar measure.  They are the bookkeeping lemmas needed when a bounded spectral
moment is localized to a measurable spectral set.

## B. Complex vector-measure density transport

The scalar measures of a complex PVM are complex vector measures, rather than positive
measures.  This is the reusable density-integral theorem needed by the inverse Cayley step.

## C. The inverse-moment transport lemma

The bounded spectral measure of the Cayley transform reconstructs `z`. An integral identity for the
inverse Cayley transform on the bounded measure transports to the real spectral measure.

    {q : α → ℂ} (hq : μ.Integrable q) {g : α → ℝ}
    (hg : (μ.withDensity q (ContinuousLinearMap.mul ℝ ℂ)).Integrable g)
    (hvar0 : (μ.withDensity q (ContinuousLinearMap.mul ℝ ℂ)).variation =
      μ.variation.withDensity (fun x => ‖q x‖ₑ)) :
    ∫ᵛ x, g x ∂[ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ (E := ℂ);
        μ.withDensity q (ContinuousLinearMap.mul ℝ ℂ)] =
      ∫ᵛ x, (g x : ℂ) * q x ∂[ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℂ; μ]

    (hfi : ∀ x y, (μ.scalarMeasure x y).Integrable id)

      μ S * ContinuousLinearMapWOT.ofCLM U =
        ContinuousLinearMapWOT.ofCLM U * μ S)

        (ContinuousLinearMap.mul ℝ ℂ)

modules.title: Transporting spectral measures along unitaries
modules.doc:
Conjugating operators and spectral measures by a unitary.

## i. Overview

A unitary `u : H ≃ₗᵢ[ℂ] H'` conjugates operators on `H` to operators on `H'`, and conjugation is a
`⋆`-isomorphism in the weak operator topology. Conjugating a spectral measure on `H` gives a
spectral measure on `H'` whose scalar and diagonal measures are those of the original, transported
along `u`.

## ii. Key results

- `unitaryConj` : conjugation of an operator by `u`.
- `unitaryConjSpectralMeasure` : conjugation of a spectral measure by `u`.
- `unitaryConjSpectralMeasure_scalarMeasure`, `unitaryConjSpectralMeasure_diagonalMeasure` : the
  transported scalar and diagonal measures.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Conjugation of a single operator
- B. Conjugation of a spectral measure
- C. Interaction with the scalar and diagonal measures

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. Conjugation of a single operator
## B. Conjugation of a spectral measure
## C. Interaction with the scalar and diagonal measures

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.unitaryConj

declarations.doc: Transport a WOT spectral measure through a Hilbert-space unitary.

    [InnerProductSpace ℂ H'] [CompleteSpace H'] (u : H ≃ₗᵢ[ℂ] H') :

    [InnerProductSpace ℂ H'] [CompleteSpace H'] (u : H ≃ₗᵢ[ℂ] H')

lemma unitaryConjSpectralMeasure_scalarMeasure_apply

    (u : H ≃ₗᵢ[ℂ] H') (μS : WOTSpectralMeasure α H) (x y : H') (S : Set α) :
    (unitaryConjSpectralMeasure u μS).scalarMeasure x y S =
      μS.scalarMeasure (u.symm x) (u.symm y) S

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.unitaryConjSpectralMeasure_scalarMeasure
declarations.statement:
lemma unitaryConjSpectralMeasure_scalarMeasure
    {H' : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup H'] [InnerProductSpace ℂ H'] [CompleteSpace H']
    (u : H ≃ₗᵢ[ℂ] H') (μS : WOTSpectralMeasure α H) (x y : H') :

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.unitaryConjSpectralMeasure_diagonalMeasure
declarations.statement:
lemma unitaryConjSpectralMeasure_diagonalMeasure
    {H' : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup H'] [InnerProductSpace ℂ H'] [CompleteSpace H']

    (unitaryConjSpectralMeasure u μS).diagonalMeasure x =
      μS.diagonalMeasure (u.symm x)

modules.title: The continuous functional calculus of a spectral measure
modules.doc:
Integrating continuous functions on a compact space against a spectral measure is a unital
⋆-homomorphism into the bounded operators.

## i. Overview

For a weak spectral measure `P` on a compact Borel space `X`, the integral `f ↦ ∫ f dP` of a
continuous function is a unital ⋆-homomorphism `C(X, ℂ) → B(H)`. This repackages the algebra of the
bounded integral so that it can be composed with other ⋆-homomorphisms, and so that the spectrum
of an integral can be controlled by the spectrum of the integrand.

## ii. Key results

- `WOTSpectralMeasure.continuousCalculus` : the ⋆-homomorphism `f ↦ ∫ f dP`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The ⋆-homomorphism

## iv. References

* None.

    P.integralCLM f = ContinuousLinearMapWOT.toCLM (P.boundedIntegral F hF hbF)

modules.title: The essential spectrum is closed
modules.doc:
The essential spectrum of a self-adjoint operator is closed.

## i. Overview

The essential spectrum of a self-adjoint operator is closed. For `λₖ → λ` in the essential spectrum,
all singular sequences of the `λₖ` lie in a separable closed subspace. A diagonal choice, almost
orthogonal to more and more vectors of a countable dense subset, is a singular sequence for `λ`.

## ii. Key results

- `isClosed_essSpectrum` : the essential spectrum is closed.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Closedness of the essential spectrum

## iv. References

- Adapted from `adambornemann-glitch/Spectra`, `SpectralTheory/Essential/Closed.lean` (Apache 2.0).

sections.text: ## A. Closedness of the essential spectrum

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.Essential.isClosed_essSpectrum
declarations.doc: The essential spectrum is closed.
declarations.statement:
lemma isClosed_essSpectrum {A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) :
    IsClosed (essSpectrum hA)

modules.title: The essential spectrum
modules.doc:
The essential spectrum of a self-adjoint operator, defined by singular sequences.

## i. Overview

A real number `λ` is in the essential spectrum of a self-adjoint operator `A` when there is a
singular sequence for `λ`: vectors `ψₙ` in the domain of `A` with `‖ψₙ‖ → 1`, `⟪g, ψₙ⟫ → 0` for
every `g`, and `‖A ψₙ - λ ψₙ‖ → 0`. Orthonormal approximate eigenvectors are singular sequences.

## ii. Key results

- `essSpectrum` : the essential spectrum of a self-adjoint operator.
- `mem_essSpectrum_of_seq` : membership from a singular sequence.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Singular sequences and the essential spectrum

## iv. References

- Adapted from `adambornemann-glitch/Spectra`, `SpectralTheory/Essential/Defs.lean` (Apache 2.0).

sections.text: ## A. Singular sequences and the essential spectrum

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.Essential.essSpectrum
declarations.doc:
The **essential spectrum** of a self-adjoint operator `A`, defined by singular (Weyl)
sequences: `λ ∈ essSpectrum hA` iff there is `ψ : ℕ → A.domain` with `‖ψ n‖ → 1`, `ψ` weakly null,
and `‖A ψ n − λ ψ n‖ → 0`. (`hA` is carried for discoverability; the set depends only on `A`.)
declarations.statement: def essSpectrum {A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} (_hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) : Set ℝ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.Essential.mem_essSpectrum_of_seq
declarations.doc:
Membership in `essSpectrum` from an `H`-valued Weyl sequence together with a domain-membership
witness. This packages the `ℕ → A.domain` data so callers can work with plain vectors.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_essSpectrum_of_seq {A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) (lam : ℝ)
    (φ : ℕ → H) (hmem : ∀ n, φ n ∈ A.domain)
    (hnorm : Tendsto (fun n => ‖φ n‖) atTop (𝓝 1))
    (hweak : ∀ g : H, Tendsto (fun n => ⟪g, φ n⟫_ℂ) atTop (𝓝 0))
    (heig : Tendsto (fun n => ‖A ⟨φ n, hmem n⟩ - (lam : ℂ) • φ n‖) atTop (𝓝 0)) :
    lam ∈ essSpectrum hA

modules.title: Scaling self-adjoint operators
modules.doc:
Real scaling preserves self-adjointness and scales the essential spectrum.

## i. Overview

For a self-adjoint operator `A` and a real `c ≠ 0`, `c • A` is self-adjoint and its essential
spectrum is the essential spectrum of `A` scaled by `c`.

## ii. Key results

- `isSelfAdjoint_smul_real` : `c • A` is self-adjoint.
- `essSpectrum_smul_real` : the essential spectrum scales with `c`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. L1: self-adjointness under real scaling
- B. L2: essential spectrum under real scaling

## iv. References

- Adapted from `adambornemann-glitch/Spectra`, `SpectralTheory/Essential/Smul.lean` (Apache 2.0).

sections.text: ## A. L1: self-adjointness under real scaling
## B. L2: essential spectrum under real scaling

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.Essential.isFormalAdjoint_smul_real
declarations.doc: For a real scalar `c`, `c • A` is formally self-adjoint when `A` is.
declarations.statement:
lemma isFormalAdjoint_smul_real {A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} (hsym : A.IsFormalAdjoint A)
    (c : ℝ) : (((c : ℂ)) • A).IsFormalAdjoint (((c : ℂ)) • A)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.Essential.exists_apply_sub_smul_eq
declarations.doc:
For self-adjoint `A` and `z` off the real axis, every vector is `A ψ - z ψ` for some `ψ` in the
domain of `A`.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_apply_sub_smul_eq {A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) {z : ℂ} (hz : z.im ≠ 0)
    (φ : H) : ∃ ψ : A.domain, A ψ - z • (ψ : H) = φ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.Essential.smul_surjective_sub_smul
declarations.doc: Surjectivity of `c•A - w` reduces to surjectivity of `A - w/c` (real `c ≠ 0`).
declarations.statement:
lemma smul_surjective_sub_smul {A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A)
    (c : ℝ) (hc : c ≠ 0) (w : ℂ) (hw : w.im ≠ 0) :
    ∀ φ : H, ∃ ψ : ((c : ℂ) • A).domain, ((c : ℂ) • A) ψ - w • (ψ : H) = φ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.Essential.isSelfAdjoint_smul_real
declarations.doc: **L1.** If `A` is self-adjoint and `c : ℝ` is nonzero, then `(c : ℂ) • A` is self-adjoint.
declarations.statement:
lemma isSelfAdjoint_smul_real {A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A)
    (c : ℝ) (hc : c ≠ 0) : IsSelfAdjoint ((c : ℂ) • A)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.Essential.mem_essSpectrum_smul_real
declarations.doc: A Weyl sequence for `A` at `λ` is a Weyl sequence for `c • A` at `c·λ` (real `c`).
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_essSpectrum_smul_real {A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A)
    (c : ℝ) (hc : c ≠ 0) {lam : ℝ} (hlam : lam ∈ essSpectrum hA) :
    c * lam ∈ essSpectrum (isSelfAdjoint_smul_real hA c hc)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.Essential.essSpectrum_congr_op
declarations.doc: `essSpectrum` depends only on the operator, not on the self-adjointness witness.
declarations.statement:
lemma essSpectrum_congr_op {A B : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) (hB : IsSelfAdjoint B)
    (h : A = B) : essSpectrum hA = essSpectrum hB

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.Essential.smul_inv_smul_pmap
declarations.doc: Scaling by `c` then by `c⁻¹` is the identity operator (real `c ≠ 0`).
declarations.statement:
lemma smul_inv_smul_pmap {A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} (c : ℝ) (hc : c ≠ 0) :
    ((c⁻¹ : ℝ) : ℂ) • (((c : ℂ)) • A) = A

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.Essential.essSpectrum_smul_real
declarations.doc:
**L2.** The essential spectrum scales by a real nonzero `c`:
`essSpectrum (c • A) = (· * c) '' essSpectrum A`.
declarations.statement:
lemma essSpectrum_smul_real {A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A)
    (c : ℝ) (hc : c ≠ 0) :
    essSpectrum (isSelfAdjoint_smul_real hA c hc) = (fun μ => c * μ) '' essSpectrum hA

modules.title: Compact operators and weakly null sequences
modules.doc:
Orthonormal sequences are weakly null, and compact operators make them norm-null.

## i. Overview

An orthonormal sequence is weakly null, by Bessel's inequality. A compact operator maps a bounded
weakly null sequence to a sequence converging to `0` in norm.

## ii. Key results

- `Orthonormal.tendsto_inner_atTop_zero` : orthonormal sequences are weakly null.
- `IsCompactOperator.tendsto_norm_apply_of_weaklyNull` : compact operators map bounded weakly null
  sequences to null sequences.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Orthonormal sequences are weakly null
- B. Compact operators on weakly null sequences

## iv. References

- Adapted from `adambornemann-glitch/Spectra`, `SpectralTheory/Essential/WeakCompact.lean` (Apache
  2.0).

sections.text: ## A. Orthonormal sequences are weakly null
## B. Compact operators on weakly null sequences

declarations.name: Orthonormal.tendsto_inner_atTop_zero
declarations.doc:
An orthonormal sequence is **weakly null**: for every fixed `g`, the inner products
`⟪g, ψ n⟫` tend to `0`. (Bessel's inequality makes `∑ ‖⟪ψ n, g⟫‖²` summable, so its terms — hence
`‖⟪g, ψ n⟫‖` — tend to `0`.)
declarations.statement:
lemma _root_.Orthonormal.tendsto_inner_atTop_zero {ψ : ℕ → H} (hψ : Orthonormal ℂ ψ) (g : H) :
    Tendsto (fun n => ⟪g, ψ n⟫_ℂ) atTop (𝓝 0)

declarations.name: IsCompactOperator.tendsto_norm_apply_of_weaklyNull
declarations.doc:
A **compact** operator maps a bounded weakly-null sequence to a norm-null sequence.

`hbdd` bounds the sequence (`‖u n‖ ≤ C`); `hweak` is weak nullness stated concretely as
`∀ g, ⟪g, u n⟫ → 0`. The proof: if `‖K (u n)‖` does *not* tend to `0`, extract a subsequence on
which it stays `≥ ε`; it lands in the compact set `closure (K '' closedBall 0 C)`, so a further
subsequence converges in norm to some `a`; weak nullness (via the adjoint) forces `⟪a, a⟫ = 0`,
i.e. `a = 0`, contradicting `ε ≤ ‖a‖`.
declarations.statement:
lemma _root_.IsCompactOperator.tendsto_norm_apply_of_weaklyNull
    {K : H →L[ℂ] H} (hK : IsCompactOperator (K : H → H)) {u : ℕ → H} {C : ℝ}
    (hbdd : ∀ n, ‖u n‖ ≤ C)
    (hweak : ∀ g : H, Tendsto (fun n => ⟪g, u n⟫_ℂ) atTop (𝓝 0)) :
    Tendsto (fun n => ‖K (u n)‖) atTop (𝓝 0)

modules.title: Weyl's theorem on the essential spectrum
modules.doc:
Weyl's theorem: compact resolvent differences preserve the essential spectrum.

## i. Overview

If the resolvents at `i` of two self-adjoint operators differ by a compact operator, the operators
have the same essential spectrum. The resolvents enter as bounded operators satisfying the defining
properties of the resolvent, `IsResolventAt`. In particular a relatively compact perturbation does
not change the essential spectrum.

## ii. Key results

- `IsResolventAt` : a bounded operator is the resolvent of a self-adjoint operator at `z`.
- `essSpectrum_eq_of_isCompactOperator_resolvent_sub` : **Weyl's theorem.**
- `essSpectrum_eq_of_isCompactOperator_perturb` : the essential spectrum is stable under relatively
  compact perturbations.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The bounded resolvent
- B. Weyl's theorem
- C. Relatively compact perturbations

## iv. References

- Adapted from `adambornemann-glitch/Spectra`, `SpectralTheory/Essential/Weyl.lean` (Apache 2.0).

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.Essential.I_im_ne_zero
declarations.doc: `i` is off the real axis, the spectral parameter used throughout.
declarations.statement: lemma I_im_ne_zero : (Complex.I).im ≠ 0

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.Essential.IsResolventAt
declarations.doc:
`R` is the resolvent of the self-adjoint operator `A` at `z`: it maps into the domain of `A`,
and inverts `A - z` on both sides.
declarations.statement:
structure IsResolventAt {A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} (_hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) (z : ℂ)
    (R : H →L[ℂ] H) : Prop where
  mem_domain : ∀ φ, R φ ∈ A.domain
  solves : ∀ φ, A ⟨R φ, mem_domain φ⟩ - z • R φ = φ
  left_inverse : ∀ ψ : A.domain, R (A ψ - z • (ψ : H)) = (ψ : H)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.Essential.essSpectrum_subset_of_isCompactOperator_resolvent_sub
declarations.doc:
**One inclusion of Weyl's theorem.** If the resolvent difference `R_B(i) − R_A(i)` is compact,
then `essSpectrum hA ⊆ essSpectrum hB`.
declarations.statement:
lemma essSpectrum_subset_of_isCompactOperator_resolvent_sub
    {A B : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) (hB : IsSelfAdjoint B)
    {RA RB : H →L[ℂ] H} (hRA : IsResolventAt hA I RA) (hRB : IsResolventAt hB I RB)
    (hcompact : IsCompactOperator ((RB - RA : H →L[ℂ] H) : H → H)) :
    essSpectrum hA ⊆ essSpectrum hB

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.Essential.essSpectrum_eq_of_isCompactOperator_resolvent_sub
declarations.doc:
**Weyl's theorem.** If the resolvents `R_A(i)`, `R_B(i)` of two self-adjoint operators differ
by a compact operator, then `A` and `B` have the same essential spectrum.
declarations.statement:
lemma essSpectrum_eq_of_isCompactOperator_resolvent_sub
    {A B : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) (hB : IsSelfAdjoint B)
    {RA RB : H →L[ℂ] H} (hRA : IsResolventAt hA I RA) (hRB : IsResolventAt hB I RB)
    (hcompact : IsCompactOperator ((RB - RA : H →L[ℂ] H) : H → H)) :
    essSpectrum hA = essSpectrum hB

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.Essential.isCompactOperator_resolvent_sub_of_isCompactOperator_perturb
declarations.doc:
**Relatively compact perturbations.** If `B - A = W (A - i)` on the domain of `A` for a compact
`W`, then `R_B(i) - R_A(i) = -R_B(i) W` is compact.
declarations.statement:
lemma isCompactOperator_resolvent_sub_of_isCompactOperator_perturb
    {A B : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) (hB : IsSelfAdjoint B)
    {RA RB : H →L[ℂ] H} (hRA : IsResolventAt hA I RA) (hRB : IsResolventAt hB I RB)
    (hdom : A.domain = B.domain) (W : H →L[ℂ] H) (hW : IsCompactOperator (W : H → H))
    (hVW : ∀ (χ : H) (hχ : χ ∈ A.domain),
        B ⟨χ, hdom ▸ hχ⟩ - A ⟨χ, hχ⟩ = W (A ⟨χ, hχ⟩ - I • χ)) :
    IsCompactOperator ((RB - RA : H →L[ℂ] H) : H → H)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.Essential.essSpectrum_eq_of_isCompactOperator_perturb
declarations.doc:
**Weyl's theorem for relatively compact perturbations.** If `B - A = W (A - i)` on the domain of
`A` for a compact `W`, then `A` and `B` have the same essential spectrum.
declarations.statement:
lemma essSpectrum_eq_of_isCompactOperator_perturb
    {A B : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) (hB : IsSelfAdjoint B)
    {RA RB : H →L[ℂ] H} (hRA : IsResolventAt hA I RA) (hRB : IsResolventAt hB I RB)
    (hdom : A.domain = B.domain) (W : H →L[ℂ] H) (hW : IsCompactOperator (W : H → H))
    (hVW : ∀ (χ : H) (hχ : χ ∈ A.domain),
        B ⟨χ, hdom ▸ hχ⟩ - A ⟨χ, hχ⟩ = W (A ⟨χ, hχ⟩ - I • χ)) :
    essSpectrum hA = essSpectrum hB

modules.title: The candidate generator of a unitary group
modules.doc:
The candidate generator of a strongly continuous unitary group, and its symmetry.

## i. Overview

For a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group `U`, the candidate generator is defined on the
vectors whose orbit `t ↦ U t ψ` is differentiable at `0`, and sends such a vector to `-i` times the
derivative. It is a symmetric operator.

## ii. Key results

- `stoneCandidateDomain` : the vectors whose orbit is differentiable at `0`.
- `stoneCandidateGenerator` : the candidate generator.
- `stoneCandidateGenerator_isSymmetric` : the candidate generator is symmetric.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The candidate domain
- B. The candidate generator
- C. Symmetry of the candidate generator

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## C. Symmetry of the candidate generator

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.stoneCandidateDomainPred
declarations.doc: A vector is in the domain of the candidate generator when its orbit is differentiable at `0`.
declarations.statement: def stoneCandidateDomainPred (ψ : H) : Prop

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.stoneCandidateDomainPred_add
declarations.doc:
The candidate domain is closed under addition. The group law is an argument so that the
domain is attached to a unitary group.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.stoneCandidateDomainPred_smul
declarations.doc: The candidate domain is closed under scalar multiplication, by the same linearity argument.
declarations.statement:
lemma stoneCandidateDomainPred_smul {ψ : H} (c : ℂ)
    (h : stoneCandidateDomainPred (U := U) ψ) :
    stoneCandidateDomainPred (U := U) (c • ψ)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.stoneCandidateDomainPred_zero
declarations.statement: lemma stoneCandidateDomainPred_zero : stoneCandidateDomainPred (U := U) (0 : H)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.stoneCandidateDomain
declarations.doc: The domain of the candidate generator of the unitary group `U`, as a submodule.
declarations.statement: def stoneCandidateDomain : Submodule ℂ H

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.stoneCandidateDeriv
declarations.doc:
The derivative witness for a vector in the candidate domain, chosen once and for all via
choice; `-Complex.I` times this is the candidate generator's action.
declarations.statement: def stoneCandidateDeriv (ψ : stoneCandidateDomain (U := U) hUmul) : H

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.stoneCandidateDeriv_spec
declarations.statement:
lemma stoneCandidateDeriv_spec (ψ : stoneCandidateDomain (U := U) hUmul) :
    HasDerivAt (fun t : ℝ => U t (ψ : H)) (stoneCandidateDeriv hUmul ψ) 0

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.stoneCandidateDeriv_add
declarations.statement:
lemma stoneCandidateDeriv_add (ψ₁ ψ₂ : stoneCandidateDomain (U := U) hUmul) :
    stoneCandidateDeriv hUmul (ψ₁ + ψ₂) =
      stoneCandidateDeriv hUmul ψ₁ + stoneCandidateDeriv hUmul ψ₂

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.stoneCandidateDeriv_smul
declarations.statement:
lemma stoneCandidateDeriv_smul (c : ℂ) (ψ : stoneCandidateDomain (U := U) hUmul) :
    stoneCandidateDeriv hUmul (c • ψ) = c • stoneCandidateDeriv hUmul ψ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.stoneCandidateLinearMap
declarations.doc: The candidate generator as a linear map on its domain.
declarations.statement:
def stoneCandidateLinearMap :
    stoneCandidateDomain (U := U) hUmul →ₗ[ℂ] H

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.stoneCandidateGenerator
declarations.doc:
The candidate Stone generator: a `LinearPMap` whose domain is exactly the vectors along which
`U`'s orbit is differentiable at `0`, sending such a vector to `-i` times that derivative.
declarations.statement: def stoneCandidateGenerator : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.stoneCandidateGenerator_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma stoneCandidateGenerator_apply (ψ : (stoneCandidateGenerator (U := U) hUmul).domain) :
    stoneCandidateGenerator (U := U) hUmul ψ = (-Complex.I) • stoneCandidateDeriv hUmul ψ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.stoneCandidateGenerator_isSymmetric
declarations.doc:
**The candidate generator is symmetric.** The inner product `⟪U t ψ₁, U t ψ₂⟫` is constant in
`t`; differentiating at `0` gives the symmetry.
declarations.statement:
lemma stoneCandidateGenerator_isSymmetric :
    (stoneCandidateGenerator (U := U) hUmul).IsSymmetric

modules.title: Gårding vectors
modules.doc:
Gårding vectors: heat-kernel smoothings along a unitary group, dense in the domain.

## i. Overview

Smoothing a vector `ψ` along the orbit of a unitary group against the heat kernel `gₑ(t) = (π
ε)^(-1/2) exp(-t² / ε)` gives the Gårding vector `∫ gₑ(t) U t ψ dt`. As `ε → 0` the Gårding vectors
converge to `ψ`. Each Gårding vector lies in the domain of the candidate generator, which acts on it
by smoothing against the derivative of the kernel.

## ii. Key results

- `gaussianKernel` : the heat kernel.
- `analyticGardingVector` : the Gårding vector of `ψ`.
- `analyticGardingVector_tendsto` : Gårding vectors converge to `ψ` as `ε → 0`.
- `stoneCandidateGenerator_analyticGardingVector` : the generator acts on a Gårding vector by
  smoothing against the derivative of the kernel.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The generator on Gårding vectors

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text:
## A. The generator on Gårding vectors

Translating a Gårding vector by `U s` translates the kernel. Differentiating under the integral in
`s` gives the action of the candidate generator.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.gaussianKernel
declarations.doc: The heat kernel `(π ε)^(-1/2) exp(-t² / ε)`, a Gaussian of variance `ε / 2` with integral `1`.
declarations.statement: def gaussianKernel (ε t : ℝ) : ℝ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.gaussianKernel_pos
declarations.statement: lemma gaussianKernel_pos {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) (t : ℝ) : 0 < gaussianKernel ε t

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.gaussianKernel_integral
declarations.statement:
lemma gaussianKernel_integral {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∫ t : ℝ, gaussianKernel ε t = 1

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.gaussianKernel_smul_integrable
declarations.doc:
The heat kernel is integrable against any bounded continuous function, in particular against
`t ↦ U t ψ` (bounded because `U t` is unitary, `‖U t ψ‖ = ‖ψ‖`).
declarations.statement:
lemma gaussianKernel_smul_integrable (hUunit : ∀ t, U t ∈ unitary (H →L[ℂ] H))
    (hUcont : ∀ ξ : H, Continuous (fun t : ℝ => U t ξ))
    {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) (ψ : H) :
    Integrable (fun t : ℝ => (gaussianKernel ε t : ℂ) • U t ψ)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.analyticGardingVector
declarations.doc: The Gårding vector of `ψ` mollified against the heat kernel of width `ε`.
declarations.statement: def analyticGardingVector (ε : ℝ) (ψ : H) : H

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.standardGaussianKernel
declarations.doc: The heat kernel with `ε = 1`.
declarations.statement: def standardGaussianKernel (x : ℝ) : ℝ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.standardGaussianKernel_pos
declarations.statement: lemma standardGaussianKernel_pos (x : ℝ) : 0 < standardGaussianKernel x

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.standardGaussianKernel_eq_gaussianKernel_one
declarations.statement:
lemma standardGaussianKernel_eq_gaussianKernel_one :
    standardGaussianKernel = gaussianKernel 1

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.standardGaussianKernel_integral
declarations.statement: lemma standardGaussianKernel_integral : ∫ x : ℝ, standardGaussianKernel x = 1

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.standardGaussianKernel_integrable
declarations.statement: lemma standardGaussianKernel_integrable : Integrable standardGaussianKernel

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.gaussianKernel_scale_eq_standardGaussianKernel
declarations.doc:
The rescaling identity at the level of the kernel itself: `√ε · gaussianKernel ε (√ε x) =
standardGaussianKernel x`, i.e. the `ε`-dependence exactly cancels once the extra `√ε` from the
change-of-variables Jacobian is absorbed.
declarations.statement:
lemma gaussianKernel_scale_eq_standardGaussianKernel {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) (x : ℝ) :
    Real.sqrt ε * gaussianKernel ε (Real.sqrt ε * x) = standardGaussianKernel x

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.analyticGardingVector_eq_standardGaussian
declarations.doc: The Gårding vector after the substitution `t = √ε x`.
declarations.statement:
lemma analyticGardingVector_eq_standardGaussian {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) (ψ : H) :
    analyticGardingVector U ε ψ =
      ∫ x : ℝ, (standardGaussianKernel x : ℂ) • U (Real.sqrt ε * x) ψ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.analyticGardingVector_tendsto
declarations.doc:
**Gårding vectors converge to `ψ` as `ε → 0`**, by dominated convergence after the substitution
`t = √ε x`.
declarations.statement:
lemma analyticGardingVector_tendsto (hU0 : U 0 = 1)
    (hUcont : ∀ ξ : H, Continuous (fun t : ℝ => U t ξ)) (ψ : H) :
    Tendsto (fun ε : ℝ => analyticGardingVector U ε ψ) (𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ)) (𝓝 ψ)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.analyticGardingVector_translate
declarations.doc: Translating a Gårding vector by `U s` translates the kernel by `s`.
declarations.statement:
lemma analyticGardingVector_translate (hUunit : ∀ t, U t ∈ unitary (H →L[ℂ] H))
    (hUcont : ∀ ξ : H, Continuous (fun t : ℝ => U t ξ)) {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) (ψ : H) (s : ℝ) :
    U s (analyticGardingVector U ε ψ) = ∫ u : ℝ, (gaussianKernel ε (u - s) : ℂ) • U u ψ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.gaussianKernel_hasDerivAt
declarations.doc:
Explicit `HasDerivAt` for the heat kernel: `gaussianKernel ε` is differentiable everywhere,
with derivative `gaussianKernel ε t * (-(2 * t) / ε)` (the usual `d/dt exp(-t²/ε) = (-2t/ε)
exp(-t²/ε)` computation, scaled by the front normalization constant).
declarations.statement:
lemma gaussianKernel_hasDerivAt {ε : ℝ} (_hε : 0 < ε) (t : ℝ) :
    HasDerivAt (gaussianKernel ε) (gaussianKernel ε t * (-(2 * t) / ε)) t

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.gaussianKernel_deriv
declarations.doc: Corollary of `gaussianKernel_hasDerivAt` as a `deriv` equation.
declarations.statement:
lemma gaussianKernel_deriv {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) (t : ℝ) :
    deriv (gaussianKernel ε) t = gaussianKernel ε t * (-(2 * t) / ε)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.gaussianKernel_deriv_continuous
declarations.doc: `deriv (gaussianKernel ε)` is continuous.
declarations.statement:
lemma gaussianKernel_deriv_continuous {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) :
    Continuous (deriv (gaussianKernel ε))

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.gaussianKernel_deriv_shift_bound
declarations.doc: The shifted derivative of the heat kernel is dominated by `C (|u| + 1) exp(-u² / (2 ε))`.
declarations.statement:
lemma gaussianKernel_deriv_shift_bound {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) {x : ℝ} (hx : x ^ 2 ≤ 1)
    (u : ℝ) :
    |deriv (gaussianKernel ε) (u - x)| ≤
      (2 * (Real.pi * ε) ^ (-(1 : ℝ) / 2) * Real.exp (1 / ε) / ε) *
        ((|u| + 1) * Real.exp (-(u ^ 2) / (2 * ε)))

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.gaussianKernel_deriv_bound_integrable
declarations.doc:
The `L¹` domination bound is itself integrable in `u`: it is `const * ((|u|+1) *
Gaussian(u))`, and `|u| * Gaussian(u)` and `Gaussian(u)` are each classically integrable
(`integrable_mul_exp_neg_mul_sq`, `integrable_exp_neg_mul_sq`).
declarations.statement:
lemma gaussianKernel_deriv_bound_integrable {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) (c : ℝ) :
    Integrable (fun u : ℝ => c * ((|u| + 1) * Real.exp (-(u ^ 2) / (2 * ε))))

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.analyticGardingVector_hasDerivAt
declarations.doc:
The orbit of a Gårding vector is differentiable at `0`, with derivative the Gårding vector of
`-g'`.
declarations.statement:
lemma analyticGardingVector_hasDerivAt
    (hUunit : ∀ t, U t ∈ unitary (H →L[ℂ] H))
    (hUcont : ∀ ξ : H, Continuous (fun t : ℝ => U t ξ)) {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) (ψ : H) :
    HasDerivAt (fun s : ℝ => U s (analyticGardingVector U ε ψ))
      (∫ u : ℝ, ((-(deriv (gaussianKernel ε) u) : ℝ) : ℂ) • U u ψ) 0

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.analyticGardingVector_mem_stoneCandidateDomain
declarations.doc: Gårding vectors lie in the domain of the candidate generator.
declarations.statement:
lemma analyticGardingVector_mem_stoneCandidateDomain (hUunit : ∀ t, U t ∈ unitary (H →L[ℂ] H))
    (hUcont : ∀ ξ : H, Continuous (fun t : ℝ => U t ξ)) {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) (ψ : H) :
    analyticGardingVector U ε ψ ∈ (stoneCandidateGenerator (U := U) hUmul).domain

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.stoneCandidateGenerator_analyticGardingVector
declarations.doc:
The candidate generator acts on a Gårding vector by smoothing against the derivative of the
kernel.
declarations.statement:
lemma stoneCandidateGenerator_analyticGardingVector (hUunit : ∀ t, U t ∈ unitary (H →L[ℂ] H))
    (hUcont : ∀ ξ : H, Continuous (fun t : ℝ => U t ξ)) {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) (ψ : H) :
    stoneCandidateGenerator (U := U) hUmul
        ⟨analyticGardingVector U ε ψ, analyticGardingVector_mem_stoneCandidateDomain hUmul
          hUunit hUcont hε ψ⟩ =
      (Complex.I : ℂ) • ∫ u : ℝ, ((deriv (gaussianKernel ε) u : ℝ) : ℂ) • U u ψ

modules.title: Gårding vectors are analytic
modules.doc:
Gårding vectors are analytic vectors of the candidate generator.

## i. Overview

Applying the candidate generator `n` times to a Gårding vector gives, up to a power of `i`, the
Gårding vector of the `n`-th derivative of the heat kernel. Its norm is at most `‖ψ‖ C^(n + 1)
√(n!)`, so every Gårding vector is an analytic vector of the candidate generator.

## ii. Key results

- `analyticGardingVector_isAnalyticVector` : Gårding vectors are analytic vectors.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The generator on iterated-kernel Gårding vectors
- B. Analyticity of Gårding vectors

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. The generator on iterated-kernel Gårding vectors

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.gardingVectorAt_iteratedKernel_mem_stoneCandidateDomain
declarations.doc:
Domain membership of the `n`-th iterated-kernel Gårding vector, derived (not assumed) from the
differentiability of its orbit — the same pattern as
`analyticGardingVector_mem_stoneCandidateDomain`, one order at a time.
declarations.statement:
lemma gardingVectorAt_iteratedKernel_mem_stoneCandidateDomain
    (hUunit : ∀ t, U t ∈ unitary (H →L[ℂ] H)) (hUcont : ∀ ξ : H, Continuous (fun t : ℝ => U t ξ))
    (n : ℕ) {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) (ψ : H) :
    gardingVectorAt U (iteratedDeriv n (gaussianKernel ε)) ψ ∈
      (stoneCandidateGenerator (U := U) hUmul).domain

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.stoneCandidateGenerator_gardingVectorAt_iteratedKernel
declarations.doc:
The commutation identity at every order: applying `stoneCandidateGenerator` to `Gₙ` gives (up
to the factor `I`) `Gₙ₊₁`. Exactly `stoneCandidateGenerator_analyticGardingVector`'s proof, one
order at a time.
declarations.statement:
lemma stoneCandidateGenerator_gardingVectorAt_iteratedKernel
    (hUunit : ∀ t, U t ∈ unitary (H →L[ℂ] H)) (hUcont : ∀ ξ : H, Continuous (fun t : ℝ => U t ξ))
    (n : ℕ) {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) (ψ : H) :
    stoneCandidateGenerator (U := U) hUmul
        ⟨gardingVectorAt U (iteratedDeriv n (gaussianKernel ε)) ψ,
          gardingVectorAt_iteratedKernel_mem_stoneCandidateDomain hUmul hUunit hUcont n hε ψ⟩ =
      (Complex.I : ℂ) • gardingVectorAt U (iteratedDeriv (n + 1) (gaussianKernel ε)) ψ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.analyticGardingVector_isAnalyticVector
declarations.doc: **Gårding vectors are analytic vectors** of the candidate generator.
declarations.statement:
lemma analyticGardingVector_isAnalyticVector (hUunit : ∀ t, U t ∈ unitary (H →L[ℂ] H))
    (hUcont : ∀ ξ : H, Continuous (fun t : ℝ => U t ξ)) {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) (ψ : H) :
    (stoneCandidateGenerator (U := U) hUmul).IsAnalyticVector (analyticGardingVector U ε ψ)

modules.title: Growth of the derivatives of the heat kernel
modules.doc:
Hermite polynomial bounds on the L¹ norms of the heat kernel's derivatives.

## i. Overview

The `n`-th derivative of the heat kernel is a Hermite polynomial times a Gaussian. The probabilists'
Hermite polynomials satisfy `∫ Hₙ(x)² exp(-x²/2) dx = √(2π) n!`, proved by one integration by parts
per step using `Hₙ₊₁' = (n + 1) Hₙ`. Cauchy–Schwarz then bounds the `L¹` norm of the `n`-th
derivative of the heat kernel by `C^(n + 1) √(n!)`.

## ii. Key results

- `hermite_derivative_succ` : `Hₙ₊₁' = (n + 1) Hₙ`.
- `hermite_gaussian_sq_integral` : `∫ Hₙ(x)² exp(-x²/2) dx = √(2π) n!`.
- `gaussianKernel_iteratedDeriv_eq` : the derivatives of the heat kernel in terms of Hermite
  polynomials.
- `gaussianKernel_iteratedDeriv_L1_bound` : the `L¹` bound on the derivatives of the heat kernel.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The Hermite derivative identity
- B. Integrability against Gaussian weights
- C. The norm of the Hermite polynomials
- D. Derivatives of the heat kernel

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.hermite_derivative_succ
declarations.doc:
The polynomial identity `Hₙ₊₁' = (n+1) · Hₙ`, absent from Mathlib, proved directly from the
defining recursion `hermite_succ : Hₙ₊₁ = X·Hₙ - Hₙ'` by induction.
declarations.statement:
lemma hermite_derivative_succ :
    ∀ n : ℕ, derivative (hermite (n + 1)) = C ((n : ℤ) + 1) * hermite n

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.hermite_aeval_deriv_succ
declarations.doc: The `aeval`/real-valued specialization of `hermite_derivative_succ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma hermite_aeval_deriv_succ (n : ℕ) (x : ℝ) :
    aeval x (derivative (hermite (n + 1))) = ((n : ℝ) + 1) * aeval x (hermite n)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.hermite_aeval_succ
declarations.doc: The `aeval`/real-valued specialization of the defining recursion `hermite_succ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma hermite_aeval_succ (n : ℕ) (x : ℝ) :
    aeval x (hermite (n + 1)) = x * aeval x (hermite n) - aeval x (derivative (hermite n))

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.integrable_pow_mul_exp_neg_mul_sq
declarations.doc:
A monomial times a Gaussian weight is integrable (the `n`-th-power case of
`integrable_aeval_mul_gaussian`, via the real-exponent Gaussian-tail estimate specialized to a
natural-number exponent through `Real.rpow_natCast`).
declarations.statement:
lemma integrable_pow_mul_exp_neg_mul_sq (n : ℕ) {c : ℝ} (hc : 0 < c) :
    Integrable (fun x : ℝ => x ^ n * Real.exp (-(c * x ^ 2)))

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.integrable_aeval_mul_gaussian
declarations.doc:
Any (integer) polynomial times a Gaussian weight is integrable — the integrability fact needed
throughout `hermite_gaussian_sq_integral_succ`'s integration-by-parts argument. Proved by
`Polynomial.induction_on'`, reducing to the monomial case.
declarations.statement:
lemma integrable_aeval_mul_gaussian (q : Polynomial ℤ) {c : ℝ} (hc : 0 < c) :
    Integrable (fun x : ℝ => aeval x q * Real.exp (-(c * x ^ 2)))

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.gaussian_hasDerivAt
declarations.doc:
The derivative of the standard Gaussian, packaged as `HasDerivAt` (Mathlib only records the
`deriv`-value form privately, inside the proof of `deriv_gaussian_eq_hermite_mul_gaussian`).
declarations.statement:
lemma gaussian_hasDerivAt (x : ℝ) :
    HasDerivAt (fun y : ℝ => Real.exp (-(y ^ 2 / 2))) (-x * Real.exp (-(x ^ 2 / 2))) x

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.hermite_gaussian_sq_integral_succ
declarations.doc: `Iₙ₊₁ = (n + 1) Iₙ` for `Iₙ = ∫ Hₙ(x)² exp(-x²/2) dx`, by integration by parts.
declarations.statement:
lemma hermite_gaussian_sq_integral_succ (n : ℕ) :
    (∫ x : ℝ, (aeval x (hermite (n + 1))) ^ 2 * Real.exp (-(x ^ 2 / 2))) =
      ((n : ℝ) + 1) * ∫ x : ℝ, (aeval x (hermite n)) ^ 2 * Real.exp (-(x ^ 2 / 2))

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.hermite_gaussian_sq_integral
declarations.doc: **The norm of the Hermite polynomials**: `∫ Hₙ(x)² exp(-x²/2) dx = √(2π) n!`.
declarations.statement:
lemma hermite_gaussian_sq_integral (n : ℕ) :
    ∫ x : ℝ, (aeval x (hermite n)) ^ 2 * Real.exp (-(x ^ 2 / 2)) =
      Real.sqrt (2 * Real.pi) * n.factorial

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.hermite_gaussian_L1_bound
declarations.doc: The weighted `L¹` bound `∫ |Hₙ(x)| exp(-x²/2) dx ≤ √(2π) √(n!)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma hermite_gaussian_L1_bound (n : ℕ) :
    ∫ x : ℝ, |aeval x (hermite n)| * Real.exp (-(x ^ 2 / 2)) ≤
      Real.sqrt (2 * Real.pi) * Real.sqrt n.factorial

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.gaussianKernel_iteratedDeriv_eq
declarations.doc: The `n`-th derivative of the heat kernel is a rescaled Hermite polynomial times the kernel.
declarations.statement:
lemma gaussianKernel_iteratedDeriv_eq {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) (n : ℕ) (t : ℝ) :
    iteratedDeriv n (gaussianKernel ε) t =
      (Real.pi * ε) ^ (-(1 : ℝ) / 2) * (Real.sqrt (2 / ε) ^ n *
        ((-1 : ℝ) ^ n * aeval (Real.sqrt (2 / ε) * t) (hermite n) *
          Real.exp (-((Real.sqrt (2 / ε) * t) ^ 2 / 2))))

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.gaussianKernel_iteratedDeriv_L1_bound
declarations.doc: **The `L¹` norm of the `n`-th derivative of the heat kernel** is at most `C^(n + 1) √(n!)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma gaussianKernel_iteratedDeriv_L1_bound {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ n : ℕ,
      Integrable (iteratedDeriv n (gaussianKernel ε)) ∧
      ∫ t : ℝ, |iteratedDeriv n (gaussianKernel ε) t| ≤ C ^ (n + 1) * Real.sqrt n.factorial

modules.title: The unitary group preserves the domain of its generator
modules.doc:
A unitary group preserves the domain of its candidate generator and commutes with it.

## i. Overview

A strongly continuous unitary group preserves the domain of its candidate generator `T` and commutes
with it there. So the orbit of a vector in the domain is differentiable at every time `s`, with
derivative `i T (U s ψ)`.

## ii. Key results

- `stoneCandidateDomain_translate` : the group preserves the domain.
- `stoneCandidateGenerator_translate` : the generator commutes with the group.
- `stoneCandidateGenerator_hasDerivAt` : orbits of domain vectors are differentiable at every time.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Invariance of the candidate domain
- B. Commutation and differentiability of orbits

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. Invariance of the candidate domain
## B. Commutation and differentiability of orbits

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.stoneCandidateGenerator_translate_comm
declarations.doc: `U t (U s ψ)` and `U s (U t ψ)` agree as functions of `s`, since `s + t = t + s`.
declarations.statement:
lemma stoneCandidateGenerator_translate_comm (ψ : H) (t : ℝ) :
    (fun s : ℝ => (U t : H →L[ℂ] H) (U s ψ)) = (fun s : ℝ => (U s : H →L[ℂ] H) (U t ψ))

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.stoneCandidateGenerator_translate_hasDerivAt
declarations.doc:
If `ψ`'s orbit is differentiable at `0` with witness `φ`, then `U t ψ`'s orbit is again
differentiable at `0`, with witness `U t φ` — the group law turns the fixed continuous linear map
`U t` applied to `ψ`'s derivative witness into a derivative witness for `U t ψ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma stoneCandidateGenerator_translate_hasDerivAt {ψ φ : H} (t : ℝ)
    (hφ : HasDerivAt (fun s : ℝ => U s ψ) φ 0) :
    HasDerivAt (fun s : ℝ => U s (U t ψ)) (U t φ) 0

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.stoneCandidateDomain_translate
declarations.doc: The candidate domain is invariant under every `U t`.
declarations.statement:
lemma stoneCandidateDomain_translate {ψ : H} (hψ : stoneCandidateDomainPred (U := U) ψ)
    (t : ℝ) : stoneCandidateDomainPred (U := U) (U t ψ)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.stoneCandidateDomain_translate_mem
declarations.doc: The candidate domain, packaged as a `Submodule`-invariance statement under every `U t`.
declarations.statement:
lemma stoneCandidateDomain_translate_mem (ψ : stoneCandidateDomain (U := U) hUmul) (t : ℝ) :
    (U t (ψ : H)) ∈ stoneCandidateDomain (U := U) hUmul

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.stoneCandidateGenerator_translate
declarations.doc:
The candidate generator commutes with the group it was built from: for `ψ` in `T.domain`,
`U t ψ` is again in `T.domain`, and `T (U t ψ) = U t (T ψ)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma stoneCandidateGenerator_translate (ψ : stoneCandidateDomain (U := U) hUmul) (t : ℝ) :
    stoneCandidateGenerator (U := U) hUmul
        ⟨U t (ψ : H), stoneCandidateDomain_translate_mem hUmul ψ t⟩ =
      U t (stoneCandidateGenerator (U := U) hUmul ψ)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.stoneCandidateGenerator_hasDerivAt
declarations.doc: The orbit of a domain vector is differentiable at every time `s`, with derivative `i T (U s ψ)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma stoneCandidateGenerator_hasDerivAt (ψ : stoneCandidateDomain (U := U) hUmul) (s : ℝ) :
    HasDerivAt (fun r : ℝ => U r (ψ : H))
      (Complex.I • U s (stoneCandidateGenerator (U := U) hUmul ψ)) s

modules.title: Gårding vectors of smooth kernels
modules.doc:
Gårding vectors of a general kernel and the differentiability of their orbits.

## i. Overview

For a kernel `k` on `ℝ`, the Gårding vector of `ψ` is `∫ k(t) U t ψ dt`. Translating it by `U s`
translates the kernel. If `k` is differentiable with a locally dominated derivative, the orbit of
the Gårding vector is differentiable at `0`, with derivative the Gårding vector of `-k'`.

## ii. Key results

- `gardingVectorAt` : the Gårding vector of `ψ` for a kernel `k`.
- `gardingVectorAt_translate` : translating a Gårding vector translates the kernel.
- `gardingVectorAt_hasDerivAt` : the orbit of a Gårding vector is differentiable at `0`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Gårding vectors and translation
- B. Differentiability of the orbit

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.gardingVectorAt
declarations.doc:
The Gårding vector of `ψ` against a generic (real-valued) kernel `k`, generalizing
`analyticGardingVector U ε ψ = gardingVectorAt U (gaussianKernel ε) ψ`.
declarations.statement: def gardingVectorAt (k : ℝ → ℝ) (ψ : H) : H

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.gardingVectorAt_translate
declarations.doc: Translating a Gårding vector by `U s` translates the kernel by `s`.
declarations.statement:
lemma gardingVectorAt_translate (k : ℝ → ℝ) (ψ : H)
    (hk_integrable : Integrable (fun t : ℝ => (k t : ℂ) • U t ψ)) (s : ℝ) :
    U s (gardingVectorAt U k ψ) = ∫ u : ℝ, (k (u - s) : ℂ) • U u ψ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.gardingVectorAt_hasDerivAt
declarations.doc:
If `k` is differentiable with a locally dominated continuous derivative `k'`, the orbit of the
Gårding vector of `k` is differentiable at `0`, with derivative the Gårding vector of `-k'`.
declarations.statement:
lemma gardingVectorAt_hasDerivAt (hUunit : ∀ t, U t ∈ unitary (H →L[ℂ] H))
    (hUcont : ∀ ξ : H, Continuous (fun t : ℝ => U t ξ)) (k k' : ℝ → ℝ)
    (hk_cont : Continuous k) (hk'_cont : Continuous k') (hk_deriv : ∀ t, HasDerivAt k (k' t) t)
    (ψ : H) (hk_integrable : Integrable (fun t : ℝ => (k t : ℂ) • U t ψ))
    (bound : ℝ → ℝ) (hbound_int : Integrable bound)
    (hbound : ∀ u : ℝ, ∀ x ∈ Metric.ball (0 : ℝ) 1, |k' (u - x)| * ‖ψ‖ ≤ bound u) :
    HasDerivAt (fun s : ℝ => U s (gardingVectorAt U k ψ))
      (∫ u : ℝ, ((-(k' u) : ℝ) : ℂ) • U u ψ) 0

modules.title: Pointwise bounds on the derivatives of the heat kernel
modules.doc:
Pointwise domination of the shifted derivatives of the heat kernel.

## i. Overview

Every derivative of the heat kernel, shifted by at most `1`, is dominated by an integrable function
`C (1 + |u|)ⁿ exp(-c u²)`. So the Gårding vectors of all derivatives of the heat kernel have
differentiable orbits.

## ii. Key results

- `hermite_aeval_le_poly_growth` : `|Hₙ(y)| ≤ Cₙ (1 + |y|)ⁿ`.
- `gaussianKernel_iteratedDeriv_shift_bound` : the local domination bound.
- `gardingVectorAt_iteratedKernel_hasDerivAt` : the orbit of the Gårding vector of the `n`-th
  derivative of the heat kernel is differentiable at `0`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Polynomial growth of the Hermite polynomials
- B. Local domination of the kernel derivatives
- C. Integrability of the dominating functions
- D. Smoothness of the heat kernel
- E. Differentiable orbits of iterated-kernel Gårding vectors

## iv. References

* None.

## B. Local domination of the kernel derivatives
## C. Integrability of the dominating functions
## D. Smoothness of the heat kernel

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.hermite_aeval_le_poly_growth
declarations.doc: `|Hₙ(y)| ≤ Cₙ (1 + |y|)ⁿ`, with `Cₙ` the sum of the absolute values of the coefficients of `Hₙ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma hermite_aeval_le_poly_growth (n : ℕ) :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 ≤ C ∧ ∀ y : ℝ, |aeval y (hermite n)| ≤ C * (1 + |y|) ^ n

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.gaussianKernel_iteratedDeriv_shift_bound
declarations.doc:
For `x² ≤ 1`, the `(n + 1)`-th derivative of the heat kernel at `u - x` is dominated by `C (1 +
|u|)ⁿ⁺¹ exp(-c u²)`, uniformly in `x`.
declarations.statement:
lemma gaussianKernel_iteratedDeriv_shift_bound (n : ℕ) {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∃ D : ℝ, 0 ≤ D ∧ ∀ {x : ℝ}, x ^ 2 ≤ 1 → ∀ u : ℝ,
      |iteratedDeriv (n + 1) (gaussianKernel ε) (u - x)| ≤
        D * ((1 + |u|) ^ (n + 1) * Real.exp (-(u ^ 2) / (2 * ε)))

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.integrable_abs_pow_mul_exp_neg_mul_sq
declarations.doc:
`|u|^n` times a Gaussian weight is integrable — the `abs`-of-argument variant of
`integrable_pow_mul_exp_neg_mul_sq`, obtained via `Integrable.abs` since `|u^n * exp(-cu²)| =
|u|^n * exp(-cu²)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma integrable_abs_pow_mul_exp_neg_mul_sq (n : ℕ) {c : ℝ} (hc : 0 < c) :
    Integrable (fun u : ℝ => |u| ^ n * Real.exp (-(c * u ^ 2)))

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.integrable_one_add_abs_pow_mul_exp_neg_mul_sq
declarations.doc: `(1 + |u|)ⁿ exp(-c u²)` is integrable.
declarations.statement:
lemma integrable_one_add_abs_pow_mul_exp_neg_mul_sq (n : ℕ) {c : ℝ} (hc : 0 < c) :
    Integrable (fun u : ℝ => (1 + |u|) ^ n * Real.exp (-(c * u ^ 2)))

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.gaussianKernel_contDiff
declarations.doc:
`gaussianKernel ε` is smooth to every order (used to get `Continuous`/`Differentiable` facts
about its iterated derivatives via the generic `ContDiff.continuous_iteratedDeriv`/
`ContDiff.differentiable_iteratedDeriv`).
declarations.statement: lemma gaussianKernel_contDiff {ε : ℝ} (_hε : 0 < ε) : ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) (gaussianKernel ε)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.gaussianKernel_iteratedDeriv_continuous
declarations.doc: `iteratedDeriv n (gaussianKernel ε)` is continuous, for every `n`.
declarations.statement:
lemma gaussianKernel_iteratedDeriv_continuous (n : ℕ) {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) :
    Continuous (iteratedDeriv n (gaussianKernel ε))

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.gaussianKernel_iteratedDeriv_hasDerivAt
declarations.doc: The `n`-th derivative of the heat kernel has derivative the `(n + 1)`-th.
declarations.statement:
lemma gaussianKernel_iteratedDeriv_hasDerivAt (n : ℕ) {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) (t : ℝ) :
    HasDerivAt (iteratedDeriv n (gaussianKernel ε))
      (iteratedDeriv (n + 1) (gaussianKernel ε) t) t

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.gaussianKernel_iteratedDeriv_smul_integrable
declarations.doc: The `n`-th derivative of the heat kernel is integrable against `t ↦ U t ψ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma gaussianKernel_iteratedDeriv_smul_integrable {H : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup H]
    [InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [CompleteSpace H] {U : ℝ → H →L[ℂ] H}
    (hUunit : ∀ t, U t ∈ unitary (H →L[ℂ] H)) (hUcont : ∀ ξ : H, Continuous (fun t : ℝ => U t ξ))
    (n : ℕ) {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) (ψ : H) :
    Integrable (fun t : ℝ => ((iteratedDeriv n (gaussianKernel ε) t : ℝ) : ℂ) • U t ψ)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.gardingVectorAt_iteratedKernel_hasDerivAt
declarations.doc:
The orbit of the Gårding vector of the `n`-th derivative of the heat kernel is differentiable at
`0`.
declarations.statement:
lemma gardingVectorAt_iteratedKernel_hasDerivAt {H : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup H]
    [InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [CompleteSpace H] {U : ℝ → H →L[ℂ] H}
    (hUmul : ∀ s t, U (s + t) = U s * U t) (hUunit : ∀ t, U t ∈ unitary (H →L[ℂ] H))
    (hUcont : ∀ ξ : H, Continuous (fun t : ℝ => U t ξ)) (n : ℕ) {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) (ψ : H) :
    HasDerivAt (fun s : ℝ => U s (gardingVectorAt U (iteratedDeriv n (gaussianKernel ε)) ψ))
      (∫ u : ℝ, ((-(iteratedDeriv (n + 1) (gaussianKernel ε) u) : ℝ) : ℂ) • U u ψ) 0

modules.title: Stone's theorem: existence of the generator
modules.doc:
Stone's theorem, existence: the candidate generator is essentially self-adjoint.

## i. Overview

The Gårding vectors of a strongly continuous unitary group are analytic vectors of its candidate
generator and are dense. By Nelson's theorem the candidate generator is essentially self-adjoint.

## ii. Key results

- `stoneCandidateGenerator_denseAnalyticVectors` : the analytic vectors of the candidate generator
  are dense.
- `stoneCandidateGenerator_isEssentiallySelfAdjoint` : **Stone's theorem, existence**: the candidate
  generator is essentially self-adjoint.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Density of analytic vectors
- B. Essential self-adjointness

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.stoneCandidateGenerator_denseAnalyticVectors
declarations.doc:
**The analytic vectors of the candidate generator are dense**: every vector is a limit of
Gårding vectors.
declarations.statement:
lemma stoneCandidateGenerator_denseAnalyticVectors (hU0 : U 0 = 1)
    (hUunit : ∀ t, U t ∈ unitary (H →L[ℂ] H)) (hUcont : ∀ ξ : H, Continuous (fun t : ℝ => U t ξ)) :
    (Submodule.span ℂ
      {x : H | (stoneCandidateGenerator (U := U) hUmul).IsAnalyticVector x}).topologicalClosure =
      (⊤ : Submodule ℂ H)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.stoneCandidateGenerator_isEssentiallySelfAdjoint
declarations.doc:
**Stone's theorem, existence.** The candidate generator of a strongly continuous unitary group
is essentially self-adjoint.
declarations.statement:
lemma stoneCandidateGenerator_isEssentiallySelfAdjoint (hU0 : U 0 = 1)
    (hUunit : ∀ t, U t ∈ unitary (H →L[ℂ] H)) (hUcont : ∀ ξ : H, Continuous (fun t : ℝ => U t ξ)) :
    (stoneCandidateGenerator (U := U) hUmul).IsEssentiallySelfAdjoint

modules.title: Stone's theorem: reconstruction of the group
modules.doc:
Stone's theorem, reconstruction: a unitary group is exp(i t T) for its generator.

## i. Overview

Let `T` be the candidate generator of a strongly continuous unitary group `U`, and `V t = exp(i t
T)` the unitary group of the spectral measure of its closure. For `x` in the domain of `T`, the
orbits `U t x` and `V t x` solve the same equation `w' = i T w` with the same initial value. Since
`T` is symmetric, `‖U t x - V t x‖²` has zero derivative, so the orbits agree. The domain is dense,
so `U = V`.

## ii. Key results

- `stoneReconstructionUnitaryGroup` : the group `exp(i t T)` of the generator.
- `stoneCandidateGenerator_domain_dense` : the domain of the candidate generator is dense.
- `stoneCandidateGenerator_reconstruction` : **Stone's theorem, reconstruction**: `U t = exp(i t
  T)`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The reconstructed unitary group
- B. Uniqueness for the evolution equation
- C. Reconstruction of the group

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.stoneReconstructionSpectralMeasure
declarations.doc:
The Cayley-transform spectral measure for `stoneCandidateGenerator hUmul`'s essential
self-adjoint closure.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def stoneReconstructionSpectralMeasure : WOTSpectralMeasure ℝ H

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.stoneReconstructionData
declarations.doc:
The domain-aware spectral theorem for `stoneCandidateGenerator hUmul`'s closure, built via the
Cayley transform from this Track's essential self-adjointness result.
declarations.statement:
lemma stoneReconstructionData :
    DomainAwareSelfAdjointSpectralTheorem (stoneCandidateGenerator (U := U) hUmul).closure
      (stoneReconstructionSpectralMeasure hU0 hUmul hUunit hUcont)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.stoneReconstructionUnitaryGroup
declarations.doc: The unitary group `exp(i t T)` of the closure of the candidate generator.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def stoneReconstructionUnitaryGroup (t : ℝ) : H →L[ℂ] H

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.hasDerivAt_generator_unique
declarations.doc:
Two curves through the same starting point, both solving `w' = i • T w` while remaining in
`T`'s domain, coincide everywhere: the standard Schrödinger-equation uniqueness argument, using
only that `T` is symmetric (so `⟪w, T w⟫` is real, killing the cross terms in `d/dt‖w‖²`).
declarations.statement:
lemma hasDerivAt_generator_unique {y z : ℝ → H} (hTsym : T.IsSymmetric)
    (hy_mem : ∀ t, y t ∈ T.domain) (hz_mem : ∀ t, z t ∈ T.domain)
    (hy_deriv : ∀ t, HasDerivAt y (Complex.I • T ⟨y t, hy_mem t⟩) t)
    (hz_deriv : ∀ t, HasDerivAt z (Complex.I • T ⟨z t, hz_mem t⟩) t)
    (h0 : y 0 = z 0) : ∀ t, y t = z t

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.stoneCandidateGenerator_reconstruction_of_mem_domain
declarations.doc:
**Stone's theorem, reconstruction direction.** `U` agrees with the concrete unitary group
`stoneReconstructionUnitaryGroup` on every vector in `stoneCandidateGenerator hUmul`'s domain.
declarations.statement:
lemma stoneCandidateGenerator_reconstruction_of_mem_domain
    (x : (stoneCandidateGenerator (U := U) hUmul).domain) (t : ℝ) :
    U t (x : H) = stoneReconstructionUnitaryGroup hU0 hUmul hUunit hUcont t (x : H)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.stoneCandidateGenerator_domain_dense
declarations.doc: The domain of the candidate generator is dense.
declarations.statement:
lemma stoneCandidateGenerator_domain_dense :
    Dense ((stoneCandidateGenerator (U := U) hUmul).domain : Set H)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.stoneCandidateGenerator_reconstruction
declarations.doc:
**Stone's theorem.** A strongly continuous unitary group is `exp(i t T)` for the closure `T` of
its candidate generator.
declarations.statement:
lemma stoneCandidateGenerator_reconstruction (x : H) (t : ℝ) :
    U t x = stoneReconstructionUnitaryGroup hU0 hUmul hUunit hUcont t x

modules.title: The unitary group of a self-adjoint operator
modules.doc:
The unitary group exp(i t T) of a self-adjoint operator and its differentiable orbits.

## i. Overview

For a self-adjoint operator `T` with spectral measure `μ`, the unitary group `exp(i t T)` is the
integral of `exp(i t λ)`. A vector `x` lies in the domain of `T` exactly when its orbit is
differentiable at `0`, and then the derivative at time `t` is `i T exp(i t T) x`.

## ii. Key results

- `expUnitaryGroup_strong_slope_tendsto` : the difference quotients of the orbit converge to `i T
  x`.
- `expUnitaryGroup_hasDerivAt` : orbits of domain vectors are differentiable at every time.
- `mem_domain_iff_expUnitaryGroup_hasDerivAt_zero` : the domain is the set of vectors with
  differentiable orbit.
- `expUnitaryGroup_star` : `exp(i t T)⋆ = exp(-i t T)`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Differentiability of orbits
- B. The domain via differentiable orbits
- C. The adjoint of the unitary group

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## B. The domain via differentiable orbits
## C. The adjoint of the unitary group

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.DomainAwareSelfAdjointSpectralTheorem.expUnitaryGroup_strong_slope_tendsto
declarations.doc:
For `x` in the domain of `T`, the difference quotients `(exp(i t T) x - x) / t` converge to `i T
x`.
declarations.statement:
lemma expUnitaryGroup_strong_slope_tendsto
    (D : DomainAwareSelfAdjointSpectralTheorem T μS) (x : T.domain) :
    Filter.Tendsto
      (fun t : ℝ => t⁻¹ • (D.expUnitaryGroup t x - x))
      (𝓝[≠] (0 : ℝ))
      (𝓝 (Complex.I • T x))

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.DomainAwareSelfAdjointSpectralTheorem.expUnitaryGroup_hasDerivAt_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma expUnitaryGroup_hasDerivAt_zero
    (D : DomainAwareSelfAdjointSpectralTheorem T μS) (x : T.domain) :
    HasDerivAt (fun t : ℝ => D.expUnitaryGroup t (x : H))
      (Complex.I • T x) 0

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.DomainAwareSelfAdjointSpectralTheorem.expUnitaryGroup_hasDerivAt
declarations.doc: For `x` in the domain of `T`, the orbit `t ↦ exp(i t T) x` is differentiable at every time.
declarations.statement:
lemma expUnitaryGroup_hasDerivAt
    (D : DomainAwareSelfAdjointSpectralTheorem T μS) (x : T.domain) (s : ℝ) :
    HasDerivAt (fun t : ℝ => D.expUnitaryGroup t (x : H))
      (D.expUnitaryGroup s (Complex.I • T x)) s

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.DomainAwareSelfAdjointSpectralTheorem.mem_domain_iff_expUnitaryGroup_strong_slope
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_domain_iff_expUnitaryGroup_strong_slope
    (D : DomainAwareSelfAdjointSpectralTheorem T μS) (x : H) :
    x ∈ T.domain ↔
      ∃ y : H, Filter.Tendsto
        (fun t : ℝ => t⁻¹ • (D.expUnitaryGroup t x - x))
        (𝓝[≠] (0 : ℝ)) (𝓝 y)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.DomainAwareSelfAdjointSpectralTheorem.mem_domain_iff_expUnitaryGroup_hasDerivAt_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_domain_iff_expUnitaryGroup_hasDerivAt_zero
    (D : DomainAwareSelfAdjointSpectralTheorem T μS) (x : H) :
    x ∈ T.domain ↔
      ∃ y : H, HasDerivAt (fun t : ℝ => D.expUnitaryGroup t x) y 0

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.DomainAwareSelfAdjointSpectralTheorem.expUnitaryGroup_star
declarations.doc: `exp(i t T)⋆ = exp(-i t T)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma expUnitaryGroup_star (D : DomainAwareSelfAdjointSpectralTheorem T μS) (t : ℝ) :
    star (D.expUnitaryGroup t) = D.expUnitaryGroup (-t)

modules.title: The generator of the unitary group
modules.doc:
The domain of T is the set of vectors with differentiable orbit under exp(i t T).

## i. Overview

A vector is in the domain of a self-adjoint operator `T` exactly when its orbit under `exp(i t T)`
is differentiable at `0`, and the derivative is then `i T x`.

## ii. Key results

- `mem_domain_iff_expUnitaryGroup_hasDerivAt` : the domain in terms of differentiable orbits.
- `expUnitaryGroup_hasDerivAt_iff` : the derivative of an orbit is `i T x`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The derivative at zero
- B. The derivative at an arbitrary time

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## B. The derivative at an arbitrary time

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.DomainAwareSelfAdjointSpectralTheorem.expUnitaryGroup_hasDerivAt_zero_iff
declarations.doc: If the orbit is differentiable at zero, its derivative is forced by the operator.
declarations.statement:
lemma expUnitaryGroup_hasDerivAt_zero_iff (x : H) (y : H) :
    HasDerivAt (fun t : ℝ => D.expUnitaryGroup t x) y 0 ↔
      ∃ hx : x ∈ T.domain, y = Complex.I • T ⟨x, hx⟩

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.DomainAwareSelfAdjointSpectralTheorem.mem_domain_iff_expUnitaryGroup_hasDerivAt
declarations.doc:
The generator domain is independent of the time at which differentiability is tested.  This
is the orbit-level form of Stone's theorem used by evolution arguments.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_domain_iff_expUnitaryGroup_hasDerivAt (x : H) (s : ℝ) :
    x ∈ T.domain ↔
      ∃ y : H, HasDerivAt (fun t : ℝ => D.expUnitaryGroup t x) y s

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.DomainAwareSelfAdjointSpectralTheorem.expUnitaryGroup_hasDerivAt_iff
declarations.doc: The derivative at an arbitrary time is uniquely the evolved generator vector.
declarations.statement:
lemma expUnitaryGroup_hasDerivAt_iff (x : H) (y : H) (s : ℝ) :
    HasDerivAt (fun t : ℝ => D.expUnitaryGroup t x) y s ↔
      ∃ hx : x ∈ T.domain,
        y = D.expUnitaryGroup s (Complex.I • T ⟨x, hx⟩)

modules.title: The unitary group preserves the domain of its generator
modules.doc:
The unitary group exp(i t T) preserves the domain of T and commutes with T.

## i. Overview

For a self-adjoint operator `T` with spectral measure `μ`, the unitary group `exp(i t T)` preserves
the domain of `T` and commutes with `T` there.

## ii. Key results

- `expUnitaryGroup_translate_mem` : `exp(i s T)` preserves the domain of `T`.
- `expUnitaryGroup_translate` : `T` commutes with `exp(i s T)` on its domain.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Invariance of the domain
- B. Commutation with the generator

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.DomainAwareSelfAdjointSpectralTheorem.expUnitaryGroup_translate_comm
declarations.doc:
The group law: `D.expUnitaryGroup t (D.expUnitaryGroup s x) = D.expUnitaryGroup (t + s) x`,
via `expUnitaryGroup_add` and the (definitional) fact that `WOT`-multiplication is composition.
declarations.statement:
lemma expUnitaryGroup_translate_comm (x : H) (s t : ℝ) :
    D.expUnitaryGroup t (D.expUnitaryGroup s x) = D.expUnitaryGroup (t + s) x

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.DomainAwareSelfAdjointSpectralTheorem.expUnitaryGroup_translate_mem
declarations.doc:
`exp(i s T)` preserves the domain of `T`: the orbit of `exp(i s T) x` is the orbit of `x`
shifted by `s`, so it is differentiable at `0`.
declarations.statement:
lemma expUnitaryGroup_translate_mem (x : T.domain) (s : ℝ) :
    D.expUnitaryGroup s (x : H) ∈ T.domain

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.DomainAwareSelfAdjointSpectralTheorem.expUnitaryGroup_translate
declarations.doc:
`T` commutes with `D.expUnitaryGroup s` on `T.domain`: for `x ∈ T.domain`,
`D.expUnitaryGroup s x ∈ T.domain` and `T (D.expUnitaryGroup s x) = D.expUnitaryGroup s (T x)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma expUnitaryGroup_translate (x : T.domain) (s : ℝ) :
    T ⟨D.expUnitaryGroup s (x : H), D.expUnitaryGroup_translate_mem x s⟩ =
      D.expUnitaryGroup s (T x)

modules.title: Criteria for essential self-adjointness
modules.doc:
Criteria for essential self-adjointness: trivial deficiency spaces, eigenbases.

## i. Overview

A densely defined symmetric operator is essentially self-adjoint when both deficiency spaces are
trivial. In particular a symmetric operator whose domain is the span of a Hilbert basis of
eigenvectors with real eigenvalues is essentially self-adjoint.

## ii. Key results

- `DefectIndexCertificate` : a densely defined symmetric operator with trivial deficiency spaces.
- `DefectIndexCertificate.essentiallySelfAdjoint` : such an operator is essentially self-adjoint.
- `isEssentiallySelfAdjoint_of_hilbertBasis_eigenvectors` : an operator diagonal in a Hilbert basis
  with real eigenvalues is essentially self-adjoint.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Von Neumann's defect criterion
- B. Essential self-adjointness from a Hilbert basis of eigenvectors

## iv. References

* Reed–Simon, *Methods of Modern Mathematical Physics I: Functional Analysis*,
  Theorem VIII.3.

sections.text:
## B. Essential self-adjointness from a Hilbert basis of eigenvectors

A symmetric operator whose domain is *exactly* the (algebraic) span of a Hilbert basis of
eigenvectors with real eigenvalues is essentially self-adjoint. This is the standard "eigenbasis
density" criterion for essential self-adjointness (see e.g. Reed–Simon, *Methods of Modern
Mathematical Physics I: Functional Analysis*, Theorem VIII.3): reality of the eigenvalues makes
`T ∓ i` bounded below by `1` on the eigenbasis span, and the Hilbert-basis expansion of an
arbitrary `y : H` (with coefficients divided by `λ - z`) produces, in the limit of its partial
sums, an explicit preimage of `y` under `T.closure ∓ i`.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.DefectIndexCertificate
declarations.doc: A densely defined symmetric operator whose deficiency spaces at `± i` are trivial.
declarations.statement:
structure DefectIndexCertificate (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) where
  symmetric : T.IsSymmetric
  dense : T.HasDenseDomain
  plus : T.defectNumber Complex.I = 0
  minus : T.defectNumber (-Complex.I) = 0

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.DefectIndexCertificate.essentiallySelfAdjoint
declarations.statement:
lemma DefectIndexCertificate.essentiallySelfAdjoint
    {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} (C : DefectIndexCertificate T) :
    T.IsEssentiallySelfAdjoint

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.DefectIndexCertificate.closure_isSelfAdjoint
declarations.statement:
lemma DefectIndexCertificate.closure_isSelfAdjoint
    {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} (C : DefectIndexCertificate T) :
    IsSelfAdjoint T.closure

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.ofSelfAdjoint_isEssentiallySelfAdjoint
declarations.doc: A self-adjoint operator is automatically an essentially self-adjoint core for itself.
declarations.statement:
lemma ofSelfAdjoint_isEssentiallySelfAdjoint
    {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} (hT : IsSelfAdjoint T) : T.IsEssentiallySelfAdjoint

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.isEssentiallySelfAdjoint_of_hilbertBasis_eigenvectors
declarations.doc:
**Essential self-adjointness from a Hilbert basis of eigenvectors.** If `T`'s domain is exactly
the (algebraic) span of a Hilbert basis `e`, and each basis vector `e i` is an eigenvector of `T`
with *real* eigenvalue `lam i`, then `T` is essentially self-adjoint.
declarations.statement:
lemma isEssentiallySelfAdjoint_of_hilbertBasis_eigenvectors
    (e : HilbertBasis ι ℂ H) (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (lam : ι → ℝ)
    (hdom : T.domain = Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range e))
    (heig : ∀ i, T ⟨e i, hdom ▸ Submodule.subset_span ⟨i, rfl⟩⟩ = (lam i : ℂ) • e i) :
    T.IsEssentiallySelfAdjoint

modules.title: Scalar and diagonal measures of a spectral measure
modules.doc:
The scalar and diagonal measures obtained by pairing a spectral measure with vectors.

## i. Overview

Pairing a spectral measure `μ` with two vectors gives the complex measure `S ↦ ⟪y, μ S x⟫`, and with
one vector the finite positive measure `μₓ S = ‖μ S x‖²`, the distribution of the observable in the
vector state `x`. A spectral measure is determined by its complex measures.

## ii. Key results

- `WOTSpectralMeasure.scalarMeasure` : the complex measure `S ↦ ⟪y, μ S x⟫`.
- `WOTSpectralMeasure.ext_of_scalarMeasure_eq` : a spectral measure is determined by its complex
  measures.
- `WOTSpectralMeasure.diagonalMeasure` : the measure `S ↦ ‖μ S x‖²`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The scalar (matrix-coefficient) measure and extensionality
- B. Positivity on the diagonal
- C. The diagonal (vector-state) measure

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. The scalar (matrix-coefficient) measure and extensionality

## B. Positivity on the diagonal

A weak spectral measure gives a positive measure in every vector state.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.innerEvaluation
declarations.doc: Evaluation of a WOT operator between two test vectors.
declarations.statement: def innerEvaluation (x y : H) : (H →WOT[ℂ] H) →+ ℂ

declarations.statement:
lemma continuous_innerEvaluation (x y : H) :
    Continuous (innerEvaluation (H := H) x y)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.scalarMeasure
declarations.doc:
The complex scalar measure obtained by testing a WOT spectral measure against `x` and `y`.
This is the measure used to state the unbounded reconstruction law weakly.
declarations.statement: def scalarMeasure (x y : H) : ComplexMeasure α

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.scalarMeasure_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma scalarMeasure_apply (x y : H) (S : Set α) :
    μS.scalarMeasure x y S = ⟪y, μS S x⟫_ℂ

A weak spectral measure is determined by all of its scalar matrix-coefficient measures.
This is the extensionality principle used when comparing two spectral constructions obtained by
different bounded or unbounded routes.
declarations.statement:
lemma ext_of_scalarMeasure_eq {μS νS : WOTSpectralMeasure α H}

declarations.statement:
lemma re_inner_nonneg (S : Set α) (x : H) :
    0 ≤ (⟪x, μS S x⟫_ℂ).re

lemma re_inner_eq_norm_sq (S : Set α) (x : H) :
    (⟪x, μS S x⟫_ℂ).re = ‖μS S x‖ ^ 2

lemma inner_eq_inner_projection (S : Set α) (x : H) :
    ⟪x, μS S x⟫_ℂ = ⟪μS S x, μS S x⟫_ℂ

lemma inner_eq_zero_of_disjoint {A B : Set α} (h : Disjoint A B)
    (hA : MeasurableSet A) (hB : MeasurableSet B) (x : H) :
    ⟪μS A x, μS B x⟫_ℂ = 0

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.diagonal_tsum
declarations.statement:
lemma diagonal_tsum {f : ℕ → Set α} (hf : ∀ i, MeasurableSet (f i))
    (hdisj : Pairwise (Disjoint on f)) (x : H) :
    ENNReal.ofReal (⟪x, μS (⋃ i, f i) x⟫_ℂ).re =
      ∑' i, ENNReal.ofReal (⟪x, μS (f i) x⟫_ℂ).re

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.diagonalMeasure
declarations.doc:
The positive scalar measure obtained by testing a weak PVM on a vector.

Its value on a measurable set is `ofReal (re ⟪x,E(S)x⟫)`. The projection identity below shows
that this is the usual vector-state spectral measure.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def diagonalMeasure (x : H) : Measure α
