lemma diagonalMeasure_apply (x : H) (S : Set α) (hS : MeasurableSet S) :
    μS.diagonalMeasure x S = ENNReal.ofReal (⟪x, μS S x⟫_ℂ).re

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.diagonalMeasure_apply_eq_norm_sq
declarations.statement:
lemma diagonalMeasure_apply_eq_norm_sq (x : H) (S : Set α) (hS : MeasurableSet S) :
    μS.diagonalMeasure x S = ENNReal.ofReal (‖μS S x‖ ^ 2)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.diagonalMeasure_univ
declarations.statement:
lemma diagonalMeasure_univ (x : H) :
    μS.diagonalMeasure x Set.univ = ENNReal.ofReal (‖x‖ ^ 2)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.diagonalMeasure_map
declarations.statement:
lemma diagonalMeasure_map {β : Type*} [MeasurableSpace β]
    (f : α → β) (hf : Measurable f) (x : H) :
    (μS.map f hf).diagonalMeasure x = Measure.map f (μS.diagonalMeasure x)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.diagonalMeasure_isFinite
declarations.statement: instance diagonalMeasure_isFinite (x : H) : IsFiniteMeasure (μS.diagonalMeasure x)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.diagonalMeasure_neg
declarations.statement:
lemma diagonalMeasure_neg (x : H) :
    μS.diagonalMeasure (-x) = μS.diagonalMeasure x

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.diagonalMeasure_I_smul
declarations.statement:
lemma diagonalMeasure_I_smul (x : H) :
    μS.diagonalMeasure (Complex.I • x) = μS.diagonalMeasure x

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.diagonalMeasure_smul
declarations.statement:
lemma diagonalMeasure_smul (c : ℂ) (x : H) :
    μS.diagonalMeasure (c • x) = ENNReal.ofReal (‖c‖ ^ 2) • μS.diagonalMeasure x

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.diagonalMeasure_parallelogram
declarations.statement:
lemma diagonalMeasure_parallelogram (x y : H) :
    μS.diagonalMeasure (x + y) + μS.diagonalMeasure (x - y) =
      (μS.diagonalMeasure x + μS.diagonalMeasure x) +
        (μS.diagonalMeasure y + μS.diagonalMeasure y)

modules.title: The spectral theorem, stated
modules.doc:
Essential self-adjointness and spectral resolutions of self-adjoint operators, with their domains.

## i. Overview

An operator is essentially self-adjoint when its closure is self-adjoint; a self-adjoint extension
is then unique. A spectral measure `μ` on `ℝ` resolves a self-adjoint operator `T` when `⟪y, T x⟫ =
∫ λ d⟪y, μ x⟫` for `x` in the domain of `T`, and it resolves `T` with its domain when in addition
the domain of `T` is the set of vectors with `∫ λ² dμₓ < ∞`.

## ii. Key results

- `SelfAdjointClosureData` : an operator with self-adjoint closure.
- `SelfAdjointClosureData.unique_selfAdjoint_extension` : the self-adjoint extension is unique.
- `IsWeakSpectralResolution` : `⟪y, T x⟫ = ∫ λ d⟪y, μ x⟫` on the domain of `T`.
- `SelfAdjointSpectralTheorem` : a spectral measure weakly resolving a self-adjoint operator.
- `spectralSquareMomentDomain` : the vectors with finite second moment.
- `DomainAwareSelfAdjointSpectralTheorem` : a spectral measure resolving a self-adjoint operator
  together with its domain.
- `DomainAwareSelfAdjointSpectralTheorem.expUnitaryGroup` : the strongly continuous unitary
  group attached to the spectral measure.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Essential self-adjointness and closure
  - A.1. Spectral resolutions with domain

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text:
## A. Essential self-adjointness and closure

An operator is essentially self-adjoint when its closure is self-adjoint.

### A.1. Spectral resolutions with domain

A spectral resolution only describes the operator on its domain. Equality of unbounded operators
also needs the domain to be the set of vectors of finite second moment.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.SelfAdjointClosureData
declarations.doc: The analytic input needed before applying the unbounded spectral theorem.
declarations.statement:
structure SelfAdjointClosureData
    (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) where
  essentiallySelfAdjoint : LinearPMap.IsEssentiallySelfAdjoint T

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.SelfAdjointClosureData.closure_isSelfAdjoint
declarations.doc: Essential self-adjointness makes the canonical closure self-adjoint.
declarations.statement: lemma closure_isSelfAdjoint : IsSelfAdjoint T.closure

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.SelfAdjointClosureData.closure_isClosed
declarations.doc: In particular, the canonical closure is closed.
declarations.statement: lemma closure_isClosed : T.closure.IsClosed

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.SelfAdjointClosureData.le_closure
declarations.doc: The core operator is contained in its canonical self-adjoint closure.
declarations.statement: lemma le_closure : T ≤ T.closure

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.SelfAdjointClosureData.unique_selfAdjoint_extension
declarations.doc: The canonical closure is the unique self-adjoint extension of the core.
declarations.statement:
lemma unique_selfAdjoint_extension {S : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H}
    (hTS : T ≤ S) (hS : IsSelfAdjoint S) : S = T.closure

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.SelfAdjointClosureData.ofDefectNumberEqZero
declarations.doc: Build closure data from the von Neumann defect-number criterion.
declarations.statement:
lemma ofDefectNumberEqZero
    (hT : T.IsSymmetric)
    (hdense : T.HasDenseDomain)
    (hpos : T.defectNumber Complex.I = 0)
    (hneg : T.defectNumber (-Complex.I) = 0) :
    SelfAdjointClosureData T

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.SelfAdjointClosureData.ofDefectIndexCertificate
declarations.doc: Package the reusable defect-index certificate as closure data.
declarations.statement:
lemma ofDefectIndexCertificate {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H}
    (C : DefectIndexCertificate T) : SelfAdjointClosureData T

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.IsWeakSpectralResolution
declarations.doc:
The spectral measure `μ` resolves `T`: for `x` in the domain of `T` the identity is integrable
against every `⟪y, μ x⟫`, and `⟪y, T x⟫ = ∫ λ d⟪y, μ x⟫`.
declarations.statement:
def IsWeakSpectralResolution
    (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H)
    (μS : WOTSpectralMeasure ℝ H) : Prop

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.SelfAdjointSpectralTheorem
declarations.doc:
The self-adjoint operator is reconstructed from its spectral measure in the weak sense.
The integrability clause is essential: the identity function is generally unbounded, so this
cannot be replaced by the bounded PVM axioms alone.
declarations.statement:
structure SelfAdjointSpectralTheorem
    (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H)
    (μS : WOTSpectralMeasure ℝ H) where
  isSelfAdjoint : IsSelfAdjoint T
  reconstruction : IsWeakSpectralResolution T μS

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.spectralSquareMomentDomain
declarations.doc: The vectors of finite second moment, `∫ λ² dμₓ < ∞`.
declarations.statement:
def spectralSquareMomentDomain
    (μS : WOTSpectralMeasure ℝ H) : Set H

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.mem_spectralSquareMomentDomain_iff
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_spectralSquareMomentDomain_iff
    (μS : WOTSpectralMeasure ℝ H) (x : H) :
    x ∈ spectralSquareMomentDomain μS ↔
      Integrable (fun (r : ℝ) ↦ r ^ 2) (μS.diagonalMeasure x)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.HasBoundedSpectralSupport
declarations.doc:
The spectral measure is supported in `[-C, C]`: it vanishes on every measurable set disjoint
from it.
declarations.statement:

modules.title: Integrating unbounded functions against a spectral measure
modules.doc:
The maximal spectral integral `∫ f dμ` of an unbounded function, built from bounded truncations.

## i. Overview

For a real measurable function `f` and a spectral measure `μ`, the integral `∫ f dμ` is defined on
the vectors `x` with `∫ f² dμₓ < ∞`, as the limit of the bounded integrals of the truncations of
`f`. It is densely defined, closable, symmetric and essentially self-adjoint. The construction is
carried out for the identity function `λ ↦ λ`, and a general `f` is handled by pushing `μ` forward
along `f`.

## ii. Key results

- `truncationFunction` : the spectral variable `λ` truncated to `[-n, n]`.
- `truncationIntegral` : the bounded integral of the `n`-th truncation.
- `spectralSquareMomentSubmodule` : the vectors of finite second moment, as a submodule.
- `maximalSpectralIntegral` : the integral `∫ λ dμ` on its maximal domain.
- `maximalSpectralIntegral_isSymmetric` : the maximal integral is symmetric.
- `maximalSpectralIntegral_hasDenseDomain` : its domain is dense.
- `maximalSpectralIntegral_isClosable` : it is closable.
- `measurableSpectralIntegral` : the integral of a measurable real function `f`, obtained by
  pushing the spectral measure forward along `f`.
- `boundedIntegral_tendsto_of_pointwise_tendsto_of_bound` : bounded spectral integrals converge
  when the integrands converge pointwise under a uniform bound.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Measurable real functional calculus
- B. Convergence of bounded spectral multipliers

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text:
## A. Measurable real functional calculus

The maximal construction is not tied to the coordinate function.  For a measurable real
multiplier `f`, push the PVM forward along `f` and apply the same construction to the new
spectral variable.  This is the concrete operator realization of the representation-free
`PVM.map` operation used by the affiliated-observable API.

## B. Convergence of bounded spectral multipliers

The next lemma is the reusable norm-convergence principle behind the resolvent construction.  It
only uses the PVM norm-square identity, so it is also useful for bounded functional calculus
approximations unrelated to the Cayley transform.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.truncationIntegral_sub_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma truncationIntegral_sub_apply (μS : WOTSpectralMeasure ℝ H) (n m : ℕ) (x : H) :
    truncationIntegral μS n x - truncationIntegral μS m x =
      boundedIntegral μS (fun r => truncationFunction n r - truncationFunction m r)
        ((truncationFunction_measurable n).sub (truncationFunction_measurable m))
        (by
          rcases truncationFunction_bounded n with ⟨Cn, hCn⟩
          rcases truncationFunction_bounded m with ⟨Cm, hCm⟩
          refine ⟨Cn + Cm, fun r => ?_⟩
          exact (norm_sub_le _ _).trans (add_le_add (hCn r) (hCm r))) x

models usually start with an operator on a smaller core and identify its closure with this

    (hsub : (maximalSpectralIntegral μS - Complex.I • (1 : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H)).toFun.range = ⊤) :
    (maximalSpectralIntegral μS).closure = maximalSpectralIntegral μS

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.truncationIntegral_inner_tendsto_weakIntegral
declarations.statement:
lemma truncationIntegral_inner_tendsto_weakIntegral
    (μS : WOTSpectralMeasure ℝ H) (x y : H)
    (hfi : (μS.scalarMeasure x y).Integrable id) :
    Filter.Tendsto
      (fun n : ℕ => ∫ᵛ r, realTruncationFunction n r ∂[
        ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ (E := ℂ); μS.scalarMeasure x y])

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.boundedIntegral_inner
declarations.statement:
lemma boundedIntegral_inner
    {α : Type*} [MeasurableSpace α] [Nonempty α]
    (μS : WOTSpectralMeasure α H) {f : α → ℂ} (hf : Measurable f)
    (hfb : ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ a, ‖f a‖ ≤ C) (x y : H)
    (hfinite : IsFiniteMeasure (μS.scalarMeasure x y).variation) :
    ⟪y, boundedIntegral μS f hf hfb x⟫_ℂ =
      ∫ᵛ a, f a ∂[ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℂ (E := ℂ);
        μS.scalarMeasure x y]

    (x y : H) :
    ⟪y, truncationIntegral μS n x⟫_ℂ =
      ∫ᵛ r, truncationFunction n r ∂[ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℂ (E := ℂ);

        ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℂ (E := ℂ); μS.scalarMeasure x y])

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.measurableSpectralIntegral
declarations.doc:
The maximal unbounded operator obtained by integrating a measurable real function against a
weak spectral measure.  It is defined by PVM pushforward, so no second truncation construction is
needed for each multiplier.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def measurableSpectralIntegral (μS : WOTSpectralMeasure ℝ H)
    (f : ℝ → ℝ) (hf : Measurable f) : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.measurableSpectralIntegral_id
declarations.statement:
lemma measurableSpectralIntegral_id (μS : WOTSpectralMeasure ℝ H) :
    measurableSpectralIntegral μS id measurable_id = maximalSpectralIntegral μS

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.measurableSpectralIntegral_comp
declarations.statement:
lemma measurableSpectralIntegral_comp
    (μS : WOTSpectralMeasure ℝ H) (f g : ℝ → ℝ)
    (hf : Measurable f) (hg : Measurable g) :
    measurableSpectralIntegral (μS.map f hf) g hg =
      measurableSpectralIntegral μS (g ∘ f) (hg.comp hf)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.measurableSpectralIntegral_domain
declarations.statement:
lemma measurableSpectralIntegral_domain (μS : WOTSpectralMeasure ℝ H)
    (f : ℝ → ℝ) (hf : Measurable f) :
    (measurableSpectralIntegral μS f hf).domain =
      spectralSquareMomentSubmodule (μS.map f hf)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.mem_measurableSpectralIntegral_domain_iff
declarations.doc:
The domain of `∫ f dE` is exactly the square-integrability domain of `f` against every
vector-state spectral measure.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_measurableSpectralIntegral_domain_iff (μS : WOTSpectralMeasure ℝ H)
    (f : ℝ → ℝ) (hf : Measurable f) (x : H) :
    x ∈ (measurableSpectralIntegral μS f hf).domain ↔
      Integrable (fun r : ℝ => f r ^ 2) (μS.diagonalMeasure x)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.measurableSpectralIntegral_domain_eq_top_of_bounded
declarations.doc:
A bounded measurable real multiplier has no unbounded domain restriction.  This is the
bounded-to-unbounded boundary in the reusable calculus: the same pushforward construction handles
both cases, and boundedness turns its square-moment domain into `⊤`.
declarations.statement:
lemma measurableSpectralIntegral_domain_eq_top_of_bounded
    (μS : WOTSpectralMeasure ℝ H) (f : ℝ → ℝ) (hf : Measurable f)
    (hfb : ∃ C : ℝ, 0 ≤ C ∧ ∀ r : ℝ, |f r| ≤ C) :
    (measurableSpectralIntegral μS f hf).domain = ⊤

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.measurableSpectralIntegral_inner_eq_complexWeakIntegral
declarations.doc:
Weak reconstruction for a measurable real multiplier.  The only integrability assumption is
the natural one on the original scalar spectral measure; the pushforward identity transports it
to the coordinate function of the new PVM.
declarations.statement:
lemma measurableSpectralIntegral_inner_eq_complexWeakIntegral
    (μS : WOTSpectralMeasure ℝ H) (f : ℝ → ℝ) (hf : Measurable f)
    (x : H) (hx : x ∈ (measurableSpectralIntegral μS f hf).domain) (y : H)
    (hfi : (μS.scalarMeasure x y).Integrable f) :
    ⟪y, (measurableSpectralIntegral μS f hf) ⟨x, hx⟩⟫_ℂ =
      μS.complexWeakIntegral (fun r : ℝ => (f r : ℂ)) x y

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.boundedIntegral_ofReal_eq_measurableSpectralIntegral
declarations.doc: For a bounded real function the bounded integral and the maximal integral are the same operator.
declarations.statement:
lemma boundedIntegral_ofReal_eq_measurableSpectralIntegral
    (μS : WOTSpectralMeasure ℝ H) (f : ℝ → ℝ) (hf : Measurable f)
    (hfb : ∃ C : ℝ, 0 ≤ C ∧ ∀ r : ℝ, |f r| ≤ C) (x : H) :
    boundedIntegral μS (fun r : ℝ => (f r : ℂ))
        (Complex.measurable_ofReal.comp hf)
        (by
          rcases hfb with ⟨C, _hC, hCbound⟩
          exact ⟨C, fun r => by
            simpa [Complex.norm_real, Real.norm_eq_abs] using hCbound r⟩) x =
      (measurableSpectralIntegral μS f hf)
        ⟨x, by
          rw [measurableSpectralIntegral_domain_eq_top_of_bounded μS f hf hfb]
          exact Submodule.mem_top⟩

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.boundedIntegral_tendsto_of_pointwise_tendsto_of_bound
declarations.statement:
lemma boundedIntegral_tendsto_of_pointwise_tendsto_of_bound
    {α : Type*} [MeasurableSpace α] [Nonempty α]
    (μS : WOTSpectralMeasure α H)
    {f : α → ℂ} {g : ℕ → α → ℂ} (x : H)
    (hf : Measurable f) (hg : ∀ n, Measurable (g n))
    (hfb : ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ a, ‖f a‖ ≤ C)
    (hgb : ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ n a, ‖g n a‖ ≤ C)
    (hlim : ∀ a, Filter.Tendsto (fun n => g n a) Filter.atTop (𝓝 (f a))) :
    Filter.Tendsto
      (fun n => boundedIntegral μS (g n) (hg n) (by
        rcases hgb with ⟨C, hC⟩
        exact ⟨C, hC n⟩) x)
      Filter.atTop
      (𝓝 (boundedIntegral μS f hf hfb x))

modules.title: The integral of the identity is self-adjoint
modules.doc:
The integral of the identity against a spectral measure on `ℝ` is self-adjoint.

## i. Overview

The integral of the identity against a spectral measure on `ℝ` has resolvents at `± i` given by the
bounded integrals of `1 / (λ ∓ i)`. So it is self-adjoint. An operator resolved by a spectral
measure equals this integral, which identifies its domain with the vectors of finite second moment.

## ii. Key results

- `resolventMultiplier` : the bounded function `λ ↦ (λ - z)⁻¹` for non-real `z`.
- `maximalSpectralIntegral_resolvent_range` : the shifts by non-real `z` of the maximal integral
  are onto.
- `maximalSpectralIntegral_isSelfAdjoint` : the integral of the identity is self-adjoint.
- `measurableSpectralIntegral_isSelfAdjoint` : so is the integral of any measurable real function.
- `maximalSpectralIntegral_eq_of_isSelfAdjoint_of_isWeakSpectralResolution` : a self-adjoint
  operator resolved by a spectral measure equals the integral of the identity.
- `domainAwareSelfAdjointSpectralTheorem_of_isWeakSpectralResolution` : a spectral measure resolving
  a self-adjoint operator resolves it together with its domain.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Weighted diagonal measures
- B. The two Cayley resolvents
- C. Resolvent values of the maximal realization
- D. The canonical self-adjoint realization
- E. Uniqueness of the domain-aware realization
- F. The canonical operator equality

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text:
## A. Weighted diagonal measures

Applying a bounded spectral multiplier changes the vector spectral measure by the squared
multiplier.  This is the measure-level statement that turns bounded resolvents into vectors in the
maximal square-moment domain.

The unit bound used by the first resolvent construction is convenient, but it is not
mathematically essential.  Keeping the finite-bound version separate makes the later general
resolvent API usable at arbitrary non-real parameters without weakening any of the existing
callers.

## B. The two Cayley resolvents

These are the bounded multipliers which realize the inverse of the shifts by `± i`.  Their
construction is independent of any pre-existing self-adjoint operator; it is purely the real PVM
calculus applied to the scalar functions `(r ± i)⁻¹`.

## C. Resolvent values of the maximal realization

The range statements above show that the two shifted maximal realizations are onto.  The
following sharpen them to an actual value formula for their partial inverses.  This is the
operator-level form of the bounded Borel identities

`(λ + i)⁻¹ (λ + i) = 1` and `(λ - i)⁻¹ (λ - i) = 1`.

These lemmas are intentionally stated for `LinearPMap.inverse`: they do not introduce a second
unbounded-operator hierarchy, and they are exactly what the Cayley adapter needs when converting
between a self-adjoint operator and its bounded unitary transform.

## D. The canonical self-adjoint realization

The preceding two range lemmas are the concrete Cayley-resolvent calculation.  They are worth
keeping separate from the abstract range criterion: this theorem is the point at which a real PVM
itself produces a self-adjoint (closed) unbounded operator, with no prior operator or domain datum.

## E. Uniqueness of the domain-aware realization

A self-adjoint operator resolved by a spectral measure is the integral of the identity on its
maximal domain.

## F. The canonical operator equality

The domain-aware certificate contains exactly the extra hypothesis needed by the uniqueness
theorem: its operator domain is the square-moment domain of its PVM.  Exposing this equality as a
method keeps later Cayley and representation proofs from reconstructing the same argument.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.diagonalMeasure_boundedIntegral_eq_withDensity
declarations.statement:
lemma diagonalMeasure_boundedIntegral_eq_withDensity
    {α : Type*} [MeasurableSpace α] [Nonempty α]
    (μS : WOTSpectralMeasure α H) {g : α → ℂ} (hg : Measurable g)
    (hgb : ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ a, ‖g a‖ ≤ C) (x : H) :
    μS.diagonalMeasure (boundedIntegral μS g hg hgb x) =
      Measure.withDensity (μS.diagonalMeasure x)
        (fun a => ENNReal.ofReal (‖g a‖ ^ 2))

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.maximalSpectralIntegral_apply_boundedMultiplier
declarations.statement:
lemma maximalSpectralIntegral_apply_boundedMultiplier
    (μS : WOTSpectralMeasure ℝ H) {g : ℝ → ℂ} (hg : Measurable g)
    (hgb : ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ a, ‖g a‖ ≤ C)
    (hcoord : ∀ a : ℝ, ‖(a : ℂ) * g a‖ ≤ 1)
    (hcoord_meas : Measurable (fun a : ℝ => (a : ℂ) * g a))
    (x : H) :
    (maximalSpectralIntegral μS)
        ⟨boundedIntegral μS g hg hgb x,
          boundedMultiplier_mem_spectralSquareMomentDomain (α := ℝ) μS hg hgb hcoord x⟩ =
      boundedIntegral μS (fun a : ℝ => (a : ℂ) * g a) hcoord_meas
        ⟨1, hcoord⟩ x

    (hcoord_meas : Measurable (fun a : ℝ => (a : ℂ) * g a))
    (x : H) :

      boundedIntegral μS (fun a : ℝ => (a : ℂ) * g a) hcoord_meas

          rcases hcoord with ⟨C, _hC0, hC⟩
          exact ⟨C, hC⟩) x

lemma maximalSpectralIntegral_shift_range_of_multiplier

    (hcoord_meas : Measurable (fun a : ℝ => (a : ℂ) * g a))
    (hidentity : ∀ a : ℝ, (a : ℂ) * g a + c * g a = 1) :

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.maximalSpectralIntegral_resolvent_range
declarations.doc:
Every non-real shift of the canonical spectral integral is onto.  This is the concrete range
form of the resolvent theorem, proved directly from the bounded scalar multiplier
`r ↦ (r - z)⁻¹`.
declarations.statement:
lemma maximalSpectralIntegral_resolvent_range {z : ℂ} (hz : z.im ≠ 0) :
    (maximalSpectralIntegral μS - z • (1 : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H)).toFun.range = ⊤

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.maximalSpectralIntegral_resolvent_inverse_apply
declarations.doc:
The value of the inverse of a general non-real shift is the corresponding bounded spectral
multiplier.  This is the operator-level resolvent formula, including its domain proof.
declarations.statement:
lemma maximalSpectralIntegral_resolvent_inverse_apply {z : ℂ} (hz : z.im ≠ 0) (x : H) :
    (maximalSpectralIntegral μS - z • (1 : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H)).inverse
        ⟨x, by
          rw [LinearPMap.inverse_domain, maximalSpectralIntegral_resolvent_range hz]
          exact Submodule.mem_top⟩ =
      boundedIntegral μS (resolventMultiplier z) (resolventMultiplier_measurable z)
        (resolventMultiplier_bounded hz) x

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.maximalSpectralIntegral_plus_resolvent_range
declarations.statement:
lemma maximalSpectralIntegral_plus_resolvent_range :
    (maximalSpectralIntegral μS + Complex.I • (1 : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H)).toFun.range = ⊤

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.maximalSpectralIntegral_minus_resolvent_range
declarations.statement:
lemma maximalSpectralIntegral_minus_resolvent_range :
    (maximalSpectralIntegral μS - Complex.I • (1 : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H)).toFun.range = ⊤

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.maximalSpectralIntegral_plus_resolvent_inverse_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma maximalSpectralIntegral_plus_resolvent_inverse_apply (x : H) :
    (maximalSpectralIntegral μS + Complex.I • (1 : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H)).inverse
        ⟨x, by
          rw [LinearPMap.inverse_domain, maximalSpectralIntegral_plus_resolvent_range]
          exact Submodule.mem_top⟩ =
      boundedIntegral μS plusResolventMultiplier plusResolventMultiplier_measurable
        plusResolventMultiplier_bounded x

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.maximalSpectralIntegral_minus_resolvent_inverse_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma maximalSpectralIntegral_minus_resolvent_inverse_apply (x : H) :
    (maximalSpectralIntegral μS - Complex.I • (1 : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H)).inverse
        ⟨x, by
          rw [LinearPMap.inverse_domain, maximalSpectralIntegral_minus_resolvent_range]
          exact Submodule.mem_top⟩ =
      boundedIntegral μS minusResolventMultiplier minusResolventMultiplier_measurable

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.maximalSpectralIntegral_isSelfAdjoint
declarations.statement:
lemma maximalSpectralIntegral_isSelfAdjoint (μS : WOTSpectralMeasure ℝ H) :
    IsSelfAdjoint (maximalSpectralIntegral μS)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.maximalSpectralIntegral_sub_smul_surjective
declarations.doc:
The canonical maximal realization has a surjective shifted operator at every non-real
spectral parameter.  The preceding explicit `± Complex.I` calculations establish
self-adjointness; this general form then follows from the self-adjoint resolvent theorem.
declarations.statement:
lemma maximalSpectralIntegral_sub_smul_surjective
    (μS : WOTSpectralMeasure ℝ H) {z : ℂ} (hz : z.im ≠ 0) :
    Function.Surjective
      (maximalSpectralIntegral μS - z • (1 : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H)).toFun

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.maximalSpectralIntegral_mem_resolventSet
declarations.doc:
Every non-real point belongs to the resolvent set of the canonical maximal spectral
integral.  This is the public `resolventSet` form of the preceding range theorem and the
self-adjoint resolvent criterion; downstream users can therefore use the ordinary resolvent API
without unpacking the Cayley shifts or the spectral multiplier construction.
declarations.statement:
lemma maximalSpectralIntegral_mem_resolventSet
    (μS : WOTSpectralMeasure ℝ H) {z : ℂ} (hz : z.im ≠ 0) :
    z ∈ LinearPMap.resolventSet (maximalSpectralIntegral μS)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.maximalSpectralIntegral_resolvent_apply
declarations.doc:
Resolvent notation for the canonical spectral integral is exactly the bounded spectral
multiplier `λ ↦ (λ - z)⁻¹`.  The subtype in the left-hand side is the canonical full-domain
element supplied by the resolvent theorem.
declarations.statement:
lemma maximalSpectralIntegral_resolvent_apply {z : ℂ} (hz : z.im ≠ 0) (x : H) :
    LinearPMap.resolvent (maximalSpectralIntegral μS) z
        ⟨x, by
          rw [LinearPMap.inverse_domain, maximalSpectralIntegral_resolvent_range hz]
          exact Submodule.mem_top⟩ =
      boundedIntegral μS (resolventMultiplier z) (resolventMultiplier_measurable z)
        (resolventMultiplier_bounded hz) x

declarations.statement:
lemma measurableSpectralIntegral_norm_sq
    (μS : WOTSpectralMeasure ℝ H) (f : ℝ → ℝ) (hf : Measurable f)
    (x : H) (hx : x ∈ (measurableSpectralIntegral μS f hf).domain) :

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.domainAwareSelfAdjointSpectralTheorem_of_isWeakSpectralResolution
declarations.doc:
**A spectral resolution determines the domain.** If `μ` resolves the self-adjoint operator `T`
and the domain of `T` has finite second moments, then the domain of `T` is exactly the set of
vectors of finite second moment.

    (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (hT : _root_.IsSelfAdjoint T)

    DomainAwareSelfAdjointSpectralTheorem T μS

modules.title: Spectral measures taking values `0` and `1`
modules.doc:
A `{0, 1}`-valued spectral measure on `ℝ` with bounded support is a point mass.

## i. Overview

A measure on `ℝ` with bounded support that only takes the values `0` and `1` is a point mass.
Bisecting the support and keeping the half of measure `1` gives nested intervals shrinking to the
point. As a consequence, a bounded self-adjoint operator all of whose spectral projections are `0`
or `1` is a scalar multiple of the identity.

## ii. Key results

- `WOTSpectralMeasure.bisect` : the nested bisection intervals.
- `WOTSpectralMeasure.bisectPoint` : the point the bisection intervals shrink to.
- `WOTSpectralMeasure.exists_forall_notMem_measure_eq_zero` : such a measure vanishes on every set
  avoiding some point `r`.
- `eq_smul_one_of_forall_spectralMeasure_eq_zero_or_one` : a bounded self-adjoint operator with
  only trivial spectral projections is a scalar multiple of the identity.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Bisection intervals
- B. The limit point of the bisection
- C. Operators with trivial spectral projections

## iv. References

* None.

## C. Operators with trivial spectral projections

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.bisectStep
declarations.doc:
One bisection step: split `[p.1, p.2]` at its midpoint and keep the left half if it has measure
`1`, otherwise the right half.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def bisectStep (p : ℝ × ℝ) : ℝ × ℝ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.bisect
declarations.doc: The `n`-th bisection interval's endpoints, starting from `(a, b)`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def bisect (a b : ℝ) : ℕ → ℝ × ℝ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.bisectStep_fst_le_snd
declarations.statement:
lemma bisectStep_fst_le_snd {p : ℝ × ℝ} (h : p.1 ≤ p.2) :
    (bisectStep μ p).1 ≤ (bisectStep μ p).2

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.bisectStep_sub
declarations.statement:
lemma bisectStep_sub (p : ℝ × ℝ) :
    (bisectStep μ p).2 - (bisectStep μ p).1 = (p.2 - p.1) / 2

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.bisectStep_fst_le
declarations.statement: lemma bisectStep_fst_le {p : ℝ × ℝ} (h : p.1 ≤ p.2) : p.1 ≤ (bisectStep μ p).1

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.bisectStep_snd_le
declarations.statement: lemma bisectStep_snd_le {p : ℝ × ℝ} (h : p.1 ≤ p.2) : (bisectStep μ p).2 ≤ p.2

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.bisectStep_subset
declarations.statement:
lemma bisectStep_subset {p : ℝ × ℝ} (h : p.1 ≤ p.2) :
    Icc (bisectStep μ p).1 (bisectStep μ p).2 ⊆ Icc p.1 p.2

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.bisect_fst_le_snd
declarations.statement:
lemma bisect_fst_le_snd {a b : ℝ} (hab : a ≤ b) :
    ∀ n, (bisect μ a b n).1 ≤ (bisect μ a b n).2

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.bisect_sub
declarations.statement:
lemma bisect_sub (a b : ℝ) :
    ∀ n, (bisect μ a b n).2 - (bisect μ a b n).1 = (b - a) / 2 ^ n

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.bisect_fst_mono
declarations.statement:
lemma bisect_fst_mono {a b : ℝ} (hab : a ≤ b) (n : ℕ) :
    (bisect μ a b n).1 ≤ (bisect μ a b (n + 1)).1

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.bisect_snd_mono
declarations.statement:
lemma bisect_snd_mono {a b : ℝ} (hab : a ≤ b) (n : ℕ) :
    (bisect μ a b (n + 1)).2 ≤ (bisect μ a b n).2

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.bisect_subset
declarations.statement:
lemma bisect_subset {a b : ℝ} (hab : a ≤ b) (n : ℕ) :
    Icc (bisect μ a b (n + 1)).1 (bisect μ a b (n + 1)).2 ⊆
      Icc (bisect μ a b n).1 (bisect μ a b n).2

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.bisectStep_measure_one
declarations.doc:
If the whole interval has measure `1`, the bisected interval does too: whichever half
`bisectStep` keeps is forced to have measure `1` by additivity across the (disjoint) split.
declarations.statement:
lemma bisectStep_measure_one (h01 : ∀ E : Set ℝ, MeasurableSet E → μ E = 0 ∨ μ E = 1)
    {p : ℝ × ℝ} (h : p.1 ≤ p.2) (hμ : μ (Icc p.1 p.2) = 1) :
    μ (Icc (bisectStep μ p).1 (bisectStep μ p).2) = 1

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.bisect_measure_one
declarations.statement:
lemma bisect_measure_one (h01 : ∀ E : Set ℝ, MeasurableSet E → μ E = 0 ∨ μ E = 1)
    {a b : ℝ} (hab : a ≤ b) (hμ : μ (Icc a b) = 1) :
    ∀ n, μ (Icc (bisect μ a b n).1 (bisect μ a b n).2) = 1

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.bisect_diff_measure_zero
declarations.doc: The half discarded at each bisection step has measure `0`.
declarations.statement:
lemma bisect_diff_measure_zero
    (h01 : ∀ E : Set ℝ, MeasurableSet E → μ E = 0 ∨ μ E = 1)
    {a b : ℝ} (hab : a ≤ b) (hμ : μ (Icc a b) = 1) (n : ℕ) :
    μ (Icc (bisect μ a b n).1 (bisect μ a b n).2 \
        Icc (bisect μ a b (n + 1)).1 (bisect μ a b (n + 1)).2) = 0

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.bisectFst_mono
declarations.statement: lemma bisectFst_mono (hab : a ≤ b) : Monotone (fun n => (bisect μ a b n).1)

declarations.statement: lemma bisectSnd_anti (hab : a ≤ b) : Antitone (fun n => (bisect μ a b n).2)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.bisectSnd_le_start
declarations.statement: lemma bisectSnd_le_start (hab : a ≤ b) (n : ℕ) : (bisect μ a b n).2 ≤ b

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.bisectFst_ge_start
declarations.statement: lemma bisectFst_ge_start (hab : a ≤ b) (n : ℕ) : a ≤ (bisect μ a b n).1

lemma bddBelow_bisectSnd (hab : a ≤ b) :
    BddBelow (Set.range (fun n => (bisect μ a b n).2))

declarations.doc: The limit point of the bisection.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def bisectPoint (_hab : a ≤ b) : ℝ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.tendsto_bisectFst
declarations.statement:
lemma tendsto_bisectFst (hab : a ≤ b) :
    Tendsto (fun n => (bisect μ a b n).1) atTop (𝓝 (bisectPoint μ hab))

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.tendsto_bisectSub
declarations.statement:
lemma tendsto_bisectSub (a b : ℝ) :
    Tendsto (fun n => (bisect μ a b n).2 - (bisect μ a b n).1) atTop (𝓝 0)

declarations.statement:
lemma tendsto_bisectSnd (hab : a ≤ b) :
    Tendsto (fun n => (bisect μ a b n).2) atTop (𝓝 (bisectPoint μ hab))

declarations.statement:
lemma bisectFst_le_bisectPoint (hab : a ≤ b) (n : ℕ) :
    (bisect μ a b n).1 ≤ bisectPoint μ hab

declarations.statement:
lemma bisectPoint_le_bisectSnd (hab : a ≤ b) (n : ℕ) :
    bisectPoint μ hab ≤ (bisect μ a b n).2

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.iInter_bisectIcc
declarations.doc: The bisection intervals shrink to exactly the bisection point.
declarations.statement:
lemma iInter_bisectIcc (hab : a ≤ b) :
    ⋂ n, Icc (bisect μ a b n).1 (bisect μ a b n).2 = {bisectPoint μ hab}

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.measure_singleton_bisectPoint
declarations.doc:
**The bisection point carries the full measure.** Since every bisection interval has measure
`1` and the intervals shrink to exactly `{bisectPoint}`, continuity from above (`Mathlib`'s
`tendsto_vectorMeasure_iInter_atTop_nat`) forces `μ {bisectPoint} = 1`.
declarations.statement:
lemma measure_singleton_bisectPoint
    (h01 : ∀ E : Set ℝ, MeasurableSet E → μ E = 0 ∨ μ E = 1) (hab : a ≤ b)
    (hμ : μ (Icc a b) = 1) :
    μ {bisectPoint μ hab} = 1

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure.exists_forall_notMem_measure_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**A `{0, 1}`-valued measure with bounded support is a point mass**: every measurable set
avoiding some point `r` has measure `0`.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_forall_notMem_measure_eq_zero
    (h01 : ∀ E : Set ℝ, MeasurableSet E → μ E = 0 ∨ μ E = 1) (hab : a ≤ b)
    (hμ : μ (Icc a b) = 1) :
    ∃ r : ℝ, μ {r} = 1 ∧ ∀ E : Set ℝ, MeasurableSet E → r ∉ E → μ E = 0

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.eq_smul_one_of_forall_spectralMeasure_eq_zero_or_one
declarations.doc:
**Schur's-lemma capstone.** If every Borel spectral projection of a bounded self-adjoint
operator `S` is trivial (`0` or `1`), `S` is a scalar multiple of the identity — without ever
separately identifying `spectrum ℝ S`. Combined with irreducibility forcing every spectral
projection to be `0` or `1`, this finishes Schur's lemma for a Weyl-family representation.
declarations.statement:
lemma eq_smul_one_of_forall_spectralMeasure_eq_zero_or_one
    (S : H →L[ℂ] H) (hSA : IsSelfAdjoint S)
    (h01 : ∀ E : Set ℝ, MeasurableSet E →
      boundedSelfAdjointSpectralMeasure S hSA E = 0 ∨
        boundedSelfAdjointSpectralMeasure S hSA E = 1) :
    ∃ c : ℂ, S = c • (1 : H →L[ℂ] H)

modules.title: The commutant of a representation of continuous functions
modules.doc:
Every bounded operator commuting with the range of `Φ` commutes with its spectral measure.

## i. Overview

The spectral measure of `Φ` commutes with every unitary operator commuting with the range of `Φ`.
A bounded operator commuting with the range of `Φ` lies in the commutant of the range, a closed
⋆-subalgebra of `B(H)` and hence a C⋆-algebra, which is spanned by its unitary elements. So the
spectral measure commutes with every operator commuting with the range of `Φ`.

## ii. Key results

- `starHomSpectralMeasure_commute_of_commute` : the spectral measure of `Φ` commutes with every
  bounded operator commuting with the range of `Φ`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Arbitrary operators in the commutant

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomCommutant
declarations.doc: The commutant of the range of `Φ`, a ⋆-subalgebra of the bounded operators.
declarations.statement: def starHomCommutant : StarSubalgebra ℂ (H →L[ℂ] H)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.mem_starHomCommutant_iff
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_starHomCommutant_iff {T : H →L[ℂ] H} :
    T ∈ starHomCommutant Φ ↔ ∀ f : C(X, ℂ), Commute (Φ f) T

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomCommutant_isClosed
declarations.statement: instance starHomCommutant_isClosed : IsClosed (starHomCommutant Φ : Set (H →L[ℂ] H))

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomSpectralOperator_commute_of_commute
declarations.doc:
**The spectral operators commute with the commutant**: every bounded operator commuting with
the range of `Φ` commutes with each spectral operator of `Φ`. A bounded operator commuting with the
range is a combination of four unitary operators in the C⋆-algebra of such operators, and the
spectral operators commute with unitaries commuting with the range.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomSpectralMeasure_commute_of_commute
declarations.doc:
**The spectral measure commutes with the commutant**: every bounded operator commuting with
the range of `Φ` commutes with each spectral projection of `Φ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma starHomSpectralMeasure_commute_of_commute {T : H →L[ℂ] H}
    (hT : ∀ f : C(X, ℂ), Commute (Φ f) T) (S : Set X) :
    starHomSpectralMeasure Φ S * ContinuousLinearMapWOT.ofCLM T =
      ContinuousLinearMapWOT.ofCLM T * starHomSpectralMeasure Φ S

modules.title: The functional calculus of a representation of continuous functions
modules.doc:
The bounded integral against the spectral measure of a ⋆-homomorphism `Φ` is `Φ`.

## i. Overview

The spectral measure of a unital ⋆-homomorphism `Φ : C(X, ℂ) → B(H)` reconstructs `Φ` on real
continuous functions. Since the bounded integral against a spectral measure is linear, it
reconstructs `Φ` on all complex continuous functions: `∫ f dE = Φ f`.

## ii. Key results

- `starHomSpectralMeasure_boundedIntegral_real` : the integral of a real continuous function.
- `starHomSpectralMeasure_boundedIntegral` : the integral of a complex continuous function is
  `Φ f`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Real and imaginary parts
- B. The diagonal measure
- C. The integral of a continuous function

## iv. References

* None.

The imaginary part of a continuous complex function on a compact space, as a compactly
supported continuous real function.
declarations.statement: def imCompact (f : C(X, ℂ)) : CompactlySupportedContinuousMap X ℝ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.realToComplex_reCompact_add_I_smul
declarations.statement:
lemma realToComplex_reCompact_add_I_smul (f : C(X, ℂ)) :
    realToComplex (reCompact f) + Complex.I • realToComplex (imCompact f) = f

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomSpectralMeasure_diagonalMeasure
declarations.doc:
The diagonal measure `S ↦ ‖E(S) x‖²` of the spectral measure of `Φ` is the Riesz measure of
the vector state of `x`.
declarations.statement:
lemma starHomSpectralMeasure_diagonalMeasure (x : H) :
    (starHomSpectralMeasure Φ).diagonalMeasure x = starHomScalarMeasure Φ x

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.integral_starHomScalarMeasure_real
declarations.doc:
The integral of a real continuous function against the Riesz measure of the vector state of
`x` is the expectation of its operator.
declarations.statement:
lemma integral_starHomScalarMeasure_real (u : CompactlySupportedContinuousMap X ℝ) (x : H) :
    ∫ z, (u z : ℂ) ∂starHomScalarMeasure Φ x = ⟪x, starHomRealOperator Φ u x⟫_ℂ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.integral_starHomScalarMeasure
declarations.doc:
The vector state of `x` in the representation `Φ` is integration against its Riesz measure:
`⟪x, Φ f x⟫ = ∫ f dμₓ` for every continuous `f`.
declarations.statement:
lemma integral_starHomScalarMeasure (f : C(X, ℂ)) (x : H) :
    ∫ z, f z ∂starHomScalarMeasure Φ x = ⟪x, Φ f x⟫_ℂ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.boundedIntegral_bound_of_continuous
declarations.statement: lemma boundedIntegral_bound_of_continuous (f : C(X, ℂ)) : ∃ C, ∀ z, ‖f z‖ ≤ C

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomSpectralMeasure_boundedIntegral_real
declarations.doc:
The bounded integral of a real continuous function against the spectral measure of `Φ` is
`Φ` of that function.
declarations.statement:
lemma starHomSpectralMeasure_boundedIntegral_real (u : CompactlySupportedContinuousMap X ℝ) :
    ContinuousLinearMapWOT.toCLM
      (WOTSpectralMeasure.boundedIntegral (starHomSpectralMeasure Φ)
        (fun z => (u z : ℂ)) (by fun_prop) ⟨‖u.toContinuousMap‖, fun z => by
          simpa using u.toContinuousMap.norm_coe_le_norm z⟩) = starHomRealOperator Φ u

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomSpectralMeasure_boundedIntegral
declarations.doc:
**The spectral measure of `Φ` reconstructs `Φ`**: the bounded integral of a continuous
function `f` against `starHomSpectralMeasure Φ` is `Φ f`.
declarations.statement:
lemma starHomSpectralMeasure_boundedIntegral (f : C(X, ℂ)) :
    ContinuousLinearMapWOT.toCLM
      (WOTSpectralMeasure.boundedIntegral (starHomSpectralMeasure Φ) f f.continuous.measurable
        (boundedIntegral_bound_of_continuous f)) = Φ f

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomSpectralMeasure_boundedIntegral_map
declarations.doc:
**Change of spectral variable**: integrating a bounded measurable function `g` against the
pushforward of the spectral measure of `Φ` along a measurable map `f` is integrating `g ∘ f`
against the spectral measure itself.
declarations.statement:
lemma starHomSpectralMeasure_boundedIntegral_map {β : Type*} [MeasurableSpace β] [Nonempty β]
    {f : X → β} (hf : Measurable f) {g : β → ℂ} (hg : Measurable g)
    (hbg : ∃ C, ∀ b, ‖g b‖ ≤ C) :
    WOTSpectralMeasure.boundedIntegral ((starHomSpectralMeasure Φ).map f hf) g hg hbg =
      WOTSpectralMeasure.boundedIntegral (starHomSpectralMeasure Φ) (g ∘ f) (hg.comp hf)
        (by obtain ⟨C, hC⟩ := hbg; exact ⟨C, fun z => hC (f z)⟩)

modules.title: The spectral forms of a representation of continuous functions
modules.doc:
Complex measures `⟪y, E(·) x⟫` of a unital ⋆-homomorphism `C(X, ℂ) → B(H)` and their sesquilinear
forms.

## i. Overview

For a unital ⋆-homomorphism `Φ` from the continuous functions on a compact Hausdorff space to the
bounded operators of a Hilbert space, the functional `f ↦ ⟪x, Φ f y⟫` is given, by the
Riesz–Markov–Kakutani theorem and polarization, by a complex measure. This is the construction of
`UnitaryInfra.SesquilinearForm` with the continuous functional calculus of a normal operator
replaced by an arbitrary ⋆-homomorphism, so that it applies to the joint spectral theory of
commuting families.

## ii. Key results

- `starHomScalarMeasure` : the measure representing `f ↦ ⟪x, Φ f x⟫`.
- `polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure` : the complex measure representing `f ↦ ⟪y, Φ f x⟫`.
- `starHomSesquilinearForm` : the bounded sesquilinear form of a measurable set.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Positive scalar functionals from a ⋆-homomorphism
- B. Sesquilinearity of the polarized measure
- C. Polarization
- D. Riesz representation of the polarized measure

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. Positive scalar functionals from a ⋆-homomorphism
## B. Sesquilinearity of the polarized measure
## D. Riesz representation of the polarized measure

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.realToComplex
declarations.doc:
Regard a real-valued continuous function on the spectrum of a normal operator as a complex
valued one.  Keeping this map explicit prevents the real/complex scalar changes in the Riesz
construction from being hidden in coercions.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def realToComplex
    (f : CompactlySupportedContinuousMap (X) ℝ) :
    C(X, ℂ)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.realToComplex_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma realToComplex_apply
    (f : CompactlySupportedContinuousMap (X) ℝ) (z : X) :
    realToComplex f z = f z

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.realToComplex_add
declarations.statement:
lemma realToComplex_add
    (f g : CompactlySupportedContinuousMap (X) ℝ) :
    realToComplex (f + g) =
      realToComplex f + realToComplex g

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.realToComplex_smul
declarations.statement:
lemma realToComplex_smul (r : ℝ)
    (f : CompactlySupportedContinuousMap (X) ℝ) :
    realToComplex (r • f) =
      (r : ℂ) • realToComplex f

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomRealOperator
declarations.doc:
The operator obtained by applying the complex continuous functional calculus to a real test
function.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def starHomRealOperator
    (f : CompactlySupportedContinuousMap (X) ℝ) : H →L[ℂ] H

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomRealOperator_isSelfAdjoint
declarations.statement:
lemma starHomRealOperator_isSelfAdjoint
    (f : CompactlySupportedContinuousMap (X) ℝ) :
    IsSelfAdjoint (starHomRealOperator Φ f)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomRealOperator_nonneg
declarations.statement:
lemma starHomRealOperator_nonneg
    (f : CompactlySupportedContinuousMap (X) ℝ)
    (hf : ∀ z, 0 ≤ f z) :
    ContinuousLinearMap.IsPositive (starHomRealOperator Φ f)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomScalarFunctional
declarations.doc:
The vector state of the continuous functional calculus, restricted to real test functions.
The positivity proof is the square-root argument above; this is the exact input required by
Riesz--Markov.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def starHomScalarFunctional (x : H) :
    CompactPositiveFunctional (X := X)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomScalarFunctional_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma starHomScalarFunctional_apply (x : H)
    (f : CompactlySupportedContinuousMap (X) ℝ) :
    (starHomScalarFunctional Φ x).functional f =
      RCLike.re ⟪x, starHomRealOperator Φ f x⟫_ℂ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomScalarMeasure
declarations.doc: The scalar spectral measure supplied by Riesz--Markov for the vector state at `x`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def starHomScalarMeasure (x : H) : Measure (X)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomScalarMeasure_regular
declarations.statement: instance starHomScalarMeasure_regular (x : H) : (starHomScalarMeasure Φ x).Regular

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomScalarMeasure_isFinite
declarations.statement: instance starHomScalarMeasure_isFinite (x : H) : IsFiniteMeasure (starHomScalarMeasure Φ x)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomScalarMeasure_integral
declarations.statement:
lemma starHomScalarMeasure_integral (x : H)
    (f : CompactlySupportedContinuousMap (X) ℝ) :
    ∫ z, f z ∂starHomScalarMeasure Φ x =
      RCLike.re ⟪x, starHomRealOperator Φ f x⟫_ℂ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomScalarMeasure_integral_complex
declarations.statement:
lemma starHomScalarMeasure_integral_complex (x : H)
    (f : CompactlySupportedContinuousMap (X) ℝ) :
    ((∫ z, f z ∂starHomScalarMeasure Φ x : ℝ) : ℂ) =
      ⟪starHomRealOperator Φ f x, x⟫_ℂ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.polarizedStarHomRealIntegral
declarations.doc: The integral of a real function against the polarized measure.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def polarizedStarHomRealIntegral
    (f : CompactlySupportedContinuousMap (X) ℝ) (x y : H) : ℂ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.polarizedStarHomRealIntegral_eq_inner
declarations.statement:
lemma polarizedStarHomRealIntegral_eq_inner
    (f : CompactlySupportedContinuousMap (X) ℝ) (x y : H) :
    polarizedStarHomRealIntegral Φ f x y =
      ⟪y, starHomRealOperator Φ f x⟫_ℂ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomScalarMeasure_parallelogram
declarations.statement:
lemma starHomScalarMeasure_parallelogram (x y : H) :
    starHomScalarMeasure Φ (x + y) + starHomScalarMeasure Φ (x - y) =
      (starHomScalarMeasure Φ x + starHomScalarMeasure Φ x) +
        (starHomScalarMeasure Φ y + starHomScalarMeasure Φ y)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomScalarMeasure_neg
declarations.statement:
lemma starHomScalarMeasure_neg (x : H) :
    starHomScalarMeasure Φ (-x) = starHomScalarMeasure Φ x

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomScalarMeasure_I_smul
declarations.statement:
lemma starHomScalarMeasure_I_smul (x : H) :
    starHomScalarMeasure Φ (Complex.I • x) = starHomScalarMeasure Φ x

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure
declarations.doc: The complex measure `⟪y, E(·) x⟫`, obtained by polarizing the four measures `⟪v, E(·) v⟫`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure (x y : H) : ComplexMeasure (X)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure_isFiniteMeasure
declarations.statement:
lemma polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure_isFiniteMeasure (x y : H) :
    IsFiniteMeasure
      (polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure Φ x y).variation

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure_complexIntegral
declarations.statement:
lemma polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure_complexIntegral
    (f : CompactlySupportedContinuousMap (X) ℝ) (x y : H) :
    ∫ᵛ z, (f z : ℂ) ∂[ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℂ (E := ℂ);
      polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure Φ x y] =
      polarizedStarHomRealIntegral Φ f x y

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure_complexIntegral_eq_inner
declarations.statement:
lemma polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure_complexIntegral_eq_inner
    (f : CompactlySupportedContinuousMap (X) ℝ) (x y : H) :
    ∫ᵛ z, (f z : ℂ) ∂[ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℂ (E := ℂ);
      polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure Φ x y] =
      ⟪y, starHomRealOperator Φ f x⟫_ℂ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure_apply {x y : H}
    {S : Set (X)} (hS : MeasurableSet S) :
    polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure Φ x y S =
      ((1 / 4 : ℝ) *
          ((starHomScalarMeasure Φ (x + y)).real S -
            (starHomScalarMeasure Φ (x - y)).real S) : ℂ) +
        Complex.I * ((1 / 4 : ℝ) *
          ((starHomScalarMeasure Φ (x + Complex.I • y)).real S -
            (starHomScalarMeasure Φ (x - Complex.I • y)).real S) : ℂ)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomScalarMeasure_real_parallelogram
declarations.doc:
The real-valued version of the parallelogram law, at a fixed (not necessarily measurable)
set `S`.  This is the algebraic engine behind the sesquilinearity proofs below.
declarations.statement:
lemma starHomScalarMeasure_real_parallelogram (a b : H) (S : Set (X)) :
    (starHomScalarMeasure Φ (a + b)).real S + (starHomScalarMeasure Φ (a - b)).real S =
      2 * (starHomScalarMeasure Φ a).real S + 2 * (starHomScalarMeasure Φ b).real S

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomScalarMeasure_real_neg
declarations.statement:
lemma starHomScalarMeasure_real_neg (a : H) (S : Set (X)) :
    (starHomScalarMeasure Φ (-a)).real S = (starHomScalarMeasure Φ a).real S

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomScalarMeasure_real_I_smul
declarations.statement:
lemma starHomScalarMeasure_real_I_smul (a : H) (S : Set (X)) :
    (starHomScalarMeasure Φ (Complex.I • a)).real S = (starHomScalarMeasure Φ a).real S

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomScalarMeasure_real_nonneg
declarations.statement:
lemma starHomScalarMeasure_real_nonneg (a : H) (S : Set (X)) :
    0 ≤ (starHomScalarMeasure Φ a).real S

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomScalarMeasure_real_univ
declarations.doc:
The Riesz measure for the vector state at `x` has total mass `‖x‖ ^ 2`: the vector-state
counterpart of `Φ 1 = 1`.
declarations.statement:
lemma starHomScalarMeasure_real_univ (x : H) :
    (starHomScalarMeasure Φ x).real Set.univ = ‖x‖ ^ 2

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomScalarMeasure_real_le_univ
declarations.statement:
lemma starHomScalarMeasure_real_le_univ (a : H) (S : Set (X)) :
    (starHomScalarMeasure Φ a).real S ≤ ‖a‖ ^ 2

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomScalarMeasure_real_polar_symm
declarations.doc:
The real polarization `Q(a + b) - Q(a - b)` of the diagonal measures is symmetric in `a` and
`b`.
declarations.statement:
lemma starHomScalarMeasure_real_polar_symm (a b : H) (S : Set (X)) :
    (starHomScalarMeasure Φ (a + b)).real S - (starHomScalarMeasure Φ (a - b)).real S =
      (starHomScalarMeasure Φ (b + a)).real S - (starHomScalarMeasure Φ (b - a)).real S

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomScalarMeasure_real_polar_add_left
declarations.doc:
First-argument additivity of the real polarization `Q(a+b) - Q(a-b)`, established by pure
algebra from the parallelogram law (`starHomScalarMeasure_real_parallelogram`); no continuity is
needed for this step, matching the classical Jordan--von Neumann polarization argument
(`Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.OfNorm`).
declarations.statement:
lemma starHomScalarMeasure_real_polar_add_left (x y z : H) (S : Set (X)) :
    (starHomScalarMeasure Φ (x + y + z)).real S - (starHomScalarMeasure Φ (x + y - z)).real S =
      ((starHomScalarMeasure Φ (x + z)).real S - (starHomScalarMeasure Φ (x - z)).real S) +
        ((starHomScalarMeasure Φ (y + z)).real S - (starHomScalarMeasure Φ (y - z)).real S)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomScalarMeasure_real_polar_add_right
declarations.doc:
Second-argument additivity of the real polarization, obtained from first-argument additivity
(`starHomScalarMeasure_real_polar_add_left`)
  via the symmetry `starHomScalarMeasure_real_polar_symm`.
declarations.statement:
lemma starHomScalarMeasure_real_polar_add_right (a b c : H) (S : Set (X)) :
    (starHomScalarMeasure Φ (a + (b + c))).real S -
        (starHomScalarMeasure Φ (a - (b + c))).real S =
      ((starHomScalarMeasure Φ (a + b)).real S - (starHomScalarMeasure Φ (a - b)).real S) +
        ((starHomScalarMeasure Φ (a + c)).real S - (starHomScalarMeasure Φ (a - c)).real S)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure_add_right
declarations.doc:
Additivity of the polarized measure in its second (right) vector argument, for a fixed
measurable set `S`.  This is the sesquilinearity step promised in the module docstring: it
follows from the parallelogram law by pure algebra, with no continuity or Riesz-representation
machinery required.
declarations.statement:
lemma polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure_add_right (x y₁ y₂ : H) {S : Set (X)}
    (hS : MeasurableSet S) :
    polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure Φ x (y₁ + y₂) S =
      polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure Φ x y₁ S +
        polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure Φ x y₂ S

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure_add_left
declarations.doc:
Additivity of the polarized measure in its first (left) vector argument, for a fixed
measurable set `S`.
declarations.statement:
lemma polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure_add_left (x₁ x₂ y : H) {S : Set (X)}
    (hS : MeasurableSet S) :
    polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure Φ (x₁ + x₂) y S =
      polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure Φ x₁ y S +
        polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure Φ x₂ y S

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure_I_smul_right
declarations.doc: Multiplying the second vector by `i` multiplies the polarized measure by `-i`.
declarations.statement:
lemma polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure_I_smul_right (x y : H) {S : Set (X)}
    (hS : MeasurableSet S) :
    polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure Φ x (Complex.I • y) S =
      -Complex.I * polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure Φ x y S

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure_I_smul_left
declarations.doc: Multiplying the first vector by `i` multiplies the polarized measure by `i`.
declarations.statement:
lemma polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure_I_smul_left (x y : H) {S : Set (X)}
    (hS : MeasurableSet S) :
    polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure Φ (Complex.I • x) y S =
      Complex.I * polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure Φ x y S

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure_norm_le
declarations.doc:
A crude but sufficient bound on the polarized measure, from the parallelogram law and
`starHomScalarMeasure_real_le_univ`.
   This is enough to see `(x, y) ↦ polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure Φ
x y S` is jointly bounded, the input a Riesz-representation argument needs.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure_real_smul_right
declarations.doc: The polarized measure is real homogeneous in the second vector.
declarations.statement:
lemma polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure_real_smul_right (x y : H) (r : ℝ) {S : Set (X)}
    (hS : MeasurableSet S) :
    polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure Φ x (r • y) S =
      (r : ℂ) * polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure Φ x y S

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure_real_smul_left
declarations.doc:
Real-scalar homogeneity in the left (first) argument, the counterpart of
`polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure_real_smul_right` needed for conjugate-linearity in `x` (real scalars
are self-conjugate, so the same statement serves both roles).
declarations.statement:
lemma polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure_real_smul_left (x y : H) (r : ℝ) {S : Set (X)}
    (hS : MeasurableSet S) :
    polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure Φ (r • x) y S =
      (r : ℂ) * polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure Φ x y S

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure_smul_left
declarations.doc: Full `ℂ`-linearity of the polarized measure in its first (left) argument.
declarations.statement:
lemma polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure_smul_left (c : ℂ) (x y : H) {S : Set (X)}
    (hS : MeasurableSet S) :
    polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure Φ (c • x) y S =
      c * polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure Φ x y S

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure_smul_right
declarations.doc: Full conjugate-`ℂ`-linearity of the polarized measure in its second (right) argument.
declarations.statement:
lemma polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure_smul_right (c : ℂ) (x y : H) {S : Set (X)}
    (hS : MeasurableSet S) :
    polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure Φ x (c • y) S =
      (starRingEnd ℂ c) * polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure Φ x y S

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure_zero_left
declarations.statement:
lemma polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure_zero_left (y : H) {S : Set (X)}
    (hS : MeasurableSet S) : polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure Φ 0 y S = 0

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure_zero_right
declarations.statement:
lemma polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure_zero_right (x : H) {S : Set (X)}
    (hS : MeasurableSet S) : polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure Φ x 0 S = 0

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure_norm_le_mul
declarations.doc: The polarized measure is bounded by `‖x‖ ‖y‖`.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomSesquilinearFormAux
declarations.doc:
The algebraic (not-yet-continuous) sesquilinear form representing `S`, conjugate-linear in the
first argument and linear in the second — the convention Mathlib's
`InnerProductSpace.continuousLinearMapOfBilin` expects.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def starHomSesquilinearFormAux (S : Set (X)) (hS : MeasurableSet S) :
    H →ₛₗ[starRingEnd ℂ] H →ₗ[ℂ] ℂ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomSesquilinearFormAux_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma starHomSesquilinearFormAux_apply (S : Set (X)) (hS : MeasurableSet S) (x y : H) :
    starHomSesquilinearFormAux Φ S hS x y =
      starRingEnd ℂ (polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure Φ x y S)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomSesquilinearForm
declarations.doc:
The continuous sesquilinear form, in the shape `InnerProductSpace.continuousLinearMapOfBilin`
consumes.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def starHomSesquilinearForm (S : Set (X)) (hS : MeasurableSet S) :
    H →L⋆[ℂ] H →L[ℂ] ℂ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomSesquilinearForm_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma starHomSesquilinearForm_apply (S : Set (X)) (hS : MeasurableSet S) (x y : H) :
    starHomSesquilinearForm Φ S hS x y =
      starRingEnd ℂ (polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure Φ x y S)

modules.title: The spectral measure of a representation of continuous functions
modules.doc:
The projection-valued measure of a unital ⋆-homomorphism from the continuous functions on a compact
Hausdorff space to the bounded operators of a Hilbert space.

## i. Overview

The sesquilinear form of the indicator of a Borel set `S` is represented by an operator `E(S)`.
These operators are projections, countably additive in the weak operator topology, and commute with
every operator commuting with the range of the ⋆-homomorphism. They form the spectral measure of the
⋆-homomorphism, whose integral of a continuous function `f` is `Φ f`. This is the construction of
`UnitaryInfra.SpectralMeasure` with the continuous functional calculus of a normal operator
replaced by an arbitrary ⋆-homomorphism, so that it applies to commuting families.

## ii. Key results

- `starHomSpectralOperator` : the operator `E(S)`.
- `starHomSpectralOperator_isStarProjection` : each `E(S)` is an orthogonal projection.
- `starHomSpectralMeasure` : the spectral measure of a ⋆-homomorphism.
- `starHomSpectralMeasure_reconstruction` : integrating a real continuous `f` gives `Φ f`.
- `starHomSpectralMeasure_commute` : `E` commutes with operators commuting with the range of `Φ`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Order properties of the spectral operators
- B. Weak countable additivity
- C. The spectral operators are projections
- D. The spectral measure
- E. Commutation with the commutant

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. Order properties of the spectral operators

## C. The spectral operators are projections

For a compact set `K` and an open `V ⊇ K`, a Urysohn function `f` gives `E(K) ≤ f(U) ≤ E(V)`. With
the estimate `‖A x‖² ≤ re ⟪x, A x⟫` for `0 ≤ A ≤ 1` and outer regularity this shows `E(K)² = E(K)`.
Inner regularity extends it to measurable sets, and multiplicativity on intersections follows from
additivity.

The idempotency proof above is the reusable order/regularity construction.  It first proves
the compact case with an Urysohn cutoff and outer regularity, then approximates an arbitrary
measurable set from inside by compact sets.  The only analytic estimate is the positive
contraction inequality `0 ≤ A ≤ 1 ⟹ ‖A x‖² ≤ re ⟪x, A x⟫`; no weak/strong operator topology
argument or multiplication of operator limits is involved.

## E. Commutation with the commutant

omit [MeasurableSpace X] in
An operator commuting with the range of `Φ` commutes with `Φ f` for continuous `f`, and by
uniqueness in the Riesz–Markov–Kakutani theorem with every spectral projection of `Φ`.

measurable `S`.

    starHomSpectralOperatorAux Φ S hS * starHomSpectralOperatorAux Φ S hS =

measurable sets, and the order/regularity theorem above on measurable sets.

    IsIdempotentElem (starHomSpectralOperator Φ S)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomSpectralMeasure
declarations.doc:
**The weak-operator spectral measure of a bounded normal operator.**  Assembled from the
Riesz-represented, weakly σ-additive family `starHomSpectralOperator` (Steps B–C, fully proved) and
the star-projection property (Step D), including the order/regularity proof of idempotency.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def starHomSpectralMeasure : QuantumMechanics.WOTSpectralMeasure (X) H

declarations.statement:
lemma starHomSpectralMeasure_apply (S : Set (X)) :
    starHomSpectralMeasure Φ S = starHomSpectralMeasureFun Φ S

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomSpectralMeasure_scalarMeasure
declarations.doc:
The scalar
  measure attached to `starHomSpectralMeasure` is exactly the polarized Riesz measure it
was built from.
declarations.statement:
lemma starHomSpectralMeasure_scalarMeasure (x y : H) :
    (starHomSpectralMeasure Φ).scalarMeasure x y = polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure Φ x y

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomSpectralMeasure_reconstruction
declarations.doc:
**The spectral measure reconstructs the functional calculus**: integrating a continuous function
`f` gives `f(U)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma starHomSpectralMeasure_reconstruction
    (f : CompactlySupportedContinuousMap (X) ℝ) (x y : H) :
    (starHomSpectralMeasure Φ).complexWeakIntegral (fun z => (f z : ℂ)) x y =
      ⟪y, starHomRealOperator Φ f x⟫_ℂ

declarations.doc: An operator commuting with the range of `Φ` commutes with `Φ` at every real test function.
declarations.statement:
lemma starHomRealOperator_commute {T : H →L[ℂ] H} (hT : ∀ f : C(X, ℂ), Commute (Φ f) T)
    (f : CompactlySupportedContinuousMap (X) ℝ) :
    Commute (starHomRealOperator Φ f) T

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomScalarMeasure_eq_of_commute_isometry
declarations.doc:
If `T` is an isometry (`star T * T = 1`) commuting with `U` and `star U`, the vector-state
Riesz measure at `T v` agrees with the one at `v`: an isometric intertwiner of `U` leaves the
diagonal spectral measure unchanged.
declarations.statement:
lemma starHomScalarMeasure_eq_of_commute_isometry
    {T : H →L[ℂ] H} (hT : ∀ f : C(X, ℂ), Commute (Φ f) T)
    (hTiso : star T * T = 1) (v : H) :
    starHomScalarMeasure Φ (T v) = starHomScalarMeasure Φ v

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure_eq_of_commute_unitary
declarations.doc:
If `T` is unitary and commutes with `U` and `star U`, the polarized Riesz measure intertwines:
testing at `(T x, y)` matches testing at `(x, star T y)`.  This is the sesquilinear form of the
commutation identity,
  and is exactly what `starHomSpectralOperator_inner` needs to see commutation of
each spectral projection with `T`.
declarations.statement:
lemma polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure_eq_of_commute_unitary
    {T : H →L[ℂ] H} (hT : ∀ f : C(X, ℂ), Commute (Φ f) T)
    (hTunit : T ∈ unitary (H →L[ℂ] H)) (x y : H) :
    polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure Φ (T x) y =
      polarizedStarHomScalarMeasure Φ x (star T y)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomSpectralOperator_commute_of_commute_unitary
declarations.doc:
Every spectral operator `starHomSpectralOperator Φ S` commutes with any unitary intertwiner of
`U` (i.e. any unitary commuting with both `U` and `star U`).  Holds for *every* `S`, measurable or
not, since `starHomSpectralOperator_inner` itself needs no measurability hypothesis.
declarations.statement:
lemma starHomSpectralOperator_commute_of_commute_unitary
    {T : H →L[ℂ] H} (hT : ∀ f : C(X, ℂ), Commute (Φ f) T)
    (hTunit : T ∈ unitary (H →L[ℂ] H)) (S : Set (X)) :
    starHomSpectralOperator Φ S * T = T * starHomSpectralOperator Φ S

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.starHomSpectralMeasure_commute_of_commute_unitary
declarations.doc:
The weak-operator spectral measure `starHomSpectralMeasure Φ` commutes with any unitary
intertwiner of `U`, at every set (measurable or not).
declarations.statement:
lemma starHomSpectralMeasure_commute_of_commute_unitary
    {T : H →L[ℂ] H} (hT : ∀ f : C(X, ℂ), Commute (Φ f) T)
    (hTunit : T ∈ unitary (H →L[ℂ] H)) (S : Set (X)) :
    starHomSpectralMeasure Φ S * ContinuousLinearMapWOT.ofCLM T =
      ContinuousLinearMapWOT.ofCLM T * starHomSpectralMeasure Φ S

modules.title: Differentiating the exponential multiplier
modules.doc:
Difference quotients of `exp(i t T) x` converge to `i T x` for `x` of finite second moment.

## i. Overview

The functions `λ ↦ exp(i t λ)` are differentiable in `t` with derivative `i λ exp(i t λ)`, and their
difference quotients are dominated by `|λ|`. Integrating against a spectral measure, the difference
quotients of `exp(i t T) x` converge for `x` of finite second moment.

## ii. Key results

- `expFunction_hasDerivAt` : the derivative of `t ↦ exp(i t λ)`.
- `expFunction_slope_norm_le` : the difference quotients are bounded by `|λ|`.
- `expSlope` : the difference quotient `t⁻¹ (exp(i t λ) - 1)`.
- `expIntegral_inner_slope_tendsto_complexWeakIntegral` : the difference quotients converge weakly.
- `expIntegral_strong_slope_tendsto` : for `x` in the maximal domain, the difference quotients of
  `exp(i t T) x` converge in norm to `i T x`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The exponential function and its difference quotients
- B. Weak convergence of the difference quotients
- C. Strong convergence of the difference quotients

## iv. References

* None.

modules.title: The unitary group of a spectral measure
modules.doc:
The strongly continuous unitary group `t ↦ exp(i t T)` obtained from a spectral measure on `ℝ`.

## i. Overview

For a spectral measure `μ` on `ℝ`, integrating `λ ↦ exp(i t λ)` gives unitaries `exp(i t T)` with
`exp(i (t + s) T) = exp(i t T) exp(i s T)`, strongly continuous in `t`.

## ii. Key results

- `expFunction` : the bounded function `λ ↦ exp(i t λ)`.
- `expIntegral` : the unitary `exp(i t T)`.
- `expIntegral_add` : `exp(i (t + s) T) = exp(i t T) exp(i s T)`.
- `expIntegral_mem_unitary` : each `exp(i t T)` is unitary.
- `expIntegral_continuous` : `t ↦ exp(i t T) x` is continuous.
- `StrongUnitaryOneParameterGroup` : a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group.
- `expUnitaryGroup` : the unitary group of a spectral measure.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The exponential multiplier
- B. The unitary group and its strong continuity

## iv. References

* None.

modules.title: The spectral forms of a bounded normal operator
modules.doc:
Complex measures `⟪y, E(·) x⟫` of a bounded normal operator and their sesquilinear forms.

## i. Overview

For a bounded normal operator `U` and vectors `x`, `y`, the functional `f ↦ ⟪x, f(U) y⟫` on
continuous functions on the spectrum is given, by the Riesz–Markov–Kakutani theorem and
polarization, by a complex measure. Evaluating these measures on a measurable set `S` gives a
bounded sesquilinear form for each such set.

## ii. Key results

- `CompactPositiveFunctional` : a positive functional on compactly supported continuous functions,
  with its Riesz measure.
- `cfcScalarMeasure` : the measure representing `f ↦ ⟪x, f(U) x⟫`.
- `polarizedCfcScalarMeasure` : the complex measure representing `f ↦ ⟪y, f(U) x⟫`.
- `polarizedCfcScalarMeasure_complexIntegral_eq_inner` : integrating a real continuous `f` against
  the polarized measure gives `⟪y, f(U) x⟫`.
- `polarizedCfcScalarMeasure_smul_left`, `polarizedCfcScalarMeasure_smul_right` : the polarized
  measure is sesquilinear in the two vectors.
- `polarizedCfcScalarMeasure_norm_le_mul` : the polarized measure of a set is bounded by
  `2 ‖x‖ ‖y‖`.
- `cfcSesquilinearForm` : the bounded sesquilinear form of a measurable set.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Integrals along the range map
- B. Complexification of finite signed measures
- C. Finiteness of the polarized scalar measures
- D. A general positive-contraction norm estimate
- E. Positive scalar functionals from the continuous functional calculus
- F. Sesquilinearity of the polarized measure
- G. Polarization
- H. Full complex sesquilinearity of the polarized measure
- I. Riesz representation of the polarized measure

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. Integrals along the range map
## B. Complexification of finite signed measures
## C. Finiteness of the polarized scalar measures

## D. A general positive-contraction norm estimate

This is a standalone fact about `H →L[ℂ] H` for any complex Hilbert space `H`, not specific to the
continuous functional calculus of a fixed normal operator: it is Step 2 of the idempotency
argument below, quantifying `0 ≤ A ≤ 1 ⟹ A ^ 2 ≤ A` into a norm bound.
## E. Positive scalar functionals from the continuous functional calculus
## F. Sesquilinearity of the polarized measure

## H. Full complex sesquilinearity of the polarized measure

Writing `c = c.re + c.im i`, homogeneity for real scalars and for `i` gives complex linearity in the
first vector and conjugate linearity in the second.
