declarations.doc:
A bounded increasing sequence has a supremum, and a normal state maps it to the supremum of the
values.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_isLUB_range_and_normal_state_image (ω : 𝓢[ℝ, E]) (hω : ω.IsNormal)
    (x : ℕ → E) (hx : Monotone x) (hbounded : BddAbove (Set.range x)) :
    ∃ a : E, IsLUB (Set.range x) a ∧
      IsLUB (Set.range fun n => ω (x n)) (ω a)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JBWAlgebra.isLUB_rangeSup_normal_state_image
declarations.doc:
The same monotone-convergence statement using the canonical chosen sequence supremum from
`MonotoneCompleteOrder`.
declarations.statement:
lemma isLUB_rangeSup_normal_state_image (ω : 𝓢[ℝ, E]) (hω : ω.IsNormal)
    (x : ℕ → E) (hx : Monotone x) (hbounded : BddAbove (Set.range x)) :
    IsLUB (Set.range fun n => ω (x n))
      (ω (MonotoneCompleteOrder.rangeSup x hx hbounded))

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JBWAlgebra.exists_normal_finite_weight_ne_zero
declarations.doc:
A nonzero positive observable is detected by a normal finite weight.  This is the canonical
state-to-weight direction: normal-state separation supplies the state, and the established
state/weight conversion transports its normality to the positive cone.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_normal_finite_weight_ne_zero {x : E} (hx : 0 ≤ x) (hxne : x ≠ 0) :
    ∃ w : Weight E, w.IsNormal ∧ w.IsFinite ∧ w ⟨x, hx⟩ ≠ 0

modules.title: Projection resolutions in JBW-algebras
modules.doc:
Normal states turn projection resolutions into probability laws and separate them.

## i. Overview

A projection resolution is defined at the Jordan order-unit level. In a JBW-algebra two further
things hold. A normal state turns a projection resolution into an ordinary probability law, and
its bounded Borel calculus into ordinary integration against that law. And normal states
separate projection resolutions, so a projection resolution is determined by its probability laws.

## ii. Key results

- `MeasurableProjectionResolution.probabilityLaw` : the probability law in a normal state.
- `MeasurableProjectionResolution.scalarBoundedBorel_eq_integral` : a normal state applied to the
  bounded Borel calculus is the integral against the scalarized measure.
- `MeasurableProjectionResolution.eq_of_forall_normal_probabilityLaw_eq` : normal-state
  probability laws determine the projection resolution.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Probability laws
- B. Separation by normal states

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.MeasurableProjectionResolution.probabilityLaw
declarations.doc: The probability law of a projection resolution in a normal state.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def probabilityLaw (P : MeasurableProjectionResolution Ω E)
    (ω : 𝓢[ℝ, E]) (hω : ω.IsNormal) : ProbabilityMeasure Ω

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.MeasurableProjectionResolution.probabilityLaw_apply
declarations.doc: The probability of an event is the state evaluated at its projection.
declarations.statement:
lemma probabilityLaw_apply (P : MeasurableProjectionResolution Ω E)
    (ω : 𝓢[ℝ, E]) (hω : ω.IsNormal) (s : Set Ω) (hs : MeasurableSet s) :
    (P.probabilityLaw ω hω : Measure Ω) s = ENNReal.ofReal (ω (P s hs : E))

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.MeasurableProjectionResolution.scalarBoundedBorel_eq_integral
declarations.doc:
A normal state applied to the bounded Borel calculus is the bounded integral against the
scalarized measure.
declarations.statement:
lemma scalarBoundedBorel_eq_integral (P : MeasurableProjectionResolution Ω E)
    (ω : 𝓢[ℝ, E]) (hω : ω.IsNormal) {f : Ω → ℝ} (hf : Measurable f) {M : ℝ}
    (hM : ∀ x, |f x| ≤ M) :
    ω (P.boundedBorel f hf hM) =
      EffectValuedMeasure.integral hf hM (P.toEffectValuedMeasure.scalarize ω hω)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.MeasurableProjectionResolution.eq_of_forall_normal_state_eq
declarations.doc: Normal states separate projection resolutions pointwise.
declarations.statement:
lemma eq_of_forall_normal_state_eq {P Q : MeasurableProjectionResolution Ω E} [JBWAlgebra E]
    (h : ∀ ω : 𝓢[ℝ, E], ω.IsNormal → ∀ s hs, ω (P s hs : E) = ω (Q s hs : E)) : P = Q

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.MeasurableProjectionResolution.eq_of_forall_normal_probabilityLaw_eq
declarations.doc:
A projection resolution in a JBW-algebra is determined by its probability laws in all normal
states.
declarations.statement:
lemma eq_of_forall_normal_probabilityLaw_eq {P Q : MeasurableProjectionResolution Ω E}
    [JBWAlgebra E]
    (h : ∀ ω : 𝓢[ℝ, E], ∀ hω : ω.IsNormal, P.probabilityLaw ω hω = Q.probabilityLaw ω hω) :
    P = Q

modules.title: Lüders operations
modules.doc:
Lüders operations `x ↦ U_{√e} x` of effects and the states conditioned on effects.

## i. Overview

An effect `e` of an ordered JB-algebra has a positive square root. The Lüders operation of `e` is
the quadratic representation `x ↦ U_{√e} x`, and conditioning a state on `e` is `x ↦ ω(U_{√e} x) /
ω(e)`. For a projection this is conditioning on the projection.

## ii. Key results

- `NormedJordanAlgebra.luedersMap` : the Lüders map of an effect.
- `NormedJordanAlgebra.luedersOperation` : the Lüders operation.
- `NormedJordanAlgebra.luedersCondition` : the state conditioned on an effect.
- `NormedJordanAlgebra.luedersCondition_isNormal` : conditioning preserves normality.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The Lüders operation
- B. Lüders operations of projections
- C. Lüders conditioning

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.NormedJordanAlgebra.effectSqrt
declarations.doc:
The intrinsic positive square root selected by the JB continuous functional calculus for an
effect.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def effectSqrt (e : Effect E) : E

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.NormedJordanAlgebra.luedersMap
declarations.doc:
The Lüders operation of an effect: the positive quadratic operation induced by its square
root.  In a special Jordan algebra it is precisely `x ↦ sqrt(e) x sqrt(e)`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def luedersMap (e : Effect E) : E →ₚ[ℝ] E

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.NormedJordanAlgebra.luedersMap_apply
declarations.statement: lemma luedersMap_apply (e : Effect E) (x : E) : luedersMap e x = U (effectSqrt e) x

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.NormedJordanAlgebra.luedersMap_one
declarations.doc:
A Lüders operation sends the order unit to its effect.  Thus its probability in a state is
exactly the probability assigned to that effect.
declarations.statement: lemma luedersMap_one (e : Effect E) : luedersMap e (1 : E) = e

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.NormedJordanAlgebra.luedersOperation
declarations.doc:
The Lüders map is an operation: it is positive and its outcome probability never exceeds
certainty.  Its outcome effect is the original effect, so this is the intrinsic Jordan analogue
of a single-Kraus measurement operation.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def luedersOperation (e : Effect E) : Operation E

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.NormedJordanAlgebra.luedersOperation_apply
declarations.statement: lemma luedersOperation_apply (e : Effect E) (x : E) : luedersOperation e x = luedersMap e x

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.NormedJordanAlgebra.luedersOperation_outcomeEffect
declarations.doc: The effect recorded by the Lüders operation is exactly the effect it implements.
declarations.statement:
lemma luedersOperation_outcomeEffect (e : Effect E) :
    (Operation.outcomeEffect (luedersOperation e) : E) = e

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.NormedJordanAlgebra.effectSqrt_toEffect_of_projection
declarations.doc:
The CFC square root of a sharp Jordan event is the event itself.  This is the point where
the general effect operation recovers projection compression.
declarations.statement:
lemma effectSqrt_toEffect_of_projection {p : E} (hp : IsJordanProjection p) :
    effectSqrt hp.toEffect = p

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.NormedJordanAlgebra.luedersMap_toEffect_of_projection
declarations.doc: Lüders filtering by a sharp event is exactly quadratic compression by that projection.
declarations.statement:
lemma luedersMap_toEffect_of_projection {p : E} (hp : IsJordanProjection p) :
    luedersMap hp.toEffect = quadRepPositiveLinearMap p

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.NormedJordanAlgebra.luedersCondition
declarations.doc: The normalized post-measurement state associated with an effect of nonzero probability.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def luedersCondition (ω : 𝓢[ℝ, E]) (e : Effect E) (hmass : 0 < ω e) :
    𝓢[ℝ, E]

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.NormedJordanAlgebra.luedersCondition_apply
declarations.doc: Formula for the normalized state after the Lüders operation.
declarations.statement:
lemma luedersCondition_apply (ω : 𝓢[ℝ, E]) (e : Effect E) (hmass : 0 < ω e) (x : E) :
    luedersCondition ω e hmass x = (ω e)⁻¹ * ω (U (effectSqrt e) x)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.NormedJordanAlgebra.luedersCondition_one
declarations.doc: The normalized Lüders state evaluates the unit to one.
declarations.statement:
lemma luedersCondition_one (ω : 𝓢[ℝ, E]) (e : Effect E) (hmass : 0 < ω e) :
    luedersCondition ω e hmass 1 = 1

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.NormedJordanAlgebra.luedersCondition_isNormal
declarations.doc:
In a JBW application, once the Lüders operation is known to preserve directed suprema,
conditioning a normal state by a nonzero-probability effect remains normal.  Normality of the
quadratic operation itself is the remaining intrinsic JBW quadratic-order theorem.
declarations.statement:
lemma luedersCondition_isNormal (ω : 𝓢[ℝ, E]) (e : Effect E) (hmass : 0 < ω e)
    (hOp : (luedersOperation e).IsNormal) (hω : ω.IsNormal) :
    (luedersCondition ω e hmass).IsNormal

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.NormedJordanAlgebra.luedersCondition_toEffect_of_projection
declarations.doc: For a projection, conditioning on the effect is conditioning on the projection.
declarations.statement:
lemma luedersCondition_toEffect_of_projection {p : E} (hp : IsJordanProjection p)
    (ω : 𝓢[ℝ, E]) (hmass : 0 < ω p) :
    luedersCondition ω hp.toEffect hmass = hp.conditionOfQuadraticPositive ω hmass

modules.title: Moments, variance and Jordan projections
modules.doc:
Moments and variance of observables, and Jordan projections as effects and compressions.

## i. Overview

The `n`-th moment of an observable `a` in a state `ω` is `ω(aⁿ)`, and the variance is `ω(a²) -
ω(a)²`. A Jordan projection is an observable `p` with `p ∘ p = p`, and two projections are
orthogonal when `p ∘ q = 0`. A Jordan projection is an effect, and its quadratic representation
`U_p` compresses onto it.

## ii. Key results

- `IsJordanOrderUnit.moment`, `IsJordanOrderUnit.variance` : moments and variance.
- `JordanAlgebra.IsJordanProjection`, `JordanAlgebra.JordanOrthogonal` : Jordan projections and
  orthogonality.
- `JordanAlgebra.IsJordanProjection.toEffect` : a projection as an effect.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Moments and variance
- B. Jordan projections and orthogonality
- C. Projections as effects
- D. Compression: `U_p` for an idempotent `p`

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.IsJordanOrderUnit.moment
declarations.doc: The `n`-th moment of the observable `a` in the state `ω`: `moment_n(ω, a) = ω(a^n)`.
declarations.statement: def moment (n : ℕ) (ω : 𝓢[ℝ, E]) (a : E) : ℝ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.IsJordanOrderUnit.moment_zero
declarations.statement: lemma moment_zero (ω : 𝓢[ℝ, E]) (a : E) : moment 0 ω a = 1

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.IsJordanOrderUnit.moment_one
declarations.statement: lemma moment_one (ω : 𝓢[ℝ, E]) (a : E) : moment 1 ω a = ω a

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.IsJordanOrderUnit.variance
declarations.doc:
The variance of the observable `a` in the state `ω`, inherited from the generic covariance
form of its underlying linear functional.
declarations.statement: def variance (ω : 𝓢[ℝ, E]) (a : E) : ℝ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.IsJordanOrderUnit.variance_eq
declarations.doc: The variance is expressed directly, unfolding `moment 2` to the Jordan square.
declarations.statement: lemma variance_eq (ω : 𝓢[ℝ, E]) (a : E) : variance ω a = ω (a * a) - (ω a) ^ 2

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.IsJordanOrderUnit.moment_two_nonneg
declarations.doc:
The second moment of any observable is nonnegative: it is the state's value on the
(possible-outcome) Jordan square.
declarations.statement: lemma moment_two_nonneg (ω : 𝓢[ℝ, E]) (a : E) : 0 ≤ moment 2 ω a

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.IsJordanProjection
declarations.doc:
A Jordan projection: an element idempotent for the Jordan product, `p ∘ p = p`. The
Jordan-algebraic analogue of a self-adjoint projection, and (in the canonical C⋆-algebra
realization) exactly an ordinary projection `p² = p = p⋆`.
declarations.statement: def IsJordanProjection (p : E) : Prop

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.JordanOrthogonal
declarations.doc:
Two elements are Jordan-orthogonal when their Jordan product vanishes, `p ∘ q = 0`: the
Jordan-algebraic analogue of `Effect.Orthogonal`.
declarations.statement: def JordanOrthogonal (p q : E) : Prop

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.isJordanProjection_zero
declarations.statement: lemma isJordanProjection_zero : IsJordanProjection (0 : E)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.isJordanProjection_one
declarations.statement: lemma isJordanProjection_one : IsJordanProjection (1 : E)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.jordanOrthogonal_comm
declarations.statement: lemma jordanOrthogonal_comm {p q : E} (h : JordanOrthogonal p q) : JordanOrthogonal q p

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.jordanOrthogonal_zero_left
declarations.statement: lemma jordanOrthogonal_zero_left (p : E) : JordanOrthogonal 0 p

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.jordanOrthogonal_zero_right
declarations.statement: lemma jordanOrthogonal_zero_right (p : E) : JordanOrthogonal p 0

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.IsJordanProjection.nonneg
declarations.doc:
A Jordan projection is automatically a possible outcome (`0 ≤ p`), since it equals its own
Jordan square.
declarations.statement: lemma IsJordanProjection.nonneg {p : E} (hp : IsJordanProjection p) : 0 ≤ p

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.IsJordanProjection.add_of_jordanOrthogonal
declarations.doc:
The sum of two orthogonal Jordan projections is again a Jordan projection: the abstract,
operator-free analogue of "two orthogonal projections add to a projection", the algebraic content
behind an event-logic (sharp-effect) sum.
declarations.statement:
lemma IsJordanProjection.add_of_jordanOrthogonal {p q : E} (hp : IsJordanProjection p)
    (hq : IsJordanProjection q) (horth : JordanOrthogonal p q) :
    IsJordanProjection (p + q)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.IsJordanProjection.complement
declarations.doc:
The complement `1 - p` of a Jordan projection is again a Jordan projection: the Jordan-algebra
analogue of `Effect.complement`.
declarations.statement:
lemma IsJordanProjection.complement {p : E} (hp : IsJordanProjection p) :
    IsJordanProjection (1 - p)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.IsJordanProjection.jordanOrthogonal_complement
declarations.doc: A Jordan projection is orthogonal to its own complement: `p ∘ (1 - p) = 0`.
declarations.statement:
lemma IsJordanProjection.jordanOrthogonal_complement {p : E} (hp : IsJordanProjection p) :
    JordanOrthogonal p (1 - p)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.IsJordanProjection.le_one
declarations.doc:
A Jordan projection is bounded above by the order unit. Its complement is another projection,
hence a nonnegative square, and `0 ≤ 1 - p` is exactly `p ≤ 1`.
declarations.statement: lemma IsJordanProjection.le_one {p : E} (hp : IsJordanProjection p) : p ≤ 1

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.IsJordanProjection.toEffect
declarations.doc: A Jordan projection, bundled as an effect.
declarations.statement: def IsJordanProjection.toEffect {p : E} (hp : IsJordanProjection p) : Effect E

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.IsJordanProjection.coe_toEffect
declarations.statement:
lemma IsJordanProjection.coe_toEffect {p : E} (hp : IsJordanProjection p) :
    (hp.toEffect : E) = p

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.IsJordanProjection.toEffect_complement
declarations.doc: Bundling a projection's algebraic complement agrees with taking its effect complement.
declarations.statement:
lemma IsJordanProjection.toEffect_complement {p : E} (hp : IsJordanProjection p) :
    hp.complement.toEffect = Effect.complement hp.toEffect

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.IsJordanProjection.effectOrthogonal_of_jordanOrthogonal
declarations.doc:
Jordan-orthogonal projections have a defined partial sum in the effect algebra. This is the
forward direction that follows from square positivity alone; the converse needs the stronger JB
order theory.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.IsJordanProjection.addOfOrthogonal_toEffect
declarations.doc:
The effect-algebra partial sum of Jordan-orthogonal projections is their algebraic projection
sum.
declarations.statement:
lemma IsJordanProjection.addOfOrthogonal_toEffect {p q : E}
    (hp : IsJordanProjection p) (hq : IsJordanProjection q) (hpq : JordanOrthogonal p q) :
    Effect.addOfOrthogonal hp.toEffect hq.toEffect
      (hp.effectOrthogonal_of_jordanOrthogonal hq hpq) =
        (hp.add_of_jordanOrthogonal hq hpq).toEffect

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.IsJordanProjection.quadRep_self
declarations.doc:
**Compression onto an event.** For a Jordan projection `p`, `U_p(p) = p`: compressing `p`
itself onto the event `p` changes nothing. The Jordan-algebraic seed of "the outcome that already
happened is unaffected by conditioning on it having happened".
declarations.statement: lemma IsJordanProjection.quadRep_self {p : E} (hp : IsJordanProjection p) : U p p = p

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.IsJordanProjection.quadRep_jordanOrthogonal
declarations.doc: `U_p q = 0` for projections `q` orthogonal to `p`.
declarations.statement:
lemma IsJordanProjection.quadRep_jordanOrthogonal {p q : E} (hp : IsJordanProjection p)
    (horth : JordanOrthogonal p q) : U p q = 0

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.IsJordanProjection.quadRep_one
declarations.doc:
**Compression of the unit recovers the event itself.** For a Jordan projection `p`,
`U_p(1) = p`: this is `quadRep_apply_one` specialized using `p² = p`.
declarations.statement: lemma IsJordanProjection.quadRep_one {p : E} (hp : IsJordanProjection p) : U p (1 : E) = p

modules.title: Powers, multiplication operators and the quadratic representation
modules.doc:
Jordan powers, multiplication operators `L_a` and the quadratic representation `U_a`.

## i. Overview

Powers of an observable are `a⁰ = 1` and `aⁿ⁺¹ = a ∘ aⁿ`. The multiplication operator is `L_a b = a
∘ b`, and the quadratic representation `U_a = 2 L_a² - L_{a²}` is the Jordan version of `b ↦ a b a`.
The Jordan identity says that `L_a` and `L_{a²}` commute.

## ii. Key results

- `JordanAlgebra.jpow` : powers.
- `JordanAlgebra.mulLeft` : the multiplication operator `L_a`.
- `JordanAlgebra.quadRep` : the quadratic representation `U_a`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Powers
- B. The multiplication operator `L_a`
- C. The quadratic representation `U_a`
- D. The Jordan commutation law
- E. The inner derivation `D_{a,b}`

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.jpow
declarations.doc:
The `n`-th Jordan power of `a`, defined by the fixed left-bracketing recursion
`a^[0] = 1`, `a^[n+1] = a ∘ a^[n]`.
declarations.statement: def jpow (a : E) : ℕ → E

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.jpow_zero
declarations.statement: lemma jpow_zero (a : E) : a ^[0] = 1

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.jpow_succ
declarations.statement: lemma jpow_succ (a : E) (n : ℕ) : a ^[n + 1] = a * a ^[n]

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.jpow_one
declarations.statement: lemma jpow_one (a : E) : a ^[1] = a

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.jpow_two
declarations.doc: The second Jordan power is the Jordan square, `a ∘ a`.
declarations.statement: lemma jpow_two (a : E) : a ^[2] = a * a

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.mulLeft
declarations.doc:
The Jordan multiplication operator `L a : E →ₗ[ℝ] E`, `L a b = a ∘ b`. Linear in `b` since the
Jordan product distributes over `+` (`NonUnitalNonAssocCommRing`) and commutes with real scalars
(`SMulCommClass ℝ E E`).
declarations.statement: def mulLeft (a : E) : E →ₗ[ℝ] E

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.mulLeft_apply
declarations.statement: lemma mulLeft_apply (a b : E) : L a b = a * b

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.mulLeft_one
declarations.statement: lemma mulLeft_one (a : E) : L a 1 = a

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.mulLeft_one_apply
declarations.statement: lemma mulLeft_one_apply (a : E) : L 1 a = a

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.quadRep
declarations.doc: The quadratic representation `U_a = 2 L_a² - L_{a²}`, the Jordan version of `b ↦ a b a`.
declarations.statement: def quadRep (a : E) : E →ₗ[ℝ] E

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.quadRep_apply
declarations.statement: lemma quadRep_apply (a b : E) : U a b = (2 : ℝ) • (a * (a * b)) - a ^[2] * b

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.quadRep_zero_apply
declarations.statement: lemma quadRep_zero_apply (b : E) : U (0 : E) b = 0

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.quadRep_add_right
declarations.statement: lemma quadRep_add_right (a b c : E) : U a (b + c) = U a b + U a c

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.quadRep_smul_right
declarations.statement: lemma quadRep_smul_right (r : ℝ) (a b : E) : U a (r • b) = r • U a b

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.quadRepPolar
declarations.doc: The polarization of the quadratic representation, `x ↦ a x b + b x a` in the associative case.
declarations.statement: def quadRepPolar (a b : E) : E →ₗ[ℝ] E

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.quadRepBilin
declarations.doc:
The standard bilinear quadratic operator.  `quadRepPolar` is its literal cross-effect
and therefore equals twice this operator.  Keeping this undivided normalization is essential for
the finite polarization identities used in the algebraic proof of the fundamental formula.
declarations.statement: def quadRepBilin (a b : E) : E →ₗ[ℝ] E

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.quadRepBilin_apply
declarations.doc: Pointwise form of the standard bilinear quadratic operator.
declarations.statement:
lemma quadRepBilin_apply (a b x : E) :
    quadRepBilin a b x = a * (b * x) + b * (a * x) - (a * b) * x

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.quadRepBilin_comm
declarations.doc: The standard bilinear quadratic operator is symmetric.
declarations.statement: lemma quadRepBilin_comm (a b : E) : quadRepBilin a b = quadRepBilin b a

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.quadRepBilin_add_left
declarations.doc: Additivity in the first variable of the standard quadratic polarization.
declarations.statement:
lemma quadRepBilin_add_left (a b c : E) :
    quadRepBilin (a + b) c = quadRepBilin a c + quadRepBilin b c

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.quadRepBilin_smul_left
declarations.doc: Real linearity in the first variable of the standard quadratic polarization.
declarations.statement:
lemma quadRepBilin_smul_left (r : ℝ) (a b : E) :
    quadRepBilin (r • a) b = r • quadRepBilin a b

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.quadRepBilin_add_right
declarations.doc: Additivity in the second variable of the standard quadratic polarization.
declarations.statement:
lemma quadRepBilin_add_right (a b c : E) :
    quadRepBilin a (b + c) = quadRepBilin a b + quadRepBilin a c

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.quadRepBilin_smul_right
declarations.doc: Real linearity in the second variable of the standard quadratic polarization.
declarations.statement:
lemma quadRepBilin_smul_right (r : ℝ) (a b : E) :
    quadRepBilin a (r • b) = r • quadRepBilin a b

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.quadRepBilin_neg_right
declarations.doc: Signed second-variable specialization of the bilinear quadratic operator.
declarations.statement:
lemma quadRepBilin_neg_right (a b : E) :
    quadRepBilin a (-b) = -quadRepBilin a b

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.quadRepBilin_neg_left
declarations.doc: Signed first-variable specialization of the bilinear quadratic operator.
declarations.statement:
lemma quadRepBilin_neg_left (a b : E) :
    quadRepBilin (-a) b = -quadRepBilin a b

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.quadRepBilin_sub_right
declarations.doc: Difference expansion in the second variable of the bilinear quadratic operator.
declarations.statement:
lemma quadRepBilin_sub_right (a b c : E) :
    quadRepBilin a (b - c) = quadRepBilin a b - quadRepBilin a c

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.quadRepPolar_eq_two_smul_quadRepBilin
declarations.doc: The cross-effect normalization is twice the standard bilinear quadratic operator.
declarations.statement:
lemma quadRepPolar_eq_two_smul_quadRepBilin (a b : E) :
    quadRepPolar a b = (2 : ℝ) • quadRepBilin a b

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.quadRepBilin_self
declarations.doc: The diagonal of the standard bilinear quadratic operator is the quadratic representation.
declarations.statement: lemma quadRepBilin_self (a : E) : quadRepBilin a a = U a

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.quadRepPolar_apply
declarations.doc: Pointwise form of the polarized quadratic representation.
declarations.statement:
lemma quadRepPolar_apply (a b x : E) :
    quadRepPolar a b x =
      (2 : ℝ) • (a * (b * x) + b * (a * x) - (a * b) * x)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.quadRepPolar_comm
declarations.doc: Polarization is symmetric in its two outer variables.
declarations.statement: lemma quadRepPolar_comm (a b : E) : quadRepPolar a b = quadRepPolar b a

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.quadRepPolar_add_left
declarations.doc: The polarization is additive in its first outer variable.
declarations.statement:
lemma quadRepPolar_add_left (a b c : E) :
    quadRepPolar (a + b) c = quadRepPolar a c + quadRepPolar b c

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.quadRepPolar_smul_left
declarations.doc: The polarization is real-linear in its first outer variable.
declarations.statement:
lemma quadRepPolar_smul_left (r : ℝ) (a b : E) :
    quadRepPolar (r • a) b = r • quadRepPolar a b

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.quadRepPolar_add_right
declarations.doc: The polarization is additive in its second outer variable.
declarations.statement:
lemma quadRepPolar_add_right (a b c : E) :
    quadRepPolar a (b + c) = quadRepPolar a b + quadRepPolar a c

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.quadRepPolar_smul_right
declarations.doc: The polarization is real-linear in its second outer variable.
declarations.statement:
lemma quadRepPolar_smul_right (r : ℝ) (a b : E) :
    quadRepPolar a (r • b) = r • quadRepPolar a b

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.quadRepPolar_self
declarations.doc: The diagonal of the polarization is twice the original quadratic representation.
declarations.statement: lemma quadRepPolar_self (a : E) : quadRepPolar a a = (2 : ℝ) • U a

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.quadRep_add_apply
declarations.doc:
The quadratic representation splits into its two diagonal pieces and its polarized
cross-effect.
declarations.statement:
lemma quadRep_add_apply (a b x : E) :
    U (a + b) x = U a x + quadRepPolar a b x + U b x

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.quadRep_add_eq
declarations.doc: Exact additive polarization of the quadratic representation in standard normalization.
declarations.statement:
lemma quadRep_add_eq (a b : E) :
    U (a + b) = U a + (2 : ℝ) • quadRepBilin a b + U b

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.quadRep_sub_eq
declarations.doc:
Signed additive polarization, obtained from the same quadratic cross-effect.  Together with
`quadRep_add_eq`, this gives the two exact evaluations used to isolate a quadratic coefficient.
declarations.statement:
lemma quadRep_sub_eq (a b : E) :
    U (a - b) = U a - (2 : ℝ) • quadRepBilin a b + U b

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.quadRep_add_add_eq
declarations.doc:
The quadratic representation of a three-term sum, expressed through the canonical symmetric
bilinear cross-effect.  This is the coefficient-expansion interface for polarizing identities in
quadratic representations; it keeps all mixed terms in the single `quadRepBilin` API.
declarations.statement:
lemma quadRep_add_add_eq (a b c : E) :
    U (a + b + c) =
      U a + U b + U c +
        (2 : ℝ) • quadRepBilin a b +
          (2 : ℝ) • quadRepBilin a c +
            (2 : ℝ) • quadRepBilin b c

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.add_mul_self
declarations.doc: Exact square expansion for the positive polarization evaluation.
declarations.statement:
lemma add_mul_self (a b : E) :
    (a + b) * (a + b) = a * a + (2 : ℝ) • (a * b) + b * b

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.sub_mul_self
declarations.doc: Exact square expansion for the signed polarization evaluation.
declarations.statement:
lemma sub_mul_self (a b : E) :
    (a - b) * (a - b) = a * a - (2 : ℝ) • (a * b) + b * b

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.quadRep_smul_apply
declarations.doc: Quadratic representations are homogeneous of degree two in their outer argument.
declarations.statement:
lemma quadRep_smul_apply (r : ℝ) (a b : E) :
    U (r • a) b = r ^ 2 • U a b

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.quadRep_smul_eq
declarations.doc: Quadratic homogeneity of the representation, as an equality of operators.
declarations.statement:
lemma quadRep_smul_eq (r : ℝ) (a : E) :
    U (r • a) = r ^ 2 • U a

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.quadRep_neg_apply
declarations.statement: lemma quadRep_neg_apply (a b : E) : U (-a) b = U a b

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.quadRep_neg
declarations.doc: Sign invariance of the quadratic representation, as an equality of operators.
declarations.statement: lemma quadRep_neg (a : E) : U (-a) = U a

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.quadRep_one_apply
declarations.doc:
The quadratic representation of the order unit is the identity: `U_1 = id`. The Jordan
identity element acts as "conjugate by the identity", i.e. does nothing.
declarations.statement: lemma quadRep_one_apply (b : E) : U (1 : E) b = b

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.quadRep_one_comp
declarations.statement: lemma quadRep_one_comp (a : E) : (U (1 : E)).comp (U a) = U a

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.quadRep_comp_one
declarations.statement: lemma quadRep_comp_one (a : E) : (U a).comp (U (1 : E)) = U a

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.quadRep_apply_one
declarations.doc:
The quadratic representation of `a`, evaluated at the order unit, recovers the Jordan square:
`U_a(1) = a²`. Conjugating the identity by `a` gives back `a²`, matching the associative picture
`a \cdot 1 \cdot a = a^2`.
declarations.statement: lemma quadRep_apply_one (a : E) : U a (1 : E) = a ^[2]

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.quadRep_mulLeft
declarations.doc: `U_a` commutes with `L_a`.
declarations.statement: lemma quadRep_mulLeft [IsCommJordan E] (a x : E) : U a (a * x) = a * U a x

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.quadRep_mulLeft_sq
declarations.doc:
Quadratic representation by `a` also commutes with multiplication by the square `a²`.
Together with `quadRep_mulLeft`, this says that `U_a` preserves the associative algebra generated
by `a` at the operator level, without appealing to an ambient associative realization.
declarations.statement:
lemma quadRep_mulLeft_sq [IsCommJordan E] (a x : E) :
    U a (a ^[2] * x) = a ^[2] * U a x

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.commute_quadRep_mulLeft
declarations.doc: Bundled form of `quadRep_mulLeft`: the quadratic representation commutes with `L_a`.
declarations.statement: lemma commute_quadRep_mulLeft [IsCommJordan E] (a : E) : Commute (U a) (L a)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.commute_quadRep_mulLeft_sq
declarations.doc: Bundled form of `quadRep_mulLeft_sq`: the quadratic representation commutes with `L_(a²)`.
declarations.statement: lemma commute_quadRep_mulLeft_sq [IsCommJordan E] (a : E) : Commute (U a) (L (a ^[2]))

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.innerDerivation
declarations.doc: The inner derivation `D_{a,b} = [L_a, L_b]`.
declarations.statement: def innerDerivation (a b : E) : E →ₗ[ℝ] E

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.innerDerivation_apply
declarations.doc: Pointwise form of the inner derivation.
declarations.statement: lemma innerDerivation_apply (a b x : E) : innerDerivation a b x = a * (b * x) - b * (a * x)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.innerDerivation_swap
declarations.doc: The inner derivation is antisymmetric in its two defining arguments.
declarations.statement: lemma innerDerivation_swap (a b : E) : innerDerivation a b = -innerDerivation b a

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.innerDerivation_self
declarations.statement: lemma innerDerivation_self (a : E) : innerDerivation a a = 0

modules.title: Power-associativity
modules.doc:
Jordan algebras are power-associative: `aᵐ ∘ aⁿ = aᵐ⁺ⁿ`.

## i. Overview

The subalgebra generated by one element of a Jordan algebra is associative: `aᵐ ∘ aⁿ = aᵐ⁺ⁿ`.
Polarizing the Jordan identity shows that `L_a` commutes with every `L_{aⁿ}`, and the power law
follows by induction.

## ii. Key results

- `JordanAlgebra.linearized_mul_sq` : the polarized Jordan identity.
- `JordanAlgebra.commute_mulLeft_pow` : `L_a` commutes with `L_{aⁿ}`.
- `JordanAlgebra.pow_add` : `aᵐ ∘ aⁿ = aᵐ⁺ⁿ`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Operator commutation for powers
- B. Strong power-associativity

## iv. References

- K. McCrimmon, *A Taste of Jordan Algebras*, Springer, 2004, Ch. II.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.commute_mulLeft_sq
declarations.doc: `L_a` and `L_{a²}` commute, which is the Jordan identity.
declarations.statement: lemma commute_mulLeft_sq (a : E) : Commute (L a) (L (a ^[2]))

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.commute_mulLeft_apply
declarations.doc:
A pointwise restatement of `Commute (L a) (L x)`: `a` and `x` "cross-associate" against any
third element `y`.
declarations.statement:
lemma commute_mulLeft_apply {a x : E} (h : Commute (L a) (L x)) (y : E) :
    a * (x * y) = x * (a * y)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.linearized_mul_sq
declarations.doc:
A polarized form of the Jordan identity. This is Basic Identity (2.1.2) in McCrimmon's
*A Taste of Jordan Algebras*. It is the algebraic engine behind the recursion for multiplication
operators of powers.
declarations.statement:
lemma linearized_mul_sq (a y z : E) :
    (a * a * y) * z =
      -(2 : ℝ) • (a * (y * (a * z))) + (a * a) * (y * z) +
        (2 : ℝ) • ((a * y) * (a * z))

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.square_mul_jpow
declarations.doc: Multiplying a Jordan power by the square raises its degree by two.
declarations.statement: lemma square_mul_jpow (a : E) (n : ℕ) : (a * a) * a ^[n] = a ^[n + 2]

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.mulLeft_jpow_add_two
declarations.doc:
The multiplication operator of `a^[n+2]`, expressed recursively in the commuting generators
`L_a` and `L_(a²)`.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.fundamental_mulLeft_commute_pow
declarations.doc:
Both fundamental commuting operators `L_a` and `L_(a²)` commute with multiplication by every
power of `a`.
declarations.statement:
lemma fundamental_mulLeft_commute_pow (a : E) (n : ℕ) :
    Commute (L a) (L (a ^[n])) ∧ Commute (L (a * a)) (L (a ^[n]))

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.commute_mulLeft_pow
declarations.doc:
`a` commutes, as a Jordan multiplication operator, with the multiplication operator of every
one of its powers.
declarations.statement: lemma commute_mulLeft_pow (a : E) (n : ℕ) : Commute (L a) (L (a ^[n]))

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.pow_add
declarations.doc: **Power-associativity**: `aᵐ ∘ aⁿ = aᵐ⁺ⁿ`.
declarations.statement: lemma pow_add (a : E) (m n : ℕ) : a ^[m] * a ^[n] = a ^[m + n]

modules.title: Jordan subalgebras generated by a set
modules.doc:
The smallest unital Jordan submodule containing a set, as a Jordan algebra in its own right.

## i. Overview

The Jordan subalgebra generated by a set of observables is the smallest unital submodule closed
under the Jordan product containing it. For a single observable it is the span of its powers.

## ii. Key results

- `JordanAlgebra.generatedBySet` : the generated subalgebra.
- `JordanAlgebra.GeneratedBySet` : it as a Jordan algebra.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Jordan-closed submodules and generation
- B. The generated subalgebra as a type
- C. Generation by one observable

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## B. The generated subalgebra as a type

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.IsJordanSubmodule
declarations.doc:
A real submodule is Jordan-closed when it contains the unit and is closed under the Jordan
product.  This is the closure notion used for arbitrary generated Jordan fragments.
declarations.statement: def IsJordanSubmodule (J : Submodule ℝ E) : Prop

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.generatedBySet
declarations.doc: The smallest unital Jordan submodule containing the set `s`.
declarations.statement: def generatedBySet (s : Set E) : Submodule ℝ E

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.subset_generatedBySet
declarations.doc: The generating set is contained in its generated Jordan submodule.
declarations.statement: lemma subset_generatedBySet (s : Set E) : s ⊆ generatedBySet s

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.one_mem_generatedBySet
declarations.doc: The generated Jordan submodule contains the order unit.
declarations.statement: lemma one_mem_generatedBySet (s : Set E) : (1 : E) ∈ generatedBySet s

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.mul_mem_generatedBySet
declarations.doc: The generated Jordan submodule is closed under the Jordan product.
declarations.statement:
lemma mul_mem_generatedBySet (s : Set E) {x y : E} (hx : x ∈ generatedBySet s)
    (hy : y ∈ generatedBySet s) : x * y ∈ generatedBySet s

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.isJordanSubmodule_generatedBySet
declarations.doc: The universal generated submodule is itself unital and Jordan-closed.
declarations.statement: lemma isJordanSubmodule_generatedBySet (s : Set E) : IsJordanSubmodule (generatedBySet s)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.generatedBySet_le
declarations.doc:
Universal property of arbitrary Jordan generation: every unital Jordan submodule containing
the generators contains `generatedBySet s`.
declarations.statement:
lemma generatedBySet_le {s : Set E} {J : Submodule ℝ E} (hs : s ⊆ J)
    (hJ : IsJordanSubmodule J) : generatedBySet s ≤ J

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.generatedBySet_mono
declarations.doc: Enlarging the generating set can only enlarge its generated Jordan fragment.
declarations.statement:
lemma generatedBySet_mono {s t : Set E} (hst : s ⊆ t) :
    generatedBySet s ≤ generatedBySet t

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.GeneratedBySet
declarations.doc: The arbitrary generated Jordan fragment as its own carrier type.
declarations.statement: abbrev GeneratedBySet (s : Set E) : Type _
instance : Mul (GeneratedBySet s)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.GeneratedBySet.val_mul
declarations.statement: lemma val_mul (x y : GeneratedBySet s) : ((x * y : GeneratedBySet s) : E) = (x : E) * (y : E)
instance : One (GeneratedBySet s)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.GeneratedBySet.val_one
declarations.statement: lemma val_one : ((1 : GeneratedBySet s) : E) = 1

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.GeneratedBySet.inclusion
declarations.doc: The canonical inclusion of a generated Jordan fragment into its ambient algebra.
declarations.statement: def inclusion : GeneratedBySet s →ₗ[ℝ] E

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.GeneratedBySet.inclusion_apply
declarations.statement: lemma inclusion_apply (x : GeneratedBySet s) : inclusion s x = (x : E)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.GeneratedBySet.inclusion_injective
declarations.statement: lemma inclusion_injective : Function.Injective (inclusion s)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.GeneratedBySet.instNonAssocCommRing
declarations.doc:
Every generated Jordan fragment inherits the ambient unital commutative nonassociative ring.
Associativity is intentionally absent: it is exceptional extra structure, not part of closure.
declarations.statement: instance instNonAssocCommRing : NonAssocCommRing (GeneratedBySet s)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.GeneratedBySet.inclusionJordanHom
declarations.doc: The canonical inclusion, bundled as a unital real Jordan homomorphism.
declarations.statement: def inclusionJordanHom : JordanHom (GeneratedBySet s) E
instance : SMulCommClass ℝ (GeneratedBySet s) (GeneratedBySet s)
instance : IsScalarTower ℝ (GeneratedBySet s) (GeneratedBySet s)

declarations.doc: The Jordan identity restricts to every generated Jordan fragment.
declarations.statement: instance : IsCommJordan (GeneratedBySet s)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.GeneratedBySet.inclusion_one
declarations.doc: The canonical inclusion preserves the order unit.
declarations.statement: lemma inclusion_one : inclusion s (1 : GeneratedBySet s) = 1

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.GeneratedBySet.inclusion_mul
declarations.doc: The canonical inclusion preserves the Jordan product.
declarations.statement:
lemma inclusion_mul (x y : GeneratedBySet s) :
    inclusion s (x * y) = inclusion s x * inclusion s y

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.generatedBySet_singleton_eq_generatedByOne
declarations.doc: The subalgebra generated by one observable is the span of its powers.
declarations.statement:
lemma generatedBySet_singleton_eq_generatedByOne (a : E) :
    generatedBySet ({a} : Set E) = generatedByOne a

modules.title: The subalgebra generated by one observable
modules.doc:
The span `J[a]` of the powers of an observable contains `1` and is Jordan-closed.

## i. Overview

The span `J[a]` of the powers of an observable `a` contains `1` and `a` and is closed under the
Jordan product.

## ii. Key results

- `JordanAlgebra.generatedByOne` : the span of the powers of `a`.
- `JordanAlgebra.mul_mem_generatedByOne` : it is closed under the Jordan product.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The generated submodule
- B. Closure under the Jordan product

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## B. Closure under the Jordan product

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.generatedByOne
declarations.doc:
The subalgebra generated by `1` and `a`, as an ℝ-submodule: the span of all Jordan powers of
`a` (which already includes `a^{[0]} = 1`).
declarations.statement: def generatedByOne (a : E) : Submodule ℝ E

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.jpow_mem_generatedByOne
declarations.statement: lemma jpow_mem_generatedByOne (a : E) (n : ℕ) : a ^[n] ∈ generatedByOne a

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.one_mem_generatedByOne
declarations.statement: lemma one_mem_generatedByOne (a : E) : (1 : E) ∈ generatedByOne a

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.self_mem_generatedByOne
declarations.statement: lemma self_mem_generatedByOne (a : E) : a ∈ generatedByOne a

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.mul_mem_generatedByOne
declarations.doc: `J[a]` is closed under the Jordan product.
declarations.statement:
lemma mul_mem_generatedByOne (a : E) {x y : E} (hx : x ∈ generatedByOne a)
    (hy : y ∈ generatedByOne a) : x * y ∈ generatedByOne a

modules.title: Quadratic representations of powers
modules.doc:
The quadratic representation on powers: `U_{aᵐ} aⁿ = a²ᵐ⁺ⁿ`.

## i. Overview

On powers the quadratic representation acts by `U_{aᵐ} aⁿ = a²ᵐ⁺ⁿ`.

## ii. Key results

- `JordanAlgebra.quadRep_jpow_jpow` : `U_{aᵐ} aⁿ = a²ᵐ⁺ⁿ`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Quadratic action on powers

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.quadRep_jpow_jpow
declarations.doc: `U_{aᵐ} aⁿ = a²ᵐ⁺ⁿ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma quadRep_jpow_jpow (a : E) (m n : ℕ) :
    U (a ^[m]) (a ^[n]) = a ^[2 * m + n]

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.quadRep_jpow
declarations.doc: A single outer factor raises the degree of a power by two.
declarations.statement: lemma quadRep_jpow (a : E) (n : ℕ) : U a (a ^[n]) = a ^[n + 2]

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.quadRep_jpow_one
declarations.doc: The quadratic representation of a power at the order unit is its even power.
declarations.statement: lemma quadRep_jpow_one (a : E) (m : ℕ) : U (a ^[m]) (1 : E) = a ^[2 * m]

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.quadRep_jpow_comp_jpow
declarations.doc: Quadratic representations compose additively on powers of a common element.
declarations.statement:
lemma quadRep_jpow_comp_jpow (a : E) (m n k : ℕ) :
    U (a ^[m]) (U (a ^[n]) (a ^[k])) = a ^[2 * m + 2 * n + k]

modules.title: `J[a]` is a commutative associative algebra
modules.doc:
The span `J[a]` of the powers of `a` is a commutative associative unital real algebra.

## i. Overview

By power-associativity the Jordan product restricted to the span `J[a]` of the powers of `a` is
associative. So `J[a]` is a commutative associative unital real algebra, to which Mathlib's theory
of commutative algebras applies.

## ii. Key results

- `JordanAlgebra.GeneratedByOne` : the subalgebra `J[a]`.
- `JordanAlgebra.GeneratedByOne.instCommRing` : its commutative ring structure.
- `JordanAlgebra.GeneratedByOne.instAlgebra` : its real algebra structure.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The carrier type and its multiplication
- B. The commutative ring structure
- C. The `ℝ`-algebra structure and inclusion

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. The carrier type and its multiplication

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.GeneratedByOne
declarations.doc:
The subalgebra generated by `1` and `a`, as its own type (the subtype of `generatedByOne a`).
This is what carries the associative `CommRing`/`Algebra ℝ` instances below; the ambient `E` itself
is generally *not* associative, so those instances cannot live on `E`.
declarations.statement: abbrev GeneratedByOne (a : E) : Type _
instance : Mul (GeneratedByOne a)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.GeneratedByOne.val_mul
declarations.statement: lemma val_mul (x y : GeneratedByOne a) : ((x * y : GeneratedByOne a) : E) = (x:E)*(y:E)
instance : One (GeneratedByOne a)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.GeneratedByOne.val_one
declarations.statement: lemma val_one : ((1 : GeneratedByOne a) : E) = 1

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.GeneratedByOne.mul_assoc
declarations.statement: lemma mul_assoc (x y z : GeneratedByOne a) : x * y * z = x * (y * z)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.GeneratedByOne.mul_comm
declarations.statement: lemma mul_comm (x y : GeneratedByOne a) : x * y = y * x

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.GeneratedByOne.one_mul
declarations.statement: lemma one_mul (x : GeneratedByOne a) : (1 : GeneratedByOne a) * x = x

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.GeneratedByOne.mul_one
declarations.statement: lemma mul_one (x : GeneratedByOne a) : x * (1 : GeneratedByOne a) = x

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.GeneratedByOne.left_distrib
declarations.statement: lemma left_distrib (x y z : GeneratedByOne a) : x * (y + z) = x * y + x * z

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.GeneratedByOne.right_distrib
declarations.statement: lemma right_distrib (x y z : GeneratedByOne a) : (x + y) * z = x * z + y * z

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.GeneratedByOne.instCommRing
declarations.doc: `J[a]` is a commutative ring under the Jordan product.
declarations.statement: instance instCommRing : CommRing (GeneratedByOne a)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.GeneratedByOne.inclusion
declarations.doc:
The inclusion `J[a] ↪ E`, the second arrow of
`C(σ(a), ℝ) → J[a] → E`. Just the submodule coercion, definitionally trivial.
declarations.statement: def inclusion : GeneratedByOne a → E

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.GeneratedByOne.inclusion_apply
declarations.statement: lemma inclusion_apply (x : GeneratedByOne a) : inclusion a x = (x : E)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.GeneratedByOne.inclusion_injective
declarations.statement: lemma inclusion_injective : Function.Injective (inclusion a)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.GeneratedByOne.instAlgebra
declarations.doc:
`J[a]` is an `ℝ`-algebra: scalars act via the ambient `Module ℝ E` structure (already
compatible with `∘` on `E`, hence with the restricted product on `J[a]`), and the algebra map is
just `c ↦ c • 1`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable instance instAlgebra : Algebra ℝ (GeneratedByOne a)

modules.title: Projection resolutions
modules.doc:
Projection resolutions: projection-valued effect measures and their bounded Borel calculus.

## i. Overview

A projection resolution is an effect-valued measure whose values are Jordan projections and whose
value on an intersection is the Jordan product of the values. Integrating bounded measurable
functions against it gives a bounded Borel functional calculus.

## ii. Key results

- `MeasurableProjectionResolution` : projection resolutions.
- `MeasurableProjectionResolution.jordanOrthogonal_of_disjoint` : disjoint sets give orthogonal
  projections.
- `MeasurableProjectionResolution.boundedBorel` : the bounded Borel functional calculus.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Bounded Borel calculus

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text:
## A. Bounded Borel calculus

The resolution does not duplicate the order-unit integral: in a JB algebra, which is complete in
its order-unit norm, this section gives that integral its spectral-calculus name.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.MeasurableProjectionResolution
declarations.doc:
A projection resolution: an effect-valued measure whose values are Jordan projections, with the
value on an intersection the Jordan product of the values.
declarations.statement:
structure MeasurableProjectionResolution (Ω : Type*) [MeasurableSpace Ω] (E : Type*)
    [IsJordanOrderUnit E] where
  /-- The underlying countably additive effect-valued measure. -/
  toEffectValuedMeasure : EffectValuedMeasure Ω E
  /-- Every measurable event is a Jordan projection. -/
  isJordanProjection' : ∀ s hs,
    JordanAlgebra.IsJordanProjection (toEffectValuedMeasure s hs : E)
  /-- Intersection of measurable events is multiplication of their projections. -/
  map_inter' : ∀ s t hs ht,
    (toEffectValuedMeasure s hs : E) * (toEffectValuedMeasure t ht : E) =
      (toEffectValuedMeasure (s ∩ t) (hs.inter ht) : E)
instance : CoeOut (MeasurableProjectionResolution Ω E) (EffectValuedMeasure Ω E)

instance : CoeFun (MeasurableProjectionResolution Ω E) fun _ =>
    ∀ s : Set Ω, MeasurableSet s → Effect E

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.MeasurableProjectionResolution.ext
declarations.doc:
Projection resolutions are determined by their event projections.  This is purely structural
and belongs below JBW: normal-state separation is only one later way to establish its premise.
declarations.statement:
lemma ext {P Q : MeasurableProjectionResolution Ω E}
    (h : ∀ s hs, (P s hs : E) = (Q s hs : E)) : P = Q

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.MeasurableProjectionResolution.map_empty
declarations.doc: The impossible event is the zero effect.
declarations.statement:
lemma map_empty (P : MeasurableProjectionResolution Ω E) :
    P ∅ MeasurableSet.empty = 0

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.MeasurableProjectionResolution.map_univ
declarations.doc: The whole outcome space is the unit effect.
declarations.statement:
lemma map_univ (P : MeasurableProjectionResolution Ω E) :
    P Set.univ MeasurableSet.univ = 1

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.MeasurableProjectionResolution.isJordanProjection
declarations.doc: Each event of a measurable projection resolution is an intrinsic Jordan projection.
declarations.statement:
lemma isJordanProjection (P : MeasurableProjectionResolution Ω E)
    (s : Set Ω) (hs : MeasurableSet s) :
    JordanAlgebra.IsJordanProjection (P s hs : E)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.MeasurableProjectionResolution.map_inter
declarations.doc: The projection product computes measurable intersection.
declarations.statement:
lemma map_inter (P : MeasurableProjectionResolution Ω E)
    (s t : Set Ω) (hs : MeasurableSet s) (ht : MeasurableSet t) :
    (P s hs : E) * (P t ht : E) = P (s ∩ t) (hs.inter ht)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.MeasurableProjectionResolution.jordanOrthogonal_of_disjoint
declarations.doc: Disjoint measurable events have Jordan-orthogonal projections.
declarations.statement:
lemma jordanOrthogonal_of_disjoint (P : MeasurableProjectionResolution Ω E)
    {s t : Set Ω} (hs : MeasurableSet s) (ht : MeasurableSet t) (hdisj : Disjoint s t) :
    JordanAlgebra.JordanOrthogonal (P s hs : E) (P t ht : E)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.MeasurableProjectionResolution.countably_additive
declarations.doc: The inherited countable-additivity law, stated in the ambient ordered Jordan algebra.
declarations.statement:
lemma countably_additive (P : MeasurableProjectionResolution Ω E) (s : ℕ → Set Ω)
    (hsm : ∀ n, MeasurableSet (s n)) (hs : Pairwise (Disjoint on s)) :
    IsLUB (Set.range fun N : ℕ => ∑ n ∈ Finset.range N, (P (s n) (hsm n) : E))
      (P (⋃ n, s n) (MeasurableSet.iUnion hsm) : E)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.MeasurableProjectionResolution.boundedBorel
declarations.doc:
The bounded Borel calculus of a measurable projection resolution. This is the existing
effect-valued integral applied to the underlying measure, not a parallel construction.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def boundedBorel (P : MeasurableProjectionResolution Ω E) (f : Ω → ℝ)
    (hf : Measurable f) {M : ℝ} (hM : ∀ x, |f x| ≤ M) : E

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.MeasurableProjectionResolution.nonneg_boundedBorel
declarations.doc: A nonnegative bounded Borel function has a positive value under the resolution calculus.
declarations.statement:
lemma nonneg_boundedBorel (P : MeasurableProjectionResolution Ω E) (f : Ω → ℝ)
    (hf : Measurable f) {M : ℝ} (hM : ∀ x, |f x| ≤ M) (hf0 : ∀ x, 0 ≤ f x) :
    0 ≤ P.boundedBorel f hf hM

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.MeasurableProjectionResolution.boundedBorel_indep_of_bound
declarations.doc:
The bounded Borel value is independent of the particular valid uniform bound used to
construct the completed order-unit integral.
declarations.statement:
lemma boundedBorel_indep_of_bound (P : MeasurableProjectionResolution Ω E) (f : Ω → ℝ)
    (hf : Measurable f) {M M' : ℝ} (hM : ∀ x, |f x| ≤ M) (hM' : ∀ x, |f x| ≤ M') :
    P.boundedBorel f hf hM = P.boundedBorel f hf hM'

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.MeasurableProjectionResolution.boundedBorel_add
declarations.doc: The bounded Borel calculus is additive.
declarations.statement:
lemma boundedBorel_add (P : MeasurableProjectionResolution Ω E) {f g : Ω → ℝ}
    (hf : Measurable f) {M : ℝ} (hM : ∀ x, |f x| ≤ M)
    (hg : Measurable g) {M' : ℝ} (hM' : ∀ x, |g x| ≤ M')
    (hfg : Measurable (f + g)) (hMfg : ∀ x, |(f + g) x| ≤ M + M') :
    P.boundedBorel (f + g) hfg hMfg =
      P.boundedBorel f hf hM + P.boundedBorel g hg hM'

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.MeasurableProjectionResolution.boundedBorel_smul
declarations.doc: The bounded Borel calculus is real-homogeneous.
declarations.statement:
lemma boundedBorel_smul (P : MeasurableProjectionResolution Ω E) (c : ℝ) {f : Ω → ℝ}
    (hf : Measurable f) {M : ℝ} (hM : ∀ x, |f x| ≤ M)
    (hcf : Measurable (c • f)) (hMcf : ∀ x, |(c • f) x| ≤ |c| * M) :
    P.boundedBorel (c • f) hcf hMcf = c • P.boundedBorel f hf hM

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.MeasurableProjectionResolution.boundedBorel_indicator
declarations.doc: The functional calculus of an indicator is the projection of the event.
declarations.statement:
lemma boundedBorel_indicator (P : MeasurableProjectionResolution Ω E) {s : Set Ω}
    (hs : MeasurableSet s) :
    P.boundedBorel (s.indicator fun _ : Ω => (1 : ℝ)) (measurable_const.indicator hs)
        (M := 1) (by intro x; by_cases hx : x ∈ s <;> simp [hx]) = (P s hs : E)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.MeasurableProjectionResolution.boundedBorel_one
declarations.doc:
The constant-one bounded Borel function integrates to the order unit.  This is the
normalization of the inherited effect-valued measure, recovered from the indicator law for the
whole outcome space.
declarations.statement:
lemma boundedBorel_one (P : MeasurableProjectionResolution Ω E) :
    P.boundedBorel (fun _ : Ω => (1 : ℝ)) measurable_const (M := 1) (by intro _; simp) = 1

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.MeasurableProjectionResolution.boundedBorelEffect
declarations.doc:
A measurable `[0,1]`-valued bounded function has an effect-valued bounded Borel calculus.
This packages positivity and normalization once at the shared projection-resolution layer; every
JBW projection resolution inherits it.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def boundedBorelEffect (P : MeasurableProjectionResolution Ω E) (f : Ω → ℝ)
    (hf : Measurable f) (hf0 : ∀ x, 0 ≤ f x) (hf1 : ∀ x, f x ≤ 1) : Effect E

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.MeasurableProjectionResolution.coe_boundedBorelEffect
declarations.doc: Coercing the bounded Borel effect forgets only its established interval bounds.
declarations.statement:
lemma coe_boundedBorelEffect (P : MeasurableProjectionResolution Ω E) (f : Ω → ℝ)
    (hf : Measurable f) (hf0 : ∀ x, 0 ≤ f x) (hf1 : ∀ x, f x ≤ 1) :
    (P.boundedBorelEffect f hf hf0 hf1 : E) =
      P.boundedBorel f hf (M := 1)
        (fun x => by rw [abs_of_nonneg (hf0 x)]; exact hf1 x)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.MeasurableProjectionResolution.ext_of_forall_boundedBorel_eq
declarations.doc:
The bounded Borel calculus determines a projection resolution.  It suffices to compare every
bounded measurable function because indicators recover exactly the event projections.

modules.title: The fundamental formula
modules.doc:
The fundamental formula `U_{U_a b} = U_a U_b U_a`, proved from the Jordan identity alone.

## i. Overview

The quadratic representation satisfies the fundamental formula `U_{U_a b} = U_a U_b U_a`. The proof
uses only the Jordan identity, through the inner derivations `[L_a, L_b]` and the triple operators.

## ii. Key results

- `JordanAlgebra.quadRep_quadRep_eq` : `U_{a²} = U_a²`.
- `JordanAlgebra.quadRep_fundamental` : **the fundamental formula** `U_{U_a b} = U_a U_b U_a`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Fundamental composition identity
- B. Polarizing the cubic commutation law: the triple commutator identity
- C. Normalizing the multiplication operator of a quadratic image
- D. The inner derivation and the Jordan-triple-system fundamental identity

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## B. Polarizing the cubic commutation law: the triple commutator identity
## C. Normalizing the multiplication operator of a quadratic image

## D. The inner derivation and the Jordan-triple-system fundamental identity

With the inner derivations `D_{a,b} = [L_a, L_b]` and the triple operators `V_{a,b} = L_{a ∘ b} +
D_{a,b}`, the fundamental identity of Jordan triple systems follows from the fact that inner
derivations are derivations of the Jordan product.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.cyclic_mulLeft_commutator
declarations.doc: The polarized Jordan identity, evaluated at a fourth element.
declarations.statement:
lemma cyclic_mulLeft_commutator (a b c x : E) :
    (a * ((b * c) * x) - (b * c) * (a * x)) +
        (b * ((c * a) * x) - (c * a) * (b * x)) +
          (c * ((a * b) * x) - (a * b) * (c * x)) = 0

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.cyclic_mulLeft_assoc_sum
declarations.doc: The polarized Jordan identity with its three commutators collected.
declarations.statement:
lemma cyclic_mulLeft_assoc_sum (a b c x : E) :
    a * ((b * c) * x) + b * ((c * a) * x) + c * ((a * b) * x) =
      (b * c) * (a * x) + (c * a) * (b * x) + (a * b) * (c * x)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.mulLeft_triple_normalize
declarations.doc:
The multiplication operator of a triple product in terms of multiplication operators of single
and double products.
declarations.statement:
lemma mulLeft_triple_normalize (a b c : E) :
    L (a * (b * c)) =
      ((L a).comp (L (b * c)) + (L b).comp (L (a * c)) + (L c).comp (L (a * b))) -
        (((L b).comp (L a)).comp (L c) + ((L c).comp (L a)).comp (L b))

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.mulLeft_cube_normalize
declarations.doc:
First specialization of `mulLeft_triple_normalize`: the multiplication operator of the third
Jordan power is a polynomial in `L_a` and `L_(a²)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma mulLeft_cube_normalize (a : E) :
    L (a * (a * a)) =
      (3 : ℝ) • ((L a).comp (L (a * a))) -
        (2 : ℝ) • (((L a).comp (L a)).comp (L a))

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.mul_self_mul_self_mulLeft_normalize
declarations.doc:
Second normalization step, evaluated at `x`: multiplication by `(a²)²` is reduced to the
commuting operators `L_a` and `L_(a²)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma mul_self_mul_self_mulLeft_normalize (a x : E) :
    ((a * a) * (a * a)) * x =
      (a * a) * ((a * a) * x) +
        (4 : ℝ) • (a * (a * ((a * a) * x))) -
          (4 : ℝ) • (a * (a * (a * (a * x))))

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.quadRep_mul_self_eq_comp
declarations.doc:
The quadratic representation of a Jordan square is the square of its quadratic
representation. This is the first nontrivial quadratic fundamental identity; its proof uses only
the finite operator normalization certificate and the Jordan commutation law.
declarations.statement:
lemma quadRep_mul_self_eq_comp (a : E) :
    U (a * a) = (U a).comp (U a)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.quadRep_add_mul_self_eq_comp
declarations.doc:
The square identity evaluated on a sum.  This keeps the polarizing source equation in a
canonical bilinear form: the remaining coefficient extraction is purely a finite calculation in
the noncommutative ring of linear endomorphisms.
declarations.statement:
lemma quadRep_add_mul_self_eq_comp (a b : E) :
    U ((a + b) * (a + b)) =
      (U a + (2 : ℝ) • quadRepBilin a b + U b).comp
        (U a + (2 : ℝ) • quadRepBilin a b + U b)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.quadRep_add_square_polarized
declarations.doc:
The positive polarization of the square identity, fully expanded in the canonical bilinear
quadratic operator.  Pairing this equation with its signed counterpart isolates the standard
mixed quadratic coefficient.
declarations.statement:
lemma quadRep_add_square_polarized (a b : E) :
    (U a).comp (U a) + (4 : ℝ) • U (a * b) + (U b).comp (U b) +
          (4 : ℝ) • quadRepBilin (a * a) (a * b) +
            (2 : ℝ) • quadRepBilin (a * a) (b * b) +
              (4 : ℝ) • quadRepBilin (a * b) (b * b) =
      (U a).comp (U a) + (4 : ℝ) • (quadRepBilin a b).comp (quadRepBilin a b) +
          (U b).comp (U b) + (U a).comp (U b) + (U b).comp (U a) +
            (2 : ℝ) • ((U a).comp (quadRepBilin a b) +
              (quadRepBilin a b).comp (U a) + (U b).comp (quadRepBilin a b) +
                (quadRepBilin a b).comp (U b))

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.quadRep_sub_square_polarized
declarations.doc:
The signed companion to `quadRep_add_square_polarized`.  Adding the two equations cancels
the cubic terms and leaves precisely the mixed quadratic coefficient.
declarations.statement:
lemma quadRep_sub_square_polarized (a b : E) :
    (U a).comp (U a) + (4 : ℝ) • U (a * b) + (U b).comp (U b) -
          (4 : ℝ) • quadRepBilin (a * a) (a * b) +
            (2 : ℝ) • quadRepBilin (a * a) (b * b) -
              (4 : ℝ) • quadRepBilin (a * b) (b * b) =
      (U a).comp (U a) + (4 : ℝ) • (quadRepBilin a b).comp (quadRepBilin a b) +
          (U b).comp (U b) + (U a).comp (U b) + (U b).comp (U a) -
            (2 : ℝ) • ((U a).comp (quadRepBilin a b) +
              (quadRepBilin a b).comp (U a) + (U b).comp (quadRepBilin a b) +
                (quadRepBilin a b).comp (U b))

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.quadRepBilin_comp_self_polarization
declarations.doc: The mixed polarization of the quadratic representation.
declarations.statement:
lemma quadRepBilin_comp_self_polarization (a b : E) :
    (4 : ℝ) • (quadRepBilin a b).comp (quadRepBilin a b) =
      (4 : ℝ) • U (a * b) + (2 : ℝ) • quadRepBilin (a * a) (b * b) -
        (U a).comp (U b) - (U b).comp (U a)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.quadRep_add_apply'
declarations.doc:
Pointwise expansion of `U (a + b)` at an arbitrary argument, the elementary consequence of
`quadRep_add_eq` used repeatedly below to unfold both sides of the polarized cubic law.
declarations.statement:
lemma quadRep_add_apply' (a b y : E) :
    U (a + b) y = U a y + (2 : ℝ) • quadRepBilin a b y + U b y

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.quadRep_sub_apply'
declarations.doc: Pointwise expansion of `U (a - b)` at an arbitrary argument.
declarations.statement:
lemma quadRep_sub_apply' (a b y : E) :
    U (a - b) y = U a y - (2 : ℝ) • quadRepBilin a b y + U b y

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.quadRepBilin_mulLeft_polarization
declarations.doc: The `(2, 1)`-component of `U_{a + b}` commuting with `L_{a + b}`.
declarations.statement:
lemma quadRepBilin_mulLeft_polarization (a b x : E) :
    U a (b * x) + (2 : ℝ) • quadRepBilin a b (a * x) =
      b * U a x + (2 : ℝ) • (a * quadRepBilin a b x)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.quadRepBilin_mulLeft_polarization'
declarations.doc: The `(1, 2)`-component of `U_{a + b}` commuting with `L_{a + b}`.
declarations.statement:
lemma quadRepBilin_mulLeft_polarization' (a b x : E) :
    U b (a * x) + (2 : ℝ) • quadRepBilin a b (b * x) =
      a * U b x + (2 : ℝ) • (b * quadRepBilin a b x)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.mulLeft_quadRep_normalize
declarations.doc: `L_{U_a b}` in terms of `L_a`, `L_b`, `L_{a²}` and `L_{a ∘ b}`.
declarations.statement:
lemma mulLeft_quadRep_normalize (a b : E) :
    L (U a b) =
      (2 : ℝ) • ((L a).comp (L (a * b))) + (L b).comp (L (a * a)) -
        (2 : ℝ) • (((L a).comp (L a)).comp (L b)) -
          (2 : ℝ) • (((L b).comp (L a)).comp (L a)) +
            (2 : ℝ) • (((L a).comp (L b)).comp (L a))

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.quadRep_quadRep_eq
declarations.doc: `U_{U_a b}` in terms of the quadratic representations of `a ∘ (a ∘ b)` and `a² ∘ b`.
declarations.statement:
lemma quadRep_quadRep_eq (a b : E) :
    U (U a b) =
      (4 : ℝ) • U (a * (a * b)) - (4 : ℝ) • quadRepBilin (a * (a * b)) (jpow a 2 * b) +
        U (jpow a 2 * b)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.innerDerivation_add_left
declarations.doc: Additivity of the inner derivation in its first defining argument.
declarations.statement:
lemma innerDerivation_add_left (a b c : E) :
    innerDerivation (a + b) c = innerDerivation a c + innerDerivation b c

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.innerDerivation_smul_left
declarations.doc: Real linearity of the inner derivation in its first defining argument.
declarations.statement:
lemma innerDerivation_smul_left (r : ℝ) (a b : E) :
    innerDerivation (r • a) b = r • innerDerivation a b

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.innerDerivation_add_right
declarations.doc: Additivity of the inner derivation in its second defining argument.
declarations.statement:
lemma innerDerivation_add_right (a b c : E) :
    innerDerivation a (b + c) = innerDerivation a b + innerDerivation a c

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.innerDerivation_smul_right
declarations.doc: Real linearity of the inner derivation in its second defining argument.
declarations.statement:
lemma innerDerivation_smul_right (r : ℝ) (a b : E) :
    innerDerivation a (r • b) = r • innerDerivation a b

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.innerDerivation_sub_left
declarations.doc: Difference expansion of the inner derivation in its first defining argument.
declarations.statement:
lemma innerDerivation_sub_left (a b c : E) :
    innerDerivation (a - b) c = innerDerivation a c - innerDerivation b c

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.jordanTriple_diag_left
declarations.doc:
The diagonal fact for the triple product at `(a, a, x)`: telescoping cancellation collapses
it to the plain associative square multiplication `a² x`.  This is the base case used in the
final specialization of the fundamental identity.
declarations.statement: lemma jordanTriple_diag_left (a x : E) : jordanTriple a a x = a ^[2] * x

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.innerDerivation_mul
declarations.doc: **Inner derivations are derivations**: `D_{a,b} (x ∘ y) = D_{a,b} x ∘ y + x ∘ D_{a,b} y`.
declarations.statement:
lemma innerDerivation_mul (a b x y : E) :
    innerDerivation a b (x * y) = (innerDerivation a b x) * y + x * (innerDerivation a b y)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.innerDerivation_mulLeft_comm
declarations.doc:
The derivation property restated as an operator commutator: `[D_{a,b}, L_x] = L_{D_{a,b} x}`.
This is `innerDerivation_mul` read as a statement about composed multiplication operators; it is
the operator-level form used to build the double commutator `innerDerivation_comm` below.
declarations.statement:
lemma innerDerivation_mulLeft_comm (a b x : E) :
    (innerDerivation a b).comp (L x) - (L x).comp (innerDerivation a b) =
      L (innerDerivation a b x)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.innerDerivation_comm
declarations.statement:
lemma innerDerivation_comm (a b c d : E) :
    (innerDerivation a b).comp (innerDerivation c d) -
        (innerDerivation c d).comp (innerDerivation a b) =
      innerDerivation (innerDerivation a b c) d + innerDerivation c (innerDerivation a b d)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.tripleOperator
declarations.doc:
The Jordan triple operator `V_{a,b} := L_{a*b} + D_{a,b}`.  Its action on any `x` is exactly
the Jordan triple product `{a,b,x}` (`triple_eq_V_apply`), so it packages `jordanTriple`'s middle
slot as a bundled linear operator, mirroring how `quadRepBilin a c` already packages `{a,·,c}`.
declarations.statement: def tripleOperator (a b : E) : E →ₗ[ℝ] E

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.triple_eq_V_apply
declarations.doc: The Jordan triple operator `V_{a,b}` computes the Jordan triple product in its middle slot.
declarations.statement: lemma triple_eq_V_apply (a b x : E) : V a b x = jordanTriple a b x

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.innerDerivation_sub_right
declarations.doc: Difference expansion of the inner derivation in its second defining argument.
declarations.statement:
lemma innerDerivation_sub_right (a b c : E) :
    innerDerivation a (b - c) = innerDerivation a b - innerDerivation a c

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.innerDerivation_mul_left
declarations.doc: The inner derivation of a product in its first argument.
declarations.statement:
lemma innerDerivation_mul_left (a b q e : E) :
    innerDerivation (a * b) q e = innerDerivation a (b * q) e + innerDerivation b (a * q) e

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.tripleOperator_comm
declarations.doc:
`[V_{a,b}, V_{c,d}] = V_{{a,b,c},d} - V_{c,{b,a,d}}`, the fundamental identity of Jordan triple
systems.
declarations.statement:
lemma tripleOperator_comm (a b c d : E) :
    (V a b).comp (V c d) - (V c d).comp (V a b) =
      V (jordanTriple a b c) d - V c (jordanTriple b a d)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.tripleOperator_quadRep_step
declarations.doc: The triple-operator commutator law specialized to `(x, y, x, z)` and evaluated at `x`.
declarations.statement:
lemma tripleOperator_quadRep_step (x y z : E) :
    V x y (U x z) =
      (2 : ℝ) • V x z (U x y) - U x (jordanTriple y x z)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.V_quadRep_eq_quadRep_triple
declarations.doc:
Combining `tripleOperator_quadRep_step` with its own `y ↔ z` companion (and
`jordanTriple_outer_comm`, which identifies `jordanTriple z x y` with `jordanTriple y x z`)
eliminates the `V x z (U x y)` cross-term entirely.
declarations.statement:
lemma V_quadRep_eq_quadRep_triple (x y z : E) :
    V x y (U x z) = U x (jordanTriple y x z)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.quadRep_fundamental_apply
declarations.doc:
Pointwise form of the fundamental formula for the quadratic representation:
`U_{U_x y} z = U_x U_y U_x z`.
declarations.statement:
lemma quadRep_fundamental_apply (x y z : E) :
    U (U x y) z = U x (U y (U x z))

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.quadRep_fundamental
declarations.doc:
The fundamental formula for the quadratic representation:
`U_{U_x y} = U_x ∘ U_y ∘ U_x`.
declarations.statement:
lemma quadRep_fundamental (x y : E) :
    U (U x y) = (U x).comp ((U y).comp (U x))

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.quadRep_fundamental_jpow
declarations.doc: The fundamental formula on powers of one element.
declarations.statement:
lemma quadRep_fundamental_jpow (a : E) (m n k : ℕ) :
    U (U ((a ^[m]) : E) ((a ^[n]) : E)) ((a ^[k]) : E) =
      U ((a ^[m]) : E) (U ((a ^[n]) : E) (U ((a ^[m]) : E) ((a ^[k]) : E)))

modules.title: Composing quadratic operations
modules.doc:
The fundamental formula as an identity between the positive linear maps `U_a`.

## i. Overview

For quadratically positive Jordan algebras the positive maps `U_a` compose according to the
fundamental formula.

## ii. Key results

- `JordanAlgebra.quadRepPositiveLinearMap_fundamental` : the fundamental formula for the positive
  maps `U_a`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Composition of positive quadratic operations

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. Composition of positive quadratic operations

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.quadRepPositiveLinearMap_mul_self
declarations.doc:
Squaring the filtering observable composes its positive quadratic operation with itself.
This is the bundled operational form of `U_(a²) = U_a ∘ U_a`.
declarations.statement:
lemma quadRepPositiveLinearMap_mul_self (a : E) :
    quadRepPositiveLinearMap (a * a) =
      (quadRepPositiveLinearMap a).comp (quadRepPositiveLinearMap a)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.quadRepPositiveLinearMap_fundamental
declarations.doc:
The quadratic fundamental formula as an equality of positive operations.  Thus a filter
whose observable is `U_a b` is precisely the sequential filter `U_a`, then `U_b`, then `U_a`.
The statement is intrinsic Jordan algebra; positivity is used only to bundle the maps.
declarations.statement:
lemma quadRepPositiveLinearMap_fundamental (a b : E) :
    quadRepPositiveLinearMap (U a b) =
      (quadRepPositiveLinearMap a).comp
        ((quadRepPositiveLinearMap b).comp (quadRepPositiveLinearMap a))

modules.title: Positive quadratic representations
modules.doc:
Quadratically positive Jordan order-unit spaces, where each `U_a` is a positive linear map.

## i. Overview

The quadratic representation `U_a` is the Jordan version of the operation `b ↦ a b a`. A Jordan
order-unit space is quadratically positive when every `U_a` preserves the positive cone; then each
`U_a` is a positive linear map.

## ii. Key results

- `JordanAlgebra.IsQuadraticallyPositive` : quadratically positive Jordan order-unit spaces.
- `JordanAlgebra.quadRepPositiveLinearMap` : `U_a` as a positive linear map.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Quadratically positive Jordan algebras
- B. The positive linear map `U_a`

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.IsQuadraticallyPositive
declarations.doc: Every quadratic representation `U_a` preserves the positive cone.
declarations.statement:
class IsQuadraticallyPositive (E : Type*) [NonAssocCommRing E] [PartialOrder E]
    [IsOrderedAddMonoid E] [Module ℝ E] [SMulCommClass ℝ E E] : Prop where
  quadRep_nonneg : ∀ (a : E) {b : E}, 0 ≤ b → 0 ≤ U a b

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.quadRep_nonneg
declarations.doc: Quadratic representations map nonnegative observables to nonnegative observables.
declarations.statement: lemma quadRep_nonneg (a : E) {b : E} (hb : 0 ≤ b) : 0 ≤ U a b

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.quadRepPositiveLinearMap
declarations.doc: The quadratic representation as a bundled positive linear operation.
declarations.statement: def quadRepPositiveLinearMap (a : E) : E →ₚ[ℝ] E

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.coe_quadRepPositiveLinearMap
declarations.statement:
lemma coe_quadRepPositiveLinearMap (a : E) :
    (quadRepPositiveLinearMap a : E →ₗ[ℝ] E) = U a

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.quadRepPositiveLinearMap_apply
declarations.statement: lemma quadRepPositiveLinearMap_apply (a b : E) : quadRepPositiveLinearMap a b = U a b

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.quadRepPositiveLinearMap_one
declarations.doc: The unit has the identity quadratic operation.
declarations.statement:
lemma quadRepPositiveLinearMap_one :
    quadRepPositiveLinearMap (1 : E) = PositiveLinearMap.id ℝ E

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.quadRep_monotone
declarations.doc: Positivity of `U a` implies monotonicity.
declarations.statement: lemma quadRep_monotone (a : E) : Monotone (U a)

modules.title: Peirce decomposition
modules.doc:
The Peirce decomposition for a Jordan projection `p`; `U_p` projects onto the `1`-component.

## i. Overview

For a Jordan projection `p` every observable splits into the Peirce components where `L_p` acts by
`1`, `½` and `0`. The quadratic representation `U_p` is the idempotent projection onto the
`1`-component.

## ii. Key results

- `JordanAlgebra.IsJordanProjection.peirceOne` : the `1`-component.
- `JordanAlgebra.IsJordanProjection.peirce_decomposition` : the Peirce decomposition.
- `JordanAlgebra.IsJordanProjection.quadRep_range_eq_peirceOne` : `U_p` projects onto the
  `1`-component.
