- `JordanAlgebra.IsJordanProjection.quadRep_comp_self` : `U_p` is idempotent.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The Peirce polynomial
- B. The Peirce-`1` compression

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.IsJordanProjection.peirce_polynomial
declarations.doc:
If `p` is idempotent, multiplication by `p` obeys the Peirce polynomial
`2 L_p^3 - 3 L_p^2 + L_p = 0`.  This is a specialization of the polarized Jordan identity and
is the exact algebraic fact needed to make `U_p` an idempotent compression.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.IsJordanProjection.peirceOne
declarations.doc:
The Peirce-`1` eigenspace of a Jordan projection: the fixed submodule of multiplication by
`p`.  This is purely algebraic; no order or norm structure is involved.
declarations.statement: def IsJordanProjection.peirceOne [SMulCommClass ℝ E E] (p : E) : Submodule ℝ E

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.IsJordanProjection.mem_peirceOne_iff
declarations.doc: Membership in the Peirce-`1` space is exactly the eigenvalue-one equation.
declarations.statement:
lemma IsJordanProjection.mem_peirceOne_iff [SMulCommClass ℝ E E] (p x : E) :
    x ∈ IsJordanProjection.peirceOne p ↔ p * x = x

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.IsJordanProjection.peirceZero
declarations.doc: The Peirce-`0` eigenspace of a projection.
declarations.statement: def IsJordanProjection.peirceZero [SMulCommClass ℝ E E] (p : E) : Submodule ℝ E

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.IsJordanProjection.mem_peirceZero_iff
declarations.doc: Membership in the Peirce-`0` space is exactly annihilation by `p`.
declarations.statement:
lemma IsJordanProjection.mem_peirceZero_iff [SMulCommClass ℝ E E] (p x : E) :
    x ∈ IsJordanProjection.peirceZero p ↔ p * x = 0

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.IsJordanProjection.peirceHalf
declarations.doc:
The Peirce-`1/2` eigenspace of a projection.  The equation is written without division so it
works directly with the real linear-map structure.
declarations.statement: def IsJordanProjection.peirceHalf [SMulCommClass ℝ E E] (p : E) : Submodule ℝ E

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.IsJordanProjection.mem_peirceHalf_iff
declarations.doc: Membership in the Peirce-`1/2` space is exactly `2 (p ∘ x) = x`.
declarations.statement:
lemma IsJordanProjection.mem_peirceHalf_iff [SMulCommClass ℝ E E] (p x : E) :
    x ∈ IsJordanProjection.peirceHalf p ↔ (2 : ℝ) • (p * x) = x

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.IsJordanProjection.disjoint_peirceZero_peirceHalf
declarations.doc: The Peirce-`0` and Peirce-`1/2` spaces intersect only at zero.
declarations.statement:
lemma IsJordanProjection.disjoint_peirceZero_peirceHalf [SMulCommClass ℝ E E] (p : E) :
    Disjoint (IsJordanProjection.peirceZero p) (IsJordanProjection.peirceHalf p)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.IsJordanProjection.disjoint_peirceZero_peirceOne
declarations.doc: The Peirce-`0` and Peirce-`1` spaces intersect only at zero.
declarations.statement:
lemma IsJordanProjection.disjoint_peirceZero_peirceOne [SMulCommClass ℝ E E] (p : E) :
    Disjoint (IsJordanProjection.peirceZero p) (IsJordanProjection.peirceOne p)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.IsJordanProjection.disjoint_peirceHalf_peirceOne
declarations.doc: The Peirce-`1/2` and Peirce-`1` spaces intersect only at zero.
declarations.statement:
lemma IsJordanProjection.disjoint_peirceHalf_peirceOne [SMulCommClass ℝ E E] (p : E) :
    Disjoint (IsJordanProjection.peirceHalf p) (IsJordanProjection.peirceOne p)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.IsJordanProjection.eq_zero_of_peirce_sum_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
The three Peirce eigenspaces are jointly direct: a vanishing sum of a `0`, `1/2`, and `1`
eigenvector has all three summands equal to zero.
declarations.statement:
lemma IsJordanProjection.eq_zero_of_peirce_sum_eq_zero [SMulCommClass ℝ E E] (p : E)
    {x₀ xhalf x₁ : E} (hx₀ : x₀ ∈ IsJordanProjection.peirceZero p)
    (hxhalf : xhalf ∈ IsJordanProjection.peirceHalf p)
    (hx₁ : x₁ ∈ IsJordanProjection.peirceOne p) (hsum : x₀ + xhalf + x₁ = 0) :
    x₀ = 0 ∧ xhalf = 0 ∧ x₁ = 0

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.IsJordanProjection.peirceZeroPart
declarations.doc: The algebraic Peirce-`0` component of `x` relative to `p`.
declarations.statement: def IsJordanProjection.peirceZeroPart (p x : E) : E

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.IsJordanProjection.peirceHalfPart
declarations.doc: The algebraic Peirce-`1/2` component of `x` relative to `p`.
declarations.statement: def IsJordanProjection.peirceHalfPart (p x : E) : E

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.IsJordanProjection.mul_peirceZeroPart
declarations.doc: The Peirce-`0` component is annihilated by `p`.
declarations.statement:
lemma IsJordanProjection.mul_peirceZeroPart [SMulCommClass ℝ E E] [IsCommJordan E] {p : E}
    (hp : IsJordanProjection p) (x : E) : p * IsJordanProjection.peirceZeroPart p x = 0

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.IsJordanProjection.peirceZeroPart_mem
declarations.doc: The algebraic zero component belongs to the Peirce-`0` subspace.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.IsJordanProjection.two_smul_mul_peirceHalfPart
declarations.doc: The Peirce-`1/2` component has eigenvalue `1/2` for multiplication by `p`.
declarations.statement:
lemma IsJordanProjection.two_smul_mul_peirceHalfPart [SMulCommClass ℝ E E] [IsCommJordan E]
    {p : E} (hp : IsJordanProjection p) (x : E) :
    (2 : ℝ) • (p * IsJordanProjection.peirceHalfPart p x) =
      IsJordanProjection.peirceHalfPart p x

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.IsJordanProjection.peirceHalfPart_mem
declarations.doc: The algebraic half component belongs to the Peirce-`1/2` subspace.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.IsJordanProjection.peirce_decomposition
declarations.doc:
Every element has a canonical algebraic Peirce decomposition.  The three summands have
eigenvalues `0`, `1/2`, and `1` respectively; the `1` summand is `U_p x`.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.IsJordanProjection.mul_quadRep
declarations.doc: Quadratic compression by a projection lands in the Peirce-`1` eigenspace.
declarations.statement:
lemma IsJordanProjection.mul_quadRep [SMulCommClass ℝ E E] [IsCommJordan E] {p : E}
    (hp : IsJordanProjection p) (x : E) : p * U p x = U p x

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.IsJordanProjection.quadRep_mem_peirceOne
declarations.doc: The `U_p` summand in `peirce_decomposition` belongs to the Peirce-`1` subspace.
declarations.statement:
lemma IsJordanProjection.quadRep_mem_peirceOne [SMulCommClass ℝ E E] [IsCommJordan E] {p : E}
    (hp : IsJordanProjection p) (x : E) : U p x ∈ IsJordanProjection.peirceOne p

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.IsJordanProjection.quadRep_eq_self_of_mul_eq_self
declarations.doc: Quadratic compression fixes every Peirce-`1` element.
declarations.statement:
lemma IsJordanProjection.quadRep_eq_self_of_mul_eq_self [SMulCommClass ℝ E E]
    {p x : E} (hp : IsJordanProjection p) (hx : p * x = x) : U p x = x

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.IsJordanProjection.quadRep_range_eq_peirceOne
declarations.doc:
For a projection, quadratic compression is exactly the algebraic projection onto the
Peirce-`1` eigenspace.
declarations.statement:
lemma IsJordanProjection.quadRep_range_eq_peirceOne [SMulCommClass ℝ E E] [IsCommJordan E]
    {p : E} (hp : IsJordanProjection p) :
    LinearMap.range (U p) = IsJordanProjection.peirceOne p

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.IsJordanProjection.quadRep_comp_self
declarations.doc:
Quadratic compression by an idempotent is idempotent: `U_p ∘ U_p = U_p`.
Consequently, `U_p` is a purely algebraic projection onto its range.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.IsJordanProjection.quadRep_eq_self_of_mem_range
declarations.doc: Every element in the range of `U_p` is fixed by `U_p`.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.IsJordanProjection.quadRep_sub_quadRep
declarations.doc: The residual after quadratic compression lies in the kernel of that compression.
declarations.statement:
lemma IsJordanProjection.quadRep_sub_quadRep [SMulCommClass ℝ E E] [IsCommJordan E]
    {p x : E} (hp : IsJordanProjection p) :
    U p (x - U p x) = 0

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.quadRep_add_sub_quadRep
declarations.doc: `x = U_p x + (x - U_p x)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma quadRep_add_sub_quadRep [SMulCommClass ℝ E E] (p x : E) :
    U p x + (x - U p x) = x

modules.title: The Jordan triple product
modules.doc:
The Jordan triple product `{a, b, c}`: symmetry, linearity and the diagonal `{a, b, a} = U_a b`.

## i. Overview

The Jordan triple product `{a, b, c} = a ∘ (b ∘ c) + c ∘ (b ∘ a) - (a ∘ c) ∘ b` is the polarization
of the quadratic representation: `{a, b, a} = U_a b`.

## ii. Key results

- `JordanAlgebra.jordanTriple` : the triple product.
- `JordanAlgebra.jordanTriple_diag` : `{a, b, a} = U_a b`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The triple product
- B. Symmetry, diagonal and linearity

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.jordanTriple
declarations.doc: The Jordan triple product, written directly to retain a computable algebraic definition.
declarations.statement: def jordanTriple (a b c : E) : E

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.jordanTriple_eq_quadRepBilin_apply
declarations.doc:
The triple product is precisely the action of the canonical bilinear quadratic operator on
its middle variable.  Thus no second bundled triple-operator API is needed: `quadRepBilin a c`
is already the operator `b ↦ {a,b,c}`.
declarations.statement:
lemma jordanTriple_eq_quadRepBilin_apply (a b c : E) :
    jordanTriple a b c = quadRepBilin a c b

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.quadRepPolar_eq_two_smul_jordanTriple
declarations.doc: The existing quadratic polarization is exactly twice the Jordan triple product.
declarations.statement:
lemma quadRepPolar_eq_two_smul_jordanTriple (a b c : E) :
    quadRepPolar a c b = (2 : ℝ) • jordanTriple a b c

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.jordanTriple_outer_comm
declarations.doc: The Jordan triple product is symmetric in its outer variables.
declarations.statement: lemma jordanTriple_outer_comm (a b c : E) : jordanTriple a b c = jordanTriple c b a

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.jordanTriple_diag
declarations.doc: The diagonal of the triple product is the quadratic representation.
declarations.statement: lemma jordanTriple_diag (a b : E) : jordanTriple a b a = U a b

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.jordanTriple_add_left
declarations.doc: Additivity in the first outer variable.
declarations.statement:
lemma jordanTriple_add_left (a b c d : E) :
    jordanTriple (a + b) c d = jordanTriple a c d + jordanTriple b c d

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.jordanTriple_smul_left
declarations.doc: Real linearity in the first outer variable.
declarations.statement:
lemma jordanTriple_smul_left (r : ℝ) (a b c : E) :
    jordanTriple (r • a) b c = r • jordanTriple a b c

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.jordanTriple_add_right
declarations.doc: Additivity in the third outer variable.
declarations.statement:
lemma jordanTriple_add_right (a b c d : E) :
    jordanTriple a b (c + d) = jordanTriple a b c + jordanTriple a b d

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.JordanAlgebra.jordanTriple_smul_right
declarations.doc: Real linearity in the third outer variable.
declarations.statement:

modules.title: Jordan derivations
modules.doc:
Jordan derivations, their commutator Lie algebra and the inner derivations `[L_a, L_b]`.

## i. Overview

A Jordan derivation is a linear map `D` with `D (a ∘ b) = D a ∘ b + a ∘ D b`, an infinitesimal
symmetry of the observables. Commutators `[L_a, L_b]` of multiplication operators are the inner
derivations.

## ii. Key results

- `JordanAlgebra.JordanDerivation` : Jordan derivations.
- `JordanAlgebra.inner` : inner derivations.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Jordan derivations
- B. The vector space of derivations
- C. The commutator Lie algebra
- D. Inner derivations

## iv. References

- Adapted from Cobord, `Jordan/StructureAlgebra.lean`.

modules.title: Measurements
modules.doc:
Measurements as normal channels from the classical outcome system, and their Born laws.

## i. Overview

A measurement with outcomes in `Ω` turns the system into a classical record: its outcome. So a
measurement is a channel from the system into the classical system of outcomes. In the Heisenberg
picture used here, it sends each observable `f` of the outcome, a bounded measurable function on
`Ω`, to the observable of the system whose expectation is the expectation of `f` after the
measurement. It is normal: it respects limits of increasing sequences.

The indicator of an event goes to the effect testing whether the outcome lands in it; these effects
form an effect-valued measure. In a normal state `ω` of the system, the outcome record is in the
normal state `ω ∘ M` of the classical system, which is a probability distribution over the outcomes:
the Born law. Measuring the outcome of a classical system itself is the identity channel.

## ii. Key results

- `Measurement Ω E` : a measurement with outcomes in `Ω`, a normal channel from the classical system
  of outcomes.
- `Measurement.toEffectValuedMeasure` : the effects of the events of a measurement.
- `Measurement.probabilityLaw` : the Born law of a measurement in a normal state.
- `Measurement.integral_probabilityLaw` : the average of `f` under the Born law is the expectation
  of `M f`.
- `Measurement.map` : measuring after a normal channel.
- `BoundedMeasurable.outcome` : measuring the outcome of a classical system.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Measurements
- B. The Born law
- C. Measuring after a channel

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Measurement
declarations.doc:
A measurement with outcomes in `Ω`: a normal channel from the classical system of outcomes
into the system.
declarations.statement:
structure Measurement (Ω : Type*) [MeasurableSpace Ω] (E : Type*) [OrderUnitSpace E] where
  /-- The channel sending observables of the outcome to observables of the system. -/
  toChannel : Channel (BoundedMeasurable Ω) E
  /-- The channel is normal. -/
  isNormal : toChannel.IsNormal

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Measurement.ext
declarations.statement: lemma ext {M N : Measurement Ω E} (h : M.toChannel = N.toChannel) : M = N

declarations.doc: The effect testing whether the outcome lies in an event.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable instance :
    CoeFun (Measurement Ω E) fun _ => ∀ s : Set Ω, MeasurableSet s → Effect E

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Measurement.coe_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma coe_apply (M : Measurement Ω E) (s : Set Ω) (hs : MeasurableSet s) :
    (M s hs : E) = M.toChannel (BoundedMeasurable.indicator s hs)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Measurement.toEffectValuedMeasure
declarations.doc: The effects of the events of a measurement form an effect-valued measure.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def toEffectValuedMeasure (M : Measurement Ω E) : EffectValuedMeasure Ω E

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Measurement.toEffectValuedMeasure_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma toEffectValuedMeasure_apply (M : Measurement Ω E) (s : Set Ω) (hs : MeasurableSet s) :
    M.toEffectValuedMeasure s hs = M s hs

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Measurement.map_empty
declarations.statement: lemma map_empty (M : Measurement Ω E) : M ∅ .empty = 0

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Measurement.map_univ
declarations.statement: lemma map_univ (M : Measurement Ω E) : M .univ .univ = 1

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Measurement.isNormal_comp
declarations.statement:
lemma isNormal_comp (M : Measurement Ω E) {ω : 𝓢[ℝ, E]} (hω : ω.IsNormal) :
    (ω.comp M.toChannel).IsNormal

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Measurement.probabilityLaw
declarations.doc: The Born law: the distribution of the outcome of `M` in the normal state `ω`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def probabilityLaw (M : Measurement Ω E) (ω : 𝓢[ℝ, E]) (hω : ω.IsNormal) :
    ProbabilityMeasure Ω

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Measurement.probabilityLaw_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma probabilityLaw_apply (M : Measurement Ω E) (ω : 𝓢[ℝ, E]) (hω : ω.IsNormal)
    (s : Set Ω) (hs : MeasurableSet s) :
    (M.probabilityLaw ω hω : Measure Ω) s = ENNReal.ofReal (ω (M s hs))

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Measurement.integral_probabilityLaw
declarations.doc:
The average of an observable `f` of the outcome under the Born law is the expectation of
`M f`.
declarations.statement:
lemma integral_probabilityLaw (M : Measurement Ω E) (ω : 𝓢[ℝ, E]) (hω : ω.IsNormal)
    (f : BoundedMeasurable Ω) : ∫ x, f x ∂(M.probabilityLaw ω hω : Measure Ω) = ω (M.toChannel f)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Measurement.probabilityLaw_eq
declarations.doc: The Born law of a measurement is the Born law of its effect-valued measure.
declarations.statement:
lemma probabilityLaw_eq (M : Measurement Ω E) (ω : 𝓢[ℝ, E]) (hω : ω.IsNormal) :
    M.probabilityLaw ω hω = M.toEffectValuedMeasure.probabilityLaw ω hω

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Measurement.map
declarations.doc:
Measuring `M` after the normal channel `φ`: the outcome observables go through `M`, then
through `φ`.
declarations.statement: def map (M : Measurement Ω E) (φ : Channel E F) (hφ : φ.IsNormal) : Measurement Ω F

declarations.statement:
lemma coe_map_apply (M : Measurement Ω E) (φ : Channel E F) (hφ : φ.IsNormal) (s : Set Ω)
    (hs : MeasurableSet s) : (M.map φ hφ s hs : F) = φ (M s hs)

declarations.statement:
lemma coe_outcome_apply (s : Set Ω) (hs : MeasurableSet s) :

declarations.name: BoundedMeasurable.probabilityLaw_outcome

declarations.statement:
lemma probabilityLaw_outcome (ω : 𝓢[ℝ, BoundedMeasurable Ω]) (hω : ω.IsNormal) :
    outcome.probabilityLaw ω hω = toMeasure ω hω

modules.title: Binary measurements
modules.doc:
The yes/no measurement defined by an effect of an Archimedean system.

## i. Overview

Every effect of an Archimedean system defines a yes/no measurement: the outcome `true` has the
effect itself, the outcome `false` its complement.

## ii. Key results

- `Effect.binaryMeasurement` : the binary measurement associated to an effect.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Binary measurements

## iv. References

* None.

The effect of each outcome of the binary measurement of `e`: `e` for `true`, its complement

    binaryMeasurement e {false} h = complement e

modules.title: The Born rule for effect-valued measures
modules.doc:
An effect-valued measure sends each normal state to a probability law on its outcomes.

## i. Overview

A state is a normal channel `ω : 𝓢[ℝ, E]`, so it pushes an effect-valued measure `μ` on `E`
forward to one, `μ.map ω`, on `ℝ`. An effect-valued measure on `ℝ` is just a probability measure.
So `μ` sends every normal state to a probability distribution over its outcomes:
`μ.probabilityLaw ω`, giving event `s` probability `ω (μ s)`.

## ii. Key results

- `EffectValuedMeasure.toProbabilityMeasure` : an effect-valued measure on `ℝ` is a
  probability measure.
- `EffectValuedMeasure.probabilityLaw` : the outcome distribution of `μ` in the state `ω`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Effect-valued measures on `ℝ` are probability measures
- B. The Born rule
- C. Relabeling outcomes

## iv. References

* None.

modules.title: Integrating bounded functions against an effect-valued measure
modules.doc:
The integral of bounded measurable functions against an effect-valued measure.

## i. Overview

If the observables are complete for the order-unit norm, the integral of simple functions extends to
bounded measurable functions. A bounded function is uniformly approximated by simple functions on a
mesh of width `1 / (n + 1)`, and simple functions within `ε` and `ε'` of `f` have integrals within
`ε + ε'`. So the integrals of the approximations converge, to a limit that does not depend on the
approximation or the bound. The integral is linear and positive, and agrees with the simple integral
on simple functions.

## ii. Key results

- `EffectValuedMeasure.meshPiece`, `EffectValuedMeasure.meshWeight` : the mesh approximation.
- `EffectValuedMeasure.orderUnitNorm_simpleIntegral_sub_le` : nearby simple functions have nearby
  integrals.
- `EffectValuedMeasure.integral` : the integral of a bounded measurable function.
- `EffectValuedMeasure.tendsto_of_uniformly_approximating` : every uniform approximation gives the
  integral.
- `EffectValuedMeasure.integral_add`, `EffectValuedMeasure.nonneg_integral` : linearity and
  positivity.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The mesh approximation of a bounded measurable function
- B. Linear operations on simple values
- C. Comparing the simple integrals of two approximations
- D. The integral, via completeness

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. The mesh approximation of a bounded measurable function
## B. Linear operations on simple values

## C. Comparing the simple integrals of two approximations

The key ingredient for both the Cauchy property and the independence of the eventual integral
from the choice of approximating sequence: if two simple functions (over possibly different
partitions) both stay within `ε`, resp. `ε'`, of the same `f` everywhere, their integrals against
`μ` stay within `ε + ε'` of each other, in the order-unit norm.

## D. The integral, via completeness

The order-unit norm makes `E` a normed group, assumed complete. Most order-unit spaces are not
complete.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.EffectValuedMeasure.meshBound
declarations.doc:
The number of width-`1/(n+1)` mesh cells it takes to reach out to `M` on either side of `0`:
`⌈(n+1)*M⌉₊`. Only depends on `M` and `n`, not on any particular function.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def meshBound (M : ℝ) (n : ℕ) : ℕ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.EffectValuedMeasure.MeshIndex
declarations.doc:
The mesh cell label set at scale `n` covering `[-M, M]`: integers from `-meshBound M n` to
`meshBound M n`.
declarations.statement: abbrev MeshIndex (M : ℝ) (n : ℕ) : Type

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.EffectValuedMeasure.meshWeight
declarations.doc: The weight of mesh cell `k` at scale `n`: `k/(n+1)`, the left endpoint of the cell.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def meshWeight (M : ℝ) (n : ℕ) (k : MeshIndex M n) : ℝ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.EffectValuedMeasure.meshPiece
declarations.doc:
The mesh cell `k` at scale `n`, pulled back along `f`: the points where `f` rounds down to
`k/(n+1)` at that scale, i.e. `⌊(n+1)*f(x)⌋ = k`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def meshPiece (f : Ω → ℝ) (M : ℝ) (n : ℕ) (k : MeshIndex M n) : Set Ω

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.EffectValuedMeasure.mem_meshPiece_iff
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_meshPiece_iff (n : ℕ) (k : MeshIndex M n) (x : Ω) :
    x ∈ meshPiece f M n k ↔ ⌊((n : ℝ) + 1) * f x⌋ = (k : ℤ)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.EffectValuedMeasure.measurableSet_meshPiece
declarations.statement: lemma measurableSet_meshPiece (n : ℕ) (k : MeshIndex M n) : MeasurableSet (meshPiece f M n k)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.EffectValuedMeasure.meshIndexOf
declarations.doc:
The label the mesh assigns to the point `x`, together with the proof that it lies in range:
`⌊(n+1)*f(x)⌋` always lies in `[-meshBound M n, meshBound M n]` once `|f x| ≤ M`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def meshIndexOf (n : ℕ) (x : Ω) : MeshIndex M n

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.EffectValuedMeasure.meshIndexOf_coe
declarations.statement:
lemma meshIndexOf_coe (n : ℕ) (x : Ω) :
    ((meshIndexOf hM n x : MeshIndex M n) : ℤ) = ⌊((n : ℝ) + 1) * f x⌋

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.EffectValuedMeasure.mem_meshPiece_meshIndexOf
declarations.statement: lemma mem_meshPiece_meshIndexOf (n : ℕ) (x : Ω) : x ∈ meshPiece f M n (meshIndexOf hM n x)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.EffectValuedMeasure.isPartition_meshPiece
declarations.doc: The mesh pieces at scale `n` form a finite measurable partition of `Ω`.
declarations.statement: lemma isPartition_meshPiece (n : ℕ) : IsPartition (meshPiece f M n)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.EffectValuedMeasure.simpleValue_meshWeight_meshPiece
declarations.doc: The value of the mesh simple function at `x` is the label `f` is assigned, over `(n+1)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma simpleValue_meshWeight_meshPiece (n : ℕ) (x : Ω) :
    simpleValue (meshWeight M n) (meshPiece f M n) x =
      (⌊((n : ℝ) + 1) * f x⌋ : ℝ) / ((n : ℝ) + 1)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.EffectValuedMeasure.abs_simpleValue_meshWeight_meshPiece_sub_le
declarations.doc:
**Uniform convergence of the mesh approximation.** At scale `n`, the mesh simple function
never differs from `f` by more than the mesh width `1/(n+1)`, at any point.
declarations.statement:
lemma abs_simpleValue_meshWeight_meshPiece_sub_le (n : ℕ) (x : Ω) :
    |simpleValue (meshWeight M n) (meshPiece f M n) x - f x| ≤ 1 / ((n : ℝ) + 1)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.EffectValuedMeasure.simpleValue_add
declarations.doc: `simpleValue` is additive in the weights, pointwise.
declarations.statement:
lemma simpleValue_add (a b : ι → ℝ) (s : ι → Set Ω) (x : Ω) :
    simpleValue (a + b) s x = simpleValue a s x + simpleValue b s x

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.EffectValuedMeasure.simpleValue_smul
declarations.doc: `simpleValue` is homogeneous in the weights, pointwise.
declarations.statement:
lemma simpleValue_smul (r : ℝ) (c : ι → ℝ) (s : ι → Set Ω) (x : Ω) :
    simpleValue (r • c) s x = r * simpleValue c s x

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.EffectValuedMeasure.isPartition_inter
declarations.doc:
The pairwise intersections of two partitions again form a partition, indexed by the product of
their labels.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.EffectValuedMeasure.simpleValue_eq_simpleValue_inter_fst
declarations.statement:
lemma simpleValue_eq_simpleValue_inter_fst {ι ι' : Type*} [Fintype ι] [Fintype ι']
    {c : ι → ℝ} {s : ι → Set Ω} (hs : IsPartition s) {s' : ι' → Set Ω} (hs' : IsPartition s')
    (x : Ω) :
    simpleValue c s x = simpleValue (fun p : ι × ι' => c p.1) (fun p => s p.1 ∩ s' p.2) x

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.EffectValuedMeasure.simpleValue_eq_simpleValue_inter_snd
declarations.statement:
lemma simpleValue_eq_simpleValue_inter_snd {ι ι' : Type*} [Fintype ι] [Fintype ι']
    {c' : ι' → ℝ} {s : ι → Set Ω} (hs : IsPartition s) {s' : ι' → Set Ω} (hs' : IsPartition s')
    (x : Ω) :
    simpleValue c' s' x = simpleValue (fun p : ι × ι' => c' p.2) (fun p => s p.1 ∩ s' p.2) x

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.EffectValuedMeasure.simpleValue_add_inter
declarations.doc:
The pointwise sum of two simple functions, over possibly different partitions, is the simple
function of their common refinement with pointwise-summed weights. Used to build an admissible
approximating sequence for `f + g` out of ones for `f` and `g`.
declarations.statement:
lemma simpleValue_add_inter {ι ι' : Type*} [Fintype ι] [Fintype ι'] {a : ι → ℝ} {s : ι → Set Ω}
    (hs : IsPartition s) {b : ι' → ℝ} {s' : ι' → Set Ω} (hs' : IsPartition s') (x : Ω) :
    simpleValue a s x + simpleValue b s' x =
      simpleValue (fun p : ι × ι' => a p.1 + b p.2) (fun p => s p.1 ∩ s' p.2) x

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.EffectValuedMeasure.simpleIntegral_eq_simpleIntegral_inter_fst
declarations.statement:
lemma simpleIntegral_eq_simpleIntegral_inter_fst {ι ι' : Type*} [Fintype ι] [Fintype ι']
    [DecidableEq ι] [DecidableEq ι'] (μ : EffectValuedMeasure Ω E) {c : ι → ℝ} {s : ι → Set Ω}
    (hs : IsPartition s) {s' : ι' → Set Ω} (hs' : IsPartition s') :
    simpleIntegral μ c s hs =
      simpleIntegral μ (fun p : ι × ι' => c p.1) (fun p => s p.1 ∩ s' p.2)
        (isPartition_inter hs hs')

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.EffectValuedMeasure.simpleIntegral_eq_simpleIntegral_inter_snd
declarations.statement:
lemma simpleIntegral_eq_simpleIntegral_inter_snd {ι ι' : Type*} [Fintype ι] [Fintype ι']
    [DecidableEq ι] [DecidableEq ι'] (μ : EffectValuedMeasure Ω E) {c' : ι' → ℝ} {s : ι → Set Ω}
    (hs : IsPartition s) {s' : ι' → Set Ω} (hs' : IsPartition s') :
    simpleIntegral μ c' s' hs' =
      simpleIntegral μ (fun p : ι × ι' => c' p.2) (fun p => s p.1 ∩ s' p.2)
        (isPartition_inter hs hs')

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.EffectValuedMeasure.simpleIntegral_sub_simpleIntegral
declarations.doc:
The difference of two simple integrals, over possibly different partitions, is itself a simple
integral over their common refinement, with weights the pointwise difference of the two original
weights. This is what lets the difference be bounded termwise.
declarations.statement:
lemma simpleIntegral_sub_simpleIntegral {ι ι' : Type*} [Fintype ι] [Fintype ι'] [DecidableEq ι]
    [DecidableEq ι'] (μ : EffectValuedMeasure Ω E) {c : ι → ℝ} {s : ι → Set Ω}
    (hs : IsPartition s) {c' : ι' → ℝ} {s' : ι' → Set Ω} (hs' : IsPartition s') :
    simpleIntegral μ c s hs - simpleIntegral μ c' s' hs' =
      simpleIntegral μ (fun p : ι × ι' => c p.1 - c' p.2) (fun p => s p.1 ∩ s' p.2)
        (isPartition_inter hs hs')

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.EffectValuedMeasure.simpleIntegral_add_simpleIntegral
declarations.doc:
The sum of two simple integrals, over possibly different partitions, is itself a simple
integral over their common refinement, with weights the pointwise sum of the two original
weights. Used to build an admissible approximating sequence for `f + g` out of ones for `f` and
`g`.
declarations.statement:
lemma simpleIntegral_add_simpleIntegral {ι ι' : Type*} [Fintype ι] [Fintype ι'] [DecidableEq ι]
    [DecidableEq ι'] (μ : EffectValuedMeasure Ω E) {c : ι → ℝ} {s : ι → Set Ω}
    (hs : IsPartition s) {c' : ι' → ℝ} {s' : ι' → Set Ω} (hs' : IsPartition s') :
    simpleIntegral μ c s hs + simpleIntegral μ c' s' hs' =
      simpleIntegral μ (fun p : ι × ι' => c p.1 + c' p.2) (fun p => s p.1 ∩ s' p.2)
        (isPartition_inter hs hs')

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.EffectValuedMeasure.sum_apply_eq_one
declarations.doc: The total measure of a partition is the certain outcome.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_apply_eq_one {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (μ : EffectValuedMeasure Ω E)
    {s : ι → Set Ω} (hs : IsPartition s) :
    ∑ i, (μ (s i) (hs.measurable i) : E) = 1

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.EffectValuedMeasure.orderUnitNorm_simpleIntegral_le
declarations.doc:
A simple integral whose weights are bounded by `δ`, on every piece the underlying measure sees
(i.e. every nonempty piece), has order-unit norm at most `δ`: every term is sandwiched between
`±δ` times a nonnegative effect, and those effects sum to the certain outcome.
declarations.statement:
lemma orderUnitNorm_simpleIntegral_le {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (μ : EffectValuedMeasure Ω E) {c : ι → ℝ} {s : ι → Set Ω} (hs : IsPartition s) {δ : ℝ}
    (hδ : 0 ≤ δ) (hc : ∀ i, (s i).Nonempty → |c i| ≤ δ) :
    orderUnitNorm (simpleIntegral μ c s hs) ≤ δ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.EffectValuedMeasure.simpleIntegral_nonneg'
declarations.doc:
A simple integral is nonnegative as soon as its weights are nonnegative on every piece the
underlying measure sees (i.e. every nonempty piece) — the same "only nonempty pieces matter"
relaxation of `simpleIntegral_nonneg` used above for the norm bound.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.EffectValuedMeasure.orderUnitNorm_simpleIntegral_sub_le
declarations.doc:
**The key comparison lemma.** Two simple functions that both stay within `ε`, resp. `ε'`, of
the same bounded function `f` everywhere give integrals against `μ` that are within `ε + ε'` of
each other, in the order-unit norm — regardless of which partitions were used to build them.
declarations.statement:
lemma orderUnitNorm_simpleIntegral_sub_le {ι ι' : Type*} [Fintype ι] [Fintype ι']
    [DecidableEq ι] [DecidableEq ι'] (μ : EffectValuedMeasure Ω E) {f : Ω → ℝ}
    {c : ι → ℝ} {s : ι → Set Ω} (hs : IsPartition s) {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 ≤ ε)
    (hc : ∀ x, |simpleValue c s x - f x| ≤ ε)
    {c' : ι' → ℝ} {s' : ι' → Set Ω} (hs' : IsPartition s') {ε' : ℝ} (hε' : 0 ≤ ε')
    (hc' : ∀ x, |simpleValue c' s' x - f x| ≤ ε') :
    orderUnitNorm (simpleIntegral μ c s hs - simpleIntegral μ c' s' hs') ≤ ε + ε'

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.EffectValuedMeasure.le_smul_one_of_orderUnitNorm_lt
declarations.doc:
Any real strictly above the order-unit norm of `y` is itself an order-unit bound of `y`: since
`orderUnitBounds y` is an up-set with infimum `orderUnitNorm y`, anything strictly past that
infimum is already in the set. The positivity argument below needs this to turn a norm estimate
into an actual order bound.
declarations.statement:
lemma le_smul_one_of_orderUnitNorm_lt {y : E} {r : ℝ} (h : orderUnitNorm y < r) :
    y ≤ r • (1 : E)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.EffectValuedMeasure.instNormedAddCommGroup
declarations.doc: The order-unit norm supplies the ambient normed additive-group structure for this section.
declarations.statement: noncomputable local instance instNormedAddCommGroup : NormedAddCommGroup E

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.EffectValuedMeasure.instCompleteSpace
declarations.doc: Completeness of the order-unit-norm copy, read on `E` itself.
declarations.statement: local instance instCompleteSpace : CompleteSpace E

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.EffectValuedMeasure.dist_eq_orderUnitNorm
declarations.statement: lemma dist_eq_orderUnitNorm (x y : E) : dist x y = orderUnitNorm (x - y)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.EffectValuedMeasure.tendsto_const_smul_of_tendsto
declarations.doc:
Scalar multiplication by a fixed real is continuous, established by hand from
`orderUnitNorm_smul_le` since no `NormedSpace ℝ E` instance is assumed at this generality.
declarations.statement:
lemma tendsto_const_smul_of_tendsto {a : ℕ → E} {L : E} (c : ℝ)
    (ha : Filter.Tendsto a atTop (𝓝 L)) : Filter.Tendsto (fun n => c • a n) atTop (𝓝 (c • L))

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.EffectValuedMeasure.cauchySeq_meshSimpleIntegral
declarations.doc:
**The mesh approximation is Cauchy.** Refining the mesh from scale `n` to scale `m`, both past
`N`, moves the simple integral by at most `2/(N+1)` in the order-unit norm — the sum of the two
meshes' uniform error bounds, via `orderUnitNorm_simpleIntegral_sub_le`.
declarations.statement:
lemma cauchySeq_meshSimpleIntegral (μ : EffectValuedMeasure Ω E) :
    CauchySeq (fun n : ℕ => simpleIntegral μ (meshWeight M n) (meshPiece f M n)
      (isPartition_meshPiece hf hM n))

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.EffectValuedMeasure.integral
declarations.doc:
**The integral of a bounded measurable function against `μ`.** The limit of the mesh
approximation's simple integrals, which exists by completeness of `E` since the sequence is
Cauchy.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def integral (μ : EffectValuedMeasure Ω E) : E

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.EffectValuedMeasure.integral_tendsto
declarations.doc: The mesh approximation's simple integrals converge to `integral hf hM μ`, by construction.
declarations.statement:
lemma integral_tendsto (μ : EffectValuedMeasure Ω E) :
    Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => simpleIntegral μ (meshWeight M n) (meshPiece f M n)
      (isPartition_meshPiece hf hM n)) atTop (𝓝 (integral hf hM μ))

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.EffectValuedMeasure.tendsto_of_uniformly_approximating
declarations.doc:
**The integral does not depend on the approximation.** For every sequence of simple functions
converging uniformly to `f`, their integrals converge to the integral of `f`.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.EffectValuedMeasure.integral_indep_of_bound
declarations.doc:
**Independence from the choice of bound.** `integral` doesn't depend on which valid bound `M`
was used to build it: swapping in another bound `M'` only changes the *range* of mesh cells, not
their width, so the `M'`-mesh sequence is itself uniformly approximating for the `M`-built
`integral hf hM μ` too, and `tendsto_nhds_unique` identifies the two limits.
declarations.statement:
lemma integral_indep_of_bound {M' : ℝ} (hM' : ∀ x, |f x| ≤ M') (μ : EffectValuedMeasure Ω E) :
    integral hf hM μ = integral hf hM' μ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.EffectValuedMeasure.integral_eq_simpleIntegral
declarations.doc:
**Consistency with the simple case.** When `f` already *is* a simple function against some
partition, `integral` agrees with `simpleIntegral` on it — the general construction extends the
special case rather than computing something else. The constant sequence `(c, s, hs)` is itself
(trivially) uniformly approximating, with error `0`, so `tendsto_of_uniformly_approximating`
applies directly.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.EffectValuedMeasure.nonneg_integral
declarations.doc:
**Positivity.** A nonnegative `f` integrates to a nonnegative value: every mesh approximation
of a nonnegative `f` has nonnegative weight on every piece it actually sees (a piece labelled `k`
that meets `f`'s graph forces `k ≥ 0`, since `f ≥ 0` there), so every term of the mesh sequence is
`≥ 0` (`simpleIntegral_nonneg'`); pass that bound to the limit using that
`-integral hf hM μ ≤ ε • 1` for every `ε > 0`, which is exactly what
`ArchimedeanOrderUnitSpace.le_zero_of_forall_pos_smul_one_le` needs to conclude `-integral ≤ 0`.
declarations.statement:
lemma nonneg_integral (hf0 : ∀ x, 0 ≤ f x) (μ : EffectValuedMeasure Ω E) :
    0 ≤ integral hf hM μ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.EffectValuedMeasure.integral_add
declarations.doc:
**Additivity.** `integral (f + g) = integral f + integral g`, built by combining the two
canonical mesh sequences into one admissible sequence for `f + g` (pieces the pairwise
intersections, weights the pointwise sums — `simpleValue_add_inter` for the uniform bound,
`simpleIntegral_add_simpleIntegral` for the exact algebraic identity) and matching limits: the
combined sequence tends to `integral hfg hMfg μ` by `tendsto_of_uniformly_approximating`, and its
terms equal `mesh_f + mesh_g` exactly at every stage, so it also tends to
`integral f + integral g` (continuity of `+`, free in any normed group).
declarations.statement:
lemma integral_add {g : Ω → ℝ} (hg : Measurable g) {M' : ℝ} (hM' : ∀ x, |g x| ≤ M')
    {hfg : Measurable (f + g)} {hMfg : ∀ x, |(f + g) x| ≤ M + M'} (μ : EffectValuedMeasure Ω E) :
    integral hfg hMfg μ = integral hf hM μ + integral hg hM' μ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.EffectValuedMeasure.integral_smul
declarations.doc:
**Homogeneity.** `integral (c • f) = c • integral f`, built from the canonical mesh sequence
for `f` with weights rescaled by `c` (same partition, so `simpleIntegral_smul` gives the exact
algebraic identity at every stage, no refinement needed); matching limits needs scalar
multiplication's continuity, established from `orderUnitNorm_smul_le` since no `NormedSpace ℝ E`
instance is assumed at this generality.
declarations.statement:
lemma integral_smul (c : ℝ) {hcf : Measurable (c • f)} {hMcf : ∀ x, |(c • f) x| ≤ |c| * M}
    (μ : EffectValuedMeasure Ω E) : integral hcf hMcf μ = c • integral hf hM μ

modules.title: Channels and integrals
modules.doc:
Normal channels commute with integration against effect-valued measures.

## i. Overview

A normal channel maps an effect-valued measure to an effect-valued measure, and it commutes with
integration of bounded functions.

## ii. Key results

- `EffectValuedMeasure.map_simpleIntegral` : for simple functions.
- `EffectValuedMeasure.map_integral` : for bounded measurable functions.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Simple integrals
- B. Bounded integrals

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.EffectValuedMeasure.map_simpleIntegral
declarations.doc: Pushing an effect-valued measure through a normal channel commutes with its simple integral.
declarations.statement:
lemma map_simpleIntegral (μ : EffectValuedMeasure Ω E) (φ : Channel E F) (hφ : φ.IsNormal)
    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (c : ι → ℝ) (s : ι → Set Ω) (hs : IsPartition s) :
    φ (simpleIntegral μ c s hs) = simpleIntegral (μ.map φ hφ) c s hs

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.EffectValuedMeasure.instNormedAddCommGroupE
declarations.statement: noncomputable local instance instNormedAddCommGroupE : NormedAddCommGroup E

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.EffectValuedMeasure.instNormedAddCommGroupF
declarations.statement: noncomputable local instance instNormedAddCommGroupF : NormedAddCommGroup F

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.EffectValuedMeasure.map_integral
declarations.doc:
A normal channel commutes with the bounded effect-valued integral.  The only analytic input is
order-unit contractivity of a unital positive map; normality is used solely to make `μ.map φ hφ`
an effect-valued measure.
declarations.statement:
lemma map_integral {f : Ω → ℝ} {M : ℝ} (hf : Measurable f) (hM : ∀ x, |f x| ≤ M)
    (μ : EffectValuedMeasure Ω E) (φ : Channel E F) (hφ : φ.IsNormal) :
    φ (integral hf hM μ) = integral hf hM (μ.map φ hφ)

modules.title: Compatibility of measurements
modules.doc:
Compatible and jointly measurable measurements, with an order criterion for binary ones.

## i. Overview

Two measurements are compatible when both can be obtained from one measurement by classical
post-processing of its outcome: performing the common measurement answers both.

A joint measurement of two measurements is a measurement of pairs of outcomes whose marginals are
the two measurements. Jointly measurable measurements are compatible. The binary measurements of
two effects `e` and `f` are jointly measurable exactly when some `g` lies above `0` and `e + f - 1`
and below `e` and `f`: `g` is the effect of both outcomes being `true`.

## ii. Key results

- `Measurement.Compatible` : compatibility of measurements.
- `Measurement.Compatible.mono` : compatibility is preserved by post-processing.
- `Measurement.Joint` : a joint measurement of two measurements.
- `Measurement.JointlyMeasurable.compatible` : jointly measurable measurements are
  compatible.
- `Effect.jointlyMeasurable_binaryMeasurement_iff` : the order criterion for joint measurability of
  two binary measurements.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Compatibility of measurements
- B. Joint measurements
- C. Binary compatibility

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Measurement.Compatible
declarations.doc:
Two measurements are compatible when they are both operational post-processings of a common
measurement.
declarations.statement: def Compatible (M : Measurement Ω E) (N : Measurement Ω' E) : Prop

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Measurement.compatible_refl
declarations.doc: Every measurement is compatible with itself.
declarations.statement: lemma compatible_refl (M : Measurement Ω E) : Compatible M M

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Measurement.compatible_symm
declarations.doc: Compatibility of measurements is symmetric.
declarations.statement:
lemma compatible_symm {M : Measurement Ω E} {N : Measurement Ω' E}
    (h : Compatible M N) : Compatible N M

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Measurement.Compatible.mono
declarations.doc: Replacing compatible measurements by post-processings preserves compatibility.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Measurement.compatible_of_postprocessing_left
declarations.doc: A measurement is compatible with each of its operational post-processings.
declarations.statement:
lemma compatible_of_postprocessing_left {M : Measurement Ω E}
    {N : Measurement Ω' E} (h : M ≤ₚ N) : Compatible M N

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Measurement.compatible_of_postprocessing_right
declarations.doc: A measurement is compatible with each measurement of which it is a post-processing.
declarations.statement:
lemma compatible_of_postprocessing_right {M : Measurement Ω E}
    {N : Measurement Ω' E} (h : N ≤ₚ M) : Compatible M N

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Measurement.Joint
declarations.doc:
A joint measurement of `M` and `N`: a measurement with outcome pairs whose marginals are `M`
and `N`.
declarations.statement:
structure Joint (M : Measurement Ω E) (N : Measurement Ω' E) where
  /-- The joint measurement. -/
  joint : Measurement (Ω × Ω') E
  /-- Its first marginal is `M`. -/
  fst_marginal : joint.mapOutcome Prod.fst measurable_fst = M
  /-- Its second marginal is `N`. -/
  snd_marginal : joint.mapOutcome Prod.snd measurable_snd = N

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Measurement.JointlyMeasurable
declarations.doc: Two measurements are jointly measurable when they have a joint measurement.
declarations.statement: def JointlyMeasurable (M : Measurement Ω E) (N : Measurement Ω' E) : Prop

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Measurement.JointlyMeasurable.compatible
declarations.doc: Jointly measurable measurements are compatible.
declarations.statement:
lemma JointlyMeasurable.compatible {M : Measurement Ω E}
    {N : Measurement Ω' E} (h : JointlyMeasurable M N) : Compatible M N

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Effect.binaryJointAtom
declarations.doc:
The four effects of a joint measurement of the binary measurements of `e` and `f` whose
`(true, true)` effect is `g`.
declarations.statement: def binaryJointAtom (e f : Effect E) (g : E) : Bool × Bool → E

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Effect.IsBinaryJointEffect
declarations.doc: Conditions on `g` making every `binaryJointAtom e f g` an effect.
declarations.statement: def IsBinaryJointEffect (e f : Effect E) (g : E) : Prop

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Effect.IsApproxBinaryJointEffect
declarations.doc: `g` is a joint effect for `e` and `f` up to `δ • 1`.
declarations.statement: def IsApproxBinaryJointEffect (e f : Effect E) (δ : ℝ) (g : E) : Prop

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Effect.IsBinaryJointEffect.isApprox
declarations.statement:
lemma IsBinaryJointEffect.isApprox {e f : Effect E} {g : E} (hg : IsBinaryJointEffect e f g)
    {δ : ℝ} (hδ : 0 ≤ δ) : IsApproxBinaryJointEffect e f δ g

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Effect.binaryJointAtom_mem
declarations.statement:
lemma binaryJointAtom_mem {e f : Effect E} {g : E} (hg : IsBinaryJointEffect e f g) :
    ∀ p, binaryJointAtom e f g p ∈ (Effect E : Set E)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Effect.sum_binaryJointAtom
declarations.statement: lemma sum_binaryJointAtom (e f : Effect E) (g : E) : ∑ p, binaryJointAtom e f g p = 1

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Effect.binaryJoint
declarations.doc:
The joint measurement of the binary measurements of `e` and `f` with `(true, true)` effect
`g`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def binaryJoint {e f : Effect E} {g : E} (hg : IsBinaryJointEffect e f g) :
    Joint (binaryMeasurement e) (binaryMeasurement f)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Measurement.Joint.jointAtom
declarations.doc: The effect of the joint outcome `p`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def _root_.ProbabilisticTheory.Measurement.Joint.jointAtom
    (J : Joint (binaryMeasurement e) (binaryMeasurement f)) (p : Bool × Bool) : E

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Measurement.Joint.jointAtom_nonneg
declarations.statement:
lemma _root_.ProbabilisticTheory.Measurement.Joint.jointAtom_nonneg (p : Bool × Bool) :
    0 ≤ J.jointAtom p

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Measurement.Joint.coe_joint_eq_sum
declarations.statement:
lemma _root_.ProbabilisticTheory.Measurement.Joint.coe_joint_eq_sum (s : Set (Bool × Bool))
    (hs : MeasurableSet s) :
    (J.joint s hs : E) = ∑ p, if p ∈ s then J.jointAtom p else 0

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Measurement.Joint.jointAtom_fst
declarations.doc: The first marginal: the joint outcomes with first entry `true` add up to `e`.
declarations.statement:
lemma _root_.ProbabilisticTheory.Measurement.Joint.jointAtom_fst :
    J.jointAtom (true, true) + J.jointAtom (true, false) = e

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Measurement.Joint.jointAtom_snd
declarations.doc: The second marginal: the joint outcomes with second entry `true` add up to `f`.
declarations.statement:
lemma _root_.ProbabilisticTheory.Measurement.Joint.jointAtom_snd :
    J.jointAtom (true, true) + J.jointAtom (false, true) = f

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Measurement.Joint.jointAtom_sum
declarations.doc: The four joint outcomes add up to the unit.
declarations.statement:
lemma _root_.ProbabilisticTheory.Measurement.Joint.jointAtom_sum :
    J.jointAtom (true, true) + J.jointAtom (true, false) +
    (J.jointAtom (false, true) + J.jointAtom (false, false)) = 1

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Measurement.Joint.isBinaryJointEffect_jointAtom
declarations.doc:
The `(true, true)` effect of a joint measurement of two binary measurements satisfies the
joint-effect conditions.
declarations.statement:
lemma _root_.ProbabilisticTheory.Measurement.Joint.isBinaryJointEffect_jointAtom :
    IsBinaryJointEffect e f (J.jointAtom (true, true))

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Effect.jointlyMeasurable_binaryMeasurement_iff
declarations.doc:
The binary measurements of `e` and `f` are jointly measurable exactly when some `g` lies below
`e` and `f` and above `0` and `e + f - 1`.
declarations.statement:
lemma jointlyMeasurable_binaryMeasurement_iff (e f : Effect E) :
    JointlyMeasurable (binaryMeasurement e) (binaryMeasurement f) ↔
      ∃ g : E, IsBinaryJointEffect e f g

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Effect.compatible_binaryMeasurement
declarations.doc: Binary measurements of effects with a common lower bound as above are compatible.
declarations.statement:
lemma compatible_binaryMeasurement {e f : Effect E} {g : E} (hg : IsBinaryJointEffect e f g) :
    Compatible (binaryMeasurement e) (binaryMeasurement f)

modules.title: Effect-valued measures
modules.doc:
Effect-valued measures: countably additive assignments of effects to events.

## i. Overview

An effect-valued measure with outcomes in `Ω` assigns to each event, a measurable set of outcomes,
an effect: the impossible event gets `0`, the certain event gets `1`, and the effects of disjoint
events add up, countably. Every measurement has one, sending an event to the effect testing whether
the outcome lands in it. For self-adjoint operators effect-valued measures are the POVMs.

On a finite discrete outcome space an effect-valued measure is the same as a family of effects
adding up to `1`, one for each outcome.

## ii. Key results

- `EffectValuedMeasure Ω E` : an effect-valued measure with outcomes in `Ω`.
- `EffectValuedMeasure.ofFintype` : the effect-valued measure of a normalized family of effects.
- `EffectValuedMeasure.map_union_of_disjoint` : additivity on two disjoint events.
- `EffectValuedMeasure.coe_apply_eq_atomSum` : on a finite outcome space, the effect of an event
  is the sum of the effects of its outcomes.
- `EffectValuedMeasure.mapOutcome` : relabeling outcomes along a measurable map.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Effect-valued measures
- B. Atomic effect sums
- C. Finite-outcome effect-valued measures
- D. Finite additivity and atomic reconstruction
- E. Relabeling outcomes

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## D. Finite additivity and atomic reconstruction

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.EffectValuedMeasure
declarations.doc: An effect-valued measure: `∅ ↦ 0`, `univ ↦ 1`, countably additive.
declarations.statement:
structure EffectValuedMeasure (Ω : Type*) [MeasurableSpace Ω] (E : Type*) [OrderUnitSpace E] where
  /-- The effect assigned to each event. -/
  toFun : ∀ s : Set Ω, MeasurableSet s → Effect E
  /-- The impossible event gets `0`. -/
  map_empty' : toFun ∅ .empty = 0
  /-- The certain event gets `1`. -/
  map_univ' : toFun .univ .univ = 1
  /-- The effects of countably many disjoint events add up to the effect of their union. -/
  countably_additive' : ∀ (s : ℕ → Set Ω) (hs : ∀ n, MeasurableSet (s n)),
    Pairwise (Disjoint on s) →
      IsLUB (Set.range fun N => ∑ n ∈ Finset.range N, (toFun (s n) (hs n) : E))
        (toFun (⋃ n, s n) (.iUnion hs) : E)
instance : CoeFun (EffectValuedMeasure Ω E) fun _ => ∀ s : Set Ω, MeasurableSet s → Effect E

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.EffectValuedMeasure.ext
declarations.statement: lemma ext {μ ν : EffectValuedMeasure Ω E} (h : ∀ s hs, μ s hs = ν s hs) : μ = ν

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.EffectValuedMeasure.map_empty
declarations.statement: lemma map_empty (μ : EffectValuedMeasure Ω E) : μ ∅ .empty = 0

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.EffectValuedMeasure.map_univ
declarations.statement: lemma map_univ (μ : EffectValuedMeasure Ω E) : μ .univ .univ = 1

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.EffectValuedMeasure.countably_additive
declarations.statement:
lemma countably_additive (μ : EffectValuedMeasure Ω E) {s : ℕ → Set Ω}
    (hs : ∀ n, MeasurableSet (s n)) (hd : Pairwise (Disjoint on s)) :
    IsLUB (Set.range fun N => ∑ n ∈ Finset.range N, (μ (s n) (hs n) : E))
      (μ (⋃ n, s n) (.iUnion hs) : E)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.EffectValuedMeasure.eventFinset
declarations.doc: The outcomes of `s` as a finite set.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def eventFinset (s : Set Ω) : Finset Ω

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.EffectValuedMeasure.atomSum
declarations.doc: The sum of the atomic effects belonging to an event.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def atomSum (a : Ω → Effect E) (s : Set Ω) : E

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.EffectValuedMeasure.atomSum_nonneg
declarations.statement: lemma atomSum_nonneg (a : Ω → Effect E) (s : Set Ω) : 0 ≤ atomSum a s

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.EffectValuedMeasure.atomSum_mono
declarations.statement:
lemma atomSum_mono (a : Ω → Effect E) {s t : Set Ω} (hst : s ⊆ t) :
    atomSum a s ≤ atomSum a t

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.EffectValuedMeasure.atomSum_univ
declarations.statement: lemma atomSum_univ (a : Ω → Effect E) : atomSum a Set.univ = ∑ x, (a x : E)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.EffectValuedMeasure.atomSum_partialSums
declarations.statement:
lemma atomSum_partialSums (a : Ω → Effect E) (s : ℕ → Set Ω)
    (hd : Pairwise (Disjoint on s)) (N : ℕ) :
    (∑ n ∈ Finset.range N, atomSum a (s n)) = atomSum a (⋃ n < N, s n)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.EffectValuedMeasure.exists_partialUnion_eq_iUnion
declarations.doc:
On a finite outcome space, the union of a sequence of events is already the union of an initial
segment.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_partialUnion_eq_iUnion [Finite Ω] (s : ℕ → Set Ω) :
    ∃ N, ⋃ n < N, s n = ⋃ n, s n

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.EffectValuedMeasure.ofFintype
declarations.doc: A normalized finite family of atomic effects as an effect-valued measure.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def ofFintype (a : Ω → Effect E) (ha : ∑ x, (a x : E) = 1) :
    EffectValuedMeasure Ω E

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.EffectValuedMeasure.coe_ofFintype_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma coe_ofFintype_apply (a : Ω → Effect E) (ha : ∑ x, (a x : E) = 1)
    (s : Set Ω) (hs : MeasurableSet s) : ((ofFintype a ha) s hs : E) = atomSum a s

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.EffectValuedMeasure.coe_ofFintype_singleton
declarations.statement:
lemma coe_ofFintype_singleton (a : Ω → Effect E) (ha : ∑ x, (a x : E) = 1) (x : Ω)
    (hx : MeasurableSet {x}) : ((ofFintype a ha) {x} hx : E) = a x

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.EffectValuedMeasure.map_union_of_disjoint
declarations.doc: An effect-valued measure is additive on two disjoint events.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.EffectValuedMeasure.coe_apply_finset
declarations.doc: The effect of a finite event is the sum of the effects of its outcomes.
declarations.statement:
lemma coe_apply_finset (M : EffectValuedMeasure Ω E) (t : Finset Ω) :
    (M t t.measurableSet : E) = ∑ x ∈ t, (M {x} (measurableSet_singleton x) : E)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.EffectValuedMeasure.coe_apply_eq_atomSum
declarations.doc: On a finite discrete outcome space, a measurement is the sum of its singleton effects.
declarations.statement:
lemma coe_apply_eq_atomSum (M : EffectValuedMeasure Ω E) (s : Set Ω) (hs : MeasurableSet s) :
    (M s hs : E) = atomSum (fun x => M {x} (measurableSet_singleton x)) s

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.EffectValuedMeasure.ext_of_singleton
declarations.doc: Two measurements on a finite discrete space agree when all singleton effects agree.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.EffectValuedMeasure.mapOutcome
declarations.doc: Relabel the outcomes of an effect-valued measure along a measurable map.
declarations.statement:
def mapOutcome (N : EffectValuedMeasure Ω' E) (f : Ω' → Ω) (hf : Measurable f) :
    EffectValuedMeasure Ω E

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.EffectValuedMeasure.coe_mapOutcome_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma coe_mapOutcome_apply (N : EffectValuedMeasure Ω' E) (f : Ω' → Ω) (hf : Measurable f)
    (s : Set Ω) (hs : MeasurableSet s) : (N.mapOutcome f hf s hs : E) = N (f ⁻¹' s) (hf hs)

modules.title: Measurements with finitely many outcomes
modules.doc:
Measurements with finitely many outcomes are the families of effects summing to `1`.

## i. Overview

On a finite discrete outcome space, every observable of the outcome is a combination of the
indicators of single outcomes. A measurement is therefore determined by the effects of its single
outcomes, and these add up to `1`. Conversely, a family of effects adding up to `1` is a
measurement: send the observable `f` to `∑ x, f x • a x`. Normality is automatic, since an
increasing sequence of functions on finitely many points converges uniformly; this uses that the
system is Archimedean.

## ii. Key results

- `BoundedMeasurable.eq_sum_indicator` : an observable of a finite classical system is a combination
  of point indicators.
- `UnitalPositiveLinearMap.isNormal_of_fintype` : a channel from a finite classical system into an
  Archimedean system is normal.
- `Measurement.ofAtoms` : the measurement of a family of effects adding up to `1`.
- `Measurement.eq_ofAtoms` : a measurement with finitely many outcomes is determined by the effects
  of its outcomes.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Observables of a finite classical system
- B. Normality is automatic
- C. Measurements from their outcome effects

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. Observables of a finite classical system
## C. Measurements from their outcome effects

declarations.name: BoundedMeasurable.eq_sum_indicator
declarations.doc: An observable of a finite classical system is a combination of point indicators.
declarations.statement:
lemma eq_sum_indicator (f : BoundedMeasurable Ω) :
    f = ∑ x, f x • indicator {x} (measurableSet_singleton x)

declarations.name: BoundedMeasurable.sum_indicator_singleton
declarations.doc: The point indicators add up to the unit.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_indicator_singleton :
    ∑ x, indicator {x} (measurableSet_singleton x) = (1 : BoundedMeasurable Ω)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.exists_le_add_smul_one
declarations.doc:
An increasing sequence of functions on a finite set comes uniformly close to its least upper
bound.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_le_add_smul_one {f : ℕ → BoundedMeasurable Ω} (hf : Monotone f)
    {g : BoundedMeasurable Ω} (hg : IsLUB (Set.range f) g) {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∃ n, g ≤ f n + ε • 1

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.isNormal_of_fintype
declarations.doc: A channel from a finite classical system into an Archimedean system is normal.
declarations.statement: lemma isNormal_of_fintype (Φ : Channel (BoundedMeasurable Ω) E) : Φ.IsNormal

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Measurement.atomsChannel
declarations.doc: The channel `f ↦ ∑ x, f x • a x` of a family of effects adding up to `1`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def atomsChannel (a : Ω → Effect E) (ha : ∑ x, (a x : E) = 1) :
    Channel (BoundedMeasurable Ω) E

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Measurement.ofAtoms
declarations.doc: The measurement of a family of effects adding up to `1`: the outcome `x` has effect `a x`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def ofAtoms (a : Ω → Effect E) (ha : ∑ x, (a x : E) = 1) : Measurement Ω E

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Measurement.ofAtoms_toChannel_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma ofAtoms_toChannel_apply (a : Ω → Effect E) (ha : ∑ x, (a x : E) = 1)
    (f : BoundedMeasurable Ω) : (ofAtoms a ha).toChannel f = ∑ x, f x • (a x : E)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Measurement.coe_ofAtoms_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma coe_ofAtoms_apply (a : Ω → Effect E) (ha : ∑ x, (a x : E) = 1) (s : Set Ω)
    (hs : MeasurableSet s) : (ofAtoms a ha s hs : E) = ∑ x, if x ∈ s then (a x : E) else 0

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Measurement.coe_ofAtoms_singleton
declarations.statement:
lemma coe_ofAtoms_singleton (a : Ω → Effect E) (ha : ∑ x, (a x : E) = 1) (x : Ω)
    (hx : MeasurableSet {x}) : (ofAtoms a ha {x} hx : E) = a x

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Measurement.sum_singleton
declarations.doc: The effects of the outcomes of a measurement add up to `1`.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_singleton (M : Measurement Ω E) :
    ∑ x, (M {x} (measurableSet_singleton x) : E) = 1

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Measurement.eq_ofAtoms
declarations.doc: A measurement with finitely many outcomes is the measurement of its outcome effects.
declarations.statement:
lemma eq_ofAtoms (M : Measurement Ω E) :
    M = ofAtoms (fun x => M {x} (measurableSet_singleton x)) M.sum_singleton

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Measurement.ext_of_singleton
declarations.doc: Two measurements with finitely many outcomes agree when their outcome effects agree.

modules.title: Instruments
modules.doc:
Finite-outcome instruments, their induced measurements and post-measurement states.

## i. Overview

An instrument with finitely many outcomes describes both the outcome probabilities and the state
after the measurement. It is a family of operations, one per outcome, whose values on the unit sum
to `1`. Forgetting the post-measurement state gives a measurement, and conditioning a state on an
outcome of nonzero probability gives the post-measurement state.

## ii. Key results

- `Instrument` : finite-outcome instruments.
- `Instrument.measurement` : the underlying measurement.
- `Instrument.conditionalState` : the post-measurement state.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Instruments
- B. The induced measurement
- C. Conditional states

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Instrument
declarations.doc:
A finite-outcome instrument: an operation for each outcome, whose images of the certain event
exhaust it. The instrument loses no probability overall, even though a single operation may.
declarations.statement:
structure Instrument (E : Type*) [OrderUnitSpace E] (ι : Type*) [Fintype ι] where
  /-- The operation associated to each possible outcome. -/
  op : ι → Operation E
  /-- The outcome probabilities exhaust the certain event. -/
  sum_op_one_eq_one : ∑ i, (op i : E → E) 1 = 1

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Instrument.measurement
declarations.doc:
The measurement an instrument induces: only the outcome probabilities remain, given by each
operation's image of the certain event.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def measurement (𝓘 : Instrument E ι) : Measurement ι E

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Instrument.coe_measurement_effects
declarations.doc: The effect of an outcome is the value of its operation on the unit.
declarations.statement:
lemma coe_measurement_effects (𝓘 : Instrument E ι) (i : ι) :
    ((𝓘.measurement {i} (measurableSet_singleton i) : Effect E) : E) =
      (𝓘.op i : E → E) 1

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Instrument.conditionalState
declarations.doc:
The post-measurement (conditional) state after outcome `i`, given a prior state `ω` for which
that outcome has nonzero probability: apply the operation, then renormalize by the outcome's
probability, so the certain event is again sent to `1`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def conditionalState (𝓘 : Instrument E ι) (i : ι) (ω : 𝓢[ℝ, E])
    (hpos : 0 < ω ((𝓘.op i : E → E) 1)) : 𝓢[ℝ, E]

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Instrument.conditionalState_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma conditionalState_apply (𝓘 : Instrument E ι) (i : ι) (ω : 𝓢[ℝ, E])
    (hpos : 0 < ω ((𝓘.op i : E → E) 1)) (a : E) :
    𝓘.conditionalState i ω hpos a =
      (ω ((𝓘.op i : E → E) 1))⁻¹ * ω ((𝓘.op i : E → E) a)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Instrument.conditionalState_isNormal
declarations.doc:
A normal instrument operation sends a normal input state to a normal conditional state,
whenever its outcome has nonzero probability.
declarations.statement:
lemma conditionalState_isNormal (𝓘 : Instrument E ι) (i : ι) (ω : 𝓢[ℝ, E])
    (hpos : 0 < ω ((𝓘.op i : E → E) 1)) (hOp : (𝓘.op i).IsNormal) (hω : ω.IsNormal) :
    (𝓘.conditionalState i ω hpos).IsNormal

modules.title: Integrating simple functions against an effect-valued measure
modules.doc:
The integral of simple functions against an effect-valued measure, linear and positive.

## i. Overview

An effect-valued measure `μ` assigns an effect to every event. Integrating a simple function `∑ᵢ cᵢ
𝟙_{sᵢ}` against it gives `∑ᵢ cᵢ μ(sᵢ)`. The effect-valued measure is finitely additive, so this does
not depend on how the function is written: two partitions representing the same function give the
same value, by passing to their common refinement. The integral is linear and positive.

## ii. Key results

- `EffectValuedMeasure.apply_iUnion_of_disjoint` : finite additivity.
- `EffectValuedMeasure.IsPartition` : finite measurable partitions.
- `EffectValuedMeasure.simpleIntegral` : the integral `∑ᵢ cᵢ μ(sᵢ)` of a simple function.
- `EffectValuedMeasure.simpleIntegral_eq_of_pointwise_eq` : the integral depends only on the
  function.
- `EffectValuedMeasure.simpleIntegral_nonneg` : the integral is positive.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Finite measurable partitions and simple functions
- B. Finite additivity
- C. The integral of a simple function

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text:
## A. Finite measurable partitions and simple functions

Nothing here refers to `E` or to a POVM at all yet: a partition and the simple function it carries
are facts about `Ω` alone.

## B. Finite additivity

`EffectValuedMeasure` only bundles *countable* additivity (`countably_additive`). Finite
additivity is the special case of a family that is eventually `∅`, and the least upper bound of an
eventually-constant, nondecreasing sequence (nondecreasing since every value of `μ` is a
nonnegative effect) is just its eventual value — which is what lets us read finite sums off
`countably_additive` directly.
## C. The integral of a simple function

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.EffectValuedMeasure.IsPartition
declarations.doc:
`s` is a finite measurable partition of `Ω`: its pieces are measurable, pairwise disjoint, and
cover `Ω`. This is the "unbundled `he : ∑ i, e i = 1`" of `Measurement.toChannel`
transported to the measure-theoretic setting: there, a finite family of
effects summing to the certain event; here, a finite family of sets whose indicators sum to the
constant function `1`.
declarations.statement:
structure IsPartition {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (s : ι → Set Ω) : Prop where
  /-- Every piece of the partition is measurable. -/
  measurable : ∀ i, MeasurableSet (s i)
  /-- Distinct pieces of the partition are disjoint. -/
  disjoint : ∀ i j, i ≠ j → Disjoint (s i) (s j)
  /-- The pieces cover all of `Ω`. -/
  cover : ⋃ i, s i = Set.univ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.EffectValuedMeasure.simpleValue
declarations.doc: The simple function `∑ᵢ cᵢ 𝟙_{sᵢ}` of a partition.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def simpleValue {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (c : ι → ℝ) (s : ι → Set Ω) (x : Ω) : ℝ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.EffectValuedMeasure.simpleValue_apply_of_mem
declarations.doc:
At a point lying in piece `i` of the partition, the simple function evaluates to `c i`: every
other term of the defining sum vanishes since the pieces are pairwise disjoint.
declarations.statement:
lemma simpleValue_apply_of_mem {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] {c : ι → ℝ} {s : ι → Set Ω}
    (hs : IsPartition s) {x : Ω} {i : ι} (hx : x ∈ s i) : simpleValue c s x = c i

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.EffectValuedMeasure.apply_congr
declarations.doc:
Applying `μ` only depends on the set, not on which proof of measurability is supplied — an
immediate consequence of `Set` equality and proof irrelevance, recorded here since it comes up
whenever a set is simplified (e.g. `if`-reduced) mid-computation.
declarations.statement:
lemma apply_congr (μ : EffectValuedMeasure Ω E) {s t : Set Ω} (h : s = t)
    {hs : MeasurableSet s} {ht : MeasurableSet t} : (μ s hs : E) = (μ t ht : E)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.EffectValuedMeasure.apply_iUnion_eq_sum_of_eventually_empty
declarations.doc:
Padding a finite disjoint family with `∅` and applying countable additivity: past the point
where every remaining piece is `∅`, the partial sums have stabilized, and since they are also
nondecreasing (every value of `μ` is a nonnegative effect), that stable value is already the least
upper bound `countably_additive` promises — so it computes `μ` of the union.
declarations.statement:
lemma apply_iUnion_eq_sum_of_eventually_empty (μ : EffectValuedMeasure Ω E) (t : ℕ → Set Ω)
    (htm : ∀ n, MeasurableSet (t n)) (htd : ∀ m n, m ≠ n → Disjoint (t m) (t n)) {N : ℕ}
    (hN : ∀ n, N ≤ n → t n = ∅) :
    (μ (⋃ n, t n) (MeasurableSet.iUnion htm) : E) =
      ∑ n ∈ Finset.range N, (μ (t n) (htm n) : E)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.EffectValuedMeasure.apply_union_of_disjoint
declarations.doc:
Binary additivity of `μ`, derived from countable additivity by padding a two-element family
with `∅`.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.EffectValuedMeasure.apply_biUnion_of_disjoint
declarations.doc:
Finite additivity of `μ` over a pairwise disjoint family indexed by a `Finset`, with the
disjointness only required on the labels actually occurring in `s`. Proved by induction on the
`Finset`, peeling one element off at a time using binary additivity
(`apply_union_of_disjoint`).
declarations.statement:
lemma apply_biUnion_of_disjoint {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] (μ : EffectValuedMeasure Ω E)
    (f : ι → Set Ω) (hfm : ∀ i, MeasurableSet (f i)) (s : Finset ι)
    (hfd : ∀ i ∈ s, ∀ j ∈ s, i ≠ j → Disjoint (f i) (f j)) :
    (μ (⋃ i ∈ s, f i) (s.measurableSet_biUnion fun i _ => hfm i) : E) =
      ∑ i ∈ s, (μ (f i) (hfm i) : E)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.EffectValuedMeasure.apply_iUnion_of_disjoint
declarations.doc:
Finite additivity of `μ` over a `Fintype`-indexed pairwise disjoint family: the workhorse used
throughout the rest of this file.
declarations.statement:
lemma apply_iUnion_of_disjoint {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (μ : EffectValuedMeasure Ω E) (f : ι → Set Ω) (hfm : ∀ i, MeasurableSet (f i))
    (hfd : ∀ i j, i ≠ j → Disjoint (f i) (f j)) :
    (μ (⋃ i, f i) (MeasurableSet.iUnion hfm) : E) = ∑ i, (μ (f i) (hfm i) : E)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.EffectValuedMeasure.simpleIntegral
declarations.doc:
The integral of the simple function `∑ i, c i • 𝟙_{s i}` against `μ`: `∑ i, c i • μ(s i)`.
Well-defined independently of the chosen partition by `simpleIntegral_eq_of_pointwise_eq`, and
this is exactly `Measurement.toChannel` in the case where every piece of
the partition is a single point mass.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def simpleIntegral {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (μ : EffectValuedMeasure Ω E)
    (c : ι → ℝ) (s : ι → Set Ω) (hs : IsPartition s) : E

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.EffectValuedMeasure.apply_eq_sum_inter
declarations.doc:
On a partition, the piece `s i` decomposes as the union of its intersections with every piece
of a second partition `s'`: `s'` covers `Ω`, so intersecting with `s i` covers `s i`. Used to
refine two partitions to their common refinement in `simpleIntegral_eq_of_pointwise_eq`.
declarations.statement:
lemma apply_eq_sum_inter {ι ι' : Type*} [Fintype ι] [Fintype ι'] [DecidableEq ι']
    (μ : EffectValuedMeasure Ω E) {s : ι → Set Ω} {s' : ι' → Set Ω} (hs : IsPartition s)
    (hs' : IsPartition s') (i : ι) :
    (μ (s i) (hs.measurable i) : E) =
      ∑ j, (μ (s i ∩ s' j) ((hs.measurable i).inter (hs'.measurable j)) : E)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.EffectValuedMeasure.apply_eq_sum_inter'
declarations.doc:
The symmetric counterpart of `apply_eq_sum_inter`, with the roles of the two partitions
swapped: the piece `s' j` decomposes as the union of its intersections with every piece of `s`.
declarations.statement:
lemma apply_eq_sum_inter' {ι ι' : Type*} [Fintype ι] [Fintype ι'] [DecidableEq ι]
    (μ : EffectValuedMeasure Ω E) {s : ι → Set Ω} {s' : ι' → Set Ω} (hs : IsPartition s)
    (hs' : IsPartition s') (j : ι') :
    (μ (s' j) (hs'.measurable j) : E) =
      ∑ i, (μ (s i ∩ s' j) ((hs.measurable i).inter (hs'.measurable j)) : E)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.EffectValuedMeasure.simpleIntegral_eq_of_pointwise_eq
declarations.doc:
**The simple integral depends only on the function.** Two partitions describing the same
function give the same integral, by passing to the common refinement.
declarations.statement:
lemma simpleIntegral_eq_of_pointwise_eq {ι ι' : Type*} [Fintype ι] [Fintype ι'] [DecidableEq ι]
    [DecidableEq ι'] (μ : EffectValuedMeasure Ω E) (c : ι → ℝ) (s : ι → Set Ω) (hs : IsPartition s)
    (c' : ι' → ℝ)
    (s' : ι' → Set Ω) (hs' : IsPartition s')
    (hval : ∀ x, simpleValue c s x = simpleValue c' s' x) :
    simpleIntegral μ c s hs = simpleIntegral μ c' s' hs'

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.EffectValuedMeasure.simpleIntegral_add
declarations.doc: The simple integral is additive in the weights, over a fixed partition.
declarations.statement:
lemma simpleIntegral_add (μ : EffectValuedMeasure Ω E) (c₁ c₂ : ι → ℝ) (s : ι → Set Ω)
    (hs : IsPartition s) :
    simpleIntegral μ (c₁ + c₂) s hs = simpleIntegral μ c₁ s hs + simpleIntegral μ c₂ s hs

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.EffectValuedMeasure.simpleIntegral_smul
declarations.doc: The simple integral is homogeneous in the weights, over a fixed partition.
declarations.statement:
lemma simpleIntegral_smul (μ : EffectValuedMeasure Ω E) (r : ℝ) (c : ι → ℝ) (s : ι → Set Ω)
    (hs : IsPartition s) :
    simpleIntegral μ (r • c) s hs = r • simpleIntegral μ c s hs

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.EffectValuedMeasure.simpleIntegral_nonneg
declarations.doc:
The simple integral of a nonnegative simple function is nonnegative — matching `μ`'s own
positivity: every term `c i • μ(s i)` is a nonnegative scalar times a nonnegative effect.
declarations.statement:
lemma simpleIntegral_nonneg (μ : EffectValuedMeasure Ω E) {c : ι → ℝ} (hc : ∀ i, 0 ≤ c i)
    (s : ι → Set Ω) (hs : IsPartition s) : 0 ≤ simpleIntegral μ c s hs

modules.title: Post-processing of measurements
modules.doc:
Post-processing of measurements through Markov kernels, the information preorder, and Born laws.

## i. Overview

A measurement `M` is a post-processing of a measurement `N` when `M` can be simulated by performing
`N` and processing its outcome classically: `M = N ∘ K` for a normal channel `K` between the
classical systems of outcomes. Thus `M ≤ₚ N` means that `N` is at least as informative as `M`.
Normal classical channels are Markov kernels, so the processing is a random relabeling of the
outcome; relabeling along a measurable map is the deterministic case. In every normal state, the
Born law of `M` is the Born law of `N` composed with the kernel.

## ii. Key results

- `Measurement.IsPostprocessing` : the information preorder on measurements.
- `Measurement.isPostprocessing_iff_kernel` : post-processing through a Markov kernel.
- `Measurement.mapOutcome` : deterministic relabeling of measurement outcomes.
- `Measurement.IsPostprocessing.probabilityLaw_eq` : the Born law of a post-processing is the
  Born law of the original measurement composed with a Markov kernel.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Post-processing
- B. Relabeling outcomes
- C. Born laws

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Measurement.IsPostprocessing
declarations.doc:
`M` is a post-processing of `N`: `M = N ∘ K` for a normal channel `K` between the classical
systems of outcomes.
declarations.statement: def IsPostprocessing (M : Measurement Ω E) (N : Measurement Ω' E) : Prop

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Measurement.postprocessing_refl

declarations.statement: lemma postprocessing_refl (M : Measurement Ω E) : M ≤ₚ M

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Measurement.isPostprocessing_iff_kernel

declarations.statement:

    M ≤ₚ N ↔ ∃ (κ : Kernel Ω' Ω) (_ : IsMarkovKernel κ),
      M.toChannel = N.toChannel.comp (ofKernel κ)

lemma coe_mapOutcome_apply (N : Measurement Ω' E) (f : Ω' → Ω) (hf : Measurable f)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Measurement.probabilityLaw_comp
declarations.doc:
The Born law of a post-processing through `K` is the Born law of the original measurement
composed with the kernel of `K`.
declarations.statement:
lemma probabilityLaw_comp {M : Measurement Ω E} {N : Measurement Ω' E}
    {K : Channel (BoundedMeasurable Ω) (BoundedMeasurable Ω')} (hK : K.IsNormal)
    (h : M.toChannel = N.toChannel.comp K) (ω : 𝓢[ℝ, E]) (hω : ω.IsNormal) :
    (M.probabilityLaw ω hω : Measure Ω) = toKernel K hK ∘ₘ N.probabilityLaw ω hω

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Measurement.IsPostprocessing.probabilityLaw_eq
declarations.doc:
The Born law of a post-processing is the Born law of the original measurement composed with a
Markov kernel, the same for every state.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Measurement.probabilityLaw_mapOutcome
declarations.doc: Relabeling outcomes pushes each Born law forward along the relabeling map.
declarations.statement:
lemma probabilityLaw_mapOutcome (N : Measurement Ω' E) (f : Ω' → Ω) (hf : Measurable f)
    (ω : 𝓢[ℝ, E]) (hω : ω.IsNormal) :
    (N.mapOutcome f hf).probabilityLaw ω hω = (N.probabilityLaw ω hω).map f

Pushing an effect-valued measure forward along a normal channel.

## i. Overview

A channel sends effects to effects. Applying a normal channel `φ : Channel E F` to every effect of

## ii. Key results

## iii. Table of contents

- B. Pushing an effect-valued measure forward
