modules.title: The bidual of a system
modules.doc:
The bidual of a system is an Archimedean order-unit space, and a lattice for classical systems.

## i. Overview

An element of the bidual of a system assigns to every positive functional a value, additively and
positively homogeneously, dominated by some observable. With the unit `φ ↦ φ 1`, the total weight,
the bidual is again an Archimedean order-unit space: a system whose observables contain those of
the original one. When the system is classical, so that the positive functionals form a lattice,
the observables of the bidual form a lattice.

## ii. Key results

- `Bidual.instOrderUnitSpace` : the bidual of a system, with the total weight as unit.
- `Bidual.instArchimedeanOrderUnitSpace` : the bidual is Archimedean.
- `Bidual.instOrderUnitLattice` : the bidual of a classical system is an order-unit lattice.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The unit of the bidual
- B. The bidual of a classical system

## iv. References

* None.

## B. The bidual of a classical system

modules.title: Interpolation of complete observables
modules.doc:
Exact interpolants and the Riesz decomposition for complete observables with a lattice dual cone.

## i. Overview

Given finitely many lower observables `a i` below finitely many upper observables `b j`, an
interpolant is an observable `g` with `a i ≤ g ≤ b j` for all `i` and `j`. When the positive
functionals form a lattice, interpolants exist up to any error `ε • 1`. When the observables are
moreover complete in the order-unit norm, interpolants with errors `(1 / 2) ^ k` converge, and
exact interpolants exist. Then the observables have the Riesz decomposition.

## ii. Key results

- `HasLatticeDualCone.exists_interpolant` : on a complete Archimedean order-unit space, exact
  interpolants exist.
- `HasLatticeDualCone.hasRieszDecomposition` : on a complete Archimedean order-unit space,
  observables then have the Riesz decomposition.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Closed order intervals
- B. Exact interpolants

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.ArchimedeanOrderUnitSpace.isClosed_setOf_le
declarations.statement: lemma isClosed_setOf_le (c : F) : IsClosed {x : F | c ≤ x}

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.ArchimedeanOrderUnitSpace.isClosed_setOf_ge
declarations.statement: lemma isClosed_setOf_ge (c : F) : IsClosed {x : F | x ≤ c}

declarations.doc: Two observables within `c • 1` of each other are at distance at most `c`.
declarations.statement:
lemma dist_le_of_le_of_le {x y : F} {c : ℝ} (hc : 0 ≤ c) (h₁ : x - c • 1 ≤ y)
    (h₂ : y ≤ x + c • 1) : dist x y ≤ c

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.ArchimedeanOrderUnitSpace.le_zero_of_forall_le_half_pow
declarations.doc: An observable below every power `(1 / 2) ^ k` of the unit is nonpositive.
declarations.statement: lemma le_zero_of_forall_le_half_pow {x : F} (hx : ∀ k : ℕ, x ≤ ((1 / 2 : ℝ) ^ k) • 1) : x ≤ 0

declarations.name: HasLatticeDualCone.IsApproxInterpolant
declarations.doc: `g` interpolates between `a` and `b` up to `δ`.
declarations.statement: def IsApproxInterpolant (a : Fin n → F) (b : Fin m → F) (δ : ℝ) (g : F) : Prop

declarations.name: HasLatticeDualCone.snoc_le_snoc
declarations.doc:
Appending `g - δ • 1` below and `g + δ • 1` above keeps the lower observables below the upper
ones.
declarations.statement:
lemma snoc_le_snoc {δ : ℝ} (hδ : 0 ≤ δ) {g : F} (hg : IsApproxInterpolant a b δ g) (i : Fin (n + 1))
    (j : Fin (m + 1)) : Fin.snoc (α := fun _ => F) a (g - δ • 1) i ≤
      Fin.snoc (α := fun _ => F) b (g + δ • 1) j

declarations.name: HasLatticeDualCone.exists_isApproxInterpolant_near
declarations.doc:
An approximate interpolant can be improved to any smaller error while moving by at most the sum
of the two errors.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_isApproxInterpolant_near [Nontrivial F] {δ δ' : ℝ} (hδ : 0 ≤ δ) (hδ' : 0 < δ')
    {g : F} (hg : IsApproxInterpolant a b δ g) :
    ∃ g', IsApproxInterpolant a b δ' g' ∧ g - (δ + δ') • 1 ≤ g' ∧ g' ≤ g + (δ + δ') • 1

declarations.name: HasLatticeDualCone.exists_seq
declarations.doc:
A sequence of interpolants with errors `(1 / 2) ^ k`, each within
`(1 / 2) ^ k + (1 / 2) ^ (k + 1)` of the next.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_seq [Nontrivial F] [NeZero n] [NeZero m] : ∃ g : ℕ → F, ∀ k,
    IsApproxInterpolant a b ((1 / 2) ^ k) (g k) ∧
      g k - ((1 / 2) ^ k + (1 / 2) ^ (k + 1) : ℝ) • 1 ≤ g (k + 1) ∧
      g (k + 1) ≤ g k + ((1 / 2) ^ k + (1 / 2) ^ (k + 1) : ℝ) • 1

declarations.name: HasLatticeDualCone.isApproxInterpolant_zero_of_tendsto
declarations.doc: A limit of interpolants with errors `(1 / 2) ^ k` is an exact interpolant.

declarations.name: HasLatticeDualCone.exists_interpolant
declarations.doc:
**Exact interpolation.** On a complete Archimedean order-unit space whose positive functionals
form a lattice, lower observables below upper observables have an interpolant.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_interpolant [CompleteSpace F] [NeZero n] [NeZero m] :
    ∃ g : F, (∀ i, a i ≤ g) ∧ ∀ j, g ≤ b j

declarations.name: HasLatticeDualCone.hasRieszDecomposition
declarations.doc:
On a complete Archimedean order-unit space whose positive functionals form a lattice,
observables have the Riesz decomposition.

lemma _root_.HasLatticeDualCone.hasRieszDecomposition {F : Type*} [ArchimedeanOrderUnitSpace F]
    [CompleteSpace F] (hF : HasLatticeDualCone F) : HasRieszDecomposition F

modules.title: Lattice-ordered observables
modules.doc:
Order-unit lattices: Archimedean order-unit spaces whose order is a lattice.

## i. Overview

An order-unit lattice is a space of observables in which any two observables have a least upper
bound. Classical observables form such a lattice, with the pointwise maximum. Quantum observables do
not: two self-adjoint matrices usually have no least upper bound.

An order-unit lattice is a vector lattice in which the unit is a strong unit, so the order theory
of vector lattices applies to it: an observable below a sum of two positive observables splits into
two pieces, one below each summand, and every observable is close to a step function.

## ii. Key results

- `OrderUnitLattice E` is an Archimedean order-unit space whose order is a lattice.
- `OrderUnitLattice.map_sup_of_map_inf` : a positive functional preserving minima preserves maxima.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Order-unit lattices

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.doc: An Archimedean order-unit space whose order is a lattice.
declarations.statement: class OrderUnitLattice (E : Type*) extends ArchimedeanOrderUnitSpace E, Lattice E

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.OrderUnitLattice.map_sup_of_map_inf
declarations.doc: A positive functional preserves suprema whenever it preserves infima.

    ω (f ⊔ g) = max (ω f) (ω g)

modules.title: Monotone-complete ordered spaces
modules.doc:
Monotone-complete orders and chosen suprema of bounded directed sets and increasing sequences.

## i. Overview

An ordered space is monotone complete when every nonempty directed set that is bounded above has a
least upper bound.

## ii. Key results

- `MonotoneCompleteOrder` : monotone-complete ordered spaces.
- `MonotoneCompleteOrder.directedSup` : the supremum of a bounded directed set.
- `MonotoneCompleteOrder.rangeSup` : the supremum of a bounded increasing sequence.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Monotone-complete orders
- B. Chosen suprema

## iv. References

* None.

modules.title: The canonical normed copy of an order-unit space
modules.doc:
The type synonym `WithOrderUnitNorm E` with the canonical order-unit norm; channels contract.

## i. Overview

An Archimedean order-unit space already has a canonical order-unit norm, but the underlying type
may carry a different norm for another purpose. `WithOrderUnitNorm E` is a type synonym that
carries the canonical norm without changing the structures on `E` itself.

## ii. Key results

- `WithOrderUnitNorm E` : the canonical normed copy of `E`.
- `WithOrderUnitNorm.linearEquiv` : the identity linear equivalence with `E`.
- `UnitalPositiveLinearMap.orderUnitNorm_map_le` : channels are contractive.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The normed copy
- B. The real scalar case
- C. Contractivity of channels

## iv. References

* None.

modules.title: The unit of an order-unit space as an order unit
modules.doc:
The unit of an order-unit space is an order unit, so weight-zero positive functionals vanish.

## i. Overview

The unit of an order-unit space is an order unit of the underlying ordered vector space, so the
general order theory of positive functionals applies to observables. In particular a positive
functional that vanishes on the unit vanishes everywhere.

## ii. Key results

- `OrderUnitSpace.isOrderUnit_one` : the unit is an order unit.
- `PositiveLinearMap.eq_zero_of_map_one_eq_zero` : a positive functional of total weight zero
  vanishes.

## iii. Table of contents

- B. Positive functionals

modules.title: Nets of algebras over the finite regions of a lattice and their quasi-local algebra
modules.doc:
A net of `*`-algebras over the finite regions of a set of sites has a quasi-local algebra: the
direct limit of the local algebras.

## i. Overview

The observables of an infinite system are those of finite regions, extended by the identity. A
*net of algebras* assigns to each finite region `X` of a set of sites a unital `*`-algebra `A X`,
and to each pair of regions `X ≤ Y` a unital `*`-homomorphism `A X → A Y`, with the identity
for `X = Y` and composition respected. The finite regions are directed under inclusion: any two
regions lie in a third. The *quasi-local algebra* is the direct limit: its elements are the
observables of some finite region, two of them being identified when they agree in a common larger
region. It is a unital complex `*`-algebra, and each local algebra maps into it.

Nothing about the nature of the local algebras enters: they may be commutative, giving a
classical system, or matrix algebras, giving a quantum system, or anything in between. The
constructions that follow, the states and thermodynamic limits, the symmetries and the dynamics,
are made once for every net.

## ii. Key results

- `AlgebraNet` : a net of unital `*`-algebras over the finite regions of a set of sites.
- `AlgebraNet.Quasilocal` : the quasi-local algebra, as the direct limit.
- `AlgebraNet.of` : the embedding of a local algebra as a unital `*`-homomorphism.
- `AlgebraNet.of_incl` : the local algebras embed compatibly.
- `AlgebraNet.exists_of` : every quasi-local observable is supported in a finite region.
- `AlgebraNet.moveHom` : a map of the quasi-local algebra induced by region-moving local maps.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Nets of algebras
- B. The quasi-local algebra

## iv. References

* O. Bratteli & D. Robinson, Operator Algebras and Quantum Statistical Mechanics 1,
  Section 2.6.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuasiLocal.AlgebraNet
declarations.doc:
A net of unital complex `*`-algebras over the finite regions of a set of sites: the algebra of
each region, and the inclusion of the algebra of a region in that of a larger region.
declarations.statement:
structure AlgebraNet (S : Type*) where
  /-- The algebra of observables of a finite region. -/
  A : Finset S → Type*
  [ring : ∀ X, Ring (A X)]
  [algebra : ∀ X, Algebra ℂ (A X)]
  [starRing : ∀ X, StarRing (A X)]
  [starModule : ∀ X, StarModule ℂ (A X)]
  /-- The inclusion of the algebra of a region in the algebra of a larger region. -/
  incl : ∀ {X Y : Finset S}, X ≤ Y → A X →⋆ₐ[ℂ] A Y
  /-- The inclusion of a region in itself is the identity. -/
  incl_refl : ∀ (X : Finset S) (a : A X), incl (le_refl X) a = a
  /-- Inclusions compose. -/
  incl_trans : ∀ {X Y Z : Finset S} (h₁ : X ≤ Y) (h₂ : Y ≤ Z) (a : A X),
    incl (h₁.trans h₂) a = incl h₂ (incl h₁ a)
instance : DirectedSystem N.A (fun X Y (h : X ≤ Y) => N.incl h)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuasiLocal.AlgebraNet.Quasilocal
declarations.doc:
**The quasi-local algebra** of a net: the direct limit of the algebras of the finite

declarations.statement: abbrev Quasilocal : Type _

declarations.statement: lemma exists_of (x : N.Quasilocal) : ∃ (X : Finset S) (a : N.A X), N.of X a = x

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuasiLocal.AlgebraNet.moveHom
declarations.doc:
A map of the quasi-local algebra induced by maps of the local algebras that move regions: a
monotone map `ρ` of regions and, for each region `X`, a unital `*`-homomorphism of its algebra
into that of `ρ X`, natural with respect to the inclusions.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def moveHom (ρ : Finset S → Finset S) (hρ : Monotone ρ)
    (φ : ∀ X, N.A X →⋆ₐ[ℂ] N.A (ρ X))
    (hφ : ∀ {X Y : Finset S} (h : X ≤ Y) (a : N.A X), φ Y (N.incl h a) = N.incl (hρ h) (φ X a)) :
    N.Quasilocal →⋆ₐ[ℂ] N.Quasilocal

declarations.statement:
lemma moveHom_of (ρ : Finset S → Finset S) (hρ : Monotone ρ) (φ : ∀ X, N.A X →⋆ₐ[ℂ] N.A (ρ X))
    (hφ : ∀ {X Y : Finset S} (h : X ≤ Y) (a : N.A X), φ Y (N.incl h a) = N.incl (hρ h) (φ X a))
    (X : Finset S) (a : N.A X) : N.moveHom ρ hρ φ hφ (N.of X a) = N.of (ρ X) (φ X a)

modules.title: Limit states of the quasi-local algebra
modules.doc:
A net of local states, one for each finite region, has limit points that are states of the
quasi-local algebra.

## i. Overview

Let `ω_Λ` be a state of the algebra of the finite region `Λ`, for every `Λ`. The expectation value
of a fixed local observable `a`, taken in the larger and larger regions `Λ`, is a net of complex
numbers. If every local observable has a bounded such net, the net has a limit along every
ultrafilter finer than the filter of large regions, by compactness of closed balls in `ℂ`. The
limits are compatible, normalized, Hermitian and positive, so they form a `LocalStateFamily`, and
hence a state of the quasi-local algebra.

Boundedness is expressed without any norm: an observable `a` is *locally bounded* if some
multiple `c · 1` of the identity exceeds `a* a` by a sum of squares. In a matrix algebra this
holds with `c = ‖a‖²`. Each state then satisfies `|ω(a)|² ≤ ω(a* a) ≤ c`, by the Cauchy–Schwarz
inequality for states.

Nothing is assumed about the nature of the local states: they may be Gibbs states with any
boundary condition. Different ultrafilters can give different limit states, which is how phase
coexistence appears.

## ii. Key results

- `AlgState.normSq_le` : the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality `|ω(a)|² ≤ ω(a* a)`.
- `AlgebraNet.IsLocallyBounded` : every local observable is bounded by a multiple of the identity.
- `limitFamily` : the ultrafilter limit of a net of local states, as a compatible family.
- `limitState` : the limit state of the quasi-local algebra.
- `limitState_of` : its value on a local observable is the limit of the local expectations.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The Cauchy–Schwarz inequality and sums of squares
- B. Local boundedness
- C. The ultrafilter limit

## iv. References

* O. Bratteli & D. Robinson, Operator Algebras and Quantum Statistical Mechanics 2,
  Section 6.2.3 (existence of limit Gibbs states by weak-⋆ compactness).

modules.title: States of the quasi-local algebra from compatible local states
modules.doc:
A family of local states, each the restriction of the next, is a state of the quasi-local algebra.

## i. Overview

A state of an infinite system is determined by the expectation values of the local observables.
A *compatible family* assigns to each finite region `X` a state of its algebra `A X` such that the
state of a larger region restricts to the state of the smaller: `ω_Y (incl a) = ω_X (a)`. Such a
family defines a linear functional on the quasi-local algebra, which is a state: normalized,
Hermitian and positive. Every element of the quasi-local algebra is local, and positivity of
`a* a` is positivity of local states.

## ii. Key results

- `LocalStateFamily` : a compatible family of local states.
- `LocalStateFamily.toAlgState` : the state of the quasi-local algebra.
- `LocalStateFamily.toAlgState_of` : its value on a local observable is the local expectation.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Compatible families
- B. The state of the quasi-local algebra

## iv. References

* O. Bratteli & D. Robinson, Operator Algebras and Quantum Statistical Mechanics 1,
  Section 2.6.

sections.text: ## B. The state of the quasi-local algebra

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuasiLocal.LocalStateFamily
declarations.doc: A compatible family of local states of a net of algebras.
declarations.statement:
structure LocalStateFamily where
  /-- The local functionals. -/
  state : ∀ X : Finset S, N.A X →ₗ[ℂ] ℂ
  /-- The functional of a larger region restricts to that of a smaller one. -/
  compat : ∀ {X Y : Finset S} (h : X ≤ Y) (a : N.A X), state Y (N.incl h a) = state X a
  /-- The local functionals are normalized. -/
  map_one : ∀ X, state X 1 = 1
  /-- The local functionals are Hermitian. -/
  map_star : ∀ X (a : N.A X), state X (star a) = star (state X a)
  /-- The local functionals are positive. -/
  nonneg : ∀ X (a : N.A X), 0 ≤ state X (star a * a)

declarations.doc: The linear functional on the quasi-local algebra defined by a compatible family.
declarations.statement: def LocalStateFamily.lift (ω : LocalStateFamily N) : N.Quasilocal →ₗ[ℂ] ℂ

declarations.statement:
lemma LocalStateFamily.lift_of (ω : LocalStateFamily N) (X : Finset S) (a : N.A X) :
    ω.lift (N.of X a) = ω.state X a

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuasiLocal.LocalStateFamily.toAlgState
declarations.doc: **The state of the quasi-local algebra** defined by a compatible family.
declarations.statement: def LocalStateFamily.toAlgState (ω : LocalStateFamily N) : AlgState N.Quasilocal

declarations.statement:

    ω.toAlgState (N.of X a) = ω.state X a

modules.title: The spectral measure of a unitary representation of an abelian group
modules.doc:
A unitary representation of a discrete abelian group on a Hilbert space is the integral of the
characters of the group against a projection-valued measure on the Pontryagin dual.

## i. Overview

The unitary operators `π(g)` of a representation of an abelian group commute and are closed under
adjoints, so they have a joint spectral measure on the character space of the C⋆-algebra they
generate. A character of that algebra restricts to a unitary character of the group, which gives
a map from the character space to the Pontryagin dual of the group. Pushing the joint spectral
measure forward along this map gives a projection-valued measure `P` on the dual with
`π(g) = ∫ χ(g) dP(χ)`. Every bounded operator commuting with the representation commutes with `P`.

## ii. Key results

- `UnitaryRep.family` : the commuting ⋆-family of the operators of the representation.
- `UnitaryRep.spectralMeasure` : the projection-valued measure on the Pontryagin dual.
- `UnitaryRep.boundedIntegral_character` : `π(g) = ∫ χ(g) dP(χ)`.
- `UnitaryRep.spectralMeasure_commute` : `P` commutes with every operator commuting with `π`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The family of the representation
- B. From the algebra's characters to the dual group
- C. The spectral measure

## iv. References

* None.

modules.title: Bloch bands
modules.doc:
The ordered eigenvalues of a Hermitian Bloch matrix are continuous functions on the Brillouin zone,
and they exhaust the spectrum of the translation-invariant operator.

## i. Overview

The eigenvalues of a Hermitian `N × N` matrix, listed in decreasing order, are the bands
`ε₁(χ) ≥ ⋯ ≥ ε_N(χ)` of a Hermitian Bloch matrix `b(χ)`. By Weyl's inequality the `k`-th
eigenvalue moves by at most the operator norm of the change of the matrix, so each band `ε_k` is a
continuous function of the matrix and hence of the crystal momentum `χ`. If the symbol of a
translation-invariant operator is Hermitian the operator is self-adjoint, and its spectrum is
contained in the union of the ranges of the bands.

## ii. Key results

- `bandOf` : the `k`-th largest eigenvalue of a Hermitian matrix.
- `abs_bandOf_sub_le` : Weyl's inequality for bands.
- `continuous_bandOf` : bands are continuous functions of a continuous Hermitian family.
- `UnitaryRep.isSelfAdjoint_blochHom` : the operator of a Hermitian symbol is self-adjoint.
- `UnitaryRep.exists_band_eq_of_mem_spectrum` : every spectral value is a band value.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Bands of Hermitian matrices
- B. Bands of a translation-invariant operator

## iv. References

* R. Bhatia, Matrix Analysis, Corollary III.2.6.

sections.text: ## B. Bands of a translation-invariant operator

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.bandOf
declarations.doc: The `k`-th largest eigenvalue of a Hermitian matrix: its `k`-th band.
declarations.statement:
def bandOf {N : ℕ} {M : Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℂ} (hM : M.IsHermitian)
    (k : Fin (Fintype.card (Fin N))) : ℝ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.abs_bandOf_sub_le
declarations.doc:
**Weyl's inequality for bands**: the `k`-th band of two Hermitian matrices differ by at most
the operator norm of the difference.
declarations.statement:
lemma abs_bandOf_sub_le {N : ℕ} {M S : Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℂ} (hM : M.IsHermitian)
    (hS : S.IsHermitian) (k : Fin (Fintype.card (Fin N))) :
    |bandOf hM k - bandOf hS k| ≤
      ‖LinearMap.toContinuousLinearMap (Matrix.toEuclideanLin (M - S))‖

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.continuous_bandOf
declarations.doc:
**Bands are continuous**: the `k`-th band of a continuous family of Hermitian matrices is a
continuous function.

declarations.doc: The operator of a Hermitian symbol is self-adjoint.
declarations.statement:
lemma isSelfAdjoint_blochHom
    (b : C(PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G), Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℂ))
    (hb : ∀ χ, (b χ).IsHermitian) : IsSelfAdjoint (blochHom π ι hι b)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.UnitaryRep.exists_band_eq_of_mem_spectrum
declarations.doc:
**Every point of the spectrum of the operator of a Hermitian symbol is a band value**: it is
the `k`-th band `ε_k(χ)` of some crystal momentum `χ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_band_eq_of_mem_spectrum
    (b : C(PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G), Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℂ))
    (hb : ∀ χ, (b χ).IsHermitian) {z : ℂ} (hz : z ∈ spectrum ℂ (blochHom π ι hι b)) :
    ∃ (χ : PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G)) (k : Fin (Fintype.card (Fin N))),
      z = ((bandOf (hb χ) k : ℝ) : ℂ)

modules.title: The commutant of a unitary representation of an abelian group
modules.doc:
Every bounded operator commuting with a unitary representation of an abelian group is decomposable
over the characters of the group.

## i. Overview

The spectral measure `P` of a unitary representation `π` commutes with every bounded operator `T`
that commutes with all `π(g)`: such an operator maps each spectral subspace into itself, it is
reduced by the spectral decomposition of `π`. Consequently the closed subspaces invariant under
the representation are exactly the closed subspaces invariant under the spectral measure, and
the spectral projection onto a single character `χ` of a countable group is the projection onto
the subspace of vectors of crystal momentum `χ`.

## ii. Key results

- `UnitaryRep.projection` : the spectral projection of a set of characters.
- `UnitaryRep.projection_commute` : the spectral projections commute with the commutant.
- `UnitaryRep.mapsTo_projection_of_invariant` : spectral projections preserve every closed
  invariant subspace.
- `UnitaryRep.range_projection_singleton` : the projection onto the character `χ` is the
  projection onto the subspace of momentum `χ`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Spectral projections
- B. Commutation with the commutant
- C. Invariant subspaces
- D. Sectors of definite momentum

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.UnitaryRep.projection
declarations.doc: The spectral projection of a set of characters, as a bounded operator.
declarations.statement: def projection (S : Set (PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G))) : H →L[ℂ] H

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.UnitaryRep.projection_isStarProjection
declarations.statement:
lemma projection_isStarProjection (S : Set (PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G))) :
    IsStarProjection (projection π S)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.UnitaryRep.projection_eq_zero_of_not_measurable
declarations.statement:
lemma projection_eq_zero_of_not_measurable {S : Set (PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G))}
    (hS : ¬ MeasurableSet S) : projection π S = 0

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.UnitaryRep.projection_commute
declarations.doc:
**The commutant is decomposable**: every bounded operator commuting with the representation
commutes with every spectral projection.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.UnitaryRep.commute_starProjection_of_mapsTo
declarations.doc:
An operator mapping a closed subspace and its orthogonal complement into themselves commutes
with the orthogonal projection onto the subspace.
declarations.statement:
lemma commute_starProjection_of_mapsTo (W : Submodule ℂ H) [W.HasOrthogonalProjection]
    {T : H →L[ℂ] H} (hW : ∀ v ∈ W, T v ∈ W) (hWo : ∀ v ∈ Wᗮ, T v ∈ Wᗮ) :
    Commute (W.starProjection : H →L[ℂ] H) T

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.UnitaryRep.inner_unitary_left
declarations.statement:
lemma inner_unitary_left (g : Multiplicative G) (x w : H) :
    ⟪((π g : unitary (H →L[ℂ] H)) : H →L[ℂ] H) x, w⟫_ℂ =
      ⟪x, ((π g⁻¹ : unitary (H →L[ℂ] H)) : H →L[ℂ] H) w⟫_ℂ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.UnitaryRep.mapsTo_projection_of_invariant
declarations.doc:
A closed subspace invariant under the representation is invariant under every spectral
projection.
declarations.statement:
lemma mapsTo_projection_of_invariant (W : Submodule ℂ H) [W.HasOrthogonalProjection]
    (hW : ∀ g, ∀ v ∈ W, ((π g : unitary (H →L[ℂ] H)) : H →L[ℂ] H) v ∈ W)
    (S : Set (PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G))) {v : H} (hv : v ∈ W) :
    projection π S v ∈ W

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.UnitaryRep.mapsTo_of_projection_invariant
declarations.doc:
A closed subspace invariant under every spectral projection is invariant under the
representation.
declarations.statement:
lemma mapsTo_of_projection_invariant (W : Submodule ℂ H) [W.HasOrthogonalProjection]
    (hW : ∀ (S : Set (PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G))), ∀ v ∈ W, projection π S v ∈ W)
    (g : Multiplicative G) {v : H} (hv : v ∈ W) :
    ((π g : unitary (H →L[ℂ] H)) : H →L[ℂ] H) v ∈ W

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.UnitaryRep.toEnd
declarations.doc: The linear action of a unitary representation on its Hilbert space.
declarations.statement: def toEnd : Multiplicative G →* Module.End ℂ H

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.UnitaryRep.toEnd_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma toEnd_apply (g : Multiplicative G) (v : H) :
    toEnd π g v = ((π g : unitary (H →L[ℂ] H)) : H →L[ℂ] H) v

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.UnitaryRep.character_mul_projection_singleton
declarations.doc:
The operator `π(g)` acts on the spectral projection of the single character `χ` as the scalar
`χ(g)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma character_mul_projection_singleton (χ : PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G))
    (g : Multiplicative G) :
    ((π g : unitary (H →L[ℂ] H)) : H →L[ℂ] H) * projection π {χ} =
      ((χ g : Circle) : ℂ) • projection π {χ}

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.UnitaryRep.ae_eq_of_mem_sector
declarations.doc:
A vector of momentum `χ` is carried by the single character `χ`: its spectral measure is
concentrated at `χ`.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.UnitaryRep.projection_singleton_eq_self_of_mem_sector
declarations.doc: **A vector of momentum `χ` lies in the range of the spectral projection of `χ`.**

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.UnitaryRep.range_projection_singleton
declarations.doc:
**The spectral projection of a single character is the projection onto the sector of
definite momentum**: its range is the subspace of vectors on which the group acts through the
character.
declarations.statement:
lemma range_projection_singleton (χ : PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G)) :
    LinearMap.range (projection π {χ} : H →L[ℂ] H).toLinearMap =
      ProbabilisticTheory.Representation.sector (toEnd π) (fun g => ((χ g : Circle) : ℂ))

modules.title: Covariant measurements and channels
modules.doc:
Symmetries acting on effects, measurable actions on outcomes, covariant measures and channels.

## i. Overview

A measurement is covariant under a symmetry group when transforming the outcome transforms the
effect: `μ (g • S) = ρ g • μ S`. A symmetry acts on effects, a group acts on outcomes by measurable
bijections, and a channel is covariant when it intertwines two symmetry actions.

## ii. Key results

- `Symmetry.instSMulEffect` : symmetries act on effects.
- `MeasurableAction` : a group acting on outcomes by measurable bijections.
- `EffectValuedMeasure.IsCovariant` : covariant effect-valued measures.
- `UnitalPositiveLinearMap.IsCovariant` : covariant channels.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Covariant channels: the general intertwiner picture

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text:
## A. Covariant channels: the general intertwiner picture

A channel between two systems is covariant when transporting the input and transporting the
output agree: the channel intertwines the two actions.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Symmetry.instSMulEffect
declarations.doc:
A symmetry acts on effects the way it acts on `E` itself, via the underlying channel — the
dual of `Symmetry`'s existing action on states.
declarations.statement: instance Symmetry.instSMulEffect : SMul (Symmetry E) (Effect E)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Symmetry.coe_smul_effect
declarations.statement:
lemma Symmetry.coe_smul_effect (φ : Symmetry E) (e : Effect E) :
    ((φ • e : Effect E) : E) = φ.1 (e : E)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Symmetry.instMulActionEffect
declarations.statement: instance Symmetry.instMulActionEffect : MulAction (Symmetry E) (Effect E)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.MeasurableAction
declarations.doc:
`G` acts on the measurable space `Ω`, and every group element moves points measurably. Since
this holds for `g` and `g⁻¹` both, the action is by measurable *bijections*: `MeasurableSet.smul`
below shows it moves measurable sets to measurable sets, not merely points.
declarations.statement:
class MeasurableAction (G Ω : Type*) [Group G] [MeasurableSpace Ω] [MulAction G Ω] : Prop where
  /-- Every group element acts as a measurable map. -/
  measurable_smul : ∀ g : G, Measurable (fun x : Ω => g • x)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.measurableSet_smul
declarations.doc:
The image of a measurable set under the action of a group element is again measurable:
`g • S` is the preimage of `S` under the (measurable) action of `g⁻¹`.
declarations.statement: lemma measurableSet_smul {S : Set Ω} (hS : MeasurableSet S) (g : G) : MeasurableSet (g • S)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.EffectValuedMeasure.IsCovariant
declarations.doc:
A measurement (POVM) `μ` is **covariant** under an action of `G` on the outcome space,
transported to the physical system via `ρ : G →* Symmetry E`, when transforming the outcome set
and transforming the assigned effect agree: `μ(g • S) = ρ(g) • μ(S)`. This is the abstract form of
`E(gS) = α_g(E(S))` — a rotated detector pointed at a rotated direction reads out what a rotation
of the original detector would have.
declarations.statement: def EffectValuedMeasure.IsCovariant (ρ : G →* Symmetry E) (μ : EffectValuedMeasure Ω E) : Prop

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.IsCovariant
declarations.doc:
A channel `φ : Channel E₁ E₂` is **covariant** under symmetry actions `ρ₁`, `ρ₂` of `G` on the
two systems when transporting the input along `ρ₁ g` then applying `φ`, or applying `φ` then
transporting the output along `ρ₂ g`, agree — the channel intertwines the two actions.
declarations.statement:
def UnitalPositiveLinearMap.IsCovariant (ρ₁ : G →* Symmetry E₁) (ρ₂ : G →* Symmetry E₂)
    (φ : Channel E₁ E₂) : Prop

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.isCovariant_id
declarations.doc:
The identity channel is covariant under any action of `G`, against itself: it trivially
intertwines an action with itself.
declarations.statement:
lemma UnitalPositiveLinearMap.isCovariant_id (ρ : G →* Symmetry E₁) :
    (UnitalPositiveLinearMap.id ℝ E₁).IsCovariant ρ ρ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.IsCovariant.comp
declarations.doc:
Covariance is preserved by composition: a covariant channel followed by a covariant channel is
covariant for the actions at the two ends, with the middle system's action cancelling out.

modules.title: Covariance of measurements under an action on the outcomes
modules.doc:
Covariance of measurements under a group action on outcomes, and its preservation.

## i. Overview

A group `G` acting measurably on an outcome space `Ω` acts on the classical system of `Ω` by
relabeling: `σ` sends an observable `f` to `x ↦ f (σ⁻¹ • x)`. The inverse makes this a left
action. A measurement is a channel out of the classical system, so its covariance, matched to a
symmetry action `ρ` on the physical system, is just covariance of that channel.

Post-processing a measurement is composing its channel with a classical channel, so covariance is
preserved by covariant post-processing. In particular, relabeling the outcomes along an
equivariant map preserves covariance, and the marginals of a covariant joint measurement, for the
diagonal action on a product of outcome spaces, are covariant.

## ii. Key results

- `BoundedMeasurable.inducedAction` : the action of `G` on the classical system of `Ω`.
- `BoundedMeasurable.comap_isCovariant` : relabeling along an equivariant map is covariant.
- `Measurement.IsCovariant` : covariance of a measurement.
- `Measurement.IsCovariant.comp` : covariant post-processing preserves covariance.
- `Measurement.IsCovariant.mapOutcome` : equivariant relabeling preserves covariance.
- `Measurement.IsCovariant.marginal` : marginals of a covariant joint measurement are covariant.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The induced action on the classical system
  - A.1. The relabeling channels
  - A.2. The induced action
  - A.3. The diagonal action on a product of outcome spaces
  - A.4. Relabeling along an equivariant map
- B. Covariant measurements
  - B.1. The definition of covariance
  - B.2. Covariant post-processing
  - B.3. Marginals of a covariant joint measurement

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. The induced action on the classical system
### A.3. The diagonal action on a product of outcome spaces
### A.4. Relabeling along an equivariant map
### B.3. Marginals of a covariant joint measurement

declarations.name: BoundedMeasurable.inducedChannel
declarations.doc:
The channel on the classical system that relabels outcomes by `σ`:
`f ↦ (x ↦ f (σ⁻¹ • x))`.
declarations.statement: def inducedChannel (σ : G) : Channel (BoundedMeasurable Ω) (BoundedMeasurable Ω)

declarations.name: BoundedMeasurable.inducedChannel_apply
declarations.doc: The relabeling channel evaluates an observable at the relabeled outcome.
declarations.statement:
lemma inducedChannel_apply (σ : G) (f : BoundedMeasurable Ω) (x : Ω) :
    inducedChannel σ f x = f (σ⁻¹ • x)

declarations.name: BoundedMeasurable.isOrderAutomorphism_inducedChannel
declarations.doc:
Relabeling by `σ⁻¹` undoes relabeling by `σ`, so each relabeling channel is an
order-automorphism.
declarations.statement:
lemma isOrderAutomorphism_inducedChannel (σ : G) :
    IsOrderAutomorphism (inducedChannel (Ω := Ω) σ)

declarations.name: BoundedMeasurable.inducedAction
declarations.doc: The action of `G` on the classical system of `Ω` induced by its action on the outcomes.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def inducedAction : G →* Symmetry (BoundedMeasurable Ω)

declarations.name: BoundedMeasurable.inducedAction_val
declarations.doc: The channel underlying the induced action of `σ` is the relabeling channel of `σ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma inducedAction_val (σ : G) :
    (inducedAction σ : Symmetry (BoundedMeasurable Ω)).1 = inducedChannel σ

declarations.doc: The diagonal action on a product of outcome spaces is measurable.
declarations.statement: instance : MeasurableAction G (Ω × Ω')

declarations.name: BoundedMeasurable.comap_isCovariant
declarations.doc: Relabeling along an equivariant measurable map is a covariant classical channel.
declarations.statement:
lemma comap_isCovariant (g : Ω' → Ω) (hg : Measurable g)
    (hequiv : ∀ (σ : G) x, g (σ • x) = σ • g x) :
    (comap g hg).IsCovariant (inducedAction (G := G)) (inducedAction (G := G))

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Measurement.IsCovariant
declarations.doc:
A measurement is covariant for an action on its outcomes, matched to the symmetry action `ρ`
on the system, when its channel intertwines the two actions.
declarations.statement: def IsCovariant (ρ : G →* Symmetry E) (M : Measurement Ω E) : Prop

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Measurement.IsCovariant.comp
declarations.doc:
Post-processing a covariant measurement by a covariant classical channel gives a covariant
channel.
declarations.statement:
lemma IsCovariant.comp {ρ : G →* Symmetry E} {M : Measurement Ω E}
    {K : Channel (BoundedMeasurable Ω') (BoundedMeasurable Ω)} (hM : M.IsCovariant ρ)
    (hK : K.IsCovariant (inducedAction (G := G)) inducedAction) :
    (M.toChannel.comp K).IsCovariant inducedAction ρ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Measurement.IsCovariant.mapOutcome
declarations.doc:
Relabeling the outcomes of a covariant measurement along an equivariant map gives a
covariant measurement.
declarations.statement:
lemma IsCovariant.mapOutcome {ρ : G →* Symmetry E} {N : Measurement Ω' E} (hN : N.IsCovariant ρ)
    (g : Ω' → Ω) (hg : Measurable g) (hequiv : ∀ (σ : G) x, g (σ • x) = σ • g x) :
    (N.mapOutcome g hg).IsCovariant ρ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Measurement.IsCovariant.marginal
declarations.doc:
The first marginal of a covariant joint measurement, for the diagonal action on the product
of outcome spaces, is covariant.

modules.title: Bloch–Floquet theory for representations with a finite-dimensional internal space
modules.doc:
Operators built from a unitary representation of an abelian group and an internal matrix algebra
are integrals of a matrix-valued symbol over the dual group.

## i. Overview

Let `π` be a unitary representation of a discrete abelian group `G` on a Hilbert space `H`, and let
`ι : M_N(ℂ) → B(H)` be a ⋆-homomorphism commuting with `π`: an `N`-dimensional internal space
attached to every point. Nothing is assumed about what `H` describes. It may carry the
wavefunctions of a quantum particle, the displacement fields of a classical lattice, or an
`L²` space of a classical statistical ensemble. The spectral measure `P` of `π` turns every
continuous matrix-valued function `f` on the dual group `Ĝ` into the operator
`∫ f dP = ∑_{ij} (∫ f_{ij} dP) ι(E_{ij})`, and this is a unital ⋆-homomorphism from `C(Ĝ, M_N)`
to `B(H)`. Operators commuting with `π` and `ι` that arise this way are the translation-invariant
operators with symbol `f`. Consequently the spectrum of the operator of a symbol is contained in the
union of the spectra of the matrices `f(χ)`: the spectrum is the union of the bands. Under full
support of the representation the map is injective.

## ii. Key results

- `UnitaryRep.calculus` : the functional calculus `f ↦ ∫ f dP` of a representation.
- `UnitaryRep.blochHom` : the ⋆-homomorphism `f ↦ ∫ f dP` on matrix-valued continuous functions.
- `UnitaryRep.spectrum_blochHom_subset` : the spectrum of the operator of a symbol is contained in
  the union of the spectra of the values of the symbol.
- `UnitaryRep.blochHom_injective` : the map is injective for a representation of full support.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The functional calculus of the representation
- B. Matrix-valued functions
- C. The spectrum
- D. Faithful representations

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. The functional calculus of the representation

declarations.statement: instance : Nonempty (PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G))

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.UnitaryRep.calculus
declarations.doc:
**The functional calculus of a unitary representation**: `f ↦ ∫ f dP` is a unital
⋆-homomorphism from the continuous functions on the Pontryagin dual to the bounded operators.
declarations.statement: def calculus : C(PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G), ℂ) →⋆ₐ[ℂ] (H →L[ℂ] H)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.UnitaryRep.calculus_character
declarations.doc: The functional calculus sends the character `χ ↦ χ(g)` to the operator `π(g)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma calculus_character (g : Multiplicative G) :
    calculus π ⟨fun χ => ((χ g : Circle) : ℂ),
      (TauCeti.PontryaginDual.continuous_coe_eval_const (G := Multiplicative G) g)⟩ =
      ((π g : unitary (H →L[ℂ] H)) : H →L[ℂ] H)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.UnitaryRep.calculus_commute
declarations.doc: An operator commuting with the representation commutes with its functional calculus.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.UnitaryRep.entry
declarations.doc: The `(i, j)` entry of a continuous matrix-valued function.
declarations.statement:
def entry (f : C(PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G), Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℂ)) (i j : Fin N) :
    C(PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G), ℂ)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.UnitaryRep.entry_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma entry_apply (f : C(PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G), Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℂ))
    (i j : Fin N) (χ : PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G)) : entry f i j χ = f χ i j

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.UnitaryRep.calculus_commute_ι
declarations.statement:
lemma calculus_commute_ι (f : C(PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G), ℂ))
    (M : Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℂ) : calculus π f * ι M = ι M * calculus π f

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.UnitaryRep.blochOp
declarations.doc: The operator `∑_{ij} (∫ f_{ij} dP) ι(E_{ij})` of a continuous matrix-valued function.
declarations.statement: def blochOp (f : C(PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G), Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℂ)) : H →L[ℂ] H

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.UnitaryRep.entry_add
declarations.statement:
lemma entry_add (f g : C(PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G), Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℂ))
    (i j : Fin N) : entry (f + g) i j = entry f i j + entry g i j

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.UnitaryRep.entry_smul
declarations.statement:
lemma entry_smul (c : ℂ) (f : C(PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G), Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℂ))
    (i j : Fin N) : entry (c • f) i j = c • entry f i j

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.UnitaryRep.entry_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma entry_zero (i j : Fin N) :
    entry (0 : C(PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G), Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℂ)) i j = 0

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.UnitaryRep.entry_mul
declarations.statement:
lemma entry_mul (f g : C(PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G), Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℂ))
    (i j : Fin N) : entry (f * g) i j = ∑ k, entry f i k * entry g k j

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.UnitaryRep.entry_star
declarations.statement:
lemma entry_star (f : C(PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G), Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℂ))
    (i j : Fin N) : entry (star f) i j = star (entry f j i)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.UnitaryRep.entry_one
declarations.statement:
lemma entry_one (i j : Fin N) :
    entry (1 : C(PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G), Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℂ)) i j =
      if i = j then 1 else 0

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.UnitaryRep.blochOp_add
declarations.statement:
lemma blochOp_add (f g : C(PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G), Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℂ)) :
    blochOp π ι (f + g) = blochOp π ι f + blochOp π ι g

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.UnitaryRep.blochOp_smul
declarations.statement:
lemma blochOp_smul (c : ℂ)
    (f : C(PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G), Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℂ)) :
    blochOp π ι (c • f) = c • blochOp π ι f

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.UnitaryRep.blochOp_one
declarations.statement:
lemma blochOp_one : blochOp π ι (1 : C(PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G),
    Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℂ)) = 1

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.UnitaryRep.blochOp_mul
declarations.statement:
lemma blochOp_mul (f g : C(PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G), Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℂ)) :
    blochOp π ι (f * g) = blochOp π ι f * blochOp π ι g

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.UnitaryRep.blochOp_star
declarations.statement:
lemma blochOp_star (f : C(PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G), Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℂ)) :
    blochOp π ι (star f) = star (blochOp π ι f)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.UnitaryRep.blochHom
declarations.doc:
**Bloch–Floquet**: the map `f ↦ ∑_{ij} (∫ f_{ij} dP) ι(E_{ij})` is a unital ⋆-homomorphism from
the continuous matrix-valued functions on the Brillouin zone to the bounded operators.
declarations.statement:
def blochHom : C(PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G), Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℂ) →⋆ₐ[ℂ]
    (H →L[ℂ] H)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.UnitaryRep.spectrum_blochHom_subset
declarations.doc:
**The spectrum of the operator of a symbol is contained in the union of the spectra of the
symbol's values**: a translation-invariant operator has no spectrum outside its Bloch bands.
declarations.statement:
lemma spectrum_blochHom_subset
    (b : C(PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G), Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℂ)) :
    spectrum ℂ (blochHom π ι hι b) ⊆
      ⋃ χ : PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G), spectrum ℂ (b χ)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.UnitaryRep.HasFullSupport
declarations.doc:
A representation has **full support** relative to the internal space when the spectral
projection of every nonempty open set of crystal momenta is nonzero on every internal state:
every crystal momentum is present in every orbital.
declarations.statement: def HasFullSupport : Prop

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.UnitaryRep.compress_blochOp
declarations.doc:
Compressing the image of a matrix-valued function to the `(i, j)` orbitals isolates the
`(i, j)` entry.
declarations.statement:
lemma compress_blochOp (f : C(PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G), Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℂ))
    (i j : Fin N) :
    ι (Matrix.single i i 1) * blochOp π ι f * ι (Matrix.single j i 1) =
      calculus π (entry f i j) * ι (Matrix.single i i 1)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.UnitaryRep.entry_eq_zero_of_blochOp_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
An entry of the image vanishes only if the entry function vanishes: this is the content of
full support.
declarations.statement:
lemma entry_eq_zero_of_blochOp_eq_zero (hfull : HasFullSupport π ι)
    (f : C(PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G), Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℂ))
    (hf : blochOp π ι f = 0) : f = 0

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.UnitaryRep.blochHom_injective
declarations.doc: Under full support the map `f ↦ ∫ f dP` is injective.
declarations.statement:
lemma blochHom_injective (hfull : HasFullSupport π ι) :
    Function.Injective (blochHom π ι hι)

modules.title: Hopping operators and their Bloch matrices
modules.doc:
The finite-range translation-invariant operators are the operators whose symbol is a trigonometric
polynomial.

## i. Overview

An operator `∑_r π(r) ι(A_r)` with finitely many matrices `A_r` couples each point to finitely many
other points through the matrices `A_r`. The general theory of `BlochFloquet` applies to it: its
symbol is the Bloch matrix `b(χ) = ∑_r χ(r) A_r`, a trigonometric polynomial, and the operator is
the integral of its Bloch matrix. This covers tight-binding Hamiltonians, the dynamical matrices of
harmonic lattices, adjacency operators of periodic graphs, and the transfer operators of
translation-invariant classical lattice models alike.

## ii. Key results

- `UnitaryRep.hopping` : the finite-range translation-invariant operator with matrices `A_r`.
- `UnitaryRep.blochMatrix` : its Bloch matrix.
- `UnitaryRep.blochHom_blochMatrix` : the operator is the integral of its Bloch matrix.
- `UnitaryRep.spectrum_hopping_subset` : the spectrum is contained in the union of the bands.
- `UnitaryRep.symmetrize` : the Hermitian completion of a family of hopping matrices.
- `UnitaryRep.isHermitian_blochMatrix` : the Bloch matrix of a Hermitian hopping family is
  Hermitian at every crystal momentum.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The hopping operator and its Bloch matrix
- B. The spectrum
- C. Hermitian hopping

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. The hopping operator and its Bloch matrix

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.UnitaryRep.hopping
declarations.doc:
A translation-invariant hopping operator `∑_r π(r) ι(A_r)` with finitely many matrices `A_r`,
the amplitude of hopping by the lattice vector `r` between orbitals.
declarations.statement: def hopping (A : G →₀ Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℂ) : H →L[ℂ] H

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.UnitaryRep.blochMatrix
declarations.doc:
The Bloch matrix `b(χ) = ∑_r χ(r) A_r` of a hopping operator, a continuous matrix-valued
function on the Brillouin zone.
declarations.statement:
def blochMatrix (A : G →₀ Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℂ) :
    C(PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G), Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℂ)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.UnitaryRep.blochMatrix_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma blochMatrix_apply (A : G →₀ Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℂ)
    (χ : PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G)) :
    blochMatrix A χ = A.sum fun r M => ((χ (Multiplicative.ofAdd r) : Circle) : ℂ) • M

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.UnitaryRep.blochHom_blochMatrix
declarations.doc: **The hopping operator is the integral of its Bloch matrix.**
declarations.statement:
lemma blochHom_blochMatrix (A : G →₀ Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℂ) :
    blochHom π ι hι (blochMatrix A) = hopping π ι A

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.UnitaryRep.spectrum_hopping_subset
declarations.doc:
The spectrum of a finite-range translation-invariant operator is contained in the union of the
spectra of its Bloch matrices.
declarations.statement:
lemma spectrum_hopping_subset (A : G →₀ Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℂ) :
    spectrum ℂ (hopping π ι A) ⊆
      ⋃ χ : PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G), spectrum ℂ (blochMatrix A χ)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.UnitaryRep.symmetrize
declarations.doc:
The Hermitian completion of a family of hopping matrices: the amplitude for hopping by `r` is
`A r` plus the adjoint of the amplitude for hopping back by `-r`.
declarations.statement: def symmetrize (A : G →₀ Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℂ) : G →₀ Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℂ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.UnitaryRep.symmetrize_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma symmetrize_apply (A : G →₀ Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℂ) (r : G) :
    symmetrize A r = A r + (A (-r))ᴴ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.UnitaryRep.conjTranspose_symmetrize
declarations.doc: A symmetrized family of hopping matrices satisfies `(A r)ᴴ = A (-r)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma conjTranspose_symmetrize (A : G →₀ Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℂ) (r : G) :
    (symmetrize A r)ᴴ = symmetrize A (-r)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.UnitaryRep.isHermitian_blochMatrix
declarations.doc:
**Hermitian hopping gives Hermitian Bloch matrices.** If `(A r)ᴴ = A (-r)` for every `r`, then
the Bloch matrix `∑_r χ(r) A_r` is Hermitian at every crystal momentum `χ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma isHermitian_blochMatrix (A : G →₀ Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℂ)
    (hA : ∀ r, (A r)ᴴ = A (-r)) (χ : PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G)) :
    (blochMatrix A χ).IsHermitian

modules.title: The Koopman representation of a measure-preserving action
modules.doc:
An abelian group acting on a probability space by measure-preserving maps acts unitarily on `L²`.

## i. Overview

Let an abelian group `G` act on a measurable space `X` by bijections preserving a measure `μ`, for
example lattice translations acting on the configurations of a classical spin system with a
translation-invariant ensemble `μ`. Then `(U_g f)(x) = f(g⁻¹ x)` is a unitary representation of `G`
on `L²(μ)`: the Koopman representation. The spectral theorem for unitary representations applies:
every `f ∈ L²(μ)`, an observable of the classical system, has a spectral measure `ν_f` on the
characters of `G` with `∫ χ(g) dν_f(χ) = ⟨f, U_g f⟩ = ∫ f̄(x) f(g⁻¹ x) dμ(x)`, the Fourier transform
of its correlation function. This is the structure factor of a classical lattice system. The
spectral projection of the trivial character projects onto the translation-invariant functions.
Nothing about quantum mechanics enters: this is the same representation theory that governs
quantum systems.

## ii. Key results

- `UnitaryRep.koopman` : the Koopman representation on `L²(μ)`.
- `UnitaryRep.koopman_apply_ae` : it acts by composition with the inverse group action.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The Koopman operators
- B. The unitary representation
- C. Invariant functions

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.UnitaryRep.koopmanIsometry
declarations.doc: The composition operator `f ↦ f ∘ T_g⁻¹` on `L²(μ)` as a linear isometry.
declarations.statement: def koopmanIsometry (g : Γ) : Lp E 2 μ →ₗᵢ[ℂ] Lp E 2 μ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.UnitaryRep.compMeasurePreserving_congr
declarations.statement:
lemma compMeasurePreserving_congr {f f' : X → X} (hf : MeasurePreserving f μ μ)
    (hf' : MeasurePreserving f' μ μ) (e : f = f') (g : Lp E 2 μ) :
    Lp.compMeasurePreserving f hf g = Lp.compMeasurePreserving f' hf' g

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.UnitaryRep.koopmanIsometry_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma koopmanIsometry_apply (g : Γ) (f : Lp E 2 μ) :
    koopmanIsometry μ T hT g f = Lp.compMeasurePreserving (T g⁻¹) (hT g⁻¹) f

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.UnitaryRep.koopmanIsometry_mul
declarations.statement:
lemma koopmanIsometry_mul (g h : Γ) (f : Lp E 2 μ) :
    koopmanIsometry μ T hT (g * h) f = koopmanIsometry μ T hT g (koopmanIsometry μ T hT h f)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.UnitaryRep.koopmanIsometry_one
declarations.statement: lemma koopmanIsometry_one (f : Lp E 2 μ) : koopmanIsometry μ T hT 1 f = f

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.UnitaryRep.koopmanEquiv
declarations.doc: The Koopman operator as a linear isometric equivalence.
declarations.statement: def koopmanEquiv (g : Γ) : Lp E 2 μ ≃ₗᵢ[ℂ] Lp E 2 μ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.UnitaryRep.koopmanEquiv_one
declarations.statement: lemma koopmanEquiv_one : koopmanEquiv (E := E) μ T hT 1 = 1

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.UnitaryRep.koopmanEquiv_mul
declarations.statement:
lemma koopmanEquiv_mul (g h : Γ) :
    koopmanEquiv (E := E) μ T hT (g * h) =
      koopmanEquiv (E := E) μ T hT g * koopmanEquiv (E := E) μ T hT h

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.UnitaryRep.koopman
declarations.doc:
**The Koopman representation**: a group acting on a measure space by measure-preserving
bijections acts unitarily on `L²(μ)` by `(U_g f)(x) = f(g⁻¹ x)`.
declarations.statement: def koopman : Γ →* unitary (Lp E 2 μ →L[ℂ] Lp E 2 μ)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.UnitaryRep.koopman_apply
declarations.doc: The Koopman operator acts by composition with the inverse of the group action.
declarations.statement:
lemma koopman_apply (g : Γ) (f : Lp E 2 μ) :
    ((koopman μ T hT g : unitary (Lp E 2 μ →L[ℂ] Lp E 2 μ)) : Lp E 2 μ →L[ℂ] Lp E 2 μ) f =
      Lp.compMeasurePreserving (T g⁻¹) (hT g⁻¹) f

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.UnitaryRep.inner_koopman
declarations.doc:
**The correlation function of an observable**: the matrix coefficient of the Koopman
representation is the covariance `∫ ⟨f(x), f(g⁻¹ x)⟩ dμ(x)` of `f` with its translate.
declarations.statement:
lemma inner_koopman (g : Γ) (f : Lp E 2 μ) :
    ⟪f, ((koopman μ T hT g : unitary (Lp E 2 μ →L[ℂ] Lp E 2 μ)) : Lp E 2 μ →L[ℂ] Lp E 2 μ) f⟫_ℂ =
      ∫ x, ⟪f x, f (T g⁻¹ x)⟫_ℂ ∂μ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.UnitaryRep.range_projection_one_koopman
declarations.doc:
**Invariant observables of a classical system have zero momentum**: the spectral projection of
the trivial character of the Koopman representation projects onto the translation-invariant
functions in `L²(μ)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma range_projection_one_koopman :
    LinearMap.range (projection (koopman (E := E) μ T hT)
        {(1 : PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G))} : Lp E 2 μ →L[ℂ] Lp E 2 μ).toLinearMap =
      ProbabilisticTheory.Representation.sector (toEnd (koopman (E := E) μ T hT)) (fun _ =>
        (1 : ℂ))

modules.title: Crystal momentum sectors
modules.doc:
Sectors and fibers of definite crystal momentum for a translation-invariant system, and their
conservation.

## i. Overview

The translation symmetry of a crystal has a basic consequence: a time evolution, a
Hamiltonian, or a response function that commutes with lattice translations conserves crystal
momentum. Let translations `g` act linearly on a vector space `V`, the states or the observables of
the crystal, by `β g`, and let `χ g` be the phase picked up by a translation: for a lattice
translation `n` and wavevector `k`, `χ n = exp (i k n)`. Two spaces are attached to `χ`:

* the *sector of momentum `χ`*, the vectors with `β g v = χ g v` for all `g`: the Bloch waves;
* the *fiber at momentum `χ`*, `V` modulo the differences `β g v - χ g v`.

In an infinite crystal a configuration of finite extent contains no Bloch wave, so the sector can
be zero, whereas the fiber is the space of Fourier transforms evaluated at momentum `χ`. A linear
map that commutes with the translations, such as the Hamiltonian, preserves every sector and acts
on every fiber. Both statements are purely algebraic. No claim is made that the space decomposes
into a sum of momentum sectors; that needs analysis and is a separate matter.

## ii. Key results

- `sector` : the Bloch waves of crystal momentum `χ`.
- `Fiber` : the space of crystal momentum `χ`, a quotient of the whole space.
- `IsEquivariant` : a linear map commuting with the translations.
- `IsEquivariant.mapsTo_sector` : a translation-invariant map conserves crystal momentum.
- `IsEquivariant.fiberMap` : a translation-invariant map acts within each fiber.
- `fiberMap_id`, `fiberMap_comp` : the action on fibers respects composition.
- `sectorToFiber` : a Bloch wave defines a vector of the fiber of the same momentum.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Sectors and fibers
- B. Equivariant maps
- C. Functoriality
- D. From sectors to fibers

## iv. References

* N. Ashcroft & N. D. Mermin, Solid State Physics, Chapters 4 and 8.
* F. Bloch, Über die Quantenmechanik der Elektronen in Kristallgittern, Z. Phys. 52 (1929). [ref:
  bloch_1929]

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Representation.sector
declarations.doc: The momentum sector of the character `χ`: vectors on which `g` acts as the scalar `χ g`.
declarations.statement: def sector (β : G →* Module.End K V) (χ : G → K) : Submodule K V

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Representation.mem_sector
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_sector {β : G →* Module.End K V} {χ : G → K} {v : V} :
    v ∈ sector β χ ↔ ∀ g, β g v = χ g • v

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Representation.cobound
declarations.doc:
The submodule `span {β g v - χ g • v}` whose quotient is the momentum fiber. It is the
"coboundary" submodule of the twisted action.
declarations.statement: def cobound (β : G →* Module.End K V) (χ : G → K) : Submodule K V

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Representation.sub_smul_mem_cobound
declarations.statement:
lemma sub_smul_mem_cobound (β : G →* Module.End K V) (χ : G → K) (g : G) (v : V) :
    β g v - χ g • v ∈ cobound β χ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Representation.Fiber
declarations.doc: The momentum fiber of the character `χ`: `V` modulo the vectors `β g v - χ g • v`.
declarations.statement: abbrev Fiber (β : G →* Module.End K V) (χ : G → K) : Type _

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Representation.Fiber.mk
declarations.doc: The canonical projection `V → V(χ)`.
declarations.statement: def Fiber.mk (β : G →* Module.End K V) (χ : G → K) : V →ₗ[K] Fiber β χ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Representation.Fiber.mk_action
declarations.doc: In the fiber, `g` acts as the scalar `χ g`.
declarations.statement:
lemma Fiber.mk_action (β : G →* Module.End K V) (χ : G → K) (g : G) (v : V) :
    Fiber.mk β χ (β g v) = χ g • Fiber.mk β χ v

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Representation.IsEquivariant
declarations.doc: A linear map intertwining two actions of the same monoid.
declarations.statement:
def IsEquivariant (β : G →* Module.End K V) (β' : G →* Module.End K W)
    (T : V →ₗ[K] W) : Prop

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Representation.IsEquivariant.mapsTo_sector
declarations.doc: Every equivariant linear map preserves each momentum sector.
declarations.statement:
lemma IsEquivariant.mapsTo_sector (hT : IsEquivariant β β' T) {v : V}
    (hv : v ∈ sector β χ) : T v ∈ sector β' χ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Representation.IsEquivariant.sectorMap
declarations.doc: The restriction of an equivariant map to a momentum sector.
declarations.statement:
def IsEquivariant.sectorMap (hT : IsEquivariant β β' T) (χ : G → K) :
    sector β χ →ₗ[K] sector β' χ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Representation.IsEquivariant.coe_sectorMap
declarations.statement:
lemma IsEquivariant.coe_sectorMap (hT : IsEquivariant β β' T) (v : sector β χ) :
    (hT.sectorMap χ v : W) = T v

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Representation.IsEquivariant.cobound_le_comap
declarations.doc:
An equivariant map sends the span defining the fiber of `V` into the span defining the fiber
of `W`.
declarations.statement:
lemma IsEquivariant.cobound_le_comap (hT : IsEquivariant β β' T) (χ : G → K) :
    cobound β χ ≤ (cobound β' χ).comap T

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Representation.IsEquivariant.fiberMap
declarations.doc: Every equivariant linear map induces a well-defined linear map on each momentum fiber.
declarations.statement:
def IsEquivariant.fiberMap (hT : IsEquivariant β β' T) (χ : G → K) :
    Fiber β χ →ₗ[K] Fiber β' χ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Representation.IsEquivariant.fiberMap_mk
declarations.statement:
lemma IsEquivariant.fiberMap_mk (hT : IsEquivariant β β' T) (χ : G → K) (v : V) :
    hT.fiberMap χ (Fiber.mk β χ v) = Fiber.mk β' χ (T v)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Representation.IsEquivariant.fiberMap_comp_mk
declarations.doc: The fiber map is the unique map making the square with the projections commute.
declarations.statement:
lemma IsEquivariant.fiberMap_comp_mk (hT : IsEquivariant β β' T) (χ : G → K) :
    (hT.fiberMap χ).comp (Fiber.mk β χ) = (Fiber.mk β' χ).comp T

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Representation.isEquivariant_id
declarations.statement: lemma isEquivariant_id (β : G →* Module.End K V) : IsEquivariant β β LinearMap.id

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Representation.IsEquivariant.comp
declarations.statement:
lemma IsEquivariant.comp (hS : IsEquivariant β' β'' S) (hT : IsEquivariant β β' T) :
    IsEquivariant β β'' (S ∘ₗ T)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Representation.fiberMap_id
declarations.statement:
lemma fiberMap_id (χ : G → K) :
    (isEquivariant_id β).fiberMap χ = LinearMap.id

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Representation.IsEquivariant.fiberMap_comp
declarations.statement:
lemma IsEquivariant.fiberMap_comp (hS : IsEquivariant β' β'' S) (hT : IsEquivariant β β' T)
    (χ : G → K) :
    (hS.comp hT).fiberMap χ = (hS.fiberMap χ) ∘ₗ (hT.fiberMap χ)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Representation.IsEquivariant.mapsTo_sector_self
declarations.doc:
Equivariant maps commute with the dynamics they generate: if `D` is an equivariant
endomorphism, it preserves every sector and descends to every fiber. This is the form used for
translation-invariant evolution.
declarations.statement:
lemma IsEquivariant.mapsTo_sector_self {D : V →ₗ[K] V} (hD : IsEquivariant β β D) {v : V}
    (hv : v ∈ sector β χ) : D v ∈ sector β χ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Representation.sectorToFiber
declarations.doc: The canonical map from the sector of `χ` to the fiber of `χ`.
declarations.statement:
def sectorToFiber (β : G →* Module.End K V) (χ : G → K) :
    sector β χ →ₗ[K] Fiber β χ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Representation.IsEquivariant.fiberMap_comp_sectorToFiber
declarations.doc: The canonical map from sector to fiber is natural for equivariant maps.
declarations.statement:
lemma IsEquivariant.fiberMap_comp_sectorToFiber (hT : IsEquivariant β β' T) (χ : G → K) :
    (hT.fiberMap χ).comp (sectorToFiber β χ)
      = (sectorToFiber β' χ).comp (hT.sectorMap χ)

modules.title: Orthogonality of characters
modules.doc:
Characters separate the points of a discrete abelian group, and the normalized Haar measure of the
dual group makes the characters orthogonal.

## i. Overview

For a discrete abelian group `G` and `g ≠ 0` there is a unitary character `χ` of `G` with
`χ(g) ≠ 1`. This comes from the injectivity of the circle: a character into `ℚ/ℤ` separating `g`
from `0`, composed with the injection `ℚ/ℤ → S¹`, `q ↦ e^{2πi q}`. The Pontryagin dual `Ĝ` is a
compact abelian group, so it carries a Haar probability measure `μ`. The evaluation `χ ↦ χ(g)` is a
nontrivial character of `Ĝ` for `g ≠ 0`, so by translation invariance
`∫ χ(g) dμ(χ) = 0`, and `= 1` for `g = 0`: the characters are orthonormal.

## ii. Key results

- `exists_character_apply_ne_one` : characters separate points.
- `dualHaar` : the Haar probability measure of the dual group.
- `integral_character_dualHaar` : `∫ χ(g) dμ(χ) = 1` for `g = 0` and `0` otherwise.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Characters separate points
- B. The Haar measure of the dual group

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## B. The Haar measure of the dual group

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.rationalCircle
declarations.doc: The injection of `ℚ/ℤ` into the circle, `q ↦ e^{2πi q}`.
declarations.statement: def rationalCircle : AddCircle (1 : ℚ) →+ Additive Circle

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.rationalCircle_eq_zero
declarations.statement: lemma rationalCircle_eq_zero {x : AddCircle (1 : ℚ)} (h : rationalCircle x = 0) : x = 0

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.exists_character_apply_ne_one
declarations.doc: **Characters separate the points of a discrete abelian group.**
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_character_apply_ne_one [TopologicalSpace G] [DiscreteTopology G] {g : G}
    (hg : g ≠ 0) : ∃ χ : PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G), χ (Multiplicative.ofAdd g) ≠ 1

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.dualHaar
declarations.doc: The normalized Haar measure of the compact dual group.
declarations.statement: def dualHaar : Measure (PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G))
instance : (dualHaar (G := G)).IsHaarMeasure
instance : IsProbabilityMeasure (dualHaar (G := G))

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.integral_character_dualHaar
declarations.doc:
**Orthogonality of characters**: the evaluation characters are orthonormal for the Haar
probability measure of the dual group.
declarations.statement:
lemma integral_character_dualHaar (g : G) :
    ∫ χ, ((χ (Multiplicative.ofAdd g) : Circle) : ℂ) ∂(dualHaar (G := G)) =
      if g = 0 then 1 else 0

modules.title: Covariance of the spectral measure under a finite group of symmetries
modules.doc:
A group acting on the translation group acts on its characters, and the spectral measure of a
covariant representation is covariant.

## i. Overview

Let a discrete abelian group `G` of translations be represented unitarily by `π`, and let a group
`P` act on `G` by automorphisms `φ p`. The group `P` acts on the characters of `G` by
`(p • χ)(g) = χ(φ(p⁻¹) g)`. A unitary representation `ρ` of `P` on the same space is *covariant*
when `ρ(p) π(g) ρ(p)⁻¹ = π(φ(p) g)`. Together `π` and `ρ` represent the semidirect product
`G ⋊ P`: for a crystal, `G` is the group of lattice translations and `P` its point group.

The spectral measure of a vector `ξ`, the distribution of `ξ` over the characters, is determined
by its Fourier transform `g ↦ ⟨ξ, π(g) ξ⟩`. Since the transform of `ρ(p) ξ` is that of `ξ`
composed with `φ(p⁻¹)`, the spectral measure of `ρ(p) ξ` is the pushforward of that of `ξ` under
the action of `p` on the characters. Consequently the spectral projection of the image of a set of
characters is carried to the image of the projection by `ρ(p)`:
`ρ(p) P(S) = P(p • S) ρ(p)`. The unitary `ρ(p)` carries the sector of total momenta in `S` onto the
sector of total momenta in `p • S`.

## ii. Key results

- `UnitaryRep.dualAct` : the action of a group of automorphisms on the characters.
- `UnitaryRep.vectorMeasure_rho` : the spectral measure of `ρ(p) ξ` is the pushforward of that of
  `ξ`.
- `UnitaryRep.rho_mul_projection` : `ρ(p) P(S) = P(p • S) ρ(p)`.

## iii. Table of contents

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.UnitaryRep.rho_mul_projection
declarations.doc:
**The spectral projections are covariant**: `ρ(p) P(S) = P(p • S) ρ(p)` for every measurable
set `S` of characters. The unitary `ρ(p)` carries the sector of momenta in `S` onto the sector of
momenta in `p • S`.
declarations.statement:
lemma rho_mul_projection (hcov : IsCovariantRep φ π ρ) (p : P)
    {S : Set (PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G))} (hS : MeasurableSet S) :
    ((ρ p : unitary (H →L[ℂ] H)) : H →L[ℂ] H) * projection π S =
      projection π (dualAct φ p '' S) * ((ρ p : unitary (H →L[ℂ] H)) : H →L[ℂ] H)

modules.title: POVMs and PVMs
modules.doc:
POVMs as effect-valued measures, and PVMs as POVMs whose values are sharp effects.

## i. Overview

For the self-adjoint part of an operator algebra, an effect-valued measure is a POVM. A PVM is a
POVM whose values are sharp effects. A POVM whose values are projections is a PVM.

## ii. Key results

- `POVM` : positive-operator-valued measures.
- `POVM.IsPVM`, `PVM` : projection-valued measures.
- `POVM.isPVM_of_forall_isIdempotentElem` : a POVM of projections is a PVM.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. POVMs
- B. POVMs of projections
- C. PVMs

## iv. References

* None.

modules.title: Schur's lemma for covariant channels
modules.doc:
Schur's lemma as a hypothesis: equivariant maps and covariant channels are scalar on blocks.

## i. Overview

If the observables split into invariant blocks `E = ⨁ᵢ Wᵢ` on each of which every equivariant map
acts as a scalar, then every equivariant map preserving the blocks is determined by one real number
per block. For the qubit, the Hermitian `2 × 2` matrices split into the scalars and the Pauli
vectors, so a rotation-covariant channel is determined by one number.

Mathlib's Schur lemma needs an algebraically closed field, while the observables are a real space.
The Schur property of a block is therefore a hypothesis, `IsSchurBlock`.

## ii. Key results

- `IsSchurBlock` : every equivariant map preserving the block acts on it as a scalar.
- `exists_scalar_of_isSchurBlock` : an equivariant map is a scalar on each block.
- `UnitalPositiveLinearMap.IsCovariant.exists_scalar_of_isSchurBlock` : the same for covariant
  channels.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The Schur hypothesis on a single block
- B. The multiplicity-free classification theorem
- C. Covariant channels

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. The Schur hypothesis on a single block

## C. Covariant channels

A channel intertwining a symmetry action with itself is a `G`-equivariant endomorphism.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.IsSchurBlock
declarations.doc:
The **Schur hypothesis** for a submodule `W`, relative to an action `smul : G → E → E`: every
linear endomorphism of `E` that is `G`-equivariant on `W` (`f (smul g x) = smul g (f x)` for
`x ∈ W`) and maps `W` into itself acts on all of `W` as a single scalar `c`. This is the abstract
shape of "every `G`-equivariant self-map of an irreducible real representation is a scalar" — taken
here as a hypothesis to be supplied per block (cited or proved separately), not derived from a
general representation-theoretic classification (see the file docstring).
declarations.statement: def IsSchurBlock (smul : G → E → E) (W : Submodule ℝ E) : Prop

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.exists_scalar_of_isSchurBlock
declarations.doc:
**Equivariant maps are scalars on Schur blocks.** If `E = ⨁ᵢ Wᵢ` with invariant Schur blocks
`Wᵢ`, every equivariant linear map preserving the blocks acts on each `Wᵢ` as a real scalar.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_scalar_of_isSchurBlock (smul : G → E → E) (W : ι → Submodule ℝ E)
    (_hsum : DirectSum.IsInternal W) (_hW_inv : ∀ i g, ∀ x ∈ W i, smul g x ∈ W i)
    (hSchur : ∀ i, IsSchurBlock smul (W i)) (f : E →ₗ[ℝ] E)
    (hf_equiv : ∀ g x, f (smul g x) = smul g (f x)) (hf_block : ∀ i, ∀ x ∈ W i, f x ∈ W i) :
    ∃ c : ι → ℝ, ∀ i, ∀ x ∈ W i, f x = c i • x

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.UnitalPositiveLinearMap.IsCovariant.exists_scalar_of_isSchurBlock
declarations.doc:
**Schur's lemma for covariant channels.** A channel covariant for a symmetry action `ρ` acts as
a real scalar on each block of a finite decomposition of `E` into invariant Schur blocks that it
preserves.
declarations.statement:
lemma UnitalPositiveLinearMap.IsCovariant.exists_scalar_of_isSchurBlock
    {ρ : G →* Symmetry E} {φ : Channel E E} (hφ : φ.IsCovariant ρ ρ) (W : ι → Submodule ℝ E)
    (hsum : DirectSum.IsInternal W)
    (hW_inv : ∀ i g, ∀ x ∈ W i, (ρ g).1 x ∈ W i)
    (hSchur : ∀ i, IsSchurBlock (fun g x => (ρ g).1 x) (W i))
    (hφ_block : ∀ i, ∀ x ∈ W i, φ x ∈ W i) :
    ∃ c : ι → ℝ, ∀ i, ∀ x ∈ W i, φ x = c i • x

modules.title: Symmetry reduction of translation-invariant operators to momentum sectors
modules.doc:
A bounded operator commuting with the translations and a covariant point group is reduced by the
momentum sectors, and the symmetry relates its restrictions to sectors in one orbit.

## i. Overview

Let `π` represent the translations `G` and `ρ` a covariant representation of a group `P` acting on
`G`, so that together they represent `G ⋊ P`. The *sector* of a set `S` of characters is the range
of the spectral projection `P(S)` of `π`: the vectors whose total momentum lies in `S`. A bounded
operator `T` commuting with all `π(g)` commutes with every `P(S)`, and so restricts to each
sector. If `T` also commutes with `ρ`, then `ρ(p)` restricts to a unitary equivalence of the
sector of `S` and the sector of `p • S` which intertwines the restrictions of `T`. In particular
the spectrum of `T` on the sector of `S` is the spectrum of `T` on the sector of `p • S`.

For a single momentum, this says that the fibre Hamiltonians at momenta related by the point group
are unitarily equivalent, so the spectrum is determined by the momenta in an irreducible zone. The
statement makes no assumption on the nature of `T`: it applies to one particle, to many particles,
to spins, to anything with a unitary representation of the symmetry group. For a self-adjoint
generator `H` of an unbounded dynamics, `T` is the unitary group `e^{itH}`.

## ii. Key results

- `UnitaryRep.sector` : the range of a spectral projection.
- `UnitaryRep.sectorEquiv` : the isometric equivalence of the sectors of `S` and `p • S`.
- `UnitaryRep.spectrum_sectorOp_eq` : the spectra of an invariant operator on the two sectors
  agree.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Sectors
- B. The equivalence of sectors
- C. Invariant operators

## iv. References

* None.
