modules.title: The structure factor of an invariant state
modules.doc:
The correlation function of a translation-invariant positive functional is the Fourier transform of
a positive measure on the momenta.

## i. Overview

Let `B` be a ⋆-algebra of observables on which a discrete abelian group `G` of translations acts by
⋆-automorphisms `α_g`, and let `ω` be a positive linear functional with `ω ∘ α_g = ω`. For an
observable `a` the correlation function `g ↦ ω(a⋆ α_g(a))` is positive definite on `G`: for any
finite family of translations `g_i` and scalars `c_i` it is the value of `ω` at `b⋆ b` with
`b = ∑ c_i α_{g_i}(a)`. By Bochner's theorem for discrete abelian groups it is the Fourier
transform of a unique finite positive measure `μ_a` on the Pontryagin dual of `G`, the group of
momenta. This measure is the structure factor of `a`: its total mass is `ω(a⋆ a)`, and
`∫ χ(g) dμ_a(χ) = ω(a⋆ α_g(a))`. No Hilbert space, representation of the algebra or Hamiltonian is
needed, and the algebra need not be a C⋆-algebra.

## ii. Key results

- `StructureFactor.isPositiveDefiniteSub_correlation` : the correlation function is positive
  definite.
- `StructureFactor.exists_measure` : the structure factor exists.
- `StructureFactor.measure_univ` : its total mass is `ω(a⋆ a)`.
- `StructureFactor.eq_of_transform_eq` : for a countable group it is unique.
- `StructureFactor.isPositiveDefiniteSub_iff_exists_measure` : positive semidefinite
  translation-invariant couplings are Fourier transforms of positive measures.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Positive definiteness of the correlation function
- B. The structure factor

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. Positive definiteness of the correlation function

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.StructureFactor.correlation
declarations.doc: The correlation function `g ↦ ω(a⋆ α_g(a))` of an observable `a`.
declarations.statement: def correlation (a : B) (g : G) : ℂ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.StructureFactor.isPositiveDefiniteSub_correlation
declarations.doc: **The correlation function of an invariant positive functional is positive definite.**
declarations.statement:
lemma isPositiveDefiniteSub_correlation (hpos : ∀ b : B, 0 ≤ ω (star b * b))
    (hinv : ∀ g b, ω (α g b) = ω b) (a : B) :
    TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub (correlation ω α a)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.StructureFactor.exists_measure
declarations.doc:
**The structure factor exists.** The correlation function of an observable in an invariant
positive functional is the Fourier transform of a finite positive measure on the momenta:
`ω(a⋆ α_g(a)) = ∫ χ(g) dμ_a(χ)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_measure (hpos : ∀ b : B, 0 ≤ ω (star b * b)) (hinv : ∀ g b, ω (α g b) = ω b)
    (a : B) :
    ∃ μ : Measure (PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G)), IsFiniteMeasure μ ∧ μ.InnerRegular ∧
      ∀ g : G, ∫ χ, ((χ (Multiplicative.ofAdd g) : Circle) : ℂ) ∂μ = correlation ω α a g

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.StructureFactor.integral_one_eq
declarations.doc: The total mass of the structure factor is the expectation of `a⋆ a`.
declarations.statement:
lemma integral_one_eq {μ : Measure (PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G))}
    (a : B) (h : ∀ g : G, ∫ χ, ((χ (Multiplicative.ofAdd g) : Circle) : ℂ) ∂μ =
      correlation ω α a g) :
    (μ.real univ : ℂ) = ω (star a * a)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.StructureFactor.eq_of_transform_eq
declarations.doc:
**The structure factor is unique.** For a countable group a finite measure on the momenta is
determined by its Fourier transform.
declarations.statement:
lemma eq_of_transform_eq {μ ν : Measure (PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G))}
    [IsFiniteMeasure μ] [IsFiniteMeasure ν]
    (h : ∀ g : G, ∫ χ, ((χ (Multiplicative.ofAdd g) : Circle) : ℂ) ∂μ =
      ∫ χ, ((χ (Multiplicative.ofAdd g) : Circle) : ℂ) ∂ν) : μ = ν

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.StructureFactor.isPositiveDefiniteSub_iff_exists_measure
declarations.doc:
**Positive semidefinite translation-invariant couplings are Fourier transforms of positive
measures.** A coupling `J(r)` depending only on the displacement `r` is positive semidefinite, in
the sense that every finite quadratic form `∑ c_i c̄_j J(r_i - r_j)` is nonnegative, if and only if
it is the Fourier transform of a finite positive measure on the momenta, whose density is the
dispersion of the coupling.
declarations.statement:
lemma isPositiveDefiniteSub_iff_exists_measure (J : G → ℂ) :
    TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteSub J ↔
      ∃ μ : Measure (PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G)), IsFiniteMeasure μ ∧ μ.InnerRegular ∧
        ∀ r : G, J r = ∫ χ, ((χ (Multiplicative.ofAdd r) : Circle) : ℂ) ∂μ

modules.title: The spectral measure of a vector
modules.doc:
The distribution of a vector over the characters of the group, and its uniqueness.

## i. Overview

For a unitary representation `π` of an abelian group and a vector `ξ`, the diagonal measure
`S ↦ ‖P(S) ξ‖²` of the spectral measure is a finite measure `μ_ξ` on the Pontryagin dual with
`⟪ξ, π(g) ξ⟫ = ∫ χ(g) dμ_ξ(χ)`. It is the distribution of `ξ` over the characters of the group;
for a state it is the momentum distribution. Its total mass is `‖ξ‖²`. For a countable group, a
finite measure on the dual is determined by its Fourier–Stieltjes transform, so `μ_ξ` is the
unique measure with this property.

## ii. Key results

- `UnitaryRep.vectorMeasure` : the spectral measure `μ_ξ` of a vector.
- `UnitaryRep.inner_eq_integral_vectorMeasure` : `⟪ξ, π(g) ξ⟫ = ∫ χ(g) dμ_ξ(χ)`.
- `UnitaryRep.vectorMeasure_univ` : the total mass of `μ_ξ` is `‖ξ‖²`.
- `UnitaryRep.eq_vectorMeasure_of_transform_eq` : uniqueness of the spectral measure of a vector.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The spectral measure of a vector
- B. Uniqueness

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.UnitaryRep.vectorMeasure
declarations.doc:
The spectral measure `S ↦ ‖P(S) ξ‖²` of a vector `ξ`, a finite measure on the Pontryagin dual:
the distribution of `ξ` over the characters of the group.
declarations.statement: def vectorMeasure (ξ : H) : Measure (PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G))
instance (ξ : H) : IsFiniteMeasure (vectorMeasure π ξ)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.UnitaryRep.vectorMeasure_apply
ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.UnitaryRep.vectorMeasure_univ
declarations.doc: The total mass of the spectral measure of a vector is its squared norm.
declarations.statement: lemma vectorMeasure_univ (ξ : H) : vectorMeasure π ξ univ = ENNReal.ofReal (‖ξ‖ ^ 2)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.UnitaryRep.vectorMeasure_eq_map
declarations.doc: The vector measure is the pushforward of the Riesz measure of the vector state.
declarations.statement:
lemma vectorMeasure_eq_map (ξ : H) :
    vectorMeasure π ξ = Measure.map (dual π) (starHomScalarMeasure (family π).starHom ξ)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.UnitaryRep.inner_eq_integral_vectorMeasure
declarations.doc:
**The spectral measure of a vector represents its matrix coefficients**:
`⟪ξ, π(g) ξ⟫ = ∫ χ(g) dμ_ξ(χ)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma inner_eq_integral_vectorMeasure (ξ : H) (g : Multiplicative G) :
    ⟪ξ, ((π g : unitary (H →L[ℂ] H)) : H →L[ℂ] H) ξ⟫_ℂ =
      ∫ χ, ((χ g : Circle) : ℂ) ∂vectorMeasure π ξ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.QuantumMechanics.UnitaryRep.eq_vectorMeasure_of_transform_eq
declarations.doc:
**Uniqueness of the spectral measure of a vector.** For a countable group, a finite measure on
the Pontryagin dual whose Fourier–Stieltjes transform is `g ↦ ⟪ξ, π(g) ξ⟫` is the spectral
measure of `ξ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma eq_vectorMeasure_of_transform_eq (ξ : H) (μ : Measure (PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G)))
    [IsFiniteMeasure μ]
    (h : ∀ g : Multiplicative G, ∫ χ, ((χ g : Circle) : ℂ) ∂μ =
      ⟪ξ, ((π g : unitary (H →L[ℂ] H)) : H →L[ℂ] H) ξ⟫_ℂ) :
    μ = vectorMeasure π ξ

modules.title: Expectation values of non-self-adjoint operators
modules.doc:
A state is defined on the self-adjoint observables, and extends uniquely to a complex-linear
functional on all operators.

## i. Overview

A state assigns an expectation value to every observable, a self-adjoint operator. Correlation
functions such as `⟨A B(t)⟩` involve products of observables, which are not self-adjoint, and so
need the expectation value of an arbitrary operator `a`. Every operator is uniquely a combination
`a = ℜ a + i ℑ a` of two self-adjoint operators, its real and imaginary parts, and the expectation
value is extended by linearity: `⟨a⟩ = ⟨ℜ a⟩ + i ⟨ℑ a⟩`. This is the unique complex-linear extension
of the state that is compatible with taking adjoints, `⟨a*⟩ = conj ⟨a⟩`.

## ii. Key results

- `complexExtension` : the complex-linear functional extending an expectation value.
- `complexExtension_coe` : on self-adjoint operators it is the original expectation value.
- `complexExtension_star` : the expectation value of the adjoint is the complex conjugate.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The extension
- B. Properties
- C. Compatibility with `*`-linear maps

## iv. References

* O. Bratteli & D. Robinson, Operator Algebras and Quantum Statistical Mechanics 1, 2nd ed.,
  Chapter 2.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.complexExtension
declarations.doc:
The complex-linear extension of an expectation value on self-adjoint operators to all
operators: `⟨a⟩ = ⟨ℜ a⟩ + i ⟨ℑ a⟩`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def complexExtension (φ : selfAdjoint A →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ) : A →ₗ[ℂ] ℂ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.complexExtension_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma complexExtension_apply (φ : selfAdjoint A →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ) (a : A) :
    complexExtension φ a = φ (ℜ a) + Complex.I * φ (ℑ a)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.complexExtension_coe
declarations.doc: On self-adjoint operators the extension is the original expectation value.
declarations.statement:
lemma complexExtension_coe (φ : selfAdjoint A →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ) (a : selfAdjoint A) :
    complexExtension φ (a : A) = φ a

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.complexExtension_star
declarations.doc: The expectation value of the adjoint is the complex conjugate of the expectation value.
declarations.statement:
lemma complexExtension_star (φ : selfAdjoint A →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ) (a : A) :
    complexExtension φ (star a) = starRingEnd ℂ (complexExtension φ a)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.realPart_linearMap
declarations.doc:
A complex-linear map commuting with the adjoint maps the real part of an operator to the real
part of its image.
declarations.statement:
lemma realPart_linearMap (f : C →ₗ[ℂ] D) (hf : ∀ a, f (star a) = star (f a)) (a : C) :
    ((ℜ (f a) : selfAdjoint D) : D) = f (ℜ a : C)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.imaginaryPart_linearMap
declarations.doc:
A complex-linear map commuting with the adjoint maps the imaginary part of an operator to the
imaginary part of its image.
declarations.statement:
lemma imaginaryPart_linearMap (f : C →ₗ[ℂ] D) (hf : ∀ a, f (star a) = star (f a)) (a : C) :
    ((ℑ (f a) : selfAdjoint D) : D) = f (ℑ a : C)

modules.title: The covariance form of a state and its symmetries
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

A state `ω` on a unital `*`-algebra `A` has the covariance form
`C(a, b) = ω(a⋆ b) - conj (ω a) ω(b)`, the inner product of the fluctuations `a - ω(a)` and
`b - ω(b)` in the pre-Hilbert space of the state. It is antilinear in `a` and linear in `b`. For
observables, `C(a, b) = Cov(a, b) + i ω⟨⁅a, b⁆⟩`, so `C` contains both matrices `Σ` and `Ω` of
Robertson's relation.

If `ω` is invariant under a `⋆`-automorphism `σ`, then `C(σ a, σ b) = C(a, b)`. If `σ` acts on
two finite families of elements by the matrices `R` and `S`, the matrix of covariances `M`
satisfies `Rᴴ M S = M`. When `R` is unitary this says `M S = R M`, so `M` is an intertwining map,
and by Schur's lemma it vanishes when a group acts on the two families by inequivalent
irreducible representations. For one-dimensional representations this says that elements
transforming with different characters have covariance zero. With `ℤ/2` it gives the vanishing of
the covariance between an even and an odd element; with translations it gives the vanishing of
the covariance between different crystal momenta.

## ii. Key results

- `AlgState.covarianceForm` : the covariance form `C(a, b) = ω(a⋆ b) - conj (ω a) ω(b)`.
- `AlgState.covarianceForm_selfAdjoint` : `C(a, b) = Cov(a, b) + i ω⟨⁅a, b⁆⟩` for observables.
- `AlgState.covarianceForm_map` : a symmetry of the state preserves `C`.
- `AlgState.posSemidef_covarianceMatrixForm` : the matrix of `C` on a family is positive
  semidefinite.
- `AlgState.conjTranspose_mul_covarianceMatrixForm_mul` : `Rᴴ M S = M`.
- `AlgState.covarianceForm_eq_zero_of_character` : elements transforming with different
  unitary characters have covariance zero.
- `AlgState.covarianceMatrixForm_eq_zero_of_irreducible` : **Schur's lemma** for covariances,
  families transforming under inequivalent irreducible unitary representations have covariance
  zero.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The covariance form
- B. Symmetries
- C. Matrices of covariances
- D. Schur's lemma

## iv. References

* E. Wigner, Group Theory and its Application to the Quantum Mechanics of Atomic Spectra,
  Chapter 21.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AlgState.fluctuationMap
declarations.doc: The fluctuation `a - ω(a)` of an element, as a linear map.
declarations.statement: def fluctuationMap : A →ₗ[ℂ] A

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AlgState.fluctuationMap_apply
declarations.statement: lemma fluctuationMap_apply (a : A) : ω.fluctuationMap a = a - ω a • 1

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AlgState.covarianceForm
declarations.doc:
The covariance form `C(a, b) = ω(a⋆ b) - conj (ω a) ω(b)`, the inner product of the
fluctuations in the pre-Hilbert space of the state.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def covarianceForm (a b : A) : ℂ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AlgState.covarianceForm_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma covarianceForm_apply (a b : A) :
    ω.covarianceForm a b = ω (star a * b) - star (ω a) * ω b

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AlgState.covarianceForm_smul_left
declarations.statement:
lemma covarianceForm_smul_left (c : ℂ) (a b : A) :
    ω.covarianceForm (c • a) b = star c * ω.covarianceForm a b

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AlgState.covarianceForm_smul_right
declarations.statement:
lemma covarianceForm_smul_right (c : ℂ) (a b : A) :
    ω.covarianceForm a (c • b) = c * ω.covarianceForm a b

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AlgState.covarianceForm_sum_left
declarations.statement:
lemma covarianceForm_sum_left {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι) (a : ι → A) (b : A) :
    ω.covarianceForm (∑ i ∈ s, a i) b = ∑ i ∈ s, ω.covarianceForm (a i) b

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AlgState.covarianceForm_sum_right
declarations.statement:
lemma covarianceForm_sum_right {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι) (a : A) (b : ι → A) :
    ω.covarianceForm a (∑ i ∈ s, b i) = ∑ i ∈ s, ω.covarianceForm a (b i)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AlgState.covarianceForm_selfAdjoint
declarations.doc: For observables, `C(a, b) = Cov(a, b) + i ω⟨⁅a, b⁆⟩`.
declarations.statement:
lemma covarianceForm_selfAdjoint (a b : selfAdjoint A) :
    ω.covarianceForm a b = ω.covariance a b + Complex.I * ω.bracket a b

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AlgState.covarianceForm_map
declarations.doc: **A symmetry of the state preserves the covariance form**: `C(σ a, σ b) = C(a, b)`.
declarations.statement: lemma covarianceForm_map (a b : A) : ω.covarianceForm (σ a) (σ b) = ω.covarianceForm a b

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AlgState.covarianceForm_eq_zero_of_smul
declarations.doc:
Elements multiplied by `χ` and `χ'` under a symmetry, with `conj χ · χ' ≠ 1`, have
covariance zero.
declarations.statement:
lemma covarianceForm_eq_zero_of_smul {a b : A} {χ χ' : ℂ} (ha : σ a = χ • a) (hb : σ b = χ' • b)
    (h : star χ * χ' ≠ 1) : ω.covarianceForm a b = 0

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AlgState.covarianceForm_eq_zero_of_neg
declarations.doc: **An even and an odd element have covariance zero.**
declarations.statement:
lemma covarianceForm_eq_zero_of_neg {a b : A} (ha : σ a = a) (hb : σ b = -b) :
    ω.covarianceForm a b = 0

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AlgState.covarianceForm_eq_zero_of_character
declarations.doc:
**Elements transforming with different unitary characters have covariance zero.** If
`α g a = χ g • a` and `α g b = χ' g • b` with `|χ g| = 1` and `χ ≠ χ'`, then `C(a, b) = 0`.
declarations.statement:
lemma covarianceForm_eq_zero_of_character {a b : A} {χ χ' : Γ → ℂ} (hχ : ∀ g, ‖χ g‖ = 1)
    (ha : ∀ g, α g a = χ g • a) (hb : ∀ g, α g b = χ' g • b) (hne : χ ≠ χ') :
    ω.covarianceForm a b = 0

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AlgState.covarianceMatrixForm
declarations.doc: The matrix `M_ik = C(a_i, b_k)` of covariances of two families.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def covarianceMatrixForm (a : ι → A) (b : κ → A) : Matrix ι κ ℂ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AlgState.posSemidef_covarianceMatrixForm
declarations.doc: **The matrix of covariances of a family is positive semidefinite**, being a Gram matrix.
declarations.statement: lemma posSemidef_covarianceMatrixForm (a : ι → A) : (ω.covarianceMatrixForm a a).PosSemidef

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AlgState.conjTranspose_mul_covarianceMatrixForm_mul
declarations.doc:
**A symmetry of the state preserves the matrix of covariances**: if `σ` acts on the two
families by the matrices `R` and `S`, then `Rᴴ M S = M`.
declarations.statement:
lemma conjTranspose_mul_covarianceMatrixForm_mul (σ : A ≃⋆ₐ[ℂ] A) (hω : ∀ x, ω (σ x) = ω x)
    {a : ι → A} {b : κ → A} {R : Matrix ι ι ℂ} {S : Matrix κ κ ℂ}
    (ha : ∀ i, σ (a i) = ∑ j, R j i • a j) (hb : ∀ k, σ (b k) = ∑ l, S l k • b l) :
    Rᴴ * ω.covarianceMatrixForm a b * S = ω.covarianceMatrixForm a b

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AlgState.covarianceMatrixForm_isIntertwining
declarations.doc:
If `α` acts on the families `a` and `b` by `ρ` and `π`, with `ρ` unitary, then the matrix of
covariances intertwines `π` with `ρ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma covarianceMatrixForm_isIntertwining {a : ι → A} {b : κ → A}
    (hρ : ∀ g, LinearMap.toMatrix' (ρ g) ∈ unitaryGroup ι ℂ)
    (ha : ∀ g i, α g (a i) = ∑ j, LinearMap.toMatrix' (ρ g) j i • a j)
    (hb : ∀ g k, α g (b k) = ∑ l, LinearMap.toMatrix' (π g) l k • b l) (g : Γ) :
    toLin' (ω.covarianceMatrixForm a b) ∘ₗ π g =
      ρ g ∘ₗ toLin' (ω.covarianceMatrixForm a b)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AlgState.covarianceMatrixForm_eq_zero_of_irreducible
declarations.doc:
**Schur's lemma for covariances.** If a group of symmetries of the state acts on the family
`a` by the irreducible unitary representation `ρ` and on the family `b` by the irreducible
representation `π`, and `π` and `ρ` are not equivalent, then `C(a_i, b_k) = 0` for all `i, k`.
declarations.statement:
lemma covarianceMatrixForm_eq_zero_of_irreducible [ρ.IsIrreducible] [π.IsIrreducible]
    [IsEmpty (π.Equiv ρ)] {a : ι → A} {b : κ → A}
    (hρ : ∀ g, LinearMap.toMatrix' (ρ g) ∈ unitaryGroup ι ℂ)
    (ha : ∀ g i, α g (a i) = ∑ j, LinearMap.toMatrix' (ρ g) j i • a j)
    (hb : ∀ g k, α g (b k) = ∑ l, LinearMap.toMatrix' (π g) l k • b l) :
    ω.covarianceMatrixForm a b = 0

modules.title: Covariances do not decrease under unital maps
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

Let `Φ : A → B` be a linear map of unital `*`-algebras, `ω` a state on `B` and `ω'` the state
`ω ∘ Φ` on `A`. The map `Φ` moves observables (Heisenberg picture), and `ω'` is the state `ω`
after the dual map. We compare the covariance forms `C` of the two states.

* **Schwarz maps.** If `Φ(X)⋆ Φ(X) ≤ Φ(X⋆ X)`, the Kadison–Schwarz inequality, which holds for
  completely positive unital maps, then `C_ω(Φ X, Φ X) ≤ C_ω'(X, X)`: the difference is
  `ω(Φ(X⋆ X) - Φ(X)⋆ Φ(X))`. Taking `X = ∑ cⱼ Xⱼ`, the same holds for the quadratic form of the
  matrix of covariances of a family at every complex `c`, so commutator part included.
* **Positive maps of matrices.** Kadison's inequality `Φ(A)² ≤ Φ(A²)` for Hermitian `A` gives
  the same bound for Hermitian matrices, and for the matrix of covariances of Hermitian matrices
  at real `c`. Writing `A = ∑ λₖ Pₖ` with orthogonal projections, `Qₖ = Φ(Pₖ)` are positive with
  `∑ Qₖ = 1`, and `Φ(A²) - Φ(A)² = ∑ₖ (λₖ - Φ A) Qₖ (λₖ - Φ A)`.
* **The gap.** The transpose of `2 × 2` matrices is positive and unital, but the bound fails for
  the non-Hermitian matrix `E₀₁`.

## ii. Key results

- `AlgState.apply_nonneg` : on a star-ordered ring a state is nonnegative on nonnegative elements.
- `AlgState.covarianceForm_map_le` : a Schwarz inequality for `Φ` bounds the covariance form.
- `AlgState.covarianceMatrixForm_map_le` : Schwarz maps do not decrease the matrix of
  covariances.
- `Matrix.kadison` : Kadison's inequality for positive unital maps of matrices.
- `AlgState.covarianceForm_map_le_of_positive` : positive unital maps do not decrease the
  covariance form of Hermitian matrices.
- `AlgState.covarianceMatrixForm_map_le_of_positive` : nor the matrix of covariances of
  Hermitian matrices at real coefficients.
- `Matrix.transposeMap_gap` : the transpose is positive and unital but increases the covariance
  form of `E₀₁` after the map.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Positivity of a state
- B. Schwarz maps
- C. Kadison's inequality
- D. Positive maps of matrices
- E. The transpose

## iv. References

* R. V. Kadison, *A generalized Schwarz inequality and algebraic invariants for operator
  algebras*, Ann. of Math. 56 (1952), 494–503.
* M.-D. Choi, *A Schwarz inequality for positive linear maps on C*-algebras*, Illinois J. Math.
  18 (1974), 565–574.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AlgState.apply_nonneg
declarations.doc: On a star-ordered ring a state is nonnegative on every nonnegative element.
declarations.statement: lemma apply_nonneg {a : A} (ha : 0 ≤ a) : 0 ≤ ω a

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AlgState.star_dotProduct_covarianceMatrixForm_mulVec
declarations.doc:
The quadratic form of the matrix of covariances at `c` is the covariance form of `∑ cⱼ aⱼ`
with itself.
declarations.statement:
lemma star_dotProduct_covarianceMatrixForm_mulVec {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (ω : AlgState A)
    (a : ι → A) (c : ι → ℂ) :
    star c ⬝ᵥ (ω.covarianceMatrixForm a a *ᵥ c) =
      ω.covarianceForm (∑ j, c j • a j) (∑ j, c j • a j)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AlgState.covarianceForm_sub_covarianceForm_map
declarations.doc:
Pulling the observable through `Φ` and pushing the state differ by the value of `ω` on
`Φ(X⋆ X) - Φ(X)⋆ Φ(X)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma covarianceForm_sub_covarianceForm_map (hω' : ∀ x, ω' x = ω (Φ x)) (X : A) :
    ω'.covarianceForm X X - ω.covarianceForm (Φ X) (Φ X) =
      ω (Φ (star X * X) - star (Φ X) * Φ X)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AlgState.covarianceForm_map_le
declarations.doc:
**A Schwarz inequality for `Φ` bounds the covariance form**: if
`Φ(X)⋆ Φ(X) ≤ Φ(X⋆ X)`, then `C_ω(Φ X, Φ X) ≤ C_ω'(X, X)`.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AlgState.covarianceMatrixForm_map_le
declarations.doc:
**Maps satisfying the Schwarz inequality do not decrease the matrix of covariances.** The
hypothesis holds for completely positive unital maps.
declarations.statement:
lemma covarianceMatrixForm_map_le {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (hω' : ∀ x, ω' x = ω (Φ x))
    (hΦ : ∀ X, star (Φ X) * Φ X ≤ Φ (star X * X)) (a : ι → A) (c : ι → ℂ) :
    star c ⬝ᵥ (ω.covarianceMatrixForm (Φ ∘ a) (Φ ∘ a) *ᵥ c) ≤
      star c ⬝ᵥ (ω'.covarianceMatrixForm a a *ᵥ c)

declarations.name: Matrix.sq_sum_le_sum_sq
declarations.doc: With positive `Qₖ` summing to `1`, `(∑ λₖ Qₖ)² ≤ ∑ λₖ² Qₖ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma sq_sum_le_sum_sq {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (Q : ι → Matrix m m ℂ)
    (hQ : ∀ k, (Q k).PosSemidef) (h1 : ∑ k, Q k = 1) (c : ι → ℝ) :
    (∑ k, (c k : ℂ) • Q k) * ∑ k, (c k : ℂ) • Q k ≤ ∑ k, ((c k : ℂ) * c k) • Q k

declarations.name: Matrix.kadison
declarations.doc:
**Kadison's inequality**: for a positive unital map and Hermitian `A`,
`Φ(A)² ≤ Φ(A²)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma kadison (Φ : Matrix n n ℂ →ₚ₁[ℂ] Matrix m m ℂ) {A : Matrix n n ℂ}
    (hA : A.IsHermitian) : (Φ A)ᴴ * Φ A ≤ Φ (Aᴴ * A)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AlgState.covarianceForm_map_le_of_positive
declarations.doc: **Positive unital maps do not decrease the covariance form of Hermitian matrices.**
declarations.statement:
lemma covarianceForm_map_le_of_positive (hω' : ∀ x, ω' x = ω (Φ x)) {X : Matrix n n ℂ}
    (hX : X.IsHermitian) : ω.covarianceForm (Φ X) (Φ X) ≤ ω'.covarianceForm X X

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AlgState.covarianceMatrixForm_map_le_of_positive
declarations.doc:
**Positive unital maps do not decrease the matrix of covariances** of Hermitian matrices at
real coefficients.
declarations.statement:
lemma covarianceMatrixForm_map_le_of_positive {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    (hω' : ∀ x, ω' x = ω (Φ x)) {a : ι → Matrix n n ℂ} (ha : ∀ i, (a i).IsHermitian)
    (c : ι → ℝ) :
    star (fun i => (c i : ℂ)) ⬝ᵥ (ω.covarianceMatrixForm (Φ ∘ a) (Φ ∘ a) *ᵥ fun i => (c i : ℂ)) ≤
      star (fun i => (c i : ℂ)) ⬝ᵥ (ω'.covarianceMatrixForm a a *ᵥ fun i => (c i : ℂ))

declarations.name: Matrix.stateZero
declarations.doc: The state `X ↦ X₀₀` of `2 × 2` matrices, the vector state of `|0⟩`.
declarations.statement: def stateZero : ProbabilisticTheory.AlgState (Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ)

declarations.name: Matrix.stateZero_apply
declarations.statement: lemma stateZero_apply (X : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ) : stateZero X = X 0 0

declarations.name: Matrix.transposeMap
declarations.doc: The transpose of `2 × 2` matrices.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def transposeMap : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ →ₚ₁[ℂ] Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ

declarations.name: Matrix.transposeMap_apply
declarations.statement: lemma transposeMap_apply (X : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ) : transposeMap X = Xᵀ

declarations.name: Matrix.stateZero_transposeMap
declarations.doc: The state `X ↦ X₀₀` is unchanged by the transpose.
declarations.statement:
lemma stateZero_transposeMap (X : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ) :
    stateZero X = stateZero (transposeMap X)

declarations.name: Matrix.transposeMap_gap
declarations.doc:
**The transpose is positive and unital, but the bound fails for `E₀₁`**: for positive maps
it holds only on Hermitian matrices.
declarations.statement:
lemma transposeMap_gap :
    ¬ stateZero.covarianceForm (transposeMap (single 0 1 1)) (transposeMap (single 0 1 1)) ≤
      stateZero.covarianceForm (single 0 1 1) (single 0 1 1)

modules.title: The GNS representation of a state on a unital `*`-algebra
modules.doc:
A state on a unital complex `*`-algebra defines a Hilbert space, the completion of the algebra for
the inner product `⟨a, b⟩ = ω(a* b)`, on which a group of state preserving `*`-automorphisms acts
unitarily.

## i. Overview

A *state* on a unital complex `*`-algebra `A` is a linear functional `ω` with `ω(1) = 1`,
`ω(a*) = conj ω(a)`, and `ω(a* a) ≥ 0` for every `a`. The form `⟨a, b⟩ = ω(a* b)` is a positive
semidefinite inner product on `A`, and the quotient by its null vectors, completed, is the
*GNS Hilbert space*. No norm on `A` is needed, so the construction applies to algebras that are
not complete, such as the quasi-local algebra of an infinite lattice before completion.

A `*`-automorphism `σ` of `A` that preserves `ω` preserves the inner product, so it defines an
isometry on the pre-Hilbert space, and a unitary operator on the GNS space. A group of such
automorphisms is represented unitarily, and each unitary fixes the class of the unit, the
cyclic vector.

## ii. Key results

- `AlgState` : a state on a unital `*`-algebra.
- `AlgState.GNS` : the Hilbert space of a state.
- `AlgState.gnsAut` : the unitary implementing a state preserving automorphism.
- `AlgState.gnsRep` : the unitary representation of a group of state preserving automorphisms.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. States and the pre-Hilbert space
- B. Implementing automorphisms
- C. Representations of groups
- D. Composition and commutation of implementing operators

## iv. References

* O. Bratteli & D. Robinson, Operator Algebras and Quantum Statistical Mechanics 1,
  Section 2.3.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AlgState
declarations.doc:
A state on a unital complex `*`-algebra: a normalized, Hermitian, positive linear
functional.
declarations.statement:
structure AlgState (A : Type*) [Ring A] [Algebra ℂ A] [StarRing A] [StarModule ℂ A] where
  /-- The linear functional. -/
  toLinearMap : A →ₗ[ℂ] ℂ
  /-- The state is normalized. -/
  map_one' : toLinearMap 1 = 1
  /-- The state is Hermitian. -/
  map_star' : ∀ a, toLinearMap (star a) = star (toLinearMap a)
  /-- The state is positive. -/
  nonneg' : ∀ a, 0 ≤ toLinearMap (star a * a)
instance : FunLike (AlgState A) A ℂ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AlgState.map_one
declarations.statement: lemma map_one : ω 1 = 1

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AlgState.map_star
declarations.statement: lemma map_star (a : A) : ω (star a) = star (ω a)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AlgState.nonneg
declarations.statement: lemma nonneg (a : A) : 0 ≤ ω (star a * a)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AlgState.map_add
declarations.statement: lemma map_add (a b : A) : ω (a + b) = ω a + ω b

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AlgState.map_smul
declarations.statement: lemma map_smul (c : ℂ) (a : A) : ω (c • a) = c * ω a

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AlgState.PreGNS
declarations.doc: The algebra with the inner product induced by a state, before completion.
declarations.statement: def PreGNS (_ω : AlgState A)
instance : AddCommGroup ω.PreGNS
instance : Module ℂ ω.PreGNS

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AlgState.toPre
declarations.doc: The identification of the algebra with its pre-Hilbert space.
declarations.statement: def toPre : A ≃ₗ[ℂ] ω.PreGNS

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AlgState.ofPre
declarations.doc: The identification of the pre-Hilbert space with the algebra.
declarations.statement: def ofPre : ω.PreGNS ≃ₗ[ℂ] A

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AlgState.core
declarations.doc: The inner product `⟨a, b⟩ = ω (a* b)`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable abbrev core : PreInnerProductSpace.Core ℂ ω.PreGNS
noncomputable instance : SeminormedAddCommGroup ω.PreGNS
noncomputable instance : InnerProductSpace ℂ ω.PreGNS

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AlgState.inner_pre
declarations.statement: lemma inner_pre (a b : ω.PreGNS) : ⟪a, b⟫_ℂ = ω (star (ω.ofPre a) * ω.ofPre b)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AlgState.GNS
declarations.doc:
The **GNS Hilbert space** of a state: the completion of the algebra for the inner product
`⟨a, b⟩ = ω (a* b)`.
declarations.statement: abbrev GNS : Type _

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AlgState.preAut
declarations.doc: The map `[a] ↦ [σ a]` on the pre-Hilbert space.
declarations.statement: def preAut : ω.PreGNS →ₗ[ℂ] ω.PreGNS

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AlgState.ofPre_preAut
declarations.statement: lemma ofPre_preAut (x : ω.PreGNS) : ω.ofPre (preAut ω σ x) = σ (ω.ofPre x)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AlgState.inner_preAut
declarations.statement:
lemma inner_preAut (hσ : ∀ a, ω (σ a) = ω a) (x y : ω.PreGNS) :
    ⟪preAut ω σ x, preAut ω σ y⟫_ℂ = ⟪x, y⟫_ℂ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AlgState.norm_preAut
declarations.statement: lemma norm_preAut (hσ : ∀ a, ω (σ a) = ω a) (x : ω.PreGNS) : ‖preAut ω σ x‖ = ‖x‖

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AlgState.preAutCLM
declarations.doc: The automorphism as a bounded operator on the pre-Hilbert space.
declarations.statement: def preAutCLM (hσ : ∀ a, ω (σ a) = ω a) : ω.PreGNS →L[ℂ] ω.PreGNS

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AlgState.gnsAut
declarations.doc: **The operator on the GNS space implementing a state preserving automorphism.**
declarations.statement: def gnsAut (hσ : ∀ a, ω (σ a) = ω a) : ω.GNS →L[ℂ] ω.GNS

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AlgState.gnsAut_coe
declarations.statement:
lemma gnsAut_coe (hσ : ∀ a, ω (σ a) = ω a) (x : ω.PreGNS) :
    gnsAut σ hσ (x : ω.GNS) = ((preAut ω σ x : ω.PreGNS) : ω.GNS)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AlgState.inner_gnsAut
declarations.statement:
lemma inner_gnsAut (hσ : ∀ a, ω (σ a) = ω a) (x y : ω.GNS) :
    ⟪gnsAut σ hσ x, gnsAut σ hσ y⟫_ℂ = ⟪x, y⟫_ℂ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AlgState.gnsAut_mul
declarations.statement:
lemma gnsAut_mul (g h : Γ) :
    gnsAut (α (g * h)) (hα (g * h)) = gnsAut (α g) (hα g) * gnsAut (α h) (hα h)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AlgState.gnsAut_one
declarations.statement: lemma gnsAut_one : gnsAut (α 1) (hα 1) = 1

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AlgState.star_gnsAut_mul_gnsAut
declarations.statement:
lemma star_gnsAut_mul_gnsAut (g : Γ) :
    star (gnsAut (α g) (hα g)) * gnsAut (α g) (hα g) = 1

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AlgState.star_gnsAut
declarations.statement: lemma star_gnsAut (g : Γ) : star (gnsAut (α g) (hα g)) = gnsAut (α g⁻¹) (hα g⁻¹)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AlgState.gnsUnitary
declarations.doc: **The unitary operator on the GNS space implementing a symmetry** of the state.
declarations.statement: def gnsUnitary (g : Γ) : unitary (ω.GNS →L[ℂ] ω.GNS)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AlgState.gnsRep
declarations.doc:
**The unitary representation of a group of symmetries on the GNS space of an invariant
state.**
declarations.statement: def gnsRep : Γ →* unitary (ω.GNS →L[ℂ] ω.GNS)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AlgState.cyclicVector
declarations.doc: The cyclic vector: the class of the unit.
declarations.statement: def cyclicVector : ω.GNS

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AlgState.gnsAut_comp
declarations.doc: The operator implementing a composite of automorphisms is the composite of the operators.
declarations.statement:
lemma gnsAut_comp :
    gnsAut (σ * τ) (fun a => by rw [StarAlgEquiv.mul_apply, hσ, hτ]) =
      gnsAut σ hσ * gnsAut τ hτ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AlgState.gnsAut_congr
declarations.doc: Equal automorphisms are implemented by equal operators.
declarations.statement:
lemma gnsAut_congr {σ τ : A ≃⋆ₐ[ℂ] A} (h : σ = τ) (hσ : ∀ a, ω (σ a) = ω a)
    (hτ : ∀ a, ω (τ a) = ω a) : gnsAut σ hσ = gnsAut τ hτ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AlgState.gnsAut_commute
declarations.doc: Commuting automorphisms are implemented by commuting operators.
declarations.statement:
lemma gnsAut_commute {σ τ : A ≃⋆ₐ[ℂ] A} (hσ : ∀ a, ω (σ a) = ω a) (hτ : ∀ a, ω (τ a) = ω a)
    (h : σ * τ = τ * σ) : Commute (gnsAut σ hσ) (gnsAut τ hτ)

modules.title: Invariant states by Følner averaging
modules.doc:
A state of a `*`-algebra with a group of automorphisms has invariant limit points, obtained by
averaging over larger and larger finite subsets of the group.

## i. Overview

A system in thermal equilibrium on an infinite crystal need not be translation invariant, because
the Gibbs states of finite boxes see the boundary of the box. Averaging a state `φ` over the
translates `α_g` with `g` in a finite set `F` gives the state `φ_F = |F|⁻¹ ∑_{g ∈ F} φ ∘ α_g`.
When the sets `F` become invariant under right translation, `|F h Δ F| / |F| → 0` for every `h`
(a Følner condition), the averaged states become invariant: `φ_F ∘ α_h - φ_F → 0`. If the values
of the averaged states on each observable are bounded, they have limit points along an
ultrafilter, and every limit point is an invariant state.

Nothing is assumed about the algebra beyond a bound `a* a + p = c · 1` with `p` a sum of squares
for each observable `a`. The statement therefore holds for the quasi-local algebra of any net,
quantum or classical, and for every state, in particular for the thermodynamic limit states of a
Gibbs ensemble.

## ii. Key results

- `IsBounded` : an observable is bounded by a multiple of the identity up to a sum of squares.
- `AlgState.limit` : the ultrafilter limit of a bounded net of states.
- `AlgState.average` : the average of a state over a finite set of automorphisms.
- `AlgState.invariantLimit` : the limit of Følner averages.
- `AlgState.invariantLimit_invariant` : the limit state is invariant under the group.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Bounded observables
- B. Limits of states
- C. Averages over a finite set of automorphisms
- D. Invariance of Følner limits
- E. Boundedness in the quasi-local algebra

## iv. References

* F. Greenleaf, Invariant Means on Topological Groups.
* O. Bratteli & D. Robinson, Operator Algebras and Quantum Statistical Mechanics 1,
  Section 4.3.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.IsBounded
declarations.doc:
An observable `a` is **bounded** if some multiple `c · 1` of the identity exceeds `a* a` by a
sum of squares.
declarations.statement: def IsBounded (a : A) : Prop

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AlgState.norm_sq_le_of_isBounded
declarations.doc: **Every state is bounded on a bounded observable**, by the same constant.
declarations.statement:
lemma AlgState.norm_sq_le_of_isBounded {a : A} {c : ℝ} {p : A} (hp : p ∈ sumSq A)
    (h : star a * a + p = (c : ℂ) • (1 : A)) (ω : AlgState A) : ‖ω a‖ ^ 2 ≤ c

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.sumSq_map
declarations.doc: A star-algebra equivalence maps sums of squares to sums of squares.
declarations.statement:
lemma sumSq_map {B : Type*} [Ring B] [Algebra ℂ B] [StarRing B]
    (σ : A ≃⋆ₐ[ℂ] B) {p : A} (hp : p ∈ sumSq A) : σ p ∈ sumSq B

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.IsBounded.map
declarations.doc: A star-algebra automorphism preserves boundedness.
declarations.statement: lemma IsBounded.map {a : A} (ha : IsBounded a) (σ : A ≃⋆ₐ[ℂ] A) : IsBounded (σ a)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.exists_tendsto_state
declarations.doc: The values of a bounded net of states on an observable have a limit along an ultrafilter.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_tendsto_state (ψ : ι → AlgState A) (𝒰 : Ultrafilter ι)
    (hb : ∀ a : A, ∃ c : ℝ, ∀ i, ‖ψ i a‖ ≤ c) (a : A) :
    ∃ z, Tendsto (fun i => ψ i a) 𝒰 (𝓝 z)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AlgState.limit
declarations.doc: **The limit of a bounded net of states along an ultrafilter** is a state.
declarations.statement:
def AlgState.limit (ψ : ι → AlgState A) (𝒰 : Ultrafilter ι)
    (hb : ∀ a : A, ∃ c : ℝ, ∀ i, ‖ψ i a‖ ≤ c) : AlgState A

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AlgState.tendsto_limit
declarations.statement:
lemma AlgState.tendsto_limit (ψ : ι → AlgState A) (𝒰 : Ultrafilter ι)
    (hb : ∀ a : A, ∃ c : ℝ, ∀ i, ‖ψ i a‖ ≤ c) (a : A) :
    Tendsto (fun i => ψ i a) 𝒰 (𝓝 (AlgState.limit ψ 𝒰 hb a))

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.starAlgEquiv_smul
declarations.statement: lemma starAlgEquiv_smul (σ : A ≃⋆ₐ[ℂ] A) (c : ℂ) (a : A) : σ (c • a) = c • σ a

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.averageMap
declarations.doc: The linear functional `a ↦ |F|⁻¹ ∑_{g ∈ F} φ (α g a)`.
declarations.statement: def averageMap (φ : AlgState A) (α : Γ → (A ≃⋆ₐ[ℂ] A)) (F : Finset Γ) : A →ₗ[ℂ] ℂ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.averageMap_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma averageMap_apply (φ : AlgState A) (α : Γ → (A ≃⋆ₐ[ℂ] A)) (F : Finset Γ) (a : A) :
    averageMap φ α F a = ((F.card : ℂ))⁻¹ * ∑ g ∈ F, φ (α g a)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AlgState.average
declarations.doc: **The average of a state over a finite set of automorphisms** is a state.
declarations.statement:
def AlgState.average (φ : AlgState A) (α : Γ → (A ≃⋆ₐ[ℂ] A)) (F : Finset Γ)
    (hF : F.Nonempty) : AlgState A

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AlgState.average_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma AlgState.average_apply (φ : AlgState A) (α : Γ → (A ≃⋆ₐ[ℂ] A)) (F : Finset Γ)
    (hF : F.Nonempty) (a : A) :
    φ.average α F hF a = ((F.card : ℂ))⁻¹ * ∑ g ∈ F, φ (α g a)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.compMap
declarations.doc: The linear functional `a ↦ φ (σ a)`.
declarations.statement: def compMap (φ : AlgState A) (σ : A ≃⋆ₐ[ℂ] A) : A →ₗ[ℂ] ℂ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.compMap_apply
declarations.statement: lemma compMap_apply (φ : AlgState A) (σ : A ≃⋆ₐ[ℂ] A) (a : A) : compMap φ σ a = φ (σ a)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AlgState.comp
declarations.doc: **The composition of a state with an automorphism** is a state.
declarations.statement: def AlgState.comp (φ : AlgState A) (σ : A ≃⋆ₐ[ℂ] A) : AlgState A

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AlgState.comp_apply
declarations.statement: lemma AlgState.comp_apply (φ : AlgState A) (σ : A ≃⋆ₐ[ℂ] A) (a : A) : φ.comp σ a = φ (σ a)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AlgState.norm_le_of_isBounded
declarations.doc: The bound on a state on a bounded observable, as a norm bound.
declarations.statement:
lemma AlgState.norm_le_of_isBounded {a : A} {c : ℝ} {p : A} (hp : p ∈ sumSq A)
    (h : star a * a + p = (c : ℂ) • (1 : A)) (ω : AlgState A) : ‖ω a‖ ≤ c + 1

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.norm_sum_sub_le
declarations.doc:
A difference of two sums of a bounded function is bounded by the size of the symmetric
difference of the index sets.
declarations.statement:
lemma norm_sum_sub_le (f : Γ → ℂ) (C : ℝ) (hf : ∀ k, ‖f k‖ ≤ C) (S T : Finset Γ) :
    ‖∑ k ∈ S, f k - ∑ k ∈ T, f k‖ ≤ ((S \ T).card + (T \ S).card) * C

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.IsRightFolner
declarations.doc:
The finite sets `F i` are **asymptotically invariant under right translation** along an
ultrafilter (a Følner condition): `|F h Δ F| / |F| → 0` for every `h`.
declarations.statement: def IsRightFolner (F : ι → Finset Γ) (𝒰 : Ultrafilter ι) : Prop

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.average_bounded
declarations.doc: The averaged states of a state over the sets `F i` are bounded on every observable.
declarations.statement:
lemma average_bounded (φ : AlgState A) (hb : ∀ a : A, IsBounded a) (a : A) :
    ∃ c : ℝ, ∀ i, ‖(φ.average (fun g => α g) (F i) (hne i)) a‖ ≤ c

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AlgState.invariantLimit
declarations.doc: **The Følner limit of a state**: the ultrafilter limit of its averages over the sets `F i`.
declarations.statement:
def AlgState.invariantLimit (φ : AlgState A) (hb : ∀ a : A, IsBounded a) (𝒰 : Ultrafilter ι) :
    AlgState A

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AlgState.invariantLimit_invariant
declarations.doc:
**The Følner limit of a state is invariant.** When the sets `F i` are asymptotically invariant
under right translation along `𝒰`, every limit of the averages of a state over them is invariant
under the group.
declarations.statement:
lemma AlgState.invariantLimit_invariant (φ : AlgState A) (hb : ∀ a : A, IsBounded a)
    (𝒰 : Ultrafilter ι) (hF : IsRightFolner F 𝒰) (h : Γ) (a : A) :
    AlgState.invariantLimit α F hne φ hb 𝒰 (α h a) = AlgState.invariantLimit α F hne φ hb 𝒰 a

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.sumSq_map_hom
declarations.doc: A star-algebra homomorphism maps sums of squares to sums of squares.
declarations.statement:
lemma sumSq_map_hom {B : Type*} [Ring B] [Algebra ℂ B] [StarRing B]
    (σ : A →⋆ₐ[ℂ] B) {p : A} (hp : p ∈ sumSq A) : σ p ∈ sumSq B

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AlgebraNet.isBounded_of_isLocallyBounded
declarations.doc: **Every observable of the quasi-local algebra of a locally bounded net is bounded.**
declarations.statement:
lemma AlgebraNet.isBounded_of_isLocallyBounded (hb : N.IsLocallyBounded) (x : N.Quasilocal) :
    IsBounded x

modules.title: The Jordan product of observables
modules.doc:
The Jordan product ½ (a b + b a) makes the self-adjoint elements a commutative Jordan ring.

## i. Overview

The product of two self-adjoint elements is self-adjoint only when they commute, but the symmetrized
product `a ∘ b = ½ (a b + b a)` is always self-adjoint. It is commutative and satisfies the Jordan
identity, so the observables form a Jordan algebra. The product is a scoped instance on `selfAdjoint
A`, since for commutative `A` Mathlib already gives `selfAdjoint A` the ordinary product.

## ii. Key results

- `selfAdjoint.jordanMul` : the Jordan product `½ (a b + b a)`.
- `selfAdjoint.jordanMul_comm` : the Jordan product is commutative.
- `selfAdjoint.jordanMul_jordanMul_jordanMul_self` : the Jordan identity.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The anticommutator
- B. The normalized Jordan product
- C. Additivity, scalars and the Jordan identity
- D. The Jordan product as a multiplication
- E. The Jordan ring structure
- F. The Jordan product of observables

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## C. Additivity, scalars and the Jordan identity
## D. The Jordan product as a multiplication
## F. The Jordan product of observables

declarations.name: selfAdjoint.anticommutator
declarations.doc:
The unnormalized anticommutator, retained as a low-level formula while `jordanMul` is the
canonical normalized Jordan product.
declarations.statement: def anticommutator (a b : selfAdjoint A) : selfAdjoint A

declarations.name: selfAdjoint.coe_anticommutator
declarations.statement:
lemma coe_anticommutator (a b : selfAdjoint A) :
    ((anticommutator a b : selfAdjoint A) : A) = (a : A) * (b : A) + (b : A) * (a : A)

declarations.name: selfAdjoint.jordanMul
declarations.doc:
The normalized Jordan product of two self-adjoint elements,
`a ∘ b := ½(ab + ba)`. It is self-adjoint regardless of whether `a` and `b` commute, since
`star (a * b + b * a) = star b * star a + star a * star b = b * a + a * b`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def jordanMul (a b : selfAdjoint A) : selfAdjoint A

declarations.name: selfAdjoint.val_jordanMul
declarations.statement:
lemma val_jordanMul (a b : selfAdjoint A) :
    ((jordanMul a b : selfAdjoint A) : A) =
      (2 : ℝ)⁻¹ • ((a : A) * (b : A) + (b : A) * (a : A))

declarations.name: selfAdjoint.jordanMul_comm
declarations.doc: The Jordan product is commutative.
declarations.statement: lemma jordanMul_comm (a b : selfAdjoint A) : jordanMul a b = jordanMul b a

declarations.name: selfAdjoint.one_jordanMul
declarations.doc: The unit of the ambient algebra is a unit for the normalized Jordan product.
declarations.statement: lemma one_jordanMul (a : selfAdjoint A) : jordanMul 1 a = a

declarations.name: selfAdjoint.jordanMul_one
declarations.doc: The normalized Jordan product has the same unit in its right argument.
declarations.statement: lemma jordanMul_one (a : selfAdjoint A) : jordanMul a 1 = a

declarations.name: selfAdjoint.jordanMul_add_right
declarations.doc: The Jordan product distributes over addition in its right argument.
declarations.statement:
lemma jordanMul_add_right (a b c : selfAdjoint A) :
    jordanMul a (b + c) = jordanMul a b + jordanMul a c

declarations.name: selfAdjoint.jordanMul_add_left
declarations.doc: The Jordan product distributes over addition in its left argument.
declarations.statement:
lemma jordanMul_add_left (a b c : selfAdjoint A) :
    jordanMul (a + b) c = jordanMul a c + jordanMul b c

declarations.name: selfAdjoint.anticommutator_smul_left
declarations.statement:
lemma anticommutator_smul_left [SMulCommClass ℝ A A] [IsScalarTower ℝ A A]
    (c : ℝ) (a b : selfAdjoint A) :
    anticommutator (c • a) b = c • anticommutator a b

declarations.name: selfAdjoint.anticommutator_smul_right
declarations.statement:
lemma anticommutator_smul_right [SMulCommClass ℝ A A] [IsScalarTower ℝ A A]
    (a : selfAdjoint A) (c : ℝ) (b : selfAdjoint A) :
    anticommutator a (c • b) = c • anticommutator a b

declarations.name: selfAdjoint.anticommutator_identity
declarations.statement:
lemma anticommutator_identity (a b : selfAdjoint A) :
    anticommutator (anticommutator a b) (anticommutator a a) =
      anticommutator a (anticommutator b (anticommutator a a))

declarations.name: selfAdjoint.jordanMul_jordanMul_jordanMul_self
declarations.doc:
The Jordan identity: `∘`-multiplication by `a` and by `a ∘ a` commute, i.e.
`(a ∘ b) ∘ (a ∘ a) = a ∘ (b ∘ (a ∘ a))`. This is the "weak associativity" law that survives
symmetrization of a possibly non-commutative, associative product.
declarations.statement:
lemma jordanMul_jordanMul_jordanMul_self [SMulCommClass ℝ A A] [IsScalarTower ℝ A A]
    (a b : selfAdjoint A) :
    jordanMul (jordanMul a b) (jordanMul a a) = jordanMul a (jordanMul b (jordanMul a a))

declarations.name: selfAdjoint.instMul
declarations.doc: The Jordan product as a scoped multiplication on `selfAdjoint A`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable scoped instance instMul : Mul (selfAdjoint A)

declarations.name: selfAdjoint.mul_def
declarations.statement: lemma mul_def (a b : selfAdjoint A) : a * b = jordanMul a b

declarations.name: selfAdjoint.coe_mul
declarations.doc:
Coercing the canonical Jordan product back to the ambient algebra gives the normalized
anticommutator.
declarations.statement:
lemma coe_mul (a b : selfAdjoint A) :
    ((a * b : selfAdjoint A) : A) =
      (2 : ℝ)⁻¹ • ((a : A) * (b : A) + (b : A) * (a : A))

declarations.name: selfAdjoint.jordanMul_smul_left
declarations.doc: Real scalars pull out of the left argument of the normalized Jordan product.
declarations.statement:
lemma jordanMul_smul_left [SMulCommClass ℝ A A] [IsScalarTower ℝ A A]
    (c : ℝ) (a b : selfAdjoint A) : jordanMul (c • a) b = c • jordanMul a b

declarations.name: selfAdjoint.jordanMul_smul_right
declarations.doc: Real scalars pull out of the right argument of the normalized Jordan product.
declarations.statement:
lemma jordanMul_smul_right [SMulCommClass ℝ A A] [IsScalarTower ℝ A A]
    (a : selfAdjoint A) (c : ℝ) (b : selfAdjoint A) :
    jordanMul a (c • b) = c • jordanMul a b

declarations.name: selfAdjoint.jordanMul_jordanMul_right
declarations.doc:
Expanding one right-nested Jordan product produces a common factor `1 / 4` and a nested
unnormalized anticommutator. This is useful for associative calculations in concrete
realizations while keeping the normalized Jordan product canonical.
declarations.statement:
lemma jordanMul_jordanMul_right [SMulCommClass ℝ A A] [IsScalarTower ℝ A A]
    (a b x : selfAdjoint A) :
    jordanMul a (jordanMul b x) =
      ((2 : ℝ)⁻¹ * (2 : ℝ)⁻¹) • anticommutator a (anticommutator b x)

declarations.name: selfAdjoint.jordanMul_zero
declarations.statement: lemma jordanMul_zero (a : selfAdjoint A) : jordanMul a 0 = 0

declarations.name: selfAdjoint.instNonUnitalNonAssocCommRing

declarations.statement: noncomputable scoped instance instNonAssocCommRing : NonAssocCommRing (selfAdjoint A)

declarations.statement: scoped instance instSMulCommClass : SMulCommClass ℝ (selfAdjoint A) (selfAdjoint A)

declarations.statement: scoped instance instIsScalarTower : IsScalarTower ℝ (selfAdjoint A) (selfAdjoint A)

declarations.name: selfAdjoint.instIsCommJordan

modules.title: The Lie bracket of observables
modules.doc:
The Lie bracket -(i / 2)(a b - b a) makes the observables a real Lie algebra.

## i. Overview

The commutator of two self-adjoint elements is skew-adjoint, so `⁅a, b⁆ = -(i / 2)(a b - b a)` is
self-adjoint. Together with the Jordan product it splits the product of observables, `a b = a ∘ b +
i ⁅a, b⁆`, and it makes the observables a real Lie algebra. The bracket is a scoped instance on
`selfAdjoint A`.

## ii. Key results

- `selfAdjoint.lieMul` : the Lie bracket `-(i / 2)(a b - b a)`.
- `selfAdjoint.isSelfAdjoint_mul_iff_commute` : `a b` is self-adjoint iff `a` and `b` commute.
- `selfAdjoint.mul_decomposition` : `a b = a ∘ b + i ⁅a, b⁆`.
- `selfAdjoint.leibniz_bracket` : the bracket satisfies the Leibniz rule.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The Lie bracket
- B. Antisymmetry and additivity
- C. Lie ring
- D. Real Lie algebra
- E. Elementary identities

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: selfAdjoint.lieMul
declarations.doc: The Lie bracket `-(i / 2)(a b - b a)` of two self-adjoint elements, again self-adjoint.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def lieMul (a b : selfAdjoint A) : selfAdjoint A

declarations.name: selfAdjoint.val_lieMul
declarations.statement:
lemma val_lieMul (a b : selfAdjoint A) :
    ((lieMul a b : selfAdjoint A) : A) = (-(Complex.I / 2)) • ((a : A) * b - (b : A) * a)

declarations.name: selfAdjoint.isSelfAdjoint_mul_iff_commute
declarations.doc: The product of two self-adjoint elements is self-adjoint iff they commute.
declarations.statement:
lemma isSelfAdjoint_mul_iff_commute (a b : selfAdjoint A) :
    IsSelfAdjoint ((a : A) * (b : A)) ↔ Commute (a : A) (b : A)

declarations.name: selfAdjoint.mul_decomposition
declarations.doc:
The ambient product of two self-adjoint elements splits into its normalized Jordan and Lie
parts: `a * b = (a ∘ b) + i ⁅a, b⁆`.
declarations.statement:
lemma mul_decomposition (a b : selfAdjoint A) :
    (a : A) * b =
      (jordanMul a b : A) + Complex.I • ((lieMul a b : selfAdjoint A) : A)

declarations.name: selfAdjoint.lieMul_swap
declarations.doc: The Lie bracket is antisymmetric.
declarations.statement: lemma lieMul_swap (a b : selfAdjoint A) : lieMul a b = -lieMul b a

declarations.name: selfAdjoint.lieMul_add_left
declarations.statement:
lemma lieMul_add_left (a b c : selfAdjoint A) :
    lieMul (a + b) c = lieMul a c + lieMul b c

declarations.name: selfAdjoint.lieMul_add_right
declarations.statement:
lemma lieMul_add_right (a b c : selfAdjoint A) :
    lieMul a (b + c) = lieMul a b + lieMul a c

declarations.name: selfAdjoint.lieMul_self
declarations.statement: lemma lieMul_self (a : selfAdjoint A) : lieMul a a = 0

declarations.name: selfAdjoint.instBracket
declarations.doc: The Lie bracket as a scoped bracket on `selfAdjoint A`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable scoped instance instBracket : Bracket (selfAdjoint A) (selfAdjoint A)

declarations.name: selfAdjoint.bracket_def
declarations.statement: lemma bracket_def (a b : selfAdjoint A) : ⁅a, b⁆ = lieMul a b

declarations.name: selfAdjoint.coe_bracket
declarations.statement:

declarations.name: selfAdjoint.leibniz_bracket
declarations.statement:
lemma leibniz_bracket (a b c : selfAdjoint A) :

declarations.name: selfAdjoint.instLieRing
declarations.doc: The self-adjoint elements form a Lie ring under the Lie bracket.
declarations.statement: noncomputable scoped instance instLieRing : LieRing (selfAdjoint A)

declarations.name: selfAdjoint.bracket_smul

declarations.name: selfAdjoint.bracket_one_left
declarations.statement: lemma bracket_one_left (a : selfAdjoint A) : ⁅(1 : selfAdjoint A), a⁆ = 0

modules.title: Observables
modules.doc:
Observables as self-adjoint elements, and the real state on observables of a complex state.

## i. Overview

An observable is a self-adjoint element of a space with an involution. A complex state on the space
restricts to a real state on its observables, the expectation-value functional.

## ii. Key results

- `Observable`, `PositiveObservable` : observables and positive observables.
- `UnitalPositiveLinearMap.onObservables` : the real state on observables of a complex state.

## iii. Table of contents

- C. Examples: states on observables

modules.title: Uncertainty relations for states on a `*`-algebra
modules.doc:
The Robertson–Schrödinger relation and Robertson's relation for several observables hold for a
state on any unital `*`-algebra, with no norm on the algebra.

## i. Overview

A state `ω` on a unital `*`-algebra `A`, as in `AlgState`, gives the positive semidefinite inner
product `⟨x, y⟩ = ω(x⋆ y)` on `A`. The fluctuation `a - ω(a)` of a self-adjoint `a` is again
self-adjoint, because `ω(a)` is real. For a family of observables `a_j`, the inner products of
their fluctuations form the matrix `Σ + iΩ`, where `Σ` is the covariance matrix and `Ω` the
matrix of expectations of brackets. It is a Gram matrix, so it is positive semidefinite, and so
is its transpose `Σ - iΩ`. Hence `|det Ω| ≤ det Σ`, by `Matrix.abs_det_le_det_of_posSemidef`.
For two observables, Cauchy–Schwarz gives `Cov(a, b)² + ω⟨⁅a, b⁆⟩² ≤ Var a · Var b`.

If `ω` is invariant under a `⋆`-automorphism `σ` with `σ a = a` and `σ b = -b`, then
`ω(a b) = ω(σ (a b)) = -ω(a b)` and `ω(b) = 0`, so the entries `Σ_ab` and `Ω_ab` vanish.

The C⋆-algebra version is `UnitalPositiveLinearMap.robertson_det`. This one also applies to an
algebra that is not complete, such as the quasi-local algebra of an infinite crystal, and so to
its translation invariant states and the thermodynamic limit states of `InvariantState`.

## ii. Key results

- `AlgState.covarianceMatrix`, `AlgState.bracketMatrix` : the matrices `Σ` and `Ω`.
- `AlgState.gram_fluctuation` : `Σ + iΩ` is the Gram matrix of the fluctuations.
- `AlgState.robertson_schrodinger` : the Robertson–Schrödinger relation.
- `AlgState.robertson_det` : **Robertson's relation for several observables**,
  `|det Ω| ≤ det Σ`.
- `AlgState.covariance_eq_zero_of_symm`, `AlgState.bracket_eq_zero_of_symm` : in a state
  invariant under a `⋆`-automorphism, an even and an odd observable have `Σ_ab = Ω_ab = 0`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Fluctuations
- B. The matrices `Σ` and `Ω`
- C. Uncertainty relations
- D. Symmetric states

## iv. References

* H. P. Robertson, *An indeterminacy relation for several observables and its classical
  interpretation*, Phys. Rev. 46 (1934) 794.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.AlgState.apply_selfAdjoint

declarations.statement: lemma apply_selfAdjoint (a : selfAdjoint A) : ω (a : A) = ((ω (a : A)).re : ℂ)

declarations.statement:
lemma apply_fluctuation_mul (a b : selfAdjoint A) :
    ω (ω.fluctuation a * ω.fluctuation b) = ω ((a : A) * b) - ω (a : A) * ω (b : A)

declarations.statement:
lemma bracket_eq_im (a b : selfAdjoint A) :
    ω.bracket a b = (ω (ω.fluctuation a * ω.fluctuation b)).im

declarations.doc: The covariance matrix `Σ_jk = Cov(a_j, a_k)` of a family of observables.

declarations.doc: The matrix `Ω_jk = ω⟨⁅a_j, a_k⁆⟩` of expectations of brackets.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def bracketMatrix (a : ι → selfAdjoint A) : Matrix ι ι ℝ
