    (x : PosCone E) :
    hw.toOrderUnitContinuousLinearMap (x : E) = (w x).toReal

modules.title: Extending finite weights
modules.doc:
A finite weight extends uniquely to a positive linear functional on the order unit space.

## i. Overview

A finite weight on the positive cone of an order-unit space extends uniquely to a positive linear
functional on the whole space. Since `1` is an order unit, any `A : E` becomes nonnegative after
adding enough copies of `1`, so we set `toFun A := w (r • 1 + A) - r * w 1` for such an `r`, and
check the result does not depend on the `r` chosen.

## ii. Key results

- `Weight.IsFinite.toLinearMap` : the `ℝ`-linear map extending a finite weight to all of `E`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The raw shifted value
- B. The linear extension

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Weight.IsFinite.rawValue
declarations.doc:
`A` shifted into the cone by `r` copies of the order unit, minus the corresponding multiple
of the weight of the order unit.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def rawValue (w : Weight E) (A : E) (r : ℝ) (h : 0 ≤ r • (1 : E) + A) : ℝ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Weight.IsFinite.rawValue_of_le
declarations.doc: Shifting by a larger `s` gives the same value as shifting by `r`.
declarations.statement:
lemma rawValue_of_le (hw : w.IsFinite) (A : E) {r s : ℝ} (hr : 0 ≤ r • (1 : E) + A)
    (hs : 0 ≤ s • (1 : E) + A) (hrs : r ≤ s) : rawValue w A s hs = rawValue w A r hr

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Weight.IsFinite.rawValue_indep
declarations.doc: The shifted value of a finite weight does not depend on the chosen shift.
declarations.statement:
lemma rawValue_indep (hw : w.IsFinite) (A : E) {r s : ℝ} (hr : 0 ≤ r • (1 : E) + A)
    (hs : 0 ≤ s • (1 : E) + A) : rawValue w A r hr = rawValue w A s hs

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Weight.IsFinite.toFun
declarations.doc: The linear extension of a finite weight from the positive cone to all of `E`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def toFun (w : Weight E) (A : E) : ℝ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Weight.IsFinite.toFun_eq
declarations.doc: The extension can be computed with any shift `r` making `r • 1 + A` nonnegative.
declarations.statement:
lemma toFun_eq (hw : w.IsFinite) (A : E) {r : ℝ} (h : 0 ≤ r • (1 : E) + A) :
    toFun w A = rawValue w A r h

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Weight.IsFinite.toFun_of_nonneg
declarations.statement: lemma toFun_of_nonneg (hw : w.IsFinite) (A : PosCone E) : toFun w (A : E) = (w A).toReal

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Weight.IsFinite.toFun_zero
declarations.doc: The extension of a finite weight sends `0` to `0`.
declarations.statement: lemma toFun_zero (hw : w.IsFinite) : toFun w (0 : E) = 0

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Weight.IsFinite.toFun_add
declarations.doc: The extension of a finite weight is additive.
declarations.statement: lemma toFun_add (hw : w.IsFinite) (A B : E) : toFun w (A + B) = toFun w A + toFun w B

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Weight.IsFinite.toFun_neg
declarations.doc: The extension of a finite weight is odd.
declarations.statement: lemma toFun_neg (hw : w.IsFinite) (A : E) : toFun w (-A) = -toFun w A

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Weight.IsFinite.toFun_real_nonneg_smul
declarations.doc: Nonnegative real homogeneity of the finite-weight extension.
declarations.statement:
lemma toFun_real_nonneg_smul (hw : w.IsFinite) {t : ℝ} (ht : 0 ≤ t) (A : E) :
    toFun w (t • A) = t * toFun w A

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Weight.IsFinite.toFun_smul
declarations.doc: Full real homogeneity of the finite-weight extension.
declarations.statement: lemma toFun_smul (hw : w.IsFinite) (t : ℝ) (A : E) : toFun w (t • A) = t * toFun w A

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Weight.IsFinite.toLinearMap
declarations.doc: The `ℝ`-linear map extending a finite weight.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def toLinearMap (hw : w.IsFinite) : E →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Weight.IsFinite.toLinearMap_apply
declarations.doc: The linear extension agrees with `toFun` by construction.
declarations.statement: lemma toLinearMap_apply (hw : w.IsFinite) (A : E) : toLinearMap hw A = toFun w A

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Weight.IsFinite.toPositiveLinearMap
declarations.doc: The positive linear extension of a finite weight.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def toPositiveLinearMap (hw : w.IsFinite) : E →ₚ[ℝ] ℝ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Weight.IsFinite.toPositiveLinearMap_apply
declarations.doc: The positive extension agrees with the underlying finite-weight extension.
declarations.statement:
lemma toPositiveLinearMap_apply (hw : w.IsFinite) (A : E) :
    hw.toPositiveLinearMap A = toFun w A

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Weight.IsFinite.toPositiveLinearMap_apply_of_nonneg
declarations.doc: On positive elements, the positive extension is the real value of the weight.
declarations.statement:
lemma toPositiveLinearMap_apply_of_nonneg (hw : w.IsFinite) (A : PosCone E) :
    hw.toPositiveLinearMap (A : E) = (w A).toReal

modules.title: W⋆-algebras and normal states
modules.doc:
W⋆-algebras with a chosen predual, their weak-⋆ topology, and normal states.

## i. Overview

A W⋆-algebra is a C⋆-algebra that is the dual of a Banach space, its predual. Mathlib's
`WStarAlgebra` only asserts that a predual exists. The weak-⋆ topology depends on the predual, so
`WStarAlgebraStructure` fixes one together with the isometric identification of `A` with its dual.
The weak-⋆ topology is coarser than the norm topology. A normal state is a state that is continuous
for the weak-⋆ topology.

## ii. Key results

- `WStarAlgebraStructure` : a C⋆-algebra with a chosen predual.
- `WStarAlgebraStructure.weakStarTopology` : the weak-⋆ topology.
- `WStarAlgebraStructure.norm_le_weakStarTopology` : the weak-⋆ topology is coarser than the norm
  topology.
- `NormalState` : a weak-⋆ continuous state.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. W⋆-algebras
- B. The predual pairing
- C. Normal states

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: Weak-⋆ convergence is convergence of all predual pairings, for filters.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.WStarAlgebraStructure
declarations.doc:
**A W⋆-algebra**: a C⋆-algebra with a chosen predual and an isometric identification of the
algebra with the dual of its predual.
declarations.statement:
class WStarAlgebraStructure (A : Type*) extends CStarAlgebra A, PartialOrder A, StarOrderedRing A
    where
  /-- The predual: a Banach space `E` with `A ≃ₗᵢ[ℂ] StrongDual ℂ E` isometrically. -/
  Predual : Type*
  predualNormedAddCommGroup : NormedAddCommGroup Predual
  predualNormedSpace : NormedSpace ℂ Predual
  predualCompleteSpace : CompleteSpace Predual
  /-- The defining isometric identification `A ≃ₗᵢ[ℂ] StrongDual ℂ (Predual A)`, `a ↦ (ξ ↦
  ⟨a, ξ⟩)` for the duality pairing `A` inherits from being `Predual A`'s dual. -/
  toDual : A ≃ₗᵢ[ℂ] StrongDual ℂ Predual

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.WStarAlgebraStructure.weakStarTopology
declarations.doc:
**The weak-⋆ topology**, induced from the dual of the predual. States converge in it when their
values on each predual element converge. It is not an instance, since `A` already carries its norm
topology.
declarations.statement: def weakStarTopology : TopologicalSpace A

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.WStarAlgebraStructure.norm_le_weakStarTopology
declarations.doc: **The weak-⋆ topology is coarser than the norm topology.**
declarations.statement:
lemma norm_le_weakStarTopology :
    (inferInstance : TopologicalSpace A) ≤ weakStarTopology A

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.WStarAlgebraStructure.predualPairing
declarations.doc: The continuous functional on `A` given by a predual element.
declarations.statement: def predualPairing (ξ : WStarAlgebraStructure.Predual A) : A →L[ℂ] ℂ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.WStarAlgebraStructure.predualPairing_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma predualPairing_apply (ξ : WStarAlgebraStructure.Predual A) (a : A) :
    predualPairing ξ a = toDual a ξ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.WStarAlgebraStructure.norm_predualPairing_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma norm_predualPairing_apply (ξ : WStarAlgebraStructure.Predual A) (a : A) :
    ‖predualPairing ξ a‖ ≤ ‖a‖ * ‖ξ‖

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.WStarAlgebraStructure.predualPairing_weakStar_continuous
declarations.doc: The functional of a predual element is weak-⋆ continuous.
declarations.statement:
lemma predualPairing_weakStar_continuous (ξ : WStarAlgebraStructure.Predual A) :
    Continuous[WStarAlgebraStructure.weakStarTopology A, inferInstance]
      (predualPairing ξ)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.WStarAlgebraStructure.ext_of_forall_predualPairing_eq
declarations.doc: Predual elements separate the points of a W⋆-algebra.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.WStarAlgebraStructure.tendsto_weakStar_iff_forall_predualPairing_tendsto
declarations.statement:
lemma tendsto_weakStar_iff_forall_predualPairing_tendsto
    {α : Type*} {l : Filter α} {f : α → A} {a : A} :
    Tendsto f l (@nhds A (WStarAlgebraStructure.weakStarTopology A) a) ↔
      ∀ ξ : WStarAlgebraStructure.Predual A,
        Tendsto (fun i => predualPairing ξ (f i)) l
          (𝓝 (predualPairing ξ a))

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.NormalState
declarations.doc: A state that is continuous for the weak-* topology of the chosen predual.
declarations.statement:
structure NormalState (A : Type*) [WStarAlgebraStructure A] where
  /-- The underlying state. -/
  toState : 𝓢[ℂ, A]
  /-- The state is continuous for the chosen weak-* topology. -/
  weakStar_continuous :
    Continuous[WStarAlgebraStructure.weakStarTopology A, inferInstance] (⇑toState : A → ℂ)
noncomputable instance : CoeFun (NormalState A) (fun _ => A → ℂ)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.NormalState.toState_apply
declarations.statement: lemma toState_apply (ω : NormalState A) (a : A) : ω.toState a = ω a

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.NormalState.continuous
declarations.doc: Weak-* continuity implies ordinary norm continuity because the weak-* topology is coarser.
declarations.statement: lemma continuous (ω : NormalState A) : Continuous (ω : A → ℂ)

modules.title: Bounded sesquilinear forms
modules.doc:
A bounded sesquilinear form on a Hilbert space is represented by a bounded operator.

## i. Overview

A bounded sesquilinear form `B` on a Hilbert space, conjugate-linear in the first argument, is
represented by a bounded operator `T` with `⟪y, T x⟫ = conj (B x y)`.

## ii. Key results

- `BoundedSesquilinearForm` : a bounded sesquilinear form.
- `BoundedSesquilinearForm.operator` : the representing operator.
- `BoundedSesquilinearForm.operator_inner` : `⟪y, T x⟫ = conj (B x y)`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Bounded sesquilinear forms
- B. The representing operator

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.BoundedSesquilinearForm
declarations.doc:
A bounded sesquilinear form in the orientation expected by Mathlib's Riesz representation
theorem.
declarations.statement:
structure BoundedSesquilinearForm (H : Type*) [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℂ H]
    [CompleteSpace H] where
  /-- The underlying sesquilinear form. -/
  form : H →ₛₗ[starRingEnd ℂ] H →ₗ[ℂ] ℂ
  /-- The form is bounded by some constant `C`. -/
  bound : ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ x y, ‖form x y‖ ≤ C * ‖x‖ * ‖y‖

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.BoundedSesquilinearForm.boundConstant
declarations.doc: A norm bound witnessing `B.bound`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def boundConstant : ℝ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.BoundedSesquilinearForm.boundConstant_spec
declarations.statement: lemma boundConstant_spec : ∀ x y, ‖B.form x y‖ ≤ B.boundConstant * ‖x‖ * ‖y‖

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.BoundedSesquilinearForm.continuous
declarations.doc: The continuous version of a bounded sesquilinear form.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def continuous : H →L⋆[ℂ] H →L[ℂ] ℂ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.BoundedSesquilinearForm.continuous_apply
declarations.statement: lemma continuous_apply (x y : H) : B.continuous x y = B.form x y

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.BoundedSesquilinearForm.operator
declarations.doc: The unique bounded operator represented by `B`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def operator : H →L[ℂ] H

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.BoundedSesquilinearForm.operator_inner
declarations.statement:
lemma operator_inner (x y : H) :
    ⟪y, B.operator x⟫_ℂ = starRingEnd ℂ (B.form x y)

modules.title: The bounded operators as a W⋆-algebra
modules.doc:
The bounded operators on a Hilbert space form a W⋆-algebra with the trace class as predual.

## i. Overview

The trace pairing `A ↦ (ρ ↦ Tr (A ρ))` is an isometric isomorphism from the bounded operators on a
Hilbert space onto the dual of the trace-class operators. So the bounded operators form a W⋆-algebra
with predual the trace-class operators.

## ii. Key results

- `tracePairingEquiv` : the trace pairing as an isometric isomorphism onto the dual.
- `instWStarAlgebraStructureContinuousLinearMap` : the bounded operators with the trace-class
  operators as predual.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The `WStarAlgebraStructure (H →L[ℂ] H)` instance

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.TraceClass.tracePairing_surjective
declarations.doc: The concrete trace pairing is surjective onto the strong dual of the trace class.
declarations.statement:
lemma tracePairing_surjective :
    Function.Surjective (⇑(tracePairingLinearIsometry (H := H)))

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.TraceClass.tracePairingEquiv
declarations.doc: The isometric identification of `H →L[ℂ] H` with the strong dual of its trace class.
declarations.statement: def tracePairingEquiv : (H →L[ℂ] H) ≃ₗᵢ[ℂ] StrongDual ℂ (TraceClass H)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.TraceClass.tracePairingEquiv_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma tracePairingEquiv_apply (A : H →L[ℂ] H) :
    tracePairingEquiv A = tracePairing A

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.instWStarAlgebraStructureContinuousLinearMap
declarations.doc:
**The bounded operators form a W⋆-algebra**, with predual the trace-class operators and the
trace pairing `a ↦ (ρ ↦ Tr (a ρ))`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable instance instWStarAlgebraStructureContinuousLinearMap :
    WStarAlgebraStructure (H →L[ℂ] H)

modules.title: The complex conjugate of a normed space
modules.doc:
The complex conjugate `ConjSpace X` of a complex normed space, with twisted scalar action.

## i. Overview

`ConjSpace X` is `X` with scalar multiplication twisted by complex conjugation: `c • x` in
`ConjSpace X` is `conj c • x` in `X`. It turns conjugate-linear maps on `X` into linear maps on
`ConjSpace X`.

## ii. Key results

- `ConjSpace` : the complex conjugate of a normed space.
- `ConjSpace.toConj`, `ConjSpace.ofConj` : the identity maps between `X` and `ConjSpace X`.
- `ConjSpace.instNormedSpace` : the conjugate normed space structure.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The conjugate space and the identity maps
- B. The additive and normed group structure
- C. The conjugate scalar action

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. The conjugate space and the identity maps
## B. The additive and normed group structure

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.ConjSpace
declarations.doc: The complex conjugate of `X`: the same type, with `c • x = conj c • x`.
declarations.statement: def ConjSpace (X : Type*) : Type _

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.ConjSpace.toConj
declarations.doc:
The identity, viewed as the map from `X` into `ConjSpace X`. Spelled out explicitly (instead
of relying on the bare definitional equality `ConjSpace X := X`) to keep instance search from
having to guess which scalar action a plain type ascription intends.
declarations.statement: def toConj (x : X) : ConjSpace X

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.ConjSpace.ofConj
declarations.doc: The identity, viewed as the map from `ConjSpace X` back into `X`.
declarations.statement: def ofConj (x : ConjSpace X) : X

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.ConjSpace.ofConj_toConj
declarations.statement: lemma ofConj_toConj (x : X) : ofConj (toConj x) = x

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.ConjSpace.toConj_ofConj
declarations.statement: lemma toConj_ofConj (x : ConjSpace X) : toConj (ofConj x) = x

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.ConjSpace.instAddCommGroup
declarations.statement: instance instAddCommGroup [AddCommGroup X] : AddCommGroup (ConjSpace X)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.ConjSpace.ofConj_add
declarations.statement:
lemma ofConj_add [AddCommGroup X] (x y : ConjSpace X) :
    ofConj (x + y) = ofConj x + ofConj y

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.ConjSpace.ofConj_zero
declarations.statement: lemma ofConj_zero [AddCommGroup X] : ofConj (0 : ConjSpace X) = 0

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.ConjSpace.toConj_add
declarations.statement:
lemma toConj_add [AddCommGroup X] (x y : X) :
    toConj (x + y) = toConj x + toConj y

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.ConjSpace.toConj_zero
declarations.statement: lemma toConj_zero [AddCommGroup X] : toConj (0 : X) = 0

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.ConjSpace.instNormedAddCommGroup
declarations.statement:
instance instNormedAddCommGroup [NormedAddCommGroup X] :
    NormedAddCommGroup (ConjSpace X)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.ConjSpace.norm_ofConj
declarations.statement: lemma norm_ofConj [NormedAddCommGroup X] (x : ConjSpace X) : ‖ofConj x‖ = ‖x‖

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.ConjSpace.norm_toConj
declarations.statement: lemma norm_toConj [NormedAddCommGroup X] (x : X) : ‖toConj x‖ = ‖x‖

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.ConjSpace.instSMul
declarations.doc:
The twisted scalar action: `c • x := (starRingEnd ℂ c) • ofConj x`, moved back into
`ConjSpace X` via `toConj`.
declarations.statement: instance instSMul : SMul ℂ (ConjSpace X)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.ConjSpace.smul_def
declarations.statement:
lemma smul_def (c : ℂ) (x : ConjSpace X) :
    c • x = toConj ((starRingEnd ℂ c) • ofConj x)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.ConjSpace.ofConj_smul
declarations.statement:
lemma ofConj_smul (c : ℂ) (x : ConjSpace X) :
    ofConj (c • x) = (starRingEnd ℂ c) • ofConj x

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.ConjSpace.instModule
declarations.doc: The conjugate module structure on `ConjSpace X`.
declarations.statement: instance instModule : Module ℂ (ConjSpace X)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.ConjSpace.instNormedSpace
declarations.doc:
The norm on `ConjSpace X` is literally `X`'s norm (via `ofConj`), so `norm_smul_le` reduces to
`‖conj c‖ = ‖c‖` (`Complex.norm_conj`) composed with `X`'s own `norm_smul_le`.
declarations.statement: instance instNormedSpace : NormedSpace ℂ (ConjSpace X)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.ConjSpace.instCompleteSpace
declarations.doc: `ConjSpace X` is complete when `X` is.
declarations.statement: instance instCompleteSpace [CompleteSpace X] : CompleteSpace (ConjSpace X)

modules.title: W⋆-algebra structures are W⋆-algebras
modules.doc:
A W⋆-algebra structure with a chosen predual gives a W⋆-algebra in Mathlib's sense.

## i. Overview

Mathlib's `WStarAlgebra` asks for a conjugate-linear isometric isomorphism from the dual of a Banach
space onto `A`. For any Banach space `X`, `f ↦ conj ∘ f` is a conjugate-linear isometric isomorphism
from the dual of `X` to the dual of `ConjSpace X`. Composing with the inverse of the linear
identification of `A` with the dual of its predual shows that a W⋆-algebra structure gives a
W⋆-algebra in Mathlib's sense, when the predual lives in the same universe as `A`.

## ii. Key results

- `PhiEquiv` : the conjugate-linear isometric isomorphism between the duals of `X` and `ConjSpace
  X`.
- `WStarAlgebraStructure.toWStarAlgebra` : a W⋆-algebra structure gives a W⋆-algebra.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The conjugate-linear self-duality `Phi` of the strong dual, via `ConjSpace`
- B. Closing the connection to Mathlib's `WStarAlgebra`

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. The conjugate-linear self-duality `Phi` of the strong dual, via `ConjSpace`
## B. Closing the connection to Mathlib's `WStarAlgebra`

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.PhiLM
declarations.doc: The map `f ↦ (x ↦ conj (f x))` from the dual of `X` to linear functionals on `ConjSpace X`.
declarations.statement: def PhiLM (f : StrongDual ℂ X) : ConjSpace X →ₗ[ℂ] ℂ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Phi
declarations.doc:
`Phi f`, as a continuous linear functional on `ConjSpace X`: the same bound `‖f‖` works, since
`conj` is an isometry of `ℂ`.
declarations.statement: def Phi (f : StrongDual ℂ X) : StrongDual ℂ (ConjSpace X)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Phi_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma Phi_apply (f : StrongDual ℂ X) (x : ConjSpace X) :
    Phi f x = starRingEnd ℂ (f (ofConj x))

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.PsiLM
declarations.doc:
The linear part of `Psi`, the same construction the other way around:
`g ↦ (x ↦ conj (g (toConj x)))`.
declarations.statement: def PsiLM (g : StrongDual ℂ (ConjSpace X)) : X →ₗ[ℂ] ℂ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Psi
declarations.doc: `Psi g`, as a continuous linear functional on `X`.
declarations.statement: def Psi (g : StrongDual ℂ (ConjSpace X)) : StrongDual ℂ X

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Psi_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma Psi_apply (g : StrongDual ℂ (ConjSpace X)) (x : X) :
    Psi g x = starRingEnd ℂ (g (toConj x))

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Psi_Phi
declarations.doc: `Psi` undoes `Phi`: `conj (conj (f x)) = f x`.
declarations.statement: lemma Psi_Phi (f : StrongDual ℂ X) : Psi (Phi f) = f

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.Phi_Psi
declarations.doc: `Phi` undoes `Psi`, the same computation run the other way.
declarations.statement: lemma Phi_Psi (g : StrongDual ℂ (ConjSpace X)) : Phi (Psi g) = g

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.PhiLM'
declarations.doc:
`Phi`, bundled as a (conjugate-)linear map `StrongDual ℂ X →ₛₗ[starRingEnd ℂ]
StrongDual ℂ (ConjSpace X)`: additive since `conj` and evaluation both are, and conjugate-linear
in `f` because `conj ((c • f) x) = conj (c * f x) = conj c * conj (f x)`.
declarations.statement: def PhiLM' : StrongDual ℂ X →ₛₗ[starRingEnd ℂ] StrongDual ℂ (ConjSpace X)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.norm_Phi_le
declarations.doc: `‖Phi f‖ ≤ ‖f‖`, from the bound used to build `Phi f` via `LinearMap.mkContinuous`.
declarations.statement: lemma norm_Phi_le (f : StrongDual ℂ X) : ‖Phi f‖ ≤ ‖f‖

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.norm_Psi_le
declarations.doc: `‖Psi g‖ ≤ ‖g‖`, the mirror-image bound for `Psi`.
declarations.statement: lemma norm_Psi_le (g : StrongDual ℂ (ConjSpace X)) : ‖Psi g‖ ≤ ‖g‖

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.norm_Phi_eq
declarations.doc:
`Phi` is isometric: `≤` from `norm_Phi_le` directly, `≥` from applying `norm_Psi_le` to
`Phi f` and using that `Psi` undoes `Phi`.
declarations.statement: lemma norm_Phi_eq (f : StrongDual ℂ X) : ‖Phi f‖ = ‖f‖

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.PhiLI
declarations.doc: `Phi`, bundled as a conjugate-linear *isometric embedding*.
declarations.statement: def PhiLI : StrongDual ℂ X →ₛₗᵢ[starRingEnd ℂ] StrongDual ℂ (ConjSpace X)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.PhiEquiv
declarations.doc:
**`Phi`, bundled as a conjugate-linear isometric equivalence.** Surjective because `Psi` is a
two-sided inverse (`Phi_Psi`); an isometric embedding is automatically injective, so this is
exactly `Phi`'s promotion to a `≃ₗᵢ⋆[ℂ]`.
declarations.statement: def PhiEquiv : StrongDual ℂ X ≃ₗᵢ⋆[ℂ] StrongDual ℂ (ConjSpace X)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.WStarAlgebraStructure.toWStarAlgebra
declarations.doc:
**A W⋆-algebra structure gives a W⋆-algebra** in Mathlib's sense, when the predual lives in the
universe of `A`.
declarations.statement:
lemma WStarAlgebraStructure.toWStarAlgebra
    {A : Type u} [WStarAlgebraStructure.{u, u} A] : WStarAlgebra A

modules.title: Rank-one operators in the trace pairing
modules.doc:
The trace pairing of a rank-one operator `|x⟩⟨y|` with a trace-class `T` is `⟪y, T x⟫`.

## i. Overview

For a bounded operator `A` and a trace-class operator `T`, the trace pairing of `A |x⟩⟨y|` with `T`
is a matrix coefficient. This recovers a predual element from its values on rank-one operators.

## ii. Key results

- `trace_rankOne_formula` : the trace of a rank-one operator times a trace-class operator.
- `TraceClass.tracePairing_rankOne_left` : the trace pairing with a rank-one operator.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The trace of a rank-one operator
- B. The trace pairing with a rank-one operator

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. The trace of a rank-one operator
## B. The trace pairing with a rank-one operator

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.TraceClass.trace_rankOne_formula
declarations.statement:
lemma trace_rankOne_formula (x y : H) :
    trace (InnerProductSpace.rankOne ℂ x y) (isTraceClass_rankOne x y) =
      ⟪y, x⟫_ℂ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.TraceClass.tracePairing_rankOne_left
declarations.statement:
lemma tracePairing_rankOne_left (T : TraceClass H) (x y : H) :
    tracePairing (InnerProductSpace.rankOne ℂ x y) T =
      ⟪y, T.1 x⟫_ℂ

modules.title: The trace pairing is isometric
modules.doc:
The trace pairing of bounded operators against trace-class operators is an isometry.

## i. Overview

The trace of `A |x⟩⟨y|` is `⟪y, A x⟫`, so testing the trace pairing of a bounded operator `A` on
rank-one operators recovers its operator norm. Together with `‖Tr (A ·)‖ ≤ ‖A‖` this shows that the
trace pairing is an isometry.

## ii. Key results

- `trace_rankOne` : the trace of a rank-one operator.
- `TraceClass.norm_tracePairing` : `‖Tr (A ·)‖ = ‖A‖`.
- `TraceClass.tracePairingLinearIsometry` : the trace pairing as a linear isometry.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Rank-one operators are trace class
- B. The trace pairing with rank-one operators
- C. The norm of the trace pairing
- D. The trace pairing as a linear isometry

## iv. References

* None.

      ⟪y, A x⟫_ℂ

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.TraceClass.norm_le_tracePairing

modules.title: The trace pairing is surjective
modules.doc:
Every continuous functional on the trace-class operators is a trace pairing `Tr (A ·)`.

## i. Overview

A continuous functional on the trace-class operators defines a bounded sesquilinear form by
evaluation on rank-one operators, and the Riesz theorem turns it into a bounded operator `A`. The
functional and `Tr (A ·)` agree on rank-one operators, whose span is dense: every trace-class
operator is approximated by finite truncations of its Hilbert–Schmidt factorization. So every
continuous functional is a trace pairing.

## ii. Key results

- `TraceClass.sesquilinearFormOfFunctional` : the sesquilinear form of a functional.
- `TraceClass.rankOneSpan_dense` : rank-one operators span a dense subspace.
- `TraceClass.tracePairing_surjective_concrete` : every continuous functional on the trace class is
  a trace pairing.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Hilbert–Schmidt finite truncations

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text:
## A. Hilbert–Schmidt finite truncations

The density theorem is obtained by truncating a Hilbert–Schmidt factor in a Hilbert basis. The
following definitions and identities are kept separate from the final topological argument so they
can also be reused for other trace-ideal approximation results.

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.TraceClass.rankOneTraceClass
declarations.doc: The rank-one operator `|x⟩⟨y|`, packaged as a trace-class operator.
declarations.statement: def rankOneTraceClass (x y : H) : TraceClass H

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.TraceClass.rankOneTraceClass_norm_le
declarations.statement:
lemma rankOneTraceClass_norm_le (x y : H) :
    ‖rankOneTraceClass x y‖ ≤ ‖x‖ * ‖y‖

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.TraceClass.rankOneSpan
declarations.doc: The trace-class subspace generated by rank-one operators.
declarations.statement: def rankOneSpan : Submodule ℂ (TraceClass H)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.TraceClass.sesquilinearFormOfFunctional
declarations.doc:
The bounded sesquilinear form `(x, y) ↦ conj (φ |x⟩⟨y|)` of a continuous functional `φ` on the
trace class.
declarations.statement:
def sesquilinearFormOfFunctional
    (φ : TraceClass H →L[ℂ] ℂ) :
    BoundedSesquilinearForm H

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.TraceClass.sesquilinearFormOfFunctional_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma sesquilinearFormOfFunctional_apply
    (φ : TraceClass H →L[ℂ] ℂ) (x y : H) :
    (sesquilinearFormOfFunctional φ).form x y =
      starRingEnd ℂ (φ (rankOneTraceClass x y))

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.TraceClass.pairing_eq_functional_on_rankOne
declarations.statement:
lemma pairing_eq_functional_on_rankOne
    (φ : TraceClass H →L[ℂ] ℂ) (x y : H) :
    tracePairing (sesquilinearFormOfFunctional φ).operator
        (rankOneTraceClass x y) = φ (rankOneTraceClass x y)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.TraceClass.tracePairing_surjective_of_rankOneSpan_dense
declarations.doc:
If rank-one operators span a dense subspace of the trace class, every continuous functional on
the trace class is a trace pairing `Tr (A ·)`, with `A` represented by the sesquilinear form of the
functional.
declarations.statement:
lemma tracePairing_surjective_of_rankOneSpan_dense
    (hDense : Dense (rankOneSpan (H := H) : Set (TraceClass H))) :
    Function.Surjective
      (tracePairingLinearIsometry (H := H) :
        (H →L[ℂ] H) → TraceClass H →L[ℂ] ℂ)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.TraceClass.hilbertSchmidtPartial
declarations.doc: The Hilbert-Schmidt partial sum `∑_{i ∈ F} |S bᵢ⟩⟨bᵢ|`.
declarations.statement:
def hilbertSchmidtPartial {w : Set H} (S : H →L[ℂ] H) (b : HilbertBasis w ℂ H)
    (F : Finset w) : H →L[ℂ] H

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.TraceClass.hilbertSchmidtPartial_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma hilbertSchmidtPartial_apply {w : Set H} (S : H →L[ℂ] H)
    (b : HilbertBasis w ℂ H) (F : Finset w) (x : H) :
    hilbertSchmidtPartial S b F x =
      ∑ i ∈ F, ⟪b i, x⟫_ℂ • S (b i)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.TraceClass.hilbertSchmidtPartial_apply_basis
declarations.statement:
lemma hilbertSchmidtPartial_apply_basis {w : Set H} (S : H →L[ℂ] H)
    (b : HilbertBasis w ℂ H) [DecidableEq w] (F : Finset w) (j : w) :
    hilbertSchmidtPartial S b F (b j) =
      if j ∈ F then S (b j) else 0

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.TraceClass.hilbertSchmidt_sub_partial_apply_basis
declarations.statement:
lemma hilbertSchmidt_sub_partial_apply_basis {w : Set H} (S : H →L[ℂ] H)
    (b : HilbertBasis w ℂ H) [DecidableEq w] (F : Finset w) (j : w) :
    (S - hilbertSchmidtPartial S b F) (b j) =
      if j ∈ F then 0 else S (b j)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.TraceClass.hilbertSchmidt_sub_partial_isHilbertSchmidt
declarations.statement:
lemma hilbertSchmidt_sub_partial_isHilbertSchmidt
    {w : Set H} (S : H →L[ℂ] H) (b : HilbertBasis w ℂ H)
    [DecidableEq w] (F : Finset w) (hS : HilbertSchmidt.IsHilbertSchmidt S) :
    HilbertSchmidt.IsHilbertSchmidt (S - hilbertSchmidtPartial S b F)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.TraceClass.hilbertSchmidt_sub_partial_tsum_norm_sq
declarations.statement:
lemma hilbertSchmidt_sub_partial_tsum_norm_sq {w : Set H} (S : H →L[ℂ] H)
    (b : HilbertBasis w ℂ H) (F : Finset w)
    (hS : HilbertSchmidt.IsHilbertSchmidt S) :
    ∑' i : w, ‖(S - hilbertSchmidtPartial S b F) (b i)‖ ^ 2 =
      ∑' j : {j : w // j ∉ F}, ‖S (b j)‖ ^ 2

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.TraceClass.traceClassPartial
declarations.doc: The trace-class partial sum `∑_{i ∈ F} |R(S bᵢ)⟩⟨bᵢ|`.
declarations.statement:
def traceClassPartial {w : Set H} (R S : H →L[ℂ] H) (b : HilbertBasis w ℂ H)
    (F : Finset w) : TraceClass H

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.TraceClass.mul_rankOne_apply_left
declarations.statement:
lemma mul_rankOne_apply_left {R : H →L[ℂ] H} (x y : H) :
    R * InnerProductSpace.rankOne ℂ x y =
      InnerProductSpace.rankOne ℂ (R x) y

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.TraceClass.traceClassPartial_coe
declarations.statement:
lemma traceClassPartial_coe {w : Set H} (R S : H →L[ℂ] H)
    (b : HilbertBasis w ℂ H) (F : Finset w) :
    (traceClassPartial R S b F).1 = R * hilbertSchmidtPartial S b F

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.TraceClass.traceClassPartial_mem_rankOneSpan
declarations.statement:
lemma traceClassPartial_mem_rankOneSpan {w : Set H} (R S : H →L[ℂ] H)
    (b : HilbertBasis w ℂ H) (F : Finset w) :
    traceClassPartial R S b F ∈ rankOneSpan (H := H)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.TraceClass.norm_sub_traceClassPartial_le
declarations.statement:
lemma norm_sub_traceClassPartial_le {T R S : H →L[ℂ] H} (hT : IsTraceClass T)
    (hfactor : R * S = T) (hR : HilbertSchmidt.IsHilbertSchmidt R)
    (hS : HilbertSchmidt.IsHilbertSchmidt S) {w : Set H}
    (b : HilbertBasis w ℂ H) (F : Finset w) :
    ‖ofOperator T hT - traceClassPartial R S b F‖ ≤
      Real.sqrt (∑' i : w, ‖R (b i)‖ ^ 2) *
        Real.sqrt (∑' i : w, ‖(S - hilbertSchmidtPartial S b F) (b i)‖ ^ 2)

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.TraceClass.rankOneSpan_dense
declarations.statement:
lemma rankOneSpan_dense :
    Dense (rankOneSpan (H := H) : Set (TraceClass H))

declarations.name: ProbabilisticTheory.TraceClass.tracePairing_surjective_concrete
declarations.doc: The density theorem discharges the only hypothesis in the Riesz/surjectivity argument.
declarations.statement:
lemma tracePairing_surjective_concrete :
    Function.Surjective
      (tracePairingLinearIsometry (H := H) :
        (H →L[ℂ] H) → TraceClass H →L[ℂ] ℂ)
